author: lanabretterebner
body:
These four commits were pushed to the branch after PR #13 had already merged, so they never reached `main`. This PR carries them.

## The Spectrum palette now reads the audio

It was a fixed sweep across the lane's width — `hue = 0.72 - 0.62 * positionAcross`. It looked like a spectrum and meant nothing: a sine tone and a drum loop came out identically coloured, and the same lane redrawn at a different zoom recoloured itself.

It now maps the **spectral centroid** of the audio under each column. Measured over a probe with three sections:

| section | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| 80 Hz sub | ramps 0→1 by position | **0.079** |
| 900 Hz mid | ramps 0→1 by position | **0.554** |
| bright noise | ramps 0→1 by position | **1.000** |

The analysis is plain C++ with no JUCE dependency, FFT included, so all of it is exercised by a test target without standing up a plugin — and the plugin does not have to link `juce_dsp` for one transform. **Spectrum is now the default palette** for a fresh instance; saved state still wins.

## The waveform is redrawn from a peak envelope

Lanes sampled a JUCE `AudioThumbnail` once per bar per repaint — tens of thousands of queries a second across six lanes, which is where the sluggishness came from, and the bars were far coarser than the well could show. Analysis now reduces each stem to a per-channel min/max envelope at ~2 ms, in the same pass that computes its spectrum, and painting becomes indexing. One column per pixel instead of a bar every four.

**The waveform also stopped crawling.** A view scrolling under a moving playhead re-bucketed the audio every frame: each column covered a slightly different span, its peak jumped to a neighbouring sample, and the whole picture shimmered while the audio sat still. The window's start now snaps to a whole column of time, so a scroll translates by whole columns and every column keeps exactly the audio it had. Columns are cached against that snapped window, so a still lane costs nothing.

**Stereo** draws as two half-height waveforms. Which side a part sits on is information, and summing hides anything that cancels.

## Gestures split in two

- Each lane gains a **drag handle**, beside the name, and dragging it carries the stem to a DAW or a folder.
- **Dragging the waveform sweeps a selection**, which is the preview loop. Double-click clears it; a click that does not move still seeks. This is the first thing to reach the selection backend that came in with 0.9.9, which until now nothing called.

## Two bugs found while wiring that up

- **Solo and mute did nothing on a split group.** The mix plays leaves, so a root that was split has no entry of its own and its flags reached nothing: muting Drums after splitting it into Kick and Snare was silent. Each leaf now carries its ancestor chain, and the mix ORs solo and mute down it.
- **A swept range only looped if its lane happened to be soloed**, because the loop followed the previewed lane. The transport is shared by every lane, so the loop is a property of the transport: the last range drawn owns it, and only that lane can clear it.

## Also

- Beats carry `bar.beat` labels once they are far enough apart to hold one.
- The layers glyph becomes a **kebab**, tooltip "Stem actions" — and is no longer hidden on stems with no adaptive split, which had left **Convert to MIDI unreachable on Bass**.
- **Lane menus anchor to their button.** Root menus targeted the whole lane row, which spans the panel, so they opened against its left edge.
- The **palette icon** is redrawn: its thumb hole crossed the body outline, and under even-odd winding the part lying outside was filled, hanging a stray crescent off the side.
- The disclosure twisty is bigger and no longer butts against the include checkbox; lane wells sit 2px apart rather than 10.

## Verification

- `StemLabWaveformAnalysisTests`: FFT checked against a naive DFT bin-for-bin, tone-lands-in-its-own-bin, centroid arithmetic including DC rejection and silence, log mapping monotonic and octave-linear, per-channel peak extremes, sub-frame and out-of-range spans, long-file decimation, and lookup clamping. Both C++ test targets pass.
- Plugin builds clean.
- Driven in the standalone against a real separation: stereo split, spectral colour tracking the probe's three sections, bar and `bar.beat` labels, a swept loop range rendering on Bass, a lane menu opening under its own button.
- **Not verified visually: the crawl fix.** The snapping logic and column cache are right by construction and the analysis is unit-tested, but a scrolling waveform cannot be judged in a headless X server — worth a look before trusting it.

author: etsu33
body:
## Context: MISSING_PIPELINE_BRIDGE

`docs/audit/shrine-knowledge-recommendation-evidence-bridge.md` (PR #2571) found that imported Shrine Knowledge never automatically becomes Recommendation Evidence. `docs/audit/recommendation-evidence-followup-design.md` (PR #2572) evaluated designs to close that gap and recommended: reuse `Shrine.goriyaku`/`GoriyakuTag` as-is, add a separate Recommendation Evidence Review document, record provenance outside the DB. This PR formalizes that recommendation as a normative contract.

## New review responsibility

Adds `docs/knowledge/recommendation-evidence-review-contract.md`, defining what a reviewer may convert into `Shrine.goriyaku`/`GoriyakuTag`, what must be rejected or held, and what audit trail is required — a responsibility current Human Review (Fact ↔ Source correctness only) does not cover.

## Fact vs Recommendation Evidence separation

The contract states explicitly: `Knowledge Fact correctness ≠ Recommendation eligibility`, with a full boundary table (explicit official blessing / deity identity / historical event / founding story / tradition / historical anecdote / tourism description / editorial summary / AI-generated interpretation).

## Existing `goriyaku` / GoriyakuTag reuse

No new Model, migration, or schema. `Shrine.goriyaku` (free-text) and the existing 39-row `GoriyakuTag` vocabulary are reused as-is, with a strict exact-match/narrow-normalization rule that prevents `backfill_goriyaku_tags`'s `get_or_create` from silently minting new taxonomy.

## Provenance

Markdown review document (shrine, Source reference, Source phrase, proposed canonical text, resulting tag, decision, reviewer note, HOLD reason) — no DB schema change, same pattern already used for Batch 17 Knowledge Fact Human Review.

## Review states

PASS / HOLD / NO_EVIDENCE / REVISE, kept fully separate from Knowledge `verification_status`.

## Batch 17 pilot next

A reusable review-table template is included (Section 13), pre-populated only with conclusions already established in the merged PR #2572 audit (北海道神宮=NO_EXPLICIT_EVIDENCE, 建部大社=REVIEW_REQUIRED, 波上宮=READY). This PR does **not** execute that review.

## Batch 18 sequencing

Recommends decoupling Knowledge Import from Recommendation Evidence Review (Option B, Section 10) — Knowledge can import first; Recommendation Evidence Review follows as an independent, non-blocking stage. Batch 18 Fact Generation is not started by this PR.

## DB/Model/Engine/UI changes

**0.** Docs-only PR.

## Mother Ship decision

Section 18 of the contract lists the open decision points (whether to run the Batch 17 pilot next, whether Batch 18 should wait) for Mother Ship input.

**STOP. Draft PR only — do not auto-merge.**

## Goal
Close the post-#721 consumer propagation gap without changing GPT/Codex role semantics.

## Scope
Bounded correction only:
- `docs/PLANNING_SEQUENCE_AND_EVIDENCE_POLICY.md`
- `skills/maintaining-project-context-and-handoff/SKILL.md`
- `skills/maintaining-project-context-and-handoff/LEARNING_LOG.md` (required freshness companion)
- `tests/test_gpt_codex_workflow_contract.py`

## Existing Solution First
No new Skill, workflow, owner, role model, or handoff framework. Reuse `docs/GPT_CODEX_WORKFLOW_POLICY.md`, `references/gpt-codex-implementation-handoff.md`, and the existing project work-instruction template as canonical semantics.

## TDD evidence
- RED test-only head: `d8e4fa8fea55a3b0b28bd8c4e12484ec6e4d8d0c`.
- The new focused contract failed exactly because the active Planning Sequence lacked `PLAY_MEANINGFUL_WORK_SLICE` and the ACTIVE Handoff Skill lacked the same Slice/stop contract.
- First production head exposed one additional existing invariant: changing an ACTIVE Skill requires a Learning Log companion. Canonical-reference freshness failed closed rather than being bypassed.
- Final exact head: `93ddada86e7655c79d7f66de839cc30293ff91c6`.

## Change
- replace the stale active `GPT-first / Codex optional` / `OPTIONAL_CODEX_EXECUTOR` planning protocol with the already-canonical `PLAY_MEANINGFUL_WORK_SLICE → PLANNING_CANON_BEFORE_HANDOFF → PRE_HANDOFF_GPT_STOP → ACTUAL GODOT PRODUCT IMPLEMENTATION → Codex` boundary;
- keep GPT as planning/review/Base/Notion owner and Codex as actual game-project Godot product implementation owner;
- make the ACTIVE Handoff Skill thin-route to the canonical policy and packaged handoff reference;
- expose `work_slice_id`, `explicit_non_scope`, data/UI/asset dependency fields and review evidence in the active handoff input contract;
- record the consumer-propagation lesson required by the existing freshness policy;
- add regression coverage for the two active consumers.

## Adversarial review 5x
1. **Duplicate-owner attack:** no new owner/Skill/reference; existing owners are reused.
2. **Role-expansion attack:** Codex remains Godot-product-only, not a general repository executor.
3. **Technical-autonomy attack:** `PRE_HANDOFF_GPT_STOP` explicitly prevents GPT from fixing Node/Scene/function implementation details before Codex.
4. **No-product-work attack:** planning without actual Godot product implementation remains GPT-owned and can close without a Codex stage.
5. **Historical-evidence attack:** historical Learning Log records are preserved; only the active Planning Sequence loses the stale current protocol.

- Validate v4.7 Workflow Alignment `32940731584`: SUCCESS

Pre-merge compare is limited to the four intended files. Runtime/project/human usability was not executed by this Base correction.

This proves Base consumer propagation and repository validation only. It does not prove actual project runtime, Codex implementation quality, or human usability.

author: jurajmajerik
body:
## Problem

claude.ai silently hides any tool whose serialized schema is longer than about 16,384 characters. Our exec tool's schema embeds a directory of all tool families, so it grows a little with every tool we enable. It recently sat 5 characters under the limit: enabling one more tool would have made the exec tool disappear for every claude.ai user, with no error anywhere. Recent trims (moving URL rules behind exec learn) bought some room back, but the wall returns as the catalog grows.

## Changes

- The exec command reference gets a size budget (15,200 characters). Under the budget, the output is unchanged, byte for byte. That is the case today: all prompt snapshots pass without changes.
- Over the budget, only the tool family directory shrinks: sub-entries fold into their family, for example the 24 experiment-* entries would become one "experiment" entry.
- This is the same shrink-on-overflow mechanism `buildExecInstructions` already uses for the Claude Code instructions payload, applied to the claude.ai schema path too.

This is a preparatory PR for #86946, which enables a new experiments tool. The two are independent: the tool currently fits, this just makes sure the next tools keep fitting.

## How did you test this code?

- Full MCP unit suite passes (2740 tests) with no snapshot updates, which proves the output is unchanged today.
- The worst-case budget test in instructions-formatter-snapshot.test.ts covers the cap; with this change the overflow path keeps it under the limit no matter how many tools are enabled.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Authored in a Claude Code session directed by @jurajmajerik. Extracted from #86946 after stamphog flagged the cross-cutting change for platform review. The budget value (15,200) leaves about 1,200 characters for the schema's fixed structure, the exec tool description, and the injected context property.

author: milospaunovic
body: Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra-ee/issues/10420. ### ✨ Description When a `YAML` `flow` or any multi-line code snippet is pasted into the `AI Copilot` composer, the sent message showed up in the chat as one long flattened string, because the user bubble rendered the prompt through default HTML whitespace collapsing. Assistant replies already render code blocks through `KsMarkdown`; only the user side was affected. Two changes in `CopilotMessage.vue`: - The user bubble now preserves line breaks and indentation (`white-space: pre-wrap`), so pasted code stays readable even without fences. - Any ``` fenced segment of the prompt is rendered as a literal monospace code block, styled with design-system tokens. An unclosed fence runs to the end of the prompt, matching how markdown renderers treat it. Full markdown rendering of user text was deliberately avoided: the prompt must stay literal, otherwise a pasted `YAML` comment like `# retries` would be reinterpreted as a heading and lists or emphasis would mangle the pasted content. Covered by three new unit tests (fenced segment, unclosed fence, plain multi-line prompt) and a new `UserPromptWithCode` Storybook story for visual review in both themes. ### 🎨 Frontend Checklist - [x] Type checking passes (`npm run check:types`) - [x] Code builds without errors (`npm run build`) - [x] Unit tests pass (`npm run test:unit`) - [x] Translations are complete if `en.json` changed (`npm run translations:check` reports no missing, extra, or stale keys) - [x] Screenshots or video recordings attached showing the `UI` changes ### Before ### After

body:
## Mission

Produce one versioned Base token contract for the next 10M baseline by combining the current executed tokenizer-family authority with TOK-115/RECOVER-173 boundary evidence.

## Contract decision

- family: canonical `s0-byte-v1`
- ordinary IDs: raw bytes `0..255`
- EOS/EOD: **none**; RECOVER-173 remains provisional and observed 0/30 EOS generation terminations
- padding: mask-only storage fill ID 0, never semantic PAD
- empty generation context: reject
- document packing: isolated; no cross-document causal transitions without EOS
- BOS/PAD/UNK/instruction/system/chat tokens: none
- HF/Transformers token mapping: all special-token IDs explicit `null`, vocab size 256
- checkpoint incompatibility: tokenizer/vocab/model-vocab/packing mismatches fail closed before mutation

At this contract cut no independent TOK-188 PR/commit/artifact is published. The PR therefore does not fabricate a concurrent decision: byte remains the current executed MILESTONE-150 10M baseline authority, and a later TOK-188 promotion must issue a new contract version.

## Executed ~500K same-contract regression authority

The terminal accepted MILESTONE-150 producer is an exact semantic regression for this proposed contract: workflow run `32937411703`, source `5838cd16869dcfcf762368d8673eddf52d51b7e3`, conclusion `success`, artifact `9595677772` (`milestone150-learned-base-ladder-v1`), artifact digest `sha256:c00b7e9006320f8916c739a3311e8cc47ad0d0b16957f8ebd7d19233fd9f1c71`.

Its 500K rung proves under DATA-25:

- 467,808 parameters; ModelSpec `208ac8ca113388e76f280d0154cae815785bee7705546f4d854d9447b9dd1f4a`;
- `s0-byte-v1`, vocab 256, no special tokens, config/vocab identities identical to this contract;
- document-isolated `s0-byte-pack-v1`, seq128, no cross-document transitions;
- 948,504 actual optimized targets over 1000 optimizer steps;
- checkpoint 500 -> fresh process -> first resumed step 501 -> step 1000 PASS;
- initial held-out BPB `7.939260616864241` -> final/best `0.2645455968814711` at step 1000;
- final strata BPB: UK `0.37933297833635227`, EN `0.12579645499499625`, code `0.1781162699814322`;
- retained final checkpoint ID `8d13262139f3fcb89c7efb141c7a449e4faba9048166d0dd2f49eba4288b4524`;
- fresh retained checkpoint verification `PASS`.

This is consumed as the required executed ~500K regression because its token/boundary/padding/empty-special-token contract is exactly the proposed v1 semantics. It is not relabeled as a TOK-189 source SHA.

## TOK-189 exact-head regression and proofs

The dedicated LOCAL_FREE workflow uses ENV-151 universal bootstrap and reruns the same retained 467,808-parameter MILESTONE-150 geometry on the exact DATA-25 truth model. It trains to checkpoint 500, resumes in a fresh process to step 1000, freshly verifies checkpoint/eval/generation, proves an intentionally incompatible tokenizer identity is rejected before model/trainer/RNG mutation, and emits `tok189-evidence/final-report.json`.

Exact TOK-189 run `32940181933` is currently queued because repository hosted-runner capacity is saturated; queued status is not claimed as PASS and is not required to fabricate the already-terminal same-contract 500K evidence above.

## Truth boundary

No tokenizer algorithm, chat/instruction token, paid compute, pretrained weights, or representative-data claim is introduced. DATA-25 remains project-authored. A future accepted family change or scientifically accepted EOS boundary requires a new immutable contract version; v1 is not silently rewritten.

author: happytomatoe
body:
## 💡 What?
Release CI now packs the GNOME extension via the same `just gnome-ext-pack` recipe used locally, so published zips include the `prefs/` and `vendor/` directories.

## ❓ Why?
The release workflow hand-copied only top-level files (`cp gnome-ext/*.js …`), never the `prefs/` subdirectory. Every published `voice-to-text@happytomatoe.com.shell-extension.zip` therefore shipped **without `prefs/config-sync.js`**, causing `ImportError` when opening extension preferences — the bug reported repeatedly after installing via the README curl command. Local installs (`just gnome-ext-install`, which rsyncs the full dir) worked, masking it.

## 🛠️ How?
- Add `extractions/setup-just@v2` step to the release job.
- Replace the manual `cp`/zip block with `just gnome-ext-pack` (rsync-based, excludes tests/run-dev.sh, includes `prefs/` + `vendor/`).
- Install `rsync zip libglib2.0-bin` in the pack step so `gnome-ext-pack` (rsync + glib-compile-schemas) runs on a clean ubuntu-latest runner.
- Keep the version-bump `sed` on `gnome-ext/metadata.json` (rsync picks it up).

## 🐛 Bug fixes
- **Missing `prefs/` in release zip** — root cause: CI copied only top-level files; fix: delegate packing to `just gnome-ext-pack` which mirrors the local install.

author: michaelcaxias
body:
## Problema

O step de SSH ficava pendurado infinitamente após o `docker compose up --build -d` ser concluído com sucesso. O deploy funcionava corretamente, mas o canal SSH não fechava.

**Causa:** o `appleboy/ssh-action` aguarda o canal SSH fechar antes de marcar o step como concluído. O `docker compose up -d` deixa processos filhos com stdin/stdout abertos, impedindo o fechamento.

## Solução

Adicionadas duas opções ao `ssh-action`:

| Opção | Valor | Efeito |
|---|---|---|
| `script_stop` | `true` | Aborta na primeira linha com erro (equivalente a `set -e`) |
| `command_timeout` | `10m` | Força o encerramento do canal SSH após 10 min, nunca deixa o CI preso para sempre |

author: igorjs
body:
## Summary

Episode edges that named a handle target with a stray leading or trailing space got rejected as an unrecognized reference. `is_handle_shaped` checked for alphanumeric characters without trimming first, while `Graph::resolve_handle` already trims before its own check. That mismatch meant a padded handle never made it to resolution.

## What Changed

- `is_handle_shaped` now trims the input before the alphanumeric check, so it agrees with `resolve_handle` on what counts as a handle.
- Added a test that remembers an episode edge whose target handle has leading and trailing whitespace and confirms it resolves to the existing node instead of failing.
- Strengthened the out of bounds and bogus reference rejection tests to check for the specific "not a recognized reference" message and the offending reference text, instead of just checking for "failed".
- Added a boundary test that rejects the index exactly one past the last valid combined fact index, so an off by one in the bounds check would get caught.

author: agash
body:
Follow-up to #14. Everything here was found by auditing the built assembly rather than the source, which turned up surface that #14 already claimed was done.

## Grouping, finished

- 60 event stream accessors were still flat extensions on the client, so half the surface was grouped and half was not. They move onto their category group, generated from the same `category` field in `protocol.json` that the requests use. `{Category}RequestGroup` becomes `{Category}Group`.
- Both client helper files had been left as ~130 lines of banner comments with nothing under them when their methods moved into groups.
- `WaitForEventAsync` had overloads split across two static classes, and the two `CallBatchAsync` overloads returned different types, so picking the lambda one silently gave untyped results.

## The protocol's numbers

JSON has one numeric type, so every `Number` became `double` and callers read scene item ids, frame counts and byte counts as floating point. Which fields are integral is not recoverable from the definition: `sceneItemId` and `inputVolumeMul` are both `Number` with a `>= 0` restriction. The classification is an explicit table, not a rule over field names, because guessing wrong on a volume field truncates it silently while an unlisted field only stays `double`. 32 field names become `int` or `long`, 10 stay `double`, and an unlisted field reports OBSWSGEN012.

## Client options

`AddObsWebSocketClient` returns a builder, so `WithAutoConnect`, `WithHealthCheck` and `WithReconnectPipeline` chain off it. `WithAutoConnect` previously hung off `IServiceCollection` and could not target one of two named clients.

## Fixes

- `GetSourceScreenshot` returns a data URI, so the in-memory helper threw and returned null for every call. The file variant was unaffected, which is why it went unnoticed.
- Six helpers decided "not found" by substring matching the exception message. `ObsWebSocketRequestException.StatusCode` exposes the reported status as the protocol enum and they match on that.
- The `RequestStatus` enum shared a name with the `RequestStatus` record on every response, which is the pair a caller has to disambiguate to write a status filter. It is `RequestStatusCode`.
- csharpier was pinned in `dotnet-tools.json` and never run; 69 of 99 files had drifted. Some of that drift was misleading rather than cosmetic. CI checks it now.
- Three tests failed only under parallel load, each for a real reason: two drove a `FakeTimeProvider` and then waited on real `Task.Delay`, and one put a 1s wall clock limit on a test that only builds a container.

## Verification

Validated live against OBS 32.2.2 on both transports, 29 checks each with value assertions. Writing an int over MessagePack is asserted explicitly, including `0`, which also covers the falsy-field fix from #11.

Closes #14

author: johnxu22786
body:
## What this PR does

Fixes the responses -> anthropic conversion path rejecting valid Responses-API `tool_choice` requests with 400 `invalid_request_error`.

### Before this PR:
`ResponsesRequestToAnthropic` passed `tool_choice` through `openAIToolChoiceToAnthropic`, which only knew the OpenAI Chat nested shape `{"type":"function","function":{"name":"x"}}` and the string forms. Spec-conformant Responses clients (e.g. Codex CLI) send the flat shape `{"type":"function","name":"x"}`; with no `"function"` key the helper passed it through unchanged, so `{"type":"function",...}` landed in the Anthropic Messages body — not a valid `tool_choice` form — and upstream answered 400.

### After this PR:
The flat Responses shape `{"type":"function","name":"x"}` is mapped to Anthropic's `{"type":"tool","name":"x"}`. The mapping is gated on the `"function"` key being absent, so the chat-nested path and all string forms (`auto`/`none`/`required` per existing conventions) are unchanged, and every other input still passes through as before.

New table-driven test `TestResponsesRequestToAnthropicToolChoice` covers the flat form, the flat form without a name, the broken `"function"` key, the chat-nested form, the string forms, and unknown-object passthrough.

### Type of change
[bug fix]

### Breaking changes (if any)
None.

author: panghy
body:
## Summary

The blue unread indicator (agent avatar dot and the bottom-bar Agents launcher dot) previously lit up for any agent with an unseen assistant message, including background (BG) and delegated child agents — noisy in coordinator workspaces with dozens of delegated agents.

This change suppresses the per-agent unread flag at its single derivation seam, deriveAgentHasUnread in src/shared/utils/agent-unread.ts (monorepo#1597):

- Background agents (isBackground or metadata.isBackground) never derive hasUnread: true
- Delegated child agents (non-empty metadata.createdByAgentId, the same predicate the agents-list tree uses for nesting) never derive hasUnread: true

author: javiercamarapp
body:
Primer lote de cierre de la auditoría 19 (PR #52, 185 hallazgos). Dos CRÍTICOS quirúrgicos, verificados contra `origin/master` antes de tocar código.

## 1. OP-19c2-3 — el outbox de WhatsApp muere en silencio
El estado `dead` (0180, agota 8 reintentos) no tenía consumidor ni alerta — es el único de los 6 crons que no llama `alertarOperador`. Migración 0189 ensancha `finalizar_wa_outbox` de `boolean` a `table(ok, muerta)` **sin tocar la condición `intentos >= 8`** (es la misma de la 0180); `route.ts` avisa exactamente cuando una fila muere, no en cualquier fallo transitorio que ya reintenta solo.

## 2. Tool-calling CRÍTICO — el tope de $/día se disfrazaba de bug
`LlmBudgetExceededError` no es un error de red, así que `isTransientError` no lo clasificaba como transitorio y el degradado determinístico RES-15 (ya construido para cuando el proveedor cae) nunca corría. El chofer recibía el mismo "se me trabó el sistema" que un bug de programación real, con sus comprobantes YA en la base. Agotar presupuesto no es un bug — el motor cuadra solo con las cifras reales.

## Descartado tras verificar
El hallazgo de operabilidad "la comprobación de sha nunca se ejecuta" (139 corridas, 0 ejecuciones) **no se reproduce** contra el historial real de GitHub Actions — confirmado con `gh run list`, el paso corre y pasa en cada push de esta sesión. Parece análisis estático sin acceso al historial de ejecución.

## Deliberadamente NO incluidos en este lote (necesitan más que un parche mecánico)
- **REND-19c2-2**: la agregación fiscal agrupa por el nombre del emisor en texto libre de OCR, sin normalizar — fragmenta al mismo proveedor en variantes distintas. Tocar la agrupación de un reporte fiscal en vivo sin más contexto de producto es riesgoso.
- **REND-19c2-3**: el anti-join de `anomalias_gasto_tenant` usa `position()` sobre una concatenación de texto en vez de una igualdad indexable — la semántica original del anti-join no está clara sin revisar la intención de quien lo escribió; reescribirlo a ciegas puede cambiar qué duplicados se reportan.
- **PRUEBA-19c2-3**: 3 de los 19 bloques amnistiados de `verificaciones.sql` contradicen su propio valor "esperado" — corregirlo exige correr contra un Postgres real para no terminar fijando el valor incorrecto como si fuera el bueno.

## Verificación
Suite completa: 519 archivos, 6525 pruebas, 1 saltada. `tsc` limpio.

author: arden-x
body:
## Summary

Add HXinfer as an out-of-tree validation prototype for pipeline-parallel
inference across independently launched CUDA and ROCm vLLM workers.

The implementation keeps vLLM core unchanged and adds:

- one EngineCore/Controller managing two remote PP workers;
- separate CUDA rank 0 and ROCm rank 1 worker services;
- persistent TCP RPC for worker lifecycle and model execution;
- full `IntermediateTensors` transfer through CUDA D2H, TCP, and ROCm H2D;
- a single OpenAI-compatible HTTP API for clients;
- Unix-socket and TCP transport experiments, diagnostics, and benchmarks;
- an end-to-end Chinese usage guide covering containers, processes, API
  validation, shutdown, and migration to two VMs;
- unit tests and validation reports from dual RTX 4090 and RTX 4090 +
  RX 7900 XTX experiments.

## Architecture

```text
Client -> HXinfer API / EngineCore / Scheduler
       -> Remote Executor
          -> CUDA Worker (PP rank 0)
          -> ROCm Worker (PP rank 1)

activation: CUDA GPU -> PCIe D2H -> host TCP -> PCIe H2D -> AMD GPU
```

The two workers form one PP world. They do not expose separate model APIs;
clients use only the controller's HTTP endpoint.

## Duplicate-work check

No matching open PR was found on
`luoyc123/vllm:vllm_single_machine_heterogeneous`. This change is also
materially different from vLLM's homogeneous multiprocessing/Ray paths: it is
an isolated external executor and transport prototype for CUDA/ROCm workers,
and it does not alter vLLM core behavior.

## Tests

Commands run:

```bash
uv pip install --python /home/arden/HXinfer/.venv/bin/python 'pytest>=7' ruff

ruff check HXinfer/external_pp HXinfer/scripts HXinfer/tests
ruff format --check HXinfer/external_pp HXinfer/scripts HXinfer/tests
bash -n HXinfer/scripts/*.sh
git diff --check

PYTHONPATH="$PWD/HXinfer:$PWD" \
  /home/arden/HXinfer/.venv/bin/python -m pytest HXinfer/tests -q
```

Results:

- Ruff check: passed;
- Ruff format check: passed;
- shell syntax: passed;
- whitespace check: passed;
- unit tests against the target vLLM source tree: `21 passed`;
- target-source imports for executor, worker, and worker service: passed.

## Model and transport validation

- Dual RTX 4090 native PP=2 and external PP=2 generation completed.
- Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct on RTX 4090 + RX 7900 XTX completed model loading,
  KV-cache initialization, prefill, greedy decode, and clean shutdown.
- The heterogeneous eight-question short-answer suite passed 8/8.
- Six longer heterogeneous QA prompts produced 530 output tokens and exercised
  101 activation transfers.
- The single OpenAI-compatible API returned successful chat and completion
  responses while both worker RPC sequences and transport logs advanced.
- Two-process TCP loopback reached 4.685 GB/s aggregate throughput with 64 MiB
  messages on the validation server.

Detailed evidence and limitations are in
`HXinfer/docs/heterogeneous_amd_nvidia_validation_report.md`.

## Known limitations

- The current remote path is restricted to PP=2 and TP=1.
- Activation transfer uses `torch.save`/`torch.load` and host staging; it is a
  functional prototype, not a zero-copy production transport.
- The API currently supports non-streaming requests and serializes inference
  calls with a lock.
- Qwen3.5-27B block-FP8 loaded both stage weights, but the gfx1100 ROCm kernel
  backend did not complete compilation; this is documented rather than claimed
  as a passing inference result.
- Production deployment still needs authentication hardening, protocol version
  negotiation, reconnection, timeouts, and sequence-gap handling.

## AI assistance and human review

AI assistance was used to implement and format code, write documentation, run
tests, and prepare this PR. The human submitter reviewed the full diff and
confirmed the relevant test verification before submission.

﻿## Summary Two items from the v0.1.18 user feedback: ### 1. Live WPM in Direct Mode (RFC 0012, amended in governance #32) Direct Mode hides the status bar, so users who enable the typing-rate display lose it in their primary mode. Reporter: *"it would be incredibly helpful to have the words-per-minute (WPM) tracker available in Direct Mode as well."* - Compact live-WPM element in the keyboard-mode mini-bar, gated by the existing **Settings → Output → typing-rate** toggle (off by default, same as standard mode) - Current rate only — the mini-bar strip has no room for max/avg; the compact form is what RFC 0012's new direct-entry clause specifies - Visibility follows mode switches (`ApplyPaneLayout`) and live setting changes (`OnTypingRateVisibilityChanged`) - RFC 0012 amended (edit-in-place + history entry) and its stale Windows status row corrected to Implemented ### 2. DasherCore v0.2.6 → v0.2.7 (the zoom-restart drift fix) The reporter's main complaint — *"as soon as you lift your finger/pointer and start zooming again, the canvas pulls you up much higher than you want… the more times you restart, the worse the drift gets"* — reproduced on Windows **and** Android, i.e. engine-side. ## Summary

merqo documents the `admin_audit` + `recordAudit()` convergence standard every sibling kit (qkit/loopkit/paykit/stockkit) follows, but never had one of its own — every admin action (kit-access grant/revoke, team add/remove, the bundle-discount toggle, support-message resolution) was completely unlogged.

- New migration `0021_admin_audit.sql`: `merqo.admin_audit` table, admin-read RLS (`merqo.is_merqo_team()`, same predicate merqo's other admin-scoped tables use), immutable at the grant level **from day one** (`service_role` gets `select`/`insert` only — no `update`/`delete` grant at all), mirroring paykit's own `admin_audit` shape and its follow-up immutability migration, landed in one migration instead of two.

author: yerzhansa
body:
Addresses the 7 findings from the umbrella #757 review (2 P1, 4 P2, 1 P3).

1. **P1 — unsigned installer public before verification.** `upload-windows-release.mjs` now accepts only `--authenticode verify` with a real `--publisher-dn` (placeholder rejected, optional `--thumbprint`), runs local Authenticode + provenance verification before any release read or mutation, and refuses anything the verifier did not mark `verified`.
2. **P1 — Authenticode cannot run on ubuntu.** `desktop-windows-release.yml` runs on `windows-latest` (bash shell, `cygpath` for `RUNNER_TEMP`), resolves the release tag to its commit (lightweight or annotated) and passes `--commit` to the verifier.
3. **P2 — non-transactional multi-asset upload.** On upload failure the uploader re-reads the release and records `uploadedAssets` / `uploaded` (`true`, `false`, or `"unknown"` when the re-read fails); a partial upload fails with `Windows release upload is incomplete`.
4. **P2 — blockmap unrelated to installer bytes.** Chunk-checksum verification is now shared: `checkWindowsInstallerBlockmap` (exported from `verify-windows-release.mjs`) recomputes blake2b-18 per chunk plus total size; the round-trip requires installer bytes when a blockmap is present.
5. **P2 — unbound provenance.** `windows-release-plan.mjs` seals `enduragent-release-commit:<sha>` into electron-builder `win.legalTrademarks` (lands in the NSIS installer's version resource, `NsisTarget.js:398`). `verify-windows-authenticode.ps1` reads `FileVersionInfo.LegalTrademarks` / `ProductVersion` into a new `versionInfo` field (summary schema bumped to `windows-authenticode-verification/2`); `decideWindowsAuthenticode` fails with `Authenticode provenance mismatch` unless commit and version match. Verify mode now requires the release commit.
6. **P2 — operator command guaranteed to fail.** CONTRIBUTING upload and `workflow run` commands updated; pending-marker instructions removed; `apps/desktop/CONTEXT.md` terms updated.
7. **P3 — record inside envelope.** An upload record inside `--directory` (including `..name.json`) is rejected before the record file is created.

No new numeric limits. Verification: focused vitest suites (upload, release-artifacts, authenticode, round-trip, release-plan, package-contract) green; desktop `tsc --noEmit` green; `git diff --check` clean; independent read-only review confirmed all 7 findings fixed (its two residuals — the `..name.json` edge and the round-trip `.d.mts` union — are patched here). The `.ps1` change was not executed locally (no `pwsh` on this Mac); it runs on the `windows-latest` job.

author: lecylindrique
body:
## Le noyau minimisait, il ne garantissait rien

Le placement d'équipe est une **réparation pondérée** : `meme-equipe-premier-tour` et `meme-equipe-meme-moitie` portent un `tier` et un `weight`, elles minimisent les rencontres sans jamais refuser un tableau.

C'est le bon comportement pour un placement — un tirage doit toujours sortir. Mais cela ne dit **pas** si la règle a été tenue. Or « deux combattants d'une même équipe ne se rencontrent pas au premier tour » est une règle de compétition, pas une préférence esthétique : elle doit être **constatable** sur le tableau produit. Sinon personne ne saura qu'elle a été enfreinte — et surtout pas le club concerné, qui le découvrira au bord du tapis, sans recours.

## Ce module ne tire rien et ne répare rien

Il regarde un tableau **déjà tiré** et dit ce qui s'y trouve. Séparer le constat du placement permet de le vérifier après **n'importe quel** chemin — première génération, régénération d'une catégorie, ajout tardif — sans dépendre de la façon dont le tableau a été obtenu.

Il distingue **deux constats qui appellent deux gestes opposés** :

- une **rencontre interne** que le placement aurait pu éviter ;
- une **entité surchargée**, dont l'effectif rend la règle intenable *quel que soit* le placement.

Un simple compte de violations les confondrait, et ferait accuser le tirage d'une contrainte impossible.

## La mesure qui borne le problème

Relevée en production le 26/08, au niveau **équipe** (et non club — une team fédère plusieurs clubs) :

| | |
|---|---|
| groupes (compétition, équipe, catégorie) | 102 814 |
| à 3 combattants ou plus | 4 895 |
| **au-delà de 6** | **333** (0,32 %) |
| pire cas | 21 |

Six est le maximum que trois lettres — A/B/C, plafonnées par un `check` du schéma — peuvent séparer à deux par lettre. La règle est donc **tenable sur 99,7 % des groupes**, et les 333 restants sont exactement ce que `surchargees` existe pour nommer.

C'est aussi ce qui rend un refus dur inapplicable tel quel : il ferait échouer la génération sur des cas réels. Le noyau constate et nomme ; c'est à l'appelant de décider quoi en faire.

## Détails qui comptent

- **L'entité de rattachement est la sous-équipe, ou le club à défaut** : un club sans équipe se voit appliquer la même règle, comme partout ailleurs dans le produit.
- **Les byes et les emplacements vides sont ignorés** : aux tours suivants, les slots sont vides au tirage, et y chercher une rencontre reviendrait à prédire des résultats.
- **Deux inscriptions sans club ne forment pas une « équipe des sans-club »**.
- **L'ordre de `surchargees` est stable** : un rapport de génération ne doit pas changer d'une exécution à l'autre sans qu'aucune donnée n'ait bougé. Un test le vérifie en inversant l'entrée.

## Vérification

**630 tests verts** (8 nouveaux), typecheck, lint et format verts. Version portée à **0.7.0**.

> La plateforme épingle le noyau par tag. Elle ne pourra passer à `v0.7.0` qu'une fois cette PR fusionnée et le tag posé — je ne l'ai pas fait sans votre accord.

author: jhcole-assistant
body:
## Summary

Adds a language runtime abstraction so `generic-grader` can test GNU Octave / MATLAB `.m` files with the same test types (starting with `output_lines_match_reference`) that already work for Python. Follow-on PRs will add function-return, file, and plot tests for Octave.

This is the first PR in the Octave/MATLAB series and builds on the Layer-1 security foundation merged in #183 — the same in-process security patches now stay behind the Python runtime, while a subprocess-level sandbox handles Octave. The sandbox itself is deliberately language-independent (POSIX `RLIMIT_*` via `preexec_fn`, scrubbed env, process-group kill on wall-clock timeout).

## User story

> Currently, `generic-grader` can only test Python code, but we would like to use the same system to test Octave/MATLAB scripts.

## What changed

### `Options.language`

New optional field, defaults to `"python"`. Validated against the runtime registry so a misspelled backend fails at `Options()` construction with a message that lists the supported languages.

### `src/generic_grader/runtimes/` (new package)

- `base.py` — `Runtime` `Protocol` + frozen `RuntimeResult` dataclass. Runtime-checkable so plugins can duck-type.
- `python.py` — `PythonRuntime` packages the pre-existing `Importer.import_obj` + `custom_stack` flow behind the new `Protocol`. No behavior change for existing Python tests.
- `octave.py` — `OctaveRuntime` shells out to `octave --no-gui --norc --no-init-file --quiet --eval <expr>` with:
  - Argument serialization for `bool`, `int`, `float`, `str` (with `NaN`/`±Inf` special-cased, `'` doubled in single-quoted strings). Cell arrays / structs / numpy arrays are explicitly out of scope for this PR.
  - Script vs. function dispatch driven by presence of `args`/`kwargs`. Script mode runs each side's own file stem so `main.m` vs. `ref_main.m` both work with a single shared `obj_name`.
  - `try / catch` wrapper around the eval body so uncaught Octave errors surface as a nonzero exit with `err.message` on stderr.
  - POSIX sandbox via `preexec_fn`: `RLIMIT_AS = memory_limit_GB`, `RLIMIT_CPU = time_limit + 1`, `RLIMIT_FSIZE = 64 MiB`, `RLIMIT_NOFILE = 256`.
  - Scrubbed env — only `PATH`, `HOME`, `LANG`, `LC_ALL`, `TMPDIR` are forwarded; `OCTAVE_HISTFILE=/dev/null` is pinned.
  - Wall-clock timeout via `subprocess.communicate(timeout=...)`; whole process group SIGKILL'd on timeout.
  - `OCTAVE_EXECUTABLE` env var lets the grader host override the binary path.

### `__User__` dispatch

`__User__.__init__` now resolves via the runtime, and `call_obj` runs through the runtime and translates `OctaveTimeoutError` / `OctaveRuntimeError` / `OctaveNotInstalledError` into the standard student-facing "Your `<obj_name>` malfunctioned … Hint:" message (with the child's stderr in the hint for runtime errors). `OctaveNotInstalledError` is treated as a grader-configuration failure and drops the student-blaming preamble.

### README

New "Grading Octave / MATLAB code" section with prerequisites, a script-mode example, script-vs-function dispatch semantics, argument-serialization limits, and sandbox description.

## Test coverage

**100% coverage on every modified source file.** Local run:

```
src/generic_grader/runtimes/__init__.py          8      0   100%
src/generic_grader/runtimes/base.py             15      0   100%
src/generic_grader/runtimes/octave.py          114      0   100%
src/generic_grader/runtimes/python.py           19      0   100%
src/generic_grader/utils/options.py             99      0   100%
src/generic_grader/utils/user.py               148      0   100%
```

New test files:

- `tests/runtimes/test_base.py` — registry, `RuntimeResult` contract, `runtime_checkable` Protocol conformance.
- `tests/runtimes/test_python.py` — pins the legacy behavior the `PythonRuntime` adapter must preserve: `Importer` delegation, `custom_stack` application, deepcopy semantics, exception propagation.
- `tests/runtimes/test_octave.py` — pure-Python unit tests for scalar & args serialization, eval-expression construction, stdin/env building, preexec construction, and subprocess-mocked coverage of every branch in `OctaveRuntime.run` (success, nonzero exit, wall-clock timeout with double-`communicate` drain, missing executable, exec-race `FileNotFoundError`, stdin piping). Plus three **live-Octave** integration tests (skipped when `octave` isn't on `PATH`).
- `tests/output/test_output_lines_match_reference_octave.py` — seam tests exercising `OctaveRuntime + __User__ + reference_test` as one unit: matching outputs, mismatched outputs, function mode with an argument, missing student file.
- `tests/utils/test_user_runtime_dispatch.py` — the new Octave exception branches in `__User__.call_obj`.
- `tests/utils/test_options.py` — extended with `language` validator negative & positive cases.

Suite summary (excluding the two pre-existing environmental flakes, `tests/utils/test_turtle_canvas.py` — no X display — and `tests/file/test_file_closed.py::test_failing_cases[case1]` — set-ordering nondeterminism):

```
808 passed in 13.48s
```

Baseline was 736 before this PR.

## Manual verification

Two smoke tests confirm the end-to-end flow works with a live Octave install:

1. `disp('hello world')` in both `main.m` and `ref_main.m` → test passes.
2. `disp('goodbye world')` vs. `disp('hello world')` → test fails with the standard "Your output did not match" hint and the actual stdout tee'd into the log.

## Follow-ups (out of scope for this PR)

- Function-return tests for Octave (needs an Octave → Python decode layer for numeric and cell arrays).
- File tests (`file_content_matches_reference`, etc.) — mostly plumbing since the runtime already runs in a CWD.
- Plot tests (`Runtime.artifacts` is already reserved for this).
- Extended argument-type support (arrays, cells, structs).

## Antecedent

Builds on #183 (Layer-1 security, merged). The Octave subprocess sandbox is the language-independent counterpart to the in-process patches from #183.

author: abdeslam-menacere
body:
Closes #255.

#198 added a guard that refuses a module which climbs out of its package from `__file__`, and shipped it with a docstring listing four known evasions. Two of those four — `globals()['__file__']` and `sys.modules[...].__file__` — were still listed as unresolved even though nothing prevented them from being covered, and the depth calculation used a fixed `>= 2` that was only correct for top-level modules. This branch closes both.

## Scope: the production tree is byte-identical

`git diff --stat 41f5cee...495fb1d` — **1 file, +118/−29**, `tools/updater/tests/test_installed_layout.py`.

QA proved "no production change" by **hashes rather than by reading the diff**: the `tools/updater/src` tree object is identical at both ends (`50e5a2db728465d1b44418ad5dfdb12425cdc223`), and a whole-repo `git ls-tree -r` comparison minus the test file is byte-identical merge-base to tip. The only changed blob anywhere in the repository is `test_installed_layout.py` (`ef2f772` → `e003f35`).

## The depth fix is proven in both directions

The guard's climb check moved from a fixed `>= 2` to `>= depth + 2`, with `depth` threaded through as a keyword-only argument and passed for real by the live scan. Correctness was established by execution at depths 0, 1 and 2 — a two-level climb flags only at depth 0, three-level at depths 0 and 1, four-level everywhere — and then by mutating the boundary **both ways**:

- **Weakened to `>= depth + 3`**: a real escape slips through, and two named tests go red — `test_a_two_level_climb_is_read_against_the_module_s_own_depth` and `test_a_deeper_module_that_still_clears_the_package_is_flagged`.
- **Reverted to a fixed `>= 2`**: a legitimate deep climb is wrongly flagged, and the depth-1 assertion in `test_a_two_level_climb_is_read_against_the_module_s_own_depth` fails.

Both failures are offender-naming `AssertionError`s, not collection-time `ImportError`s. Mutating the boundary silenced no evasion case, so the two concerns are independently pinned.

**Stated plainly, because it matters:** there are five live modules at depth 1 (`providers/base`, `fixtures`, `foundry`, `network`, `__init__`), so the depth path genuinely executes on Linux CI — but none of them climbs, so the real and the fixed boundary both report **0** live offenders. The depth *discrimination* is exercised only by the two synthetic fixtures. That is a real limitation and it is written down rather than glossed.

## The two evasions are covered, and the coverage is behaviourally pinned

`isinstance(args[0], Name) and .id == "__file__"` became a `_is_file_expr(...)` helper that also matches the subscript forms, while still matching bare `__file__`. Breaking `_is_file_expr` makes both named evasions go quiet, which turns their parametrized cases red — so the coverage is pinned by behaviour, not by a docstring edit.

The evasion table was extended with **invented** forms, not just the named ones. Also caught: `Path(os.__file__)` and `Path(m.__file__)`, via the broader rule. Still slipping, and reported rather than hidden: `getattr(m, '__file__')`, `Path(f'{__file__}')`, and — the one worth your eye — **`globals().get('__file__')`**, a near-twin of the subscript form the docstring now declares resolved. Seven legitimate constructs stay quiet and there are zero live offenders, so there is no false-positive regression.

## The 29 deletions, each with a successor

Every deleted line has an equal-or-stronger replacement, and **no load-bearing limitation was deleted while it still applies**. All four documented limits and the "this is not a proof of the negative" disclaimer are preserved verbatim; two now-covered forms were moved out of that list because they are genuinely covered. The remaining deletions are the signature change (adds `*, depth=0`), the `>= 2` → `>= depth + 2` fix, the call site that makes the fix live, a rename (`test_widening…` → `test_demonstration_widening…`), and docstring rewrites whose bodies are unchanged.

That rename is the honest part of the change: the renamed test now declares in its own docstring that it is **not** a guard and names the real guard instead. The pre-existing admission that it does not modify `runner.py` is preserved and sharpened rather than dropped.

## The real guard behind the rename is not vacuous

`test_a_resume_under_an_installed_layout_refuses_a_recorded_long_tail_id` drives the real `runner.resume_creator_run`. The production catch at `runner.py:290` is the narrow `except ProfileError`; `longtail.py:504` raises `FileNotFoundError("installed distribution…")`; widening that catch reshapes the outcome to `ProfileMismatch` and turns the test red.

QA could not re-execute that one locally — `runner` imports `agent_framework`, which is not installable here — and said so rather than claiming otherwise. Every pure-AST probe did run, because `_climbs_from_file_root` has no such dependency. Green CI and #198's recorded execution corroborate.

## Counts

CI run `32939010057`, headSha `495fb1d` confirmed equal to the tip, conclusion success: **715 passed / 3 deselected** on Python 3.11 and 3.13.

Branch delta against its own merge-base `41f5cee` is **+4** — two new `def test_` functions (30 → 32) and two new `GUARD_EVASIONS` cases (8 → 10), none removed.

`main` moved twice while this branch sat in the gates — 770, then **771** with #268. The file is byte-identical between the merge-base and current `main`, so the post-merge prediction is **775 passed / 3 deselected**. `3 deselected` (2 `live` + 1 `network`) is exactly 3 at the merge-base, on the branch, and in the prediction; no marker was added.

CI also settles the platform risk recorded in #246 by execution: this ran on Linux, which exercises the two symlink tests that skip on Windows with `WinError 1314`.

## Gate record

Review and QA both PASS, bound to `495fb1daa26c177248983f8af89cf6b6d2930073`, re-confirmed unmoved at start and at verdict, each working from the issue body and the diff alone. `git merge-tree --write-tree` exits 0 against `main`. Verdicts recorded as comments on #255 because the `drydock` CLI is not installed here.

**Merge order with #165:** no conflict in either direction. #165 edits the docstring at lines 216–230; this branch's earliest touched line is 309.

## Follow-ups, proposed and not fixed here

1. `globals().get('__file__')` slips while `globals()['__file__']` is now caught. Since the docstring names the subscript form as resolved, the `.get` twin should either be covered or explicitly listed.
2. `getattr(<mod>, '__file__')` and the f-string form `Path(f'{__file__}')` slip — undocumented, low urgency against the stated threat model.
3. The broadened `_is_file_expr` will flag any `Path(<other>.__file__)` deep climb. Zero live today; a latent false-positive vector worth awareness.

None are gate-blocking: the acceptance criteria named exactly two slips, both are covered, and the known-limits docstring explicitly disclaims completeness.

author: dasabhinaba34
body:
## Summary
- Follow-up to #189. The very first real run of the fixed `get-active` polling loop (in production, right after #189 merged) actually worked — it correctly saw `requested` then `deleting unreferenced blobs` — but died on its third check because `doctl` itself returned non-zero once, and `set -euo pipefail` treats that as fatal inside a pipe. The job's `continue-on-error: true` hid it, and the deploy happened to still succeed since the GC had already progressed far enough, but the wait had stopped waiting again, just from a different cause.
- `|| echo '[{"status":"unknown"}]'` keeps the pipeline itself at exit 0. A failed poll now reads as `unknown` and falls into the same "keep waiting" branch as any real in-progress status, rather than crashing the script or being misread as `none` (finished).
- Verified the exact failure and the fix's behavior locally (bash, not the workflow's actual runner) by simulating both a failing and succeeding `doctl` call through the same pipeline shape.

## Test plan
- [x] YAML validated (`js-yaml` parse)
- [x] Bash syntax validated (`bash -n` on the extracted script)
- [x] Simulated a failing `doctl` call through the exact pipeline — resolves to `unknown`, script continues (confirmed `pipefail` no longer kills it)
- [x] Simulated a real in-progress status — parses correctly, unaffected by the change
- [ ] Will watch the deploy this merge triggers as the real end-to-end confirmation

## What

One comment fix in `mobile/public/index.html`.

## Why

[#90](https://github.com/wyne/yarukoto/pull/90) regenerated the derived icon assets and deleted `mobile/assets/brand-mark.svg`, but `index.html` still introduced the PWA icons as "all cut from assets/brand-mark.svg" — a path that no longer exists. Anyone following that reference hits a dead end.

The replacement keeps the provenance (they *were* cut from that mark) and adds the part that actually matters now: those four files in `mobile/public/` — `apple-touch-icon.png`, `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`, `icon-maskable-512.png` — still show the old black-square-and-blue-check mark. They are the one icon family #90 did not regenerate, so they are now inconsistent with the crane used everywhere else.

- Comment text only. No markup, hrefs, or behaviour touched.
- The rewrap makes the diff three lines instead of one; the prose change is confined to the first sentence.

body:
## Summary
Adds a pure Cynefin sense-making domain classification (`DISORDER`/`CONVERGED`/`COMPLEX`/`CHAOTIC`), read from graph evidence `compute_cycle_signals` already fetches (`fetch_entity_neighborhood`), and uses it to give `COMPLEX`-classified investigation anchors (live rules genuinely disagree — an enabling constraint, per Cynefin's technical definition) more `DEEPENING` cycles before escalating out, while `CONVERGED`/`CHAOTIC`/`DISORDER` anchors keep today's exact flat-constant behavior unchanged. Extracted from `backlog/A216.md` Part 1's design discussion as an execution-ready v1 slice — full research context in that card.

Deliberately narrow scope: `plan_generator.py` and the whole-episode `annatar_unproductive_anchor_streak` mechanism are explicitly untouched, so any behavior change can be attributed to this one mechanism.

## What the live-smoke test found
Independently ran a fresh live smoke test against the real ARC API + hippocampy daemon (the implementing agent's sandboxed worktree couldn't reach either). Result: **same pre-fix pattern** — 12 distinct coordinates tried, each exactly once, zero deepening.

Traced precisely why rather than stopping at "no observable effect": `classify_domain()` correctly reads `fetch_entity_neighborhood`'s `hypotheses + rules`, but that call returns genuinely empty for this run's entities — confirmed directly against the live graph. An entity with 11 prior attempts and 11 contradictions (per the *separate* reward-counter evidence layer) had zero rule-level evidence at all. Root cause: `record_rule_evidence`'s changed_cells-empty early return (A213's own, deliberately-kept behavior) means an entity that reliably produces no visible effect never gets any rule-level graph trace, however many times it's tried — so `classify_domain()` reads `DISORDER` for it forever, never `COMPLEX`.

This sharpens A213's original conclusion rather than contradicting it: A213 correctly found a no-op rule-signal would have been inert with no consumer at the time. A217 is now a real consumer. A follow-up card is recommended (not yet opened) to revisit that specifically in light of this new dependency.

**The implementation itself is correct and will activate** the moment any entity accumulates genuine rule-level disagreement (an inconsistent, not absent, effect) — this run's puzzle just didn't happen to produce that condition.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/test_a217_domain_aware_anchor_patience.py` — 17 tests, independently re-run: `classify_domain()` coverage for all four domains plus the `to_color`/`claim` field-shape distinction (confirmed correct against real `fetch_entity_neighborhood` fixtures), `transition()` domain-aware-patience behavior (including a regression guard that `CONVERGED`/`CHAOTIC`/`DISORDER` are byte-for-byte unchanged), `compute_cycle_signals` wiring including exception-degradation to `DISORDER`.
- [x] `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q` — independently re-run against a verified `.venv`: 911 passed, 4 skipped (894 baseline + 17 new, zero regressions).
- [x] `git diff --stat` independently re-confirms `agents/arc4/plan_generator.py` has zero diff, and the unproductive-anchor-streak mechanism is unchanged.
- [x] Live smoke test run against the real ARC API + hippocampy daemon (see "What the live-smoke test found" above) — the actual point of this card, not just unit tests.

## Problem
The public v1.3.7 installer can fall back to the startup safety page for an upgraded legacy profile and incorrectly report LEASE_UNAVAILABLE.

## Root cause
The coin-outcome schema migration rebuilt a table while triggers on two other tables still referenced it. SQLite validated those trigger bodies during the rename and raised an OperationalError. Generic startup exception handling then lost the exact failure and the diagnostics page inferred a lease error.

## Fix
- preserve and recreate both dependent triggers atomically during the schema migration
- surface STARTUP_INITIALIZATION_FAILED for unexpected startup initialization failures without leaking exception details
- add regression coverage for the exact legacy schema and misleading lease fallback

Faz 7 yeniden yapılanmasının ikinci fazı. **Kullanıcıya görünen hiçbir davranış değişmiyor** — amaç yeni sınıflandırma hattının ineceği yeri açmak. Net −784 satır.

## Kapatılan açık

Üç uç nokta kimlik doğrulaması olmadan açıktaydı:

| Uç nokta | Ne veriyordu |
|---|---|
| `GET /admin/status` | Kaynak sayıları, makale durum dağılımı, abone sayısı, e-posta teslim hataları, yapılandırılmış LLM sağlayıcısı — dağıtımın haritası |
| `GET /subscribers` | Abone e-posta adresleri. Docstring'i zaten "admin-only" olduğunu iddia ediyordu; o iddia kimsenin kontrol etmemesinin sebebiydi |
| `POST /editions/{date}/rebuild` | Yayımlanmış bir günü herkesin yeniden derletebildiği, LLM bütçesini harcayan yazma uç noktası |

Üçü de `ADMIN_TOKEN` taşıyıcı belirtecinin arkasında (`app/api/deps.py`). **Belirteç ayarlanmamışsa 503 döndürür, açılmaz** — bir değişken unutulduğunda kendini sessizce açan bir operatör uç noktası, bunların en baştan herkese açık olmasının sebebi. Karşılaştırma `secrets.compare_digest` ile.

Abone kaydı (`POST /subscribers`) açık kaldı: abone yaratmanın tek yolu o, CLI komutu yok.

> Planda bu ikisi için "sil" yazıyordu. Silmek yerine korumaya aldım — asıl sorun işlevleri değil korumasız olmalarıydı, ve ikisinin de operatör için gerçek karşılığı var.

## Sessiz hata: `ensure_seeded()` sadece ekliyordu

Bir kaynağın adı veritabanında varsa satır atlanıyordu. Sonuçları:

- Düzeltilmiş bir URL veya yeniden katmanlanmış bir güven ağırlığı canlıya **hiç ulaşmıyordu** — düzenleme diff'te uygulanmış görünüp production'da hiçbir şey yapmıyordu.
- Tohum listesinden **silinen** bir kaynak sonsuza dek aktif kalıyordu.

İkincisi Faz 5'i doğrudan bloke ediyordu: "Reddit'i kaldır" dediğimde dosyadan silinecek ama beslemeden gelmeye devam edecekti. Artık uzlaştırıyor — listede olan yazılır, listede olmayan devre dışı bırakılır (silinmez; makaleler kaynağa referans veriyor). Üç yeni test bunu doğruluyor.

## Taksonomi: dört kopya → tek kaynak

Türkçe kategori etiketleri dört yerde elle yazılıydı (öneriler servisi, e-posta şablonu, gazete sayfası, ön yüz taksonomisi), bölge etiketleri iki, risk etiketleri iki yerde. Hepsi `app/taxonomy.py`'de.

Ön yüz bunları `scripts/export_taxonomy.py`'nin ürettiği `taxonomy.gen.ts` üzerinden alıyor. Slug'lar TypeScript birleşim tipi olduğu için **bir tarafta olup diğerinde olmayan slug artık derleme hatası**, üretimde boş kalan bir filtre değil. CI tazeliği kontrol ediyor. Renk ve ikonlar ön yüzde kaldı — arka uçta karşılıkları yok.

## APScheduler kaldırıldı

GitHub Actions ile aynı dört işi aynı aralıklarla tanımlıyordu. Vercel'de ölüydü (fonksiyon istekler arasında donduruluyor) ve başka her yerde çift tetikliyordu, çünkü iş akışları aynı veritabanına karşı koşuyor.

## Silinen ölü kod

Hiçbir yerden içe aktarılmayan önbellek modülü (requirements'ta bulunmayan `redis`'i çağırıyordu — içe aktarılsa `ImportError` verirdi), kullanıcı şeması, Elasticsearch taslağı, boş depolama dizini, var olmayan `/auth/login` ve `/auth/me` uç noktalarına giden ön yüz kimlik doğrulama dosyası, 6 kullanılmayan bileşen.

Öksüz `/pivot` API'si (709 satır servis + uç nokta + test; ön yüzü daha önce silinmişti) ve kök `/taxonomy` uç noktası — amacı ön yüzün sapmadığını doğrulamaktı, kod üretimi bunu artık CI zorunluluğuyla yapıyor.

Bağımlılıklar: `python-jose`, `passlib`, `bcrypt`, `python-multipart`, `apscheduler`. `docker-compose` artık kullanılmayan Redis ve Elasticsearch konteynerlerini ayağa kaldırmıyor (Elasticsearch tek başına ~1 GB).

Ayrıca `EditionPdf` models paketinden dışa aktarılıyor — `from app.models import EditionPdf` çalışmıyordu.

## Doğrulama

- `pytest`: **373 geçiyor**
- `ruff check app scripts`: temiz
- `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, `next build`: temiz
- Uygulama açılıyor, 31 rota

Yeni testler operatör korumasını (belirteçsiz / yanlış belirteçli / doğru belirteçli / yapılandırılmamış), kaynak uzlaştırmasını ve etiket kapsamasını doğruluyor.

## Yayına alma notu

`ADMIN_TOKEN` Vercel ortam değişkenlerine eklenmeli. Eklenmezse operatör uç noktaları 503 döndürür — kullanıcıya görünen sayfaların hiçbiri etkilenmez.

author: beeman
body:
## Problem

A freshly scaffolded `expo-kit-anchor` fails to build for Android:

```
expo-modules-core/android/src/main/cpp/worklets/WorkletJSCallInvoker.cpp:27:21:
error: no member named 'executeSync' in 'worklets::WorkletRuntime'
```

`expo-router` declares `react-native-reanimated: "*"`, so a fresh install takes the newest release. 4.6.0 moved its `react-native-worklets` peer to `0.12.x`, and worklets 0.12 removed `WorkletRuntime::executeSync` — which `expo-modules-core@57.0.13` still calls. The two requirements cannot both be satisfied:

| Package | Requires `react-native-worklets` |
| --- | --- |
| `react-native-reanimated@4.6.0` (via `expo-router`) | `0.12.x` |
| `expo-modules-core@57.0.13` (via `expo`) | `^0.7.4 \|\| ^0.8.0 \|\| ^0.9.0 \|\| ^0.10.0` |

Two things make this worse than a normal version bump:

- **There is nothing to upgrade into.** `expo-modules-core@57.0.13` is the latest release and `expo@57.0.16`, also the latest, depends on it.
- **`expo install --check` does not catch it.** On an affected project it reports only a React patch difference. This is a transitive peer conflict, outside the compatibility table it checks.

Nothing actually requires 4.6.0 — `expo-router` and `@expo/ui` declare `*`, `react-native-drawer-layout` declares `>= 2.0.0`. The resolver just took the newest published version.

## Fix

Pin reanimated to **4.5.4** and worklets to **0.10.4** — the one pair satisfying both sides:

| | worklets requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `expo-modules-core@57.0.13` | `^0.7.4 \|\| ^0.8.0 \|\| ^0.9.0 \|\| **^0.10.0**` |
| `react-native-reanimated@4.5.4` | `**0.10.x** - 0.11.x` |

`reanimated@4.5.4` supports react-native `0.83 - 0.86`, covering the `0.86.2` this template installs.

### Why the pin is declared three times

No single field covers every package manager the template supports. Verified by forcing a transitive dependency (`express@4.18.2` → `debug@2.6.9` → `4.3.4`) with each:

| Package manager | `overrides` | `resolutions` | `pnpm.overrides` | `pnpm-workspace.yaml` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| npm 11.16 | ✅ | — | — | — |
| bun 1.3.5 | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| yarn 1.22 | ❌ | ✅ | — | — |
| pnpm 11.24 | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ ignored | ✅ |

pnpm 10 and later no longer read the `pnpm` field from `package.json`:

```
[WARN] The "pnpm" field in package.json is no longer read by pnpm.
The following keys were ignored: "pnpm.overrides".
```

It warns rather than fails, so an override left there looks applied and silently is not.

### CI

The anchor job overwrote a template's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` when injecting `strictDepBuilds`:

```bash
printf 'strictDepBuilds: false\n' > "$DIR/pnpm-workspace.yaml"
```

That would have discarded these overrides and tested a dependency tree no user receives. It appends now; the result parses with both keys intact.

## Verification

Installing this template with the pin applied:

| Package manager | `react-native-worklets` | `react-native-reanimated` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| npm | 0.10.4 | 4.5.4 |
| pnpm | 0.10.4 | 4.5.4 |

And the Android build, which failed before the pin, on a scaffolded project:

```
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m 11s
app-debug.apk   100660289 bytes
```

Swapping the dependency in an already-built tree also leaves stale CMake state — consumers of the worklets prefab bake the old config hash into their ninja graphs and fail with `libworklets.so ... missing and no known rule to make it`. Clearing `node_modules/*/android/{build,.cxx}` resolves it. A fresh scaffold is unaffected.

## Not covered

`npm run ci` ends at `expo prebuild -p android`, which generates the Android project without compiling it, so no C++ is built in CI. That is why this reached users. These jobs will confirm the overrides resolve, but nothing here proves the native build works — closing that gap needs a real `assembleDebug` step and is a larger change than this PR.

body: Wave 3 of the S.Ai beat workflow. Version **0.32.0** (`versionCode` 31). ## What landed - **To Rack** — Sampler **To Rack** saves slices into the library and assigns them to Channel Rack rows (empty rows first, then new rows up to 8). - **Pattern length** — per-pattern **8 / 16 / 32** steps. Clicks are not written into Export WAV. - **Loop** — **SONG** / **PAT** / **RNG**. Long-press a tracker row number to set a loop range. - **Duplicate pattern** — Channel Rack **...** copies the current pattern’s phrases into the next empty song row. - **Rack solo** — yellow LED next to mute. If any row is soloed, only soloed (unmuted) rows play, including in mixdown. ## Verify `gradle :core:test :app:compileDebugKotlin --no-daemon` passed locally. ## After merge Tag `v0.32.0` so Release CI attaches `S.Ai-v0.32.0.apk`.

author: jarmandoanaya
body:
## What changed

The annotation job becomes the unit a person enters and the unit a model pre-labels, and the batch gallery shows a batch's frames one job at a time.

**Pre-label is a job operation.** `POST /jobs/{job_id}/pre-label` queues one `annotation.pre_label` row for one job (202 with a `Location` header, the contract the batch route had), keyed by `annotation_job_id` beside `batch_id` in the row's payload. `POST /batches/{id}/pre-label` and `POST /projects/{id}/batches/pre-label` stay, as fan-outs over each batch's open jobs, answering `PreLabelFanOutOut` — one row per job with `annotation_job_id`, the queued or joined background job, and `joined`. A finished job is passed over by a fan-out and refused by the job route (409 `JOB_FINISHED`). `JobOut.pre_label_run` remembers a job's newest run; `BatchOut.pre_label_run` is the newest across its jobs. The kernel declares `JobAction.PRE_LABEL` on an open job of an `in_annotation` batch (`JOB_GATES`, on `BatchAction.PRE_LABEL`'s precedent); the CLI gains `visionset job pre-label` and the MCP server `pre_label_job`, and the batch and project verbs of both report one outcome per job. The plan stays batch-addressed — `GET /batches/{id}/pre-label` — because it is a property of the batch's pin and the model. A queue row enqueued before `annotation_job_id` existed is skipped by readers and fails its worker with a sentence saying why.

**The gallery enters by job.** The header carries `Start annotating` only for an `approved` batch — the `approved → in_annotation` transition, without an icon. Once a batch is open, the gallery is an accordion of its jobs (`JobPanels.tsx`): at most one panel is open, every panel may be closed, and the panel open on arrival is the first job with work left. A collapsed header states `Job N · F frames · state · A of F annotated · assignee` with a progress bar; the open panel carries the door (`Annotate` takes a `pending` job to `in_progress` and opens it; `Continue` and `View` only open), `Pre-label` gated on the job's `allowed_actions`, the assignee, segment chips counted from `GET /jobs/{id}/progress`, the order select, that job's timeline and only that job's frames, read through the new `job` filter on `GET /batches/{id}/assets` (`BatchService.asset_page(job=)`, also on the MCP `list_batch_assets`). The thumbnail-size control is one shared setting on the header's caption line. A draft batch keeps the flat grid and its membership tools. The project's `Annotate` control opens a batch's one job directly and the gallery otherwise; the dropdown stays batch-level. The virtualised grid, selection and bulk bar moved unchanged into `FrameGrid.tsx`; `JobsStrip`/`JobRow` are gone.

**Docs and rules.** `docs/content/` (`batches`, `jobs`, `api`, `background-jobs`, `cli`, `mcp`, `ui`, `inference`, `architecture/backend/jobs`) describe the job as the unit; `mcp-tools.md`, `openapi.json`, the generated client and the wire fixtures are regenerated. The `batch-lifecycle` skill's decision 10 now names a job-level pre-label action; the `information-architecture` skill records that Annotate enters by job and that a batch with jobs shows one job's frames at a time.

## Found, not fixed

- `JobPanels.tsx` and `GalleryScreen.tsx` import each other (`Toolbar`, `Timeline`, `StartJobButton` still live in the screen module). Inert today — only hoisted function declarations cross the edge — and the fix is to move those three into their own module.
- A collapsed panel's header names an `aria-controls` id that is not mounted; the panel is unmounted rather than hidden so its filter and selection reset on switch.
- `BatchOut.of` keeps a `pre_label_run=None` default; `JobOut.of` no longer has one.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest tests/kernel tests/inference tests/jobs tests/server tests/cli tests/mcp tests/architecture` — green (the documented-refusals gate included)
- [x] `uv run mypy src/visionset` (175 files), `uv run lint-imports` (4/4), `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .`
- [x] `scripts/export_openapi.py`, `pnpm generate:client:check`, `scripts/export_wire_fixtures.py`, `scripts/export_mcp_tools.py --check` — no drift
- [x] `pnpm -r build && pnpm -r test && pnpm -r lint` — annotator 1071, ui-core 1331, app 11
- [x] Playwright `gallery`, `project-nav`, `annotate`, `navigation`, `viewport`, `visual`; `pnpm cycle` (real server: approve → open the job from its panel → annotate → back reads `in progress`/`Continue`)
- [ ] CI: the full matrix, including the browser cycle job

body:
<!-- author: dhajdu dave@edge8.co -->

## What this does

Three changes to the client portal AI Programs experience, plus two cross-cutting fixes.

### 1. Leverage normalization (central)
`lib/hub/tokens.ts` now defines `CLAUDE_TOKENS_PER_VALUE_TOKEN = 100_000`. Leverage is computed as `valueTokens / deliveredHours` where `valueTokens = aiTokens / 100_000`, and rendered by a shared `formatLeverage()` as a multiple like `27.3×` (or `n/a`, never an em dash). `lib/hub/program.ts` imports the same helper. Every render site swapped to it: the admin/team hub band "AI leverage" MetricCard, the admin + team program KPIs, the portal Tokens page, and the new portal overview.

**Australian Payroll Association (company `1750a8ca-93ea-4369-aca1-c55553a49073`), ~236,147,691 AI tokens over 86.47 delivered hours:**
- **Before:** `2,730,978.3` (raw tokens per hour)
- **After:** `27.3×`

### 2. Fat font on the delivered-hours bar chart
The inline (non-stacked) `BarChart` had `viewBox` width 320 but no `maxWidth`, so a wide container upscaled the SVG ~2.8x and its 12px text rendered ~34px. Capped the inline variant at `maxWidth: 360` (its native `CHART_W` plus a little); the stacked variant keeps its 840 cap. Admin consumers render in narrow columns, so the cap only prevents blow-up.

### 3. /portal/hub becomes a simple "AI Programs" hub
- Page title and sidebar nav label renamed to **AI Programs**; the old "Client Hub" + "AI Programs" nav items collapse to one item pointing at `/portal/hub`.
- New layout: a four-MetricCard overview row (Human Tokens balance with bought as sub, AI Tokens compact total, total merged Pull Requests, normalized Leverage), an **Add AI Program** button to `/portal/programs/add`, and the AI Program cards linking to `/portal/programs/[id]`.
- Company-grain figures come from a new client-safe aggregate `getPortalHubOverview()` in `lib/portal/program-hub.ts` (counts/totals only, scoped by `actor.companyScope`; no repo org/name or author logins).
- **`/portal/programs` now redirects to `/portal/hub`** so there is one list. `/portal/programs/[id]` and `/portal/programs/add` are unchanged.

### 4. Program detail tabs
Tabs are now exactly **Overview / Roadmap / Work Board / Documents / Meetings** (the old "Progress" became "Overview"; the separate "Plan" tab folded into Overview).
- **Overview:** a KPI row (Human Tokens = delivered hours, AI Tokens, Pull Requests merged count, Leverage ×), then the weekly delivered-hours chart (the fixed BarChart), shipped highlights, and the plan brief (BriefViewer) if present. Zero state (no repo) shows "Delivery tracking starts when a repo is connected" and no leverage.
- **Roadmap / Work Board / Documents / Meetings:** unchanged behavior. Work Board renders the program's tagged boards via `ClientBoardView` (APA's "Australian Payroll" board is tagged to the Payroll IQ program and renders there).
- The client-safe `PortalProgramDelivery` projection gained `aiTokens`, `leverage`, and `prsMergedTotal` so the Overview KPIs work without leaking unsafe fields.

## Client-safe boundary
Portal surfaces still render no repo org/name, author logins, PR numbers/URLs, or sync details. New aggregates expose scalars only.

## Checks
- `npm run check:design` — exit 0 (pre-existing warnings only)
- `npm run check:crons` — 18 cron paths OK
- `npm run build` — compiled successfully, types valid

## Notes / decisions
- The "Add AI Program" button is gated to contributors+ (`contributorCompanyScope`), matching the prior AI Programs list page.
- Leverage MetricCard sub text changed from "AI tokens per delivered hour" to "AI value delivered per human hour" so it matches the new normalized meaning.
- The meetings detail back-link still reads "← Client Hub"; left untouched as out of scope for this rename.

body: ## What Layer-2 of `081M0WTB5MN`. Fixes the *real* reason phase-2 restore is silent: the unit fails **before `ExecStart`**. - `full-ai-cluster/nixos/modules/zeta-creds-restore.nix`: `WorkingDirectory = cfg.repoRoot` → `WorkingDirectory = "/"`. The `ExecStart` uses only absolute paths, so cwd is irrelevant; `/` never fails the chdir. Plus an unconditional first line `zeta-creds-restore: ExecStart entered`. - `src/Core.TypeScript/ci/qemu-full-install-test.ts`: add the `execStartEntered` marker. - `qemu-full-install-test.test.ts`: drift guards (`WorkingDirectory = "/"`, entered marker). - Workitem `081M0WTB5MN` updated with the corrected root cause. ## Why Layer-1 (#15374) moved the precondition checks into `ExecStart`, but the `workflow_dispatch` verification run [32873212247](https://github.com/Lucent-Financial-Group/Zeta/actions/runs/32873212247) — built from that fix — still showed **zero `zeta-creds-restore` lines in phase-2**, not even the new `MISSING precondition` logging. So the unit wasn't skipping on a precondition; it was **failing before `ExecStart` ran at all**. The service is enabled by default (`common.nix`: `zeta.credsRestore.enable = lib.mkDefault true`), so the only remaining pre-`ExecStart` filesystem dependency is `WorkingDirectory = cfg.repoRoot` (the cloned repo). When that directory is absent as the unit fires (`After = local-fs.target`, early), systemd fails the unit at chdir before `ExecStart`, and every log line — including the precondition gate — is unreachable. The earlier "blob delivery" hypothesis was one layer too shallow; the verification run corrected it. ## Verification - `bun test qemu-full-install-test.test.ts` → 71 pass, 0 fail; `bun run typecheck` → clean; markdownlint → clean. - Dispatched restore run [32940147157](https://github.com/Lucent-Financial-Group/Zeta/actions/runs/32940147157) on this branch: the phase-2 serial must now show `zeta-creds-restore: ExecStart entered` (proving the chdir fix), then either restore completes or the precondition gate **names** the next missing path. I'll report the serial. Why: - Restore was mute because the unit failed its chdir before ExecStart; make cwd always-valid so the (already-legible) ExecStart can run and diagnose the rest. What: - WorkingDirectory="/" + an unconditional ExecStart-entered marker; contract marker + drift-guard tests; workitem update. Proof: - 71/0 tests, tsc + markdownlint clean; verification dispatch in flight (ExecStart-entered expected on phase-2 serial). Limits: - nix eval is the ISO build (no local nix). Any residual pre-ExecStart failure shows as a missing "ExecStart entered" marker on the next dispatch.
