author: vitatsui
body:
框选修了三轮启发式，每修一处冒出另一处。这一版换了做法：**别再猜**。

## 0% → 100%

写讲稿的模型手里有整页的元素清单和 id，它写每一句时知道自己在讲哪一块。`NarrationSegment.element_refs` 就是让它说出来的字段，提示词第九节整节在讲这件事，第十三节有「第六步：绑定元素」，镜头第一步也是先读它。

真片子里，**155 句，0 次**。

三处原因：第六步只有一句话「逐句判断是否对应具体页面元素」，而第三步先说了「先不要考虑 element_refs」；「整体背景」这个口子宽到几乎任何一句都能钻；填没填没人检查，所以 0% 一直是静默失败。

三处都改了。重跑同一份文档：**146 句，146 句都绑了**。

## 镜头照着框

绑定明确时**只信它，而且是全部的 id**——「落到供应链、外贸、招投标三类情报」点了三个格子，框住一个等于指着这句话的三分之一。

| | 靠猜 | 靠讲稿说 |
|---|---|---|
| 框数 | 110 | 80 |
| **多元素合框** | 13 | **47** |
| 重合度 | 0.33 | **0.38** |
| 只框住一个名字 | 12 | **0** |
| 框住 >25% 版面 | 3 | **0** |
| 内容页一个框都没有 | 有 | **0 页** |

## 过渡句不框

这一页只要有一句绑了，空数组就当真——它是看过之后给的答案，镜头不动。整页一句都没绑，那是这一步没做（老工程），空数组什么也不说明，还是得猜。

## 不许框标题

一句只报了个名字的话——「再说招募目的。」「最上面是场景应用层。」——得到一个框在那四五个字上，而它接下来那句才在讲这一节真正说了什么。规则：框里只有一个标题、没有它领的内容，就不画。

判断「是不是标题」不能只看短。目录页是一列短行，「(一)背景及技术牵头方」在那里就是内容。所以认四种形状：下面压着长正文、同一行右边有长正文、同一行右边站着一排东西（那排跟它一样短，所以找「更长的」找不到它）、它自己就是 subtitle。数字和图片豁免。

两件只有动手才发现的事：圆点不算框（一带而过的小目标本来就该用圆点）；闸门必须放在手势归一之后——标题又小又是一带而过，先被选成圆点、正好通过豁免，随后「一页只用一种手势」又把圆点统一改成了框。

## 前快后慢，是个真 bug

`TTSProvider.natural_rate` 基类是 1.0，Edge 是 0.86。而取语速那一行读的是 `self._provider`，**那个字段要等第一次合成跑完才会被改成真正说话的引擎**。配音一次并发八页，第一批八页在任何一页跑完之前就都读到了默认的 1.0。

`1 / 0.86 = 1.16`。台阶落在第 8 和第 9 页之间，两部片子都是，因为 `MAX_SPEAKERS = 8`。

    第 1–8 页   7.02–7.59  →  6.21–6.56
    第 9–30 页  5.81、5.96 →  一个没动
    前半/后半   6.59/6.02  →  6.10/6.02

## 密页不要报菜名

上一版把密页从 426 字压到 203 字，读下来是四个名字加一串属性——旧版会走完四层数据集各自收什么。因为密度提示写的是「先把骨架点到：每个小标题、每一栏都要有」，逼着把所有标题念一遍，剩下的名额只够报名字。

改成：挑哪几处由你定，但挑中的每一处都要讲成话——是什么、做什么用、页面给了什么数字；宁可少挑两处。

## 返工能点开看

卡片在没有产物时是禁用的，而返工那次调用记了 0 个产物——一条写着「第 13 页｜返工」又打不开的记录，只告诉你有一页被重写过，不告诉你改了什么。现在挂「为什么返工 / 返工前 / 返工后」，压字数那次挂「压之前 / 压之后」。

541 测试通过。

author: varuas37
body:
Adds a docs page for `RandomAvatar`, the deterministic generative avatar that landed in the library ([`bff7df9`](https://github.com/nessalabs/nessa_ui/commit/bff7df9)).

## What's here

- **Vendored the component** — `nessa-ui/components/random-avatar.tsx` plus its export block, copied by `scripts/sync-nessa-ui.mjs` from the library branch. Only this component is picked up; the rest of the vendored mirror is untouched, so the diff stays about the avatar.
- **Catalog and registry entries** so the page, the sidebar, the overview card and the Behaviours chips all derive from the real library as usual.
- **Four previews**, all rendering the real component:
  - a roster at list size (the main preview),
  - several seeds painting one group picture,
  - the working state under `busy`,
  - the four tone presets alongside `ground="ink"`.
- **A card motif** for the overview grid.

Copy follows the `component-copy` skill: `An avatar painted from a seed, where the same identity always paints the same picture.`

The ink row renders inside a `dark` scope so it sits on the library's own dark tokens in either colour mode, rather than a hard-coded `bg-neutral-950` — the only raw-palette class the site would otherwise have.

## Known issue, upstream

`RandomAvatar` derives its SVG path coordinates from `Math.sin`/`Math.cos`. Those are **not** bit-identical across V8 versions, so the value Node computes at build time and the value Chrome computes on hydration differ in the last digit or two, and React logs a hydration mismatch on this page. Verified directly: hashing 200k `sin`/`cos` results gives `44ade537…` on Node 22 and `10fb701d…` in Chrome 148.

The painting is visually identical either way — the divergence is at the 1e-17 level, exposed by cancellation near zero in the blob rotation. The fix belongs in the library (round coordinates before serialising them into the path string, which also shrinks the markup), not in the vendored copy here. Happy to open that PR next.

One other thing to sequence: the install command on the page points at `https://nessalabs.ai/r/random-avatar.json`, which only exists once the library branch merges.

## Verification

`npm run build` passes (TypeScript included). Page checked in the browser in both colour modes: all four previews render, the Code tabs show the extracted source, and the sidebar and overview card pick the component up.

author: mordvic
body:
> **Stacked on #60**, which is stacked on #59. Merge in order, and **retarget each PR to
> `main` before deleting the branch below it** — deleting a merged base closes the dependent PR.

Fixes #46, fixes #55. Part of #50 (the fence half) and #58 (item 2).

`LineScanner` was written so the engine's layers could not disagree about what a line is; its
own doc comment records the drift that cost. Three places were not using it, and all three of
this PR's findings are that fact.

## The lone-CR splice

`InlineCodeRestorer` split on `"\n"`. `Chunker` only ends a chunk at a blank line, so a lone
CR — or NEL, or U+2028 — sits happily *inside* a chunk, and that chunk then read as one long
line here. Backticks paired across the break into a span that exists in no other layer:

```
source: "Version 5` tall\r`code` here"

flat split on "\n"  →  one phantom span:  [" tall\r"]
LineScanner         →  the real one:      ["code"]
MarkupSkeleton      →  [.inlineCode("code")]      ← already agreed with the scanner
```

Both counts are 1, so the equal-count gate passed, and `restore` spliced `" tall\r"` over the
real `` `code` `` span: the code destroyed and a CR injected into `final`. Reproduced against
the repo's own sources before the fix and pinned by a test after it.

**The rejoin is the other half and is not optional.** The restorer also rejoined with `"\n"`,
which was lossless only by accident — a lone `"\r"` survived because it stayed *inside* a
line's content. Scanning properly while still rejoining with a chosen terminator would have
started normalising the reply's own line endings, which is a byte change in what gets written
to the user's disk. `LineScanner.pieces` carries each terminator, and a round-trip test pins
`pieces(t).map { $0.content + $0.terminator }.joined() == t`.

## The CRLF reply

`ResponseCleaner.clean` had two line disciplines and neither was the engine's:

- `firstIndex(of: "\n")` is a **grapheme** search, and the single `Character` `"\r\n"` is not
  `"\n"` — so on a CRLF reply the preamble check never ran and «Here is the translation:»
  shipped in `final`.
- `components(separatedBy: .newlines)` splits on **scalars**, so `"\r\n"` became two breaks
  with an empty line between: ```` ```\r\na\r\nb\r\n``` ```` unwrapped to `"a\n\nb"` — a
  paragraph break that existed nowhere, plus a phantom «added» diff on a faithful translation.

`LineScanner`'s own comment already documents this exact `CharacterSet.newlines` trap as having
cost a defect in `MarkupSkeleton`. It was still live here.

*Trigger caveat, unchanged from the ledger:* this needs the model to emit `\r\n` in its own
reply. The mechanism is proven; the in-the-wild frequency is unmeasured.

## The streaming twin

`Translator.streamChunkReply`'s fence check trimmed `.whitespaces`, a set that **excludes** line
terminators — so a reply opening `"\n```"` never looked like a fence, the whole-answer unwrap
was skipped, and literal fence markers shipped into the translation. Its first-line decision
used the same grapheme search. `sourceSpanCount` now asks `InlineCodeRestorer` instead of
counting spans a second time, so the decision to buffer a chunk whole cannot disagree with the
gate it exists to serve.

**Half of #50 remains open** and is deliberately not fixed here: the streaming decision still
runs on the *untrimmed* buffer, so a reply beginning `"\n"` delivered character by character
still takes the first-line branch before the fence check can see anything. That is the trimming
asymmetry, and it is the follow-up PR's subject. The test here says so in its own comment rather
than implying the finding is closed.

## Test fixture

`FakeLLMClient` gains a `tokenizer` (default: one character per event). Some decisions in
`streamChunkReply` are made **per event**, and a fake that can only ever emit one character at a
time cannot reach them — which is precisely why two of these behaviours had no test. Nothing in
the `LLMClient` contract promises a token boundary anywhere, and a BPE tokeniser, a batching
server or a proxy all deliver multi-character pieces.

## Verification

- `swift build --build-tests` — zero warnings. `swift test` — 918 tests, green. All 903 tests
  that existed before this PR still pass unchanged, which is the first thing a refactor of this
  shape has to show.
- Six mutations, six red runs: the restorer splitting on `"\n"` again; the restorer rejoining
  with a chosen terminator; the cleaner back to `firstIndex(of:)`; the fence unwrap back to
  `CharacterSet.newlines`; the fence check back to `.whitespaces`; `pieces` normalising
  terminators. (A seventh attempt did not apply cleanly and was re-run properly rather than
  counted.)
- **Live acceptance**, `--model translategemma:12b --chunk 4000`, verdict ACCEPTED, recorded in
  `BASELINE.md` as Run F. Against the comparable Run C: chunking, term counts and markup lines
  identical; adherence 92.5→93.3 % and 92.9→92.9 %, where the single differing run is the
  model's own sampling and is **not** claimed as an improvement.

### What that run does not show

Every file in `corpus/` is pure LF — checked, zero CR bytes across all five — so **none of the
paths this PR repairs is reachable from it**. Run F establishes that four call sites moved
without changing anything the engine already handled; it cannot confirm the fix, and the
BASELINE entry says so rather than being left to read as if it did. The repaired behaviour is
pinned offline, where the inputs can be written down. A CRLF corpus file would close the gap
and is worth adding, but a sixth file changes every future run's comparability and is a decision
of its own.

author: ruslan-rv-ua
body:
**This dispatch never reached the bucket.** The bucket's handler builds the
manifest path from `client_payload.app`, and this payload never carried one —
so it resolved to `bucket/.json`, which does not exist, and the run failed at
its first step. The bucket's dispatch history bears that out: it holds runs
from `audiocaptor`, `axygen-shot`, `marka` and `quick-snippets`, and **none**
from `browserselector`. `bucket/browserselector.json` has been updated by
hand all along.

So this removes a step that cost a release-time failure and bought nothing.

**What replaces it.** The bucket now runs Scoop's own **Excavator**: it reads
this manifest's `checkver` and `autoupdate` and bumps
`bucket/browserselector.json` itself, started by hand from the bucket's
Actions tab or on its daily run at 04:20 UTC.

**Verified before removing, not assumed.** The Excavator was run against the
whole bucket and `checkver` resolved `0.2.0` for this application. Then
`autoupdate` was checked directly: the URL template resolves to an asset that
really exists in the v0.2.0 release, and its `.sha256` sidecar hash matches
that asset's digest as GitHub reports it. So the path that has never worked
is being replaced by one that has been shown to.

**The trade:** a scoop update is no longer immediate — it waits for the button
or the daily run. In this repository's case that is strictly better than what
it had, which was nothing.

**After merging:** delete the `SCOOP_BUCKET_TOKEN` secret from this
repository. It sat in five repositories on one token; this is the last of the
five to stop using it.

body:
## Resumo

- **O que esta PR entrega:** o fechamento da wave 3 (redesign dark-first do frontend). Promove ao catálogo do shell as 8 lacunas de CSS que as 6 frentes de tela registraram e contornaram com `<style>` escopado, corrige 5 divergências visuais achadas na comparação tela a tela com o protótipo, verifica os 6 critérios cross-feature no estado integrado e documenta a wave (HLD 1.5, FDD §5 v1.1, retro).
- **Resultado esperado:** um único lugar (`studio/web/style.css`) volta a ser o contrato visual das 11 telas — seis prefixos concorrentes (`.bs-`, `.md-`, `.sb-`/`.sh-`, `.an-`, `.mu-`/`.ed-`, `.ex-`/`.pb-`/`.pr-`) deixam de reimplementar as mesmas regras. Dois bugs de especificidade que afetavam o usuário somem: o rótulo da paleta que virava um quadrado de 22 px (3 px de scroll horizontal na etapa 5) e o `input.mini` de 60 px que cortava `0.511` na etapa 8.
- **Tipo de mudança:** chore (fechamento de wave) — CSS/markup + docs + 3 asserts reapontados. Nenhuma rota, regra de negócio ou dependência muda.

## Contexto e motivação

A wave 3 foi organizada em duas sub-waves: `shell-redesign` (sub-wave 0) entregou o **catálogo de classes** como contrato e foi mergeada antes de tudo; as 6 frentes de tela (sub-wave 1) consumiram esse catálogo em paralelo. Pela regra 3 da wave (e pela ADR-010), **nenhuma frente de tela edita `studio/web/*`**: quem precisasse de uma classe que o shell não previu usava `<style>` escopado no próprio `view.html` com prefixo da etapa e registrava a lacuna no final report, deixando para a integração decidir a promoção.

O catálogo nasceu antes de qualquer tela existir — e as 6 frentes acharam 8 lacunas nele. Esta é a janela de promoção prevista.

Rastreabilidade: `docs/domains/studio/waves/wave-3.md` (spec da wave, §"Critérios cross-feature"), `docs/domains/studio/recon-wave-3.md` (terreno, §2 strings fixadas por teste), `docs/domains/studio/features/shell-redesign-fdd.md` §5 (catálogo), e a seção "lacunas de CSS" dos 6 FDDs de tela.

## Alterações técnicas

### Principais mudanças

**1. Duas lacunas eram BUGS de especificidade, não ausências**

- `.palette .lbl` (0,2,0) perdia para `.palette.sm>span` (0,2,1): o rótulo herdava o quadrado de 22 px do swatch e estourava a linha. Corrigido com `:not(.lbl):not(.fine):not(.ext)` nas regras do swatch — medido depois: rótulo em **84×16 px**, borda `0px`.
- `input.mini` (0,1,1) perdia para `.inline input[type=number]` (0,2,1) e voltava a 60 px, cortando valores de 3 casas. Corrigido com `.inline input.mini`/`.ctl input.mini` (64 px), mais `input.mini.wide` (76 px, valor em reais do pitch) e `input.mini.num`.

**2. Seis ausências reais**

- `input.prompt-inline` só casava `input`; o prompt da etapa 6 é `textarea` → `input.prompt-inline, textarea.prompt-inline` + `resize:vertical`/`min-height:56px`.
- `.take` não zerava a aparência de `<button>` (`font-weight`, `text-align:center`, `line-height`, `white-space:nowrap`) nem tratava `:disabled`.
- `.beats .cut{top:1px}` caía sobre as barras de impacto (100 % da altura, mesma cor accent) → `top:-6px` + `z-index:2` + `text-shadow`. **Sem mexer em padding nem altura**, então o `.beats-axis` continua alinhado.
- `.player .term` usava `#C9CFD8` sobre gradiente `transparent→.72`: ilegível no tema claro, onde o placeholder listrado é claro → gradiente `.25→.85` + branco `#EDEFF2`.
- `@media (max-width:900px)` colapsava `.shot-row` em 1 coluna e a thumb 16/9 tomava a largura inteira → só `.scene-row` e `.clip-row` colapsam; `.shot-row` mantém `110px minmax(0,1fr)`.
- Utilitários que seis telas reinventaram: `.grow`/`.grow-sm`/`.grow-lg`, `.row.stretch`, `.flat` (+ regra automática de `margin-top:0` para `.fine`/`.note` dentro de `.row`/`.cli`/`.ctl`/`.takes`), `.pre`, `.card.static`, `.card .card-act`, `.thumb.none`/`.thumb>.empty`, `.rowcard.col`/`.rowcard.pick`, `.scene-row .media/.edit/.acts`, `.drop.inline`, `.pub-row .fb`.

**3. Cinco divergências do protótipo corrigidas** (comparação de 12 pares de prints, tema escuro)

| O que o protótipo faz | O que o app fazia | Correção |
|---|---|---|
| legenda do tile legível | `.card .term` `#C9CFD8` sobre `transparent→.72`: o hash sumia sobre foto clara | mesmo tratamento do `.player .term` |
| nome do clipe inteiro | `.clip-row` com coluna de 120 px cortando `cena01/shot01 ta…` (precisa de 133 px) | `minmax(170px,1fr)` |
| nenhum painel com caixa vazia | `#baseLog`, `#shotsLog`, `#boardOut`, `#renderLog` desenhavam uma barra 1058×22 px com borda | `.log:empty{display:none}` |
| tile "+ gerar take N" legível | `.take.empty` em `--ink-5` (≈2,6:1 de contraste) | `--ink-4` + hover |
| hairline sólida no pitch | `.pitch-table .tr` pontilhada | `1px solid` |

E **"Gerar via CLI (gasta créditos)" vira `ghost`** nas cinco telas onde aparece (2, 3, 4, 5, 7). Era `primary` preenchido em quatro e sem classe na 4 — o app estava inconsistente consigo mesmo. É a alternativa **paga**: o protótipo a desenha ghost e o gate de fidelidade lembra que "na aula 008 o custo é o principal critério".

**4. Limpeza de CSS morto:** `.an-takes .row` e `.an-takes .row.sel` saem — a frente `views-animate` reescreveu o markup e os seletores deixaram de casar.

### Arquivos e componentes relevantes

- `studio/web/style.css` (+96/−18) — **comece por aqui**. É o único arquivo de núcleo tocado.
- `studio/etapas/*/view.{html,js}` (18 arquivos) — passam a consumir as classes do shell; as regras escopadas equivalentes saem dos `<style>`. Fica escopado só o que é mesmo de uma tela (larguras de mídia, elipses, molduras de painel) — a tabela está na retro.
- `docs/domains/studio/hld.md` → **v1.5**; `docs/domains/studio/features/shell-redesign-fdd.md` → **v1.1** (§5); `docs/domains/studio/waves/wave-3.md` (§Fechamento); `docs/domains/studio/waves/wave-3-retro.md` (novo).
- `tests/test_{base,shots,storyboard}_api.py` — 3 asserts **reapontados**, não relaxados (ver abaixo).

### Contratos, APIs e dados

- **Nenhum endpoint, schema ou payload muda.** Nenhum arquivo de `studio/*/service.py`, `router.py`, `guide.py`, `app.py` ou `steps.py` foi tocado. Sem coleção Postman: não há contrato HTTP nesta entrega.
- **Contrato visual (o que muda):** o catálogo do shell **só ganhou nomes** — nenhuma classe foi renomeada ou removida do que as telas usam, exceto `.an-takes .row.sel`, que já não casava com markup nenhum. Compatibilidade retroativa preservada: as três substrings que `test_api.py` verifica sem espaços (`prefers-color-scheme:dark`, `max-width:900px`, `:root[data-theme="dark"]`) continuam literais.
- **Asserts reapontados** (rastreiam a promoção, não afrouxam a checagem):
  - `test_base_api.py`: exige `class="grow"` e `class="grow-lg"` no HTML **e** que `.bs-grow` tenha sumido (assert a mais, não a menos);
  - `test_shots_api.py`: `class="rowcard sh-scene` → `class="rowcard col pick`;
  - `test_storyboard_api.py`: `card wide sb-base` → `card wide static sb-base`.

### Segurança, privacidade e observabilidade

- Sem dado sensível: a mudança é CSS, classes de markup e documentação. Nenhum segredo, token ou credencial no diff.
- Sem log novo. `.log:empty{display:none}` esconde a **caixa** quando não há log; assim que o `view.js` escreve conteúdo, ela reaparece (`:empty` deixa de casar).
- O caminho `/mnt/c/Users/arthu/Downloads` que aparece nos prints é o diretório de Downloads local da máquina de teste, renderizado pela própria tela — não entra no diff.

## Rastreabilidade SDD/Compozy

- **Task-Id:** `ADH-OS-20260826-09`
- **PRD/TechSpec:** não se aplica no formato SDD. A spec normativa é `docs/domains/studio/waves/wave-3.md` (§"Contrato transversal" e §"Critérios cross-feature") e os 7 FDDs da wave; o terreno é `docs/domains/studio/recon-wave-3.md`.
- **ADRs:** nenhuma nova. A entrega **cumpre** a ADR-010 (só a frente de integração edita `studio/web/*`) e não contraria ADR-001 (sem dependência nova, sem build), ADR-004 (nenhum texto de aula alterado) nem ADR-008 (verificação visual fora do CI, registrada por prints).
- **Tasks:** implementação

body:
## Summary

`/api/diagnostics` on production returned `tudor_inbox_scan.messages: []` — Gmail has no message matching `subject:TUDOR OR filename:TUDOR OR subject:AGENT`, yet the report is said to arrive as an Excel attachment on that account. So the Tudor workbook is landing under a subject/filename the classifier doesn't recognise.

To find its real name, the scan is generalised and a second, name-agnostic pass is added:

```python
ATTACHMENT_QUERY = 'has:attachment (filename:xlsx OR filename:xls OR filename:csv)'

inspect_messages(app, query, limit)          # was inspect_tudor_messages, now query-driven
inspect_tudor_messages(app)                  # -> inspect_messages(app, TUDOR_QUERY)
inspect_attachment_messages(app, limit=40)   # -> inspect_messages(app, ATTACHMENT_QUERY)
```

`/api/diagnostics` gains an `attachment_scan` key listing every recent spreadsheet attachment with its `subject`, `sender`, `filenames`, `sender_allowed`, `classified_as` and `matches_sync_query` — so a workbook the classifier returns `null` for is immediately visible. Each scan is wrapped independently, so one failing scan no longer blanks the whole response.

No sync behaviour changes; this is read-only diagnostics.

## Verification

- `/api/diagnostics` registers and 302s to login when unauthenticated.
- `inspect_attachment_messages` returns the no-account sentinel (now including the `query` it used) when no Gmail token is stored.
- `pyflakes` clean apart from the pre-existing unused `get_tudor_summary` import.

Adds a finalizing callback to the custom headed scan flow so Dev Suite can update the UI immediately after the external browser is closed.

Previously, the scan remained in the “Headed Scan in progress” state while Oobee continued generating reports via mergeAxeResults, which made the Join/End controls briefly appear stale. author: imshashank
body:
## What this changes Relative timestamps now render through a single `RelativeTime` element instead of calling `relativeTime()` inline in twelve places. The element confines the value to one `` node and marks it `suppressHydrationWarning`, so the string can no longer fail hydration. ## Why `relativeTime(from, now = new Date())` reads the wall clock through its default second argument. In a client component that default runs twice, once during the server render and once during hydration. When the two straddle the 45 second `just now` cutoff or a minute boundary, the strings differ and React throws `Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client`. That is a real intermittent bug on dev builds, and it also makes CI flaky. It failed the End-to-end (Playwright) job on #358 at `apps/web/e2e/account-and-workspaces.spec.ts:123`, on a pull request that does not touch `apps/web/src/features/account` at all. The Next dev overlay renders a codeframe of `sessions-panel.tsx` line 61, whose source text contains `This device`, so `page.getByText('This device')` matched two elements and failed strict mode. Every other call site had the same latent flake, and it was not theoretical: the app dehydrates prefetched query state into the server render (`app/(app)/layout.tsx` plus six page level `HydrationBoundary`s), so the inbox, docs, pulls and activity lists all ship real rows rather than skeletons. ## How you know it works `apps/web/tests/components/ui/relative-time.test.tsx` renders to HTML at one system time, moves the clock across the `just now` boundary with `setSystemTime`, then hydrates and collects both `onRecoverableError` and `console.error`. It is a real guard rather than a green rubber stamp, two ways: - A control case in the same file renders the old inline pattern through the same harness and asserts React **does** complain. It passes, so the harness detects mismatches. - Removing `suppressHydrationWarning` and re-running turns the suite red with React's own `+ 1m ago / - just now` diff. A fifth test scans every `.ts` and `.tsx` under `apps/web/src` and fails if anything but the component calls `relativeTime(` again, so a new call site cannot silently reintroduce this. `bun run lint`, `check-comments`, `check-bytes`, `check-bun-imports`, `check-deps` and the `apps/web` typecheck are green. Root `bun run typecheck` halts on two pre-existing `Buffer` errors in `scripts/`, identical with and without this branch. On tests, rather than claim a clean sweep: this suite flakes locally on full process runs, so each touched directory was baselined against a stash of the same tree. `features/docs` fails 3 and `features/issues` fails 10 both with and without the change, identically. `inbox`, `pulls`, `account`, `comments`, `settings` and `components/ui` are green in isolation. Nothing here moved the failure set. ## Anything reviewers should know **Why `suppressHydrationWarning` and not a stable server `now`.** Threading a server timestamp down to every call site works, but it is a rule every future call site has to remember, and it silently rots the first time someone forgets. React documents this attribute for exactly a rendered timestamp. Confining it to one `` element means the only text it can ever mask is the relative string itself, never sibling content. The source scan is what keeps the rule enforced. **The value is the server's, not the client's.** React keeps the server text and does not correct it after hydration, so when the two renders straddle a boundary the DOM sits one bucket behind, `just now` where the client would say `1m ago`. I measured this rather than assuming it, and two things came out of it. The first is that the obvious fix does not work. Neither a `useState` initializer with an effect that recomputes, nor a deterministic `null` sentinel with an effect that stores `Date.now()`, changes the DOM. The effect runs and the re-render happens, but `suppressHydrationWarning` has already told React to accept the server text, so React's committed value is `1m ago` while the DOM says `just now`, and a re-render producing `1m ago` again is a no-op. Once the attribute accepts the server text, no later render producing the same string can correct that node. Correcting it needs a hydration render that matches the server byte for byte, which means threading the server's `now` through every call site, which is the option rejected above. The second is that what ships is narrower than "stale text". The drift is at most one bucket, only on a straddled boundary, and it self-heals on the next re-render that crosses a bucket, because that render does produce a different string and React does patch it. Left with no re-render, the label sits where the server put it, which is where it would have sat anyway had hydration not straddled a boundary. That is not worth a timestamp threaded through twelve call sites. **Two server components gained a client island.** `github-deliveries.tsx` and `pull-detail.tsx` are reached from a server page and a client parent respectively, and neither could mismatch as it stood. Migrating them anyway keeps the rule uniform and the scan simple, which seemed worth a `` element of JavaScript. **`DocsHomeSection` lost its `now` prop.** It existed only to keep the rows of one section consistent with each other, which `RelativeTime` now gets for free. **Adjacent, deliberately not in this PR.** `toLocaleDateString(undefined, ...)` and `Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, ...)` in client components carry the same hazard through locale and timezone rather than the clock, and `sprint-header.tsx:44` passes `new Date()` to `sprintDay`. The date cases need a midnight straddle to bite, so they are far less likely than a 45 second cutoff, and folding them in would balloon this diff. Worth their own issue. ## Checklist - [ ] `bun run verify` is green, all four checks (lint, comments, bytes, bun imports, deps and the `apps/web` typecheck are green; root `typecheck` halts on two pre-existing `Buffer` errors in `scripts/` that are identical on `main`, so `verify` never reaches the test step) - [x] Tests added or updated, and they fail without the change - [x] No comments added to code, and no em-dash characters anywhere - [x] No `any`, no non-null assertions - [ ] External input is parsed with a Zod schema from `@orbit/shared` (not applicable, no external input) - [ ] Authorization is enforced on the server (not applicable, presentation only) - [ ] Docs updated if behaviour, configuration or setup changed (not applicable) - [ ] `bun run db:release` and `bun run db:check-drift` (not applicable, no schema change)

Greptile Summary

Centralizes relative timestamp rendering in a hydration-warning-suppressed `` component. - Replaces inline `relativeTime()` calls across account, comments, documents, inbox, issues, pull requests, and settings. - Adds hydration-boundary regression tests and a source scan preventing new inline relative-time rendering.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge. No blocking failure remains.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/web/src/components/ui/relative-time.tsx | Introduces a focused client component that confines clock-dependent text to one hydration-warning-suppressed `` element. | | apps/web/tests/components/ui/relative-time.test.tsx | Tests the server/client clock-boundary mismatch, verifies suppression behavior and semantic markup, and guards against future inline call sites. | | apps/web/src/features/docs/docs-home.tsx | Migrates document timestamps to the shared component and removes the now-unnecessary shared `now` prop. | | apps/web/src/features/inbox/inbox-view.tsx | Migrates both notification-row and notification-detail timestamps without changing their surrounding content. | | apps/web/src/features/pulls/

author: rokartur
body:
Findings from a production-bar review of the whole app, verified against the code before being acted on. Each commit is one unrelated bug, so they revert independently.

## Blockers

- **`$` in a secret never reached the container.** `escapeEnvValue` did not escape `$`, so Compose interpolated `p$ssw0rd` away. Proven with a real `docker compose run`: `p$$ssw0rd` renders identically to the literal.
- **A closed log stream stranded a goroutine.** Every SSE send is now inside a `select` with `ctx.Done()`, and `pr`/`errPr` are closed so a parked `stdcopy.StdCopy` write unblocks.
- **Deleting the default environment tore it down before refusing.** The `IsDefault` guard ran after `composeProject.Down(...)`, so the refusal arrived with the containers already gone.
- **A failed update truncated `compose.yml`.** The download went straight over the live file. It now lands beside it and is moved only once whole; the update backup includes `compose.yml`, which it had omitted.

## Security

- **Origin check ignored the port**, so a deployed project publishing a port on the panel's hostname passed as the panel. This platform deploys arbitrary projects, which makes that ordinary rather than theoretical.
- **Origin check then still ignored the scheme.** A default port is absent from both Origin and Host, so `http://panel` and the HTTPS panel reduced to the same string. Nothing compensates: no response sets HSTS and port 80 only redirects. Now scheme, host and port, with the default port filled in on both sides so `panel:443` and `https://panel` still match.
- **Pruning unused volumes asked for nothing** while deleting one volume required `confirm=true`. A stopped project's data volume has no container referencing it. Only volumes gate; images and networks are rebuildable.
- **Registry host and login name reach `docker login` unvalidated.** No shell is involved, but the command parses its own flags, so a leading dash was read as an option.

## Docs

Twenty-eight routes were registered in the mux and absent from the API reference. All are described now.

## Checks

`make check` green, `go test -race ./...` clean, `shellcheck` clean on all three tracked shell scripts, `$` escaping and volume behaviour confirmed against a real Docker daemon.

Three findings the review raised were **refuted and deliberately not acted on**: the collect endpoint does have a rate limit (Nginx, both vhosts), the handler preamble is already factored behind existing helpers used 8/5/29 times, and the route components are already factored behind `DataTable`/`Page`/`Section`.

author: devaeterne
body:
## Summary
Adds the customer shipment / warehouse fulfillment workflow on top of the Invoice-enabled customer/order domain.

### Shipment domain
- `customer_shipments` and `customer_shipment_items`
- shipment numbering (`SHP-000001`)
- statuses: Draft, Picking, Packed, Shipped, Delivered, Cancelled
- shipment/order/customer snapshots and carrier/tracking metadata
- partial shipment support based on remaining order quantities

### Warehouse fulfillment
- shipment lines are configured with source warehouse + inventory location
- quantity cannot exceed the remaining unallocated order quantity
- stock is deducted only when the shipment is marked **Shipped**
- fulfillment uses the existing `stock_out` RPC so stock validation and movement history stay centralized
- stock mutation and shipment/order status changes run in the same database transaction
- shipped/delivered shipments cannot be casually cancelled and corrupt inventory history

### Order integration
- Create Shipment action on Order Detail
- Draft/Cancelled orders cannot create shipments
- full fulfillment advances the order to `shipped`
- partial fulfillment keeps the order in `ready_for_shipment`
- when all shipment quantities are delivered, the order advances to `delivered`

### UI
- global `/customers/shipments` list with search/status filter
- customer-specific shipment history
- shipment detail and fulfillment screen
- source stock location selection and quantity configuration
- carrier, service level and tracking fields
- Customers sidebar → Shipments

## SQL application order
After Invoice PR #12 is merged/applied:
1. `modulex-admin/sql/customer-shipments.sql`
2. `modulex-admin/sql/customer-shipments-runtime-fix.sql`

The second migration aligns fulfillment with the current `stock_out` RPC signature (`p_quantity`, `p_reference_no`, `p_reason`, `p_notes`).

## Manual test checklist
1. Create/confirm an order with products that have available stock.
2. From Order Detail, click **Create Shipment**.
3. Confirm shipment lines contain the remaining quantities from the order.
4. Configure each line with source warehouse/location and shipment quantity.
5. Move Draft → Picking → Packed if desired.
6. Ship and confirm inventory decreases through stock movements with `SHIPMENT:<number>` reference.
7. Confirm a partial shipment leaves remaining order quantity available for another shipment.
8. Fully ship the order and confirm order status becomes `shipped`.
9. Mark all shipments Delivered and confirm order becomes `delivered`.
10. Confirm Shipped/Delivered shipments cannot be cancelled through the pre-fulfillment status action.
11. Verify global and customer shipment lists, carrier/tracking search, and sidebar navigation.

## Dependency / merge order
This is intentionally stacked on `feature/customer-invoices` because PR #12 promotes that branch to `main`.
Merge order:
1. PR #12
2. this Shipment PR

No Vercel deployment or automatic merge is performed.

Ignore this PR until it has been reviewed by @ChrisRackauckas.

## What changed

The BasicNeuralDE tests now import `BFGS` directly from its owning package, Optim. Optim is declared as a test dependency with the same major-version constraint already required by OptimizationOptimJL.

OptimizationOptimJL still supplies the `Optimization.solve` integration. The tests no longer rely on that wrapper transitively reexporting all of Optim's public names.

## Root cause

Optimization commit [`0c726c0c`](https://github.com/SciML/Optimization.jl/commit/0c726c0cf0b2f4c150b26ca03c4117e8a35434af) removed `@reexport using Optim` from OptimizationOptimJL. The change first shipped in [OptimizationOptimJL v0.4.19](https://github.com/SciML/Optimization.jl/releases/tag/OptimizationOptimJL-v0.4.19); v0.4.18 still supplied bare `BFGS` as a side effect of loading the wrapper.

The exact dependency transition reproduces independently of DiffEqFlux:

```text
OptimizationOptimJL=0.4.18
bare_BFGS=true
bare_constructor=BFGS{...}(...)
owner=Optim

OptimizationOptimJL=0.4.19
bare_BFGS=false
bare_constructor=FAIL UndefVarError: `BFGS` not defined in `Main`
owner_import=BFGS{...}(...)
owner=Optim
```

Optim 2.2.2 exports and documents `BFGS`, and `parentmodule(Optim.BFGS) === Optim`. Optim and DiffEqFlux are both MIT-licensed. The broader wrapper reexport restoration is tracked separately in [Optimization PR #1315](https://github.com/SciML/Optimization.jl/pull/1315); this direct-owner import remains correct independently of that PR.

## Failing before / passing after

On an unmodified checkout of DiffEqFlux master at `5bc0b77fc62db7dedc7e595d5c71ec3f3365cccd`, the focused mass-matrix test failed:

Neural DAE    |      2      2  1m09.6s

author: ningsheng-ali
body:
## Motivation

In the sparse prefill kernel, Q is loop-invariant across the `n_block` (KV block) loop, but the QK GEMM re-reads the Q A-operand from shared memory on every iteration, keeping the QK GEMM smem-traffic bound.

## Modifications

`csrc/ppu/prefill/sparse/sparse_prefill_std.cuh` only:

- Define `kKeepQQkSteps = 24`, guarded by a `static_assert` against the compile-time QK k-step count of `tSrQ` (36 for `HEAD_DIM_QK = 576` with 16x16x16 MMA atoms).
- On `n_block == 0`, copy the leading 24 QK k-steps of Q from smem into the register fragment once.
- Replace `flash::gemm<Kernel_traits::Is_Q_in_regs>` with the existing `flash::gemm_rss<kKeepQQkSteps>` (`csrc/utils.h`), so the resident Q fragment is reused for all subsequent KV blocks and only the remaining k-steps are streamed from smem.
- Follow-up (0c56288): wrap the resident-Q staging in `if constexpr (!Kernel_traits::Share_Q_K_smem)` and fall back to the original `flash::gemm` when Q/K alias the same smem. The current dispatch always instantiates `Share_Q_K_smem = 0`, so the shipped code path is unchanged and this only adds robustness (addresses the automated review note).

No API or launch-config changes. The warp-interleave path (`sparse_prefill_wg.cuh`) is untouched; dispatch routes long `h_q == 128` prefills there, so this change targets the std path (short/odd-length prefills, non-128 head counts, `s_kv < topk`).

## Accuracy Tests

- Validated on the same kernel shape in our internal tree: Oracle reference 15/15 and seqwheel 144/144 passed.
- [x] `python tests/test_flash_mla_sparse_prefill.py` on this HEAD (commit ce24390): **All 737 cases passed** (single ZW-M890P, PPU_SDK 2.1.2 / HGGC 13.0 / driver 2.2.2-r691b0, torch 2.10.0, built from source with `-arch=ppu_15`, `FLASH_MLA_DISABLE_FP16=TRUE`). The same suite also passes on the base commit (main @ 8290ad9) as a control.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel-level micro-benchmark (internal baseline, identical launch configs), 8 sparse-prefill workloads: geometric mean speedup **1.1226x**, best workload **1.1384x**.

End-to-end serving A/B (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8/CP8/EP8, fp8 KV cache, chunked prefill 3840; only the flash_mla extension differs): input throughput **+0.81% / +2.15% / +1.18% / +1.83%** at 4k / 16k / 64k / 100k context respectively.

- [x] Re-measured on this HEAD over the full `benchmark/dsa_prefill.list` (560 bf16 sparse-prefill cases), as an A/B between two builds of this repo at main @ 8290ad9 (baseline) and this HEAD (ce24390), run back-to-back on the same idle ZW-M890P. Since `run_flash_mla.py::run_dsa_prefill` currently performs a single untimed forward, the kernel was timed with the same `kernelkit.bench_kineto` methodology used by `tests/test_flash_mla_sparse_prefill.py` (kernel time of `flash_sparse_prefill_fwd`, 10 timed runs per case), reproducing `run_dsa_prefill`'s input generation (same seeds, same case list). Environment as in the accuracy test above.

  | Case group | Cases | Geomean speedup | Min / Median / Max |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | std path (modified by this PR) | 330 | **1.1362x** | 1.118x / 1.136x / 1.147x |
  | wg path (untouched, acts as control) | 230 | 1.0001x | 0.998x / 1.000x / 1.004x |
  | All | 560 | 1.0782x | — |

  Every std-path case is faster (no regressions); the untouched wg-path cases show no systematic drift between the two runs (±0.4% noise band), confirming the std-path gain is not a machine-state artifact. This is consistent with the internal-tree micro-benchmark geomean above (1.1226x).

Note: `kKeepQQkSteps = 24` was tuned empirically (register residency vs. register pressure trade-off); happy to expose it as a traits-level knob if preferred.

author: icecube-acc
body:
## Scope

- **Finding/task:** W-0374 — `projectSingleLiability()` falls back to "cleared at retirement age" for an undated debt, computed as `$retirementAge - $currentAge`. Both were the **viewer's**, for both members.
- **User-visible change:** A spouse's undated debt was discharged on their partner's schedule. Where the viewer's retirement age is already behind them the term is `max(0, 60 - 70) = 0` and the debt **vanished from the projection entirely**.

### Two sites, where the item names one

Said plainly because this file has a history of "I found every site" turning out wrong:

1. `projectLiabilities()` passed the viewer's pair for the spouse — the one the item describes.
2. `projectMainResidenceNetValue()` builds **one closure** and applies it to both members, capturing the viewer's ages on the way in. This feeds the projected residence-band cap rather than the estate total, so it is invisible in `projected_liabilities` and needs its own test.

Both now read `ageFrameFor($member)` — one home, two callers (Rule 20).

### The trap in the fix

`projectMemberLiabilities()` **derived the horizon** from the same `$currentAge` it used for the fallback, so handing it the spouse's age would have moved the horizon too and regressed **W-0188**. `$yearsToProject` is now computed once by the caller and passed in, so the shared household horizon and the per-member fallback are separate parameters that cannot be conflated again. That is acceptance 2, and it has its own test.

`projectMainResidenceNetValue()`'s now-unused age parameters are **removed** rather than left — passing them looks like it means something, which is how this bug worked.

## Verification

- **PHP command and result:** `pest tests/Feature/Estate tests/Unit/Services/Estate` → 515 passed. `--testsuite=Architecture` → 177 passed. Pint clean.
- **Frontend command and result:** n/a — no frontend change.
- **Desktop browser evidence:** n/a — projection change with no UI of its own.
- **/m browser evidence:** n/a — reaches `/m` through the shared API.

The residence-path test is **differential** (two households identical but for the spouse's own retirement age) and was verified to **fail with the defect reinstated** — a differential test that passes for the wrong reason is worth nothing, and this one initially passed for the wrong reason twice.

## Mobile impact

Mobile impact: shared-backend

## Deployment

- **csjones feature-branch SHA:** not deployed
- **Migration/corpus/cache actions:** none
- **Rollback:** revert the commit; no data written

author: hamzatal
body:
ستّة تغييرات — كلّها أشياء **كانت ناقصة** في الهوية لا أشياء كانت خطأ.

## 1) الشعار صار أوّل الريدمي

كان مدفوناً داخل بانر المنتج يزاحمه ثلاث شاشات، فأوّل ما يراه القارئ **شاشات لا علامة**. الآن **لوحة علامة** مستقلّة أولاً — أيقونة التطبيق، الاسم، الشِعار — وبانر المنتج نزل تحت «الفكرة» حيث **يشرح شيئاً** فعلاً.

## 2) نقطة الوجهة صارت كهرمانية

**الوصول هو المكافأة**، فهو وحده يحمل لون التمييز. وقطرها `7/96` فتكلفتها البصرية ضئيلة ومعناها ليس كذلك.

وأُعلنت قاعدة صريحة: هذا **الاستخدام الوحيد المسموح** للون ثانٍ في الهوية. الكهرماني لا يظهر في مكان آخر إلّا حالة `live` على الخرائط، **ولا يحمل نصّاً أبداً** لأنّ أبيض على `#F59E0B` = **2.15:1** ويسقط.

## 3) شِعار للمشروع

| الطبقة | النصّ |
|---|---|
| **الشِعار** | **مقعدك إلى الجامعة** |
| **الوعد** | تدفع مقعداً، لا رحلة |
| **الإنجليزية** | YOUR SEAT TO CAMPUS |

يقول **ما الذي تشتريه** — وهو نموذج العمل كلّه — وقصير بما يكفي لشاشة سبلاش. مسجَّل في قسم «الصوت» حتى لا ينحرف، ومعه قاعدة: لا نَعِد بما لا نملك، ونقول الحقيقة غير المريحة **في الواجهة** لا نخفيها.

## 4) السبلاش حُسم

خريطة باهتة تتبع **مساراً واحداً** من حلقة انطلاق إلى نقطة وصول، وحجاب دائري يُنقّي المركز، وفوقه العلامة والاسم والشِعار.

**فاتح للطالب، داكن للكابتن** — وليس ذوقاً: الكابتن يفتح التطبيق فجراً وليلاً داخل مركبة، والشاشة البيضاء الكاملة تُبهر.

## 5) كود الصعود 4 أرقام لا 6

التصميم كان يعرض 6، لكن `TripService::uniqueTripCode` **يولّد 4 دائماً** وفريدة داخل الرحلة. فهذا تصحيح **للتصميم ليطابق الكود** لا العكس — وهو ما يستطيع طالب وكابتن أن يتبادلاه فعلاً.

> **وأُضيف البند 1.20:** أربعة أرقام = **10,000 احتمال**، فغياب الـthrottle على مسارَي الصعود/الإنزال صار **إلزاماً لا تحسيناً**. بدونه يستطيع الكابتن تأكيد إنزال راكب لم ينزل **بالتخمين**، وهذا يهزم ضابط «التأكيد من الطرفين» الذي يبني عليه مركز النزاعات.

## 6) مرجع ألوان كامل في الريدمي

كل توكن مع hex ونسبته المقيسة على أبيض وعلى `n900` **وما يُسمح له أن يكون** — لأنّ ليس كل لون يصلح نصّاً. كل النسب محسوبة بمعادلة **WCAG 2.1 لا مقدَّرة بالنظر**، وكل قرار مرفوض مسجَّل **مع الرقم الذي قتله**:

| مرفوض | الرقم |
|---|---|
| كحلي `#002045` | **16.25:1** ≈ أسود، فأجبر على لون ثانٍ داكن يفرقه عنه **2.51:1** فقط ⇒ صفر تراتُب |
| `warn` `#F79009` | **2.35:1** كنصّ — يسقط AA وهو في **كل** شارة «قيد المراجعة» |
| أبيض على الكهرماني | **2.15:1** |

## وأيضاً — إزالة تكرار

العلامة كانت **خمس نسخ SVG مكرّرة** في `admin.mjs` و`gen-student` و`gen-extra` و`gen-admin` و`gen-readme`. صارت `mark()` واحدة مُصدَّرة من `ui.mjs` — فتغيير لون النقطة اليوم يمسّ **ملفاً واحداً**. ولهذا أُعيد تصيير صفائح `v2` المتأثّرة.

## الفحص

- [x] 21 صورة ورابطاً ومرساةً في الريدمي مفحوصة آلياً — لا مفقود
- [x] كل صورة جديدة فُحصت بصرياً (`brand` · `splash` · `logo`) بعد ثلاث دورات ضبط للكثافة
- [x] صفر بقايا «ستة أرقام»
- [x] لا تغيير في كود التطبيق

Fixes #29395

Grafana Operator v5.25.0 adds a `FolderUIDMismatch` condition with negative polarity: `False` with reason `ConsistentUID` means the folder is healthy, while `True` means a UID mismatch is present. The existing customization treated all false conditions as degraded and all true conditions as healthy.

Handle both states explicitly while retaining existing behavior for failures such as `FolderSynchronized=False`. Tests include realistic v5.25-style fixtures for both consistent and mismatched folder UIDs.

author: jadhavgaurav
body:
Two fixes that came out of investigating the SEO team's crawl-stats audit, plus the verification companion for it.

## The sitemap was frozen between deploys

`apps/web/src/app/sitemap.ts` exported no route-level `revalidate`, so the segment was prerendered once at build and served unchanged until the next deploy. The per-fetch `revalidate` refreshed the data cache but never re-ran the function, and no CMS hook purged the route.

Measured on production 2026-08-26: the live sitemap listed 537 URLs with a newest `lastmod` of `2026-08-24T13:55`, predating the last deploy. Two documents published after it were absent while returning `200 / index,follow`, and the CMS API returned both correctly, ruling out a CMS or CDN cause.

Fixed on two levels so neither is a single point of failure:

- `sitemap.ts` exports `revalidate = 3600`, the backstop for changes that bypass the hook.
- The publish and delete hooks add `/sitemap.xml` to the purge set for the nine collections that contribute `<loc>` entries, so a publish lands in seconds.

Collections that only affect a hard-coded static route are excluded, since publishing one cannot change the URL set: `webinars` and `case-studies` list at constants in the web sitemap, and `emailSignatures` is noindex throughout.

Verified with a production-CMS build: **539 URLs including both missing documents**, and the route table reports a 1h revalidate on `/sitemap.xml`.

**This fix cannot take effect until it deploys, which is the bug it fixes.**

## CMS reads are uncacheable at the edge

The CMS collection API sends no `Cache-Control`, so Cloudflare marks every response `DYNAMIC` and caches nothing. Every `apps/web` render reaches the droplet, including all ~531 during a production build. That droplet runs the CMS, Postgres and Meilisearch inside 1,967 MB, and saturating it is the documented cause of the 520/522/525 origin errors and the 9.2s and 16.4s crawl latencies recorded on 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18 (`14a17c94`).

`apps/cms/src/proxy.ts` marks a response cacheable only when the request is a GET, carries no `payload-token` cookie and no `Authorization` header, and targets one of thirteen allow-listed public content collections.

### Shipped inert, and the gate is load-bearing

`CMS_EDGE_CACHE_SMAXAGE` is unset, so **no response changes on merge**. `/api` is also the Payload admin's data path and Cloudflare's default cache key ignores cookies, so a stored anonymous response could be served to a signed-in editor and hide their drafts.

**Two things must happen, in order, before this does anything:**

1. Add the Cloudflare cache rule that bypasses cache when a `payload-token` cookie is present. The exact rule is in `apps/cms/.env.example`.
2. Only then set `CMS_EDGE_CACHE_SMAXAGE=300`.

## Verification companion

`docs/seo/2026-08-26-crawlstats-verification-companion.html`, published at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/fb64b6ad-b911-483c-a6be-eb39cd846ecd

Claim-by-claim check of the crawl audit against the source workbook and live production. Their arithmetic reconciles exactly, but four of their findings are refuted (the CSR claim, the JSON-LD inference, and both halves of the source-map action), and the central "worsened three months straight" trend is an artifact of calendar-month buckets straddling the migration.

## Notes

- Writing the proxy tests caught a parsing bug: `parseInt("3.5")` silently became `3`, so a typo in the deploy environment would have produced a wrong cache window without complaint. Parsing now rejects anything that is not a clean positive integer.
- The three security guards (credentials, allowlist, GET-only) were mutation-tested; each fails loudly when removed.
- The Apollo tracker already reached `main` via #254, so it is correctly absent from this diff.

### Description

Fix #561 

Allow resources with `consumer_credentials` that lack a `name` field.

Some older credentials created via the Admin API may lack a `name` field, but the ADC treats this as a required field, causing an internal error. Because it attempts to generate a hashed ID for a value that is undefined.

author: wmadden-electric
body:
This PR moves create-prisma off its emergency version pin and onto the current Prisma release line — CLI **8.0.0-rc.11**, Composer **0.15.0**, ORM **8.0.0-rc.8** — and updates the scaffold code that the new line requires. Without those code updates, a project scaffolded on the new versions fails its own typecheck before the user has written a line of code:

```
$ bunx tsc --noEmit
src/prisma/users.ts(8,97): error TS2339: Property 'take' does not exist on type 'Collection<Contract, "User", ...>'.
```

## Why we're pinned, and why we're moving

Version 0.9.4 pinned the whole stack to a snapshot — CLI rc.9, Composer 0.14.0, ORM rc.4 — because CLI rc.10 broke every scaffold (it dropped an `orm init` flag we passed and scaffolded schemas the pinned ORM rejected). The pin was the right hotfix, but it left new projects on a frozen, aging line.

Today the whole stack released in lockstep: ORM rc.8, Composer 0.15.0 (which exact-peer-pins ORM rc.8), and CLI rc.11 (which bundles Composer 0.15.0 and ORM rc.8). These versions form a chain of exact pins, so create-prisma has to move all of them together — a project whose installed ORM differs from the one bundled in the CLI it runs breaks at `contract emit`. That is why the diff moves five versions at once, plus `effect` to 4.0.0-rc.112 (Composer 0.15.0's own pin).

## What the move required

**1. Drop `--skip-skills`.** The ORM removed the flag along with what it controlled: `orm init` no longer installs agent skills at all. Skills setup lives in `prisma init`, which the scaffold already runs as a separate step — so the flag is simply deleted. (Bonus: rc.11's `prisma init` now writes the `postinstall: prisma skills sync || exit 0` hook itself, which our e2e suite always expected.)

**2. Teach the templates the current ORM API.** Two things changed under the scaffolded starter code:
- `.take(n)` was renamed to `.limit(n)` on collections.
- Timestamp columns now come back as ISO strings, not `Date` objects. The next/svelte/astro/nuxt/tanstack starter pages formatted them with `Date` methods (`user.createdAt.toISOString()`); they now treat the value as the string it is.

**3. Move the Deno path onto the same CLI as everyone else.** Deno scaffolds ran a separate package, `prisma-next` — and under Deno, a bare `npm:prisma-next` specifier resolves to the highest *non-prerelease* version. Every 8.x release is a prerelease, so Deno silently got the frozen 0.12.0 CLI, which cannot emit against today's ORM. Deno now runs the same pinned `prisma` CLI as every other package manager: one shared `orm init` invocation, a rendered `prisma.config.ts` (whose `prisma/config` import makes `prisma` a devDependency for Deno too), and current command spellings in the generated scripts.

**What deliberately stays:** the baseline-migration step from #65. Composer 0.15.0 deploys are replay-only — the pipeline replays committed migrations and never creates schema — so a scaffold without a committed baseline fails its very first deploy. The step that plans and commits `migrations/` at scaffold time is now what makes a new project's first deploy succeed.

## Verification

The full e2e suite runs against the published npm registry and passes **5/5**: the Composer-backed test provisions a local Prisma Postgres, replays the scaffolded baseline migration, boots the dev loop, and fetches the seeded users over HTTP; the Deno test emits and builds on the consolidated CLI. Typecheck, lint, build, and unit tests pass. A preview is published under the `pr69` dist-tag: `npm create prisma@pr69`.

## Alternatives considered

- **Float on `prisma@latest` instead of pinning.** Rejected: the rc line ships breaking changes between releases by policy, and floating is exactly what broke every scaffold when rc.10 landed. The pin comment in `dependencies.ts` now records the lockstep rule so the next bump moves everything together.
- **Keep Deno on `prisma-next` with a pinned version.** Rejected: the package is frozen (its repo is archived into prisma/prisma) and will only drift further from the ORM line.
- **Satisfy the Deno config import with an `@prisma/cli-engine` devDependency** (what `orm init`'s generated config imports). Rejected: that adds a second version pin that must track the CLI. Rendering our own config that imports `prisma/config` reuses the `prisma` pin we already carry and matches what every non-Deno scaffold does.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## Follow-up hardening

Deno 2.9 applies a 24-hour minimum dependency age by default. Because preview tags and coordinated Prisma RCs are exercised immediately after publication, the documented Deno invocation and create-prisma’s initial delegated resolution use Deno’s official `--minimum-dependency-age=0` control. This applies only while scaffolding; generated projects do not permanently disable Deno’s dependency-age policy.

The stale unit expectations are updated, the unused `prisma-next` command helper is removed, preview and release publishing now run unit tests before npm publication, and the Composer E2E uses a unique app name so repeated local runs cannot reuse a stale emulator database.

author: nekodas-neko
body:
Docs-only.

## What this prevents

Q-500 shipped `RECOVERY_INDEX_OPTIMAL_HOURS = 5` and left one follow-up: *"re-derive the anchor once ~15 BLE-era nights exist."* Read top-down — which is how a session picks work off the queue — that is an instruction to wait for data and then move a scoring constant. Both halves are stale:

- **The data arrived weeks ago.** `oura_daily_summary` holds **50 of 51** BLE-era nights (2026-07-07 → 2026-08-26) at mean **2.625 h**. The sample-size condition reads as the blocker and has not been one for a long time.
- **The refit was already run, and argued against.** Q-509 ran it at n = 42, landed on **3.31 h**, then said not to apply it: the anchor shrank **0.715×** while its input shrank **0.74×**, so an anchor moved to match would absorb a **multiplicative bias in the estimator** rather than correct a score. Its own words: *"Do NOT move `RECOVERY_INDEX_OPTIMAL_HOURS`."*

The next session to take Q-500 would have re-derived an anchor another entry had already told them not to apply. Both entries now say so.

This also matters because the owner approved recalibrating the readiness cluster and accepting that history moves. That approval does not extend to this constant — Q-509's finding is that the input changed for measurement reasons, not that the score is miscalibrated.

## Re-measured, and the finding is stronger than when filed

Eight more nights since Q-509's window moved the mean by **0.03 h** (2.657 at n = 42 → 2.625 at n = 50). The level shift is not a small-sample artefact and more data will not change the answer — worth stating, because "get more data" is exactly the reflex this entry pair invites.

The real work item is unchanged and is Q-509's: smooth the BLE HR series to Cloud-like noise *before* the argmin and re-measure the ratio. If it goes to ~1.0 the estimator is fine and the input needed conditioning.

## A mistake made getting here, recorded because it nearly shipped

`recovery_index_hours` exists on **two** tables. I counted it on `oura_daily_derived`, got **0 non-null across all 100 rows and the entire history**, and drew the confident conclusion that the estimator had never produced anything and Q-500's follow-up was permanently impossible. That was written down and one step from being filed as a finding.

Q-509's own `n = 42` contradicted it, which forced a re-check: the populated column is `oura_daily_summary.recovery_index_hours`; the derived one is a known always-null column.

Same shape as the `n_live_tup` error that got Q-528's predecessor retracted — **a number from the wrong source is not a weaker fact than a right one, it is a different claim entirely**, and it arrives with the same confidence. The caution now sits on Q-500 beside the follow-up, where someone about to measure this will read it.

## Verification

`pnpm check:rules` **Ran 59 of 59**; both edited files within their size baselines (no raise needed); production figures pulled live from `claude_ro`.

**Stated precisely:** `claude_ro` is row-scoped to one user, so every count here is **the owner's** rows. That is the right population — they are the only ring wearer — but it is not a claim about any other account.

author: calebjubal
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces native Windows support for Anchor while preserving the existing Linux and macOS behavior.

It covers the complete Windows workflow: CLI execution, file protection, lock-daemon communication, cross-platform tests, CI, release packaging, installation, and uninstallation.

## What changed

### Windows CLI support

- Added handling for Windows canonical and verbatim paths.
- Improved compatibility with `cmd.exe`.
- Updated Git repository inspection to use NUL-delimited output.
- Added support for filenames containing spaces, Unicode characters, and rename records.
- Added a helpful error when Git for Windows is unavailable or missing from `PATH`.
- Preserved the existing behavior for directories that are not Git repositories.

### Execroot support

- Added Windows-aware symbolic-link recreation.
- Falls back to copying link targets when Windows symlink privileges are unavailable.
- Added cycle detection to prevent recursive-copy loops.
- Normalized Windows path separators in benchmark and semantic-document checks.

### File protection

- Added cross-platform protection-state schema v2.
- Windows source files are protected using their read-only attribute.
- Original Windows file attributes are restored when protection is disabled.
- Added rollback handling for partial protection and controlled-write failures.
- Existing Unix permission-mode behavior remains unchanged.
- Legacy v1 protection state is migrated automatically on Unix and rejected safely on Windows.

Windows directories are intentionally not marked read-only because that attribute does not provide meaningful directory write protection on Windows.

### Lock daemon

- Added Windows IPC through per-user named pipes.
- Named pipes use an owner-only protected access control list.
- Preserved Unix socket behavior and mode `0600`.
- Preserved the existing protocol characteristics:
  - newline-delimited JSON
  - 500 ms client timeout
  - 1 MiB response limit
- Added portable daemon integration and transport tests.

### Tests

- Replaced shell-specific test setup with portable helpers for Unix shells and `cmd.exe`.
- Fixed platform-specific path assertions.
- Added Windows protection, transport, endpoint, Git parsing, and execroot coverage.
- Existing Linux and macOS test paths remain supported.

### CI and releases

- Added Linux, macOS, and Windows test/build jobs.
- Windows CI builds, tests, and smoke-tests both Anchor and the lock daemon.
- Windows releases now produce `anchor-windows-x64.zip`.
- The Windows archive contains:
  - `anchor.exe`
  - `anchor-lockd.exe`
  - `LICENSE`
- Added SHA-256 checksum sidecars for every release artifact.
- Updated the release action to `softprops/action-gh-release@v2`.

### Installation

Added non-admin PowerShell installation scripts:

- `docs/install.ps1`
- `docs/uninstall.ps1`

The installer:

- Downloads the Windows release archive.
- Verifies its SHA-256 checksum.
- Installs Anchor under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Anchor\bin`.
- Adds the installation directory to the user `PATH` without duplicate entries.
- Smoke-tests the installed executables.

The uninstaller removes the installed binaries and cleans the corresponding user `PATH` entry.

## Validation

Completed successfully on native Windows:

- `cargo test --all-targets`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo build --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`
- `go test ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- 17 Python benchmark tests
- GitHub Actions workflow lint
- PowerShell parser validation
- Release archive creation
- `anchor.exe` smoke test
- `anchor-lockd.exe` smoke test
- Rust client to Go named-pipe acquire/release test

## Release artifact

The generated Windows artifact is:

`anchor-windows-x64.zip`

author: gaspardmerten
body:
<!-- Closes #3860 -->

# Rationale for this change

`upsert` compares the matched rows one cell at a time. For every matched row, it takes a one-row slice of the source and of the target, then calls `.as_py()` on each non-key column until it finds a difference. That is one PyArrow call per row
and per column, so the cost grows with the size of the table and not with the amount of data that actually changed.

On a table with 200 columns, comparing 20k matched rows takes around 20 seconds before anything is written on a standard computer (mine), while it takes 0.15s if we push this comparison logic to PyArrow Compute (PC).


Two other things come out of that:

- PyArrow cannot compare struct columns, so I implemented nested comparison, still pushing to PC.
- The previous system was casting the source table to the target schema, which in itself is expensive. In addition, when some types such as `timestamp[us]` were not cast to `timestamp[us, UTC]` as PyArrow refuses, it reverted back to Python, which made every row reported as changed. This is a small thing we gain.

! Lists and maps have no fields to compare and still go to Python, a slice at a time so the objects of a whole column are never held at once.

The result is the same: two nulls still count as equal, a null and a value still count as a change, and rows whose non-key columns did not change are still skipped.

# Are these changes tested?

Yes, 10 tests in `tests/table/test_upsert.py`.

Eight cover the comparison itself: nulls, a struct that is null, a nested struct, a list column, a column whose type differs from the target, a cast PyArrow refuses, a source missing one of the target columns, and no match at all.

Two cover the change in the way rows are compared, which no assertion on the result can see, because both ways return the same rows. One counts the comparisons and checks there is one per column, whatever the number of rows. The other checks a struct never reaches the Python comparison, with the types the upsert path really produces (a scan reads a `string` as a `large_string`).

The existing `tests/table/test_upsert.py` and `tests/table` suites pass unchanged.

# Are there any user-facing changes?

No API or behaviour change. `get_rows_to_update` returns the same rows.

One error message changes. A source that does not have every column of the target was rejected by `Table.cast` with `Target schema's field names are not matching the table's field names`. It is now rejected by an explicit check, with a message naming the source. Without that check, the missing columns would never be compared and would
be written as null.

author: spokodev
body:
With `separateMilliseconds`, the sub-second component is rounded independently of the seconds, so a fractional value near the boundary rounds up to `1000` and is emitted as its own `ms` unit — an impossible combination:

```js
prettyMilliseconds(1999.5, {separateMilliseconds: true});      // '1s 1000ms'
prettyMilliseconds(59_999.5, {separateMilliseconds: true});    // '59s 1000ms'
prettyMilliseconds(86_399_999.5, {separateMilliseconds: true}); // '23h 59m 59s 1000ms'
```

The milliseconds unit only ranges 0–999, so `1000ms` should never appear. This is the same "rounding rolls a unit past its max" class as the seconds→`60s` issue (#38), which is handled for seconds by flooring (`floorDecimals`), but the separate-milliseconds component still used a bare `Math.round`.

## Fix

Cap the rounded component at `999` so it stays within range:

```js
const roundedMilliseconds = millisecondsAndBelow >= 1
  ? Math.min(Math.round(millisecondsAndBelow), 999)
  : Math.ceil(millisecondsAndBelow);
```

Output becomes `1s 999ms` / `23h 59m 59s 999ms` — valid unit combinations, consistent with how the seconds component is kept below 60. Non-boundary values are unaffected (`1337` → `1s 337ms`, `1500` → `1s 500ms`).

## Tests

Three regression cases added to the `separateMilliseconds` test; they produce the impossible `1000ms` output before the change and pass after. Full suite green.

author: devcoda25
body:
🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability:** URL validation (`isValidUrl`) and sanitization (`sanitizeUrl`) functions used `.includes('evzone.com')` for domain checking, which allowed SSRF/Open Redirects via domains like `attacker-evzone.com` or `evzone.com.attacker.com`. Additionally, `sanitizeUrl` failed to validate protocols, allowing XSS payloads such as `javascript:alert(1)//evzone.com`, which the URL constructor parses with an empty hostname and a `javascript:` protocol.
🎯 **Impact:** Attackers could bypass URL validation to execute XSS via injected `javascript:` payloads in sanitized URLs, or perform SSRF and Open Redirects by registering subdomains or domains containing the target string.
🔧 **Fix:** Refactored the `src/sanitizers/url.ts` utilities to enforce strict protocol allowlists (`['https:', 'http:']` for validation, and `['http:', 'https:', 'mailto:', 'tel:']` for sanitization). Replaced `.includes()` with strict hostname equality checks (`=== 'evzone.com'`) and suffix matching (`.endsWith('.evzone.com')`). Safe relative paths are now explicitly allowed, and whitespace characters are stripped before validation.
✅ **Verification:** Verified that XSS payloads and malicious domains return false/empty strings, while valid production domains and safe relative paths are handled correctly without regressions. Ran the global Vitest test suite (`pnpm test --run`) and verified specific linting success for the file. Note: Global linting errors in other files are pre-existing.

author: stryapinev-odsoft
body:
**Lane B reports 33 matching lines and gates nothing. The consequence is the part worth naming: a 34th line arriving among 33 existing ones is invisible — not because nobody looked, but because there is nothing there to see.**

That is the mechanism by which an internal service path reached this public SDK twice. The most recent was `c78533d` on #61, and lane B **did** count it — 33 → 34 — and nothing acted, because a number moving by one inside a standing report is not a signal.

The lane cannot be gated at zero today: 33 lines of real debt exist and failing on them breaks every build. So it is gated on **change**. The number may fall and may not rise.

## What it does, verified against the real class

Not toy fixtures — the actual leak, restored from the commit that shipped it.

| case | result |
|---|---|
| clean tree | exit 0 — *"held at 11 file(s), 33 occurrence(s)"* |
| `c78533d`'s actual leak restored | **exit 1** — `2 pkg/crash/capture.go` |
| a count falls, baseline not updated | **exit 1** — *"rerun with `--write-baseline`"* |
| leak **plus** a baseline rewritten to fit it | **exit 1** — *"the baseline was raised (1 → 2)"* |
| a file named `odd name.go`, or `foo\141.go` | named literally; neither borrows another file's count |
| the baseline replaced by a symlink | **exit 2** — the two sides would compare different objects |
| an unresolvable base ref | **exit 2** — a broken instrument is not a clean fleet |
| a target with no baseline, or an older format | skipped **and said so** |

## Six review rounds, and what they were actually about

Fourteen findings. Most were one mistake in different clothes — **treating "the instrument returned nothing" as "there is nothing"**: a path absent from the target baseline, `|| true` over a failed read, all-zeros `before` on a new ref, `git show` failing on an unreadable object, then `cat-file -e` failing on both absence and error.

Patching each instance did not converge. What converged was changing the **shape of the question**: `git ls-tree <ref> -- <path>` exits 0 whether or not the path exists and prints only when it does, so success-with-empty-output *is* absence and nonzero *is* failure. **A probe whose failure has two meanings cannot be interpreted, only replaced.**

Three findings were about **path serialization** — trailing whitespace, leading whitespace, backslash decoding through `awk -v`. Same lesson at a different altitude: every layer between the filesystem and the comparison can transform the string, so the lookup now has no layers. Read the row, cut at the first space, compare bytes.

## The new-ref arm: removed, then restored on evidence

I removed it arguing *"a branch is not a publication"*. **`ci.yml`'s own header, three lines above my edit, says otherwise** — it runs on every push because *"this repository is PUBLIC: a branch pushed here is readable the moment it lands"*, and a release was once cut off-main. Publication is not reaching `main`; it is being readable.

It is back, comparing against the **default branch** rather than the pushed commit's parent (which on a multi-commit branch push is itself newly published). Residual stated rather than hidden: a branch cut from an older `main` can false-alarm after `main` pays debt — an obvious remedy, and the cheaper error.

## What this does not catch

Counts are **per file**, so removing one matching line and adding another in the **same file** nets to zero and passes. Identity pinning would close that at the price of failing every reword of a grandfathered line — the swap is deliberate and visible in a diff; the reword is an accident that would train people to edit the baseline. **The rarer hole is traded for the commoner false alarm, on purpose.**

The full zero-debt state — empty tally *and* comments-only baseline — is fixed by construction and **not reproducible** in a tree that still carries 33 occurrences. Not claimed as tested.

## Self-test

Two fixture assertions pin the per-file tally, floor **15 → 17**, and both were confirmed to bite: emptying the tally exits 2 rather than reporting "held" over nothing.

*(Body rewritten before merge. It described the design as it stood at round one — one fetch arm, a `cat-file` probe, two commits — none of which is what merges here.)*

## Follow-up

`shardpilot-defold` carries the same script and reports **14 file(s), 80 matching line(s)**: same change, separate PR. And a per-refusal control harness is owed as its own unit — two of the last four findings were checks that were correct two rounds earlier and were lost in a restructure.

author: lars010101
body:
## Summary

Four issues identified by code review and fixed:

### 1. apiKey dropped at computeCoverage boundary (confirmed bug)

`loadProviderConfig()` returns `{ providerName, apiKey }`, but `computeCoverage` had no `apiKey` parameter in its signature. Two callers (`coverageAction` in fx.js, `scanCompany` in fx-scanner.js) destructured `apiKey` then never passed it. For OXR (the only shipped provider requiring a key), `fetchRange` threw `'Open Exchange Rates requires an App ID'` → `computeCoverage` caught it and returned `{status:'na'}` → the Periods grid showed `—` forever, and the scanner silently skipped OXR companies every 6h indefinitely.

**Fix:** Added `apiKey` parameter to `computeCoverage`, threaded through to `getPublicationDaysWithRows`. Both callers now pass it.

### 2. §4b fire-and-forget became synchronous await (spec drift)

`posting_rules.attr.save` awaited `scanCompany` synchronously, blocking the save response. For ECB that's one HTTP call per period; for OXR, one per day per period — potentially minutes.

**Fix:** Restored fire-and-forget (`.catch` only, no `await`); response returns `{saved: true, key}` immediately per spec §4b.

### 3. fx.provider.save bypassed §4b automation trigger (drift)

The legacy `fx.provider.save` action writes provider config directly but never triggered `scanCompany`. Any API/agent caller switching to a real provider via this path silently skipped the immediate scan.

**Fix:** Added fire-and-forget `scanCompany` trigger when `provider !== 'manual'`.

### 4. Specs said Company tab, code uses Posting Rules tab (spec drift)

Both `fx-automation-spec.md §1` and `settings-ux-spec.md §7 item 1` (marked ✅ SHIPPED) claimed Multi-Currency/FX Provider/FX API Key live on the Company tab via `company.attr.*`. The actual code places them on a Posting Rules tab via `posting_rules.attr.*`.

**Fix:** Updated both specs to rev. 4 (2026-08-26) reflecting the Posting Rules tab placement.

- [x] All 209 API tests pass
- [x] FX revaluation tests pass
- [x] FX exposed-currencies tests pass

Onward had **no container image and no CI/CD** — deployment was manual. This adds a single portable Docker image, built and published automatically by GitHub Actions to GHCR.

Because Vite inlines `VITE_API_URL` into the bundle at build time, we use **runtime env injection** so the image is built once and the backend URL is supplied per-environment at deploy time (`docker run -e VITE_API_URL=…` / K8s / compose).

- Multi-stage `Dockerfile` (`node:22-alpine` build → `nginx:1.27-alpine` runtime)

- `docker/entrypoint.sh` + `docker/env.template.js` — regenerate `window.__ENV__` from `$VITE_API_URL` at container start (auto-run via nginx's `/docker-entrypoint.d/`)

**CI/CD** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

1. Human-vs-AI: check show-black and/or show-white, start, close, reopen the same dialog in-session. Boxes reset to unchecked.
2. Engine-vs-engine: check “从 SGF 开始”, quit, restart, reopen. Unchecked.
3. Engine-vs-engine: pick different black and white engines, quit, restart, reopen. Picks not restored.

Sibling settings in those dialogs already persist via `uiConfig`.

## Cause
`NewGameDialog` / `NewAnaGameDialog` always construct show-black/white as unchecked and only sync toolbar/menu on apply. `chkEngineSgfStart` is a runtime field; the `uiConfig.optBoolean("engine-sgf-start", true)` read is commented. Black/white engine combos store toolbar indexes only; `EngineManager` resets them to 0 after rebuild.

## Fix
- Write/read the three settings in `uiConfig`, like the siblings.
- Missing keys stay unchecked / false. Do not revive the commented `engine-sgf-start` default `true`.
- Persist engine identity (command+name), not ComboBox index. Missing saved engine falls back safely.
- Human-vs-AI engine still follows the foreground engine.
- SGF-start vs continue-from-position mutex unchanged.

## Verification
Headless: `ConfigNewGameDialogSettingsTest`, `EnginePkIdentityTest`, `NewEngineGameDialogHandicapApplyTest` (22 tests). Merge gate is existing Windows/Linux `mvn verify`.

Windows desktop on `4268836d`, `D:\dev\weiqi\lizzieyzy-next\target\lizzie-yzy2.5.3-shaded.jar`, work dir `C:\Users\Public\Documents\LizzieYzyNext`:
1. Human-vs-AI show-black / show-white: first open unchecked; after start, same-session reopen still checked. After clean quit and restart, both still checked. `new-game-show-black` / `new-game-show-white` are `true`.
2. Engine-vs-engine SGF-start (加载开局SGF): first open unchecked; same-session reopen and restart both stay checked. `engine-sgf-start` is `true`.
3. Engine-vs-engine black/white: after quit and restart, dialog restored black `zen7` and white `bb18`. `engine-pk-black-name` / `engine-pk-white-name` match those identities.

4 PASS. Deleted-engine fallback was not hand-tested; covered by `EnginePkIdentityTest`.

Fixes #336

author: wtatarski
body:
`SSL_get_peer_certificate()` returns a certificate whose reference count has been
incremented, so the caller owns that reference and must release it with `X509_free()`.
On OpenSSL 3.x the name is a compatibility macro for `SSL_get1_peer_certificate()`,
which has the same owning semantics.

81a9efe96db6 ("pmproxy: enforce -Q (CERT_REQD) for REST API connections") called it
inline in the NULL test and discarded the result:

```c
	if (!client->stream.secure ||
	    !client->secure.ssl ||
	    SSL_get_peer_certificate(client->secure.ssl) == NULL) {
	    client->u.http.parser.status_code = HTTP_STATUS_FORBIDDEN;
	}
```

Because of the short-circuit order the reference is only taken when the connection is
TLS and an SSL object exists, and it is leaked precisely when a certificate **is**
present — that is, on the path where the request is allowed through. The rejection paths
do not leak. `on_headers_complete()` runs once per request, so a `pmproxy` started with
`-Q` accumulates one `X509` per authenticated REST request for the lifetime of the
daemon.

This only affects deployments that have opted into client-certificate enforcement; `-Q`
is not enabled by the shipped `pmproxy.conf`. It is a reliability defect rather than a
security issue, since reaching it requires a client certificate that already passed
validation.

The fix captures the reference and frees it, leaving the accept/reject logic unchanged.
`SSL_get0_peer_certificate()` would avoid taking a reference at all, but it is not
available on the older OpenSSL versions pcp still supports, so `X509_free()` is the
portable form.

Found while backporting 81a9efe96db6 to pcp 6.3.7 and 6.0.1 (OpenSSL 3.2.2). Verified
against current `main` (55365f2e): the block is unchanged there, this commit introduces
the only call to `SSL_get_peer_certificate()` under `src/`, and there is no other
`X509_free()` in the tree — so nothing else was releasing it.

## Related Issues

Fixes #2693
