body: ## The gate was asking its own questions, not yours Two separate faults, and both looked exactly like the feature working. **1. The gate drew synchronously.** The first chamber is cleared long before four Firebase CDN modules have imported, the sign-in has resolved, the `zhConfig/admin` pointer has been read and the whole bank has been fetched — so `jqBank()` was empty and every question came out of the built-in set. On a school connection that is several gates in a row. `BANK.ready` is now the promise the gate waits on (`jqWaitForBank`), behind a *"正在取来老师的题目…"* card and bounded by `JQ_BANK_WAIT` so a gate can never fail to open. Every terminal state in the module settles that promise — a branch that announces and does not `done()` would leave every gate for the rest of the run waiting the full timeout, which the harness now pins. **2. The allowlist refused an `explanation` block** — and the portal's own AI writes one onto very nearly every question it builds. `buildOpenBody` hides an explanation and a widget until the student has answered, and `renderImportedBlockStudent` returns `''` for an answer key and a page break, so `IGNORED_BLOCKS` is now the portal's *own* "not shown inside the question" set. Also widened, all of it still short: **one picture is carried** (an image block, or an `` pasted into the wording — several is a figure study and is refused), stem cap 320 characters, option cap 90. 阅读理解, every cloze, 词语搭配 and the rest still fall out without being named. A refusal now returns a **reason** (`{no: 'clozemcq'}`), the load tallies them to the console, and the card's fallback chip says *which* fallback — 未登录 and 题库里没有短题 are very different things to tell a teacher. Signed out, the card **offers to sign in** rather than quietly asking its own questions; refusing is remembered for the run, not asked at every one of a hundred gates. ## 🏆 The Journey leaderboard (西游榜) Its own page (🏆 in the sidebar), one row per student at `zhJourneyBoard`, written by the gate and read by the portal. **Top 3 each month win a $10 voucher.** - **It ranks on the questions, never on how far the run got.** A chapter number is climbed by replaying the easy chapters, and there is money on this board. `bestChapter` is shown because players care about it; it decides nothing. - **correct × accuracy², the family's own formula** — so 900 questions at 35% cannot beat 400 at 88%. `jbScore` is the ONE place a row becomes a number. It clamps `correct` **down** to `answered`; clamping the other way handed a row claiming five right out of nothing answered a perfect score, and every student can write their own row. - **Only bank questions are published.** The built-in set is two dozen questions met over and over — counting them would turn a board meant to measure work into one that measures how long a tab was left open. - **Ranking and paying are different questions.** A tiny perfect run really can lead the board — that is the formula — and `JB_MIN_QUESTIONS` is why it is not paid for it. An ineligible row is still shown; it is a real student. - **The voucher badge is on the month board only.** The first draft badged the all-time top three, offering the voucher to the wrong people on a page that read perfectly. The new harness caught it. - The month key is **Singapore time**, and the game carries its own copy because it is a separate page — the harness checks the two against each other. - Retired accounts are off the board, display names are escaped, ties break on accuracy → questions → chapter. ## Checks - `node tools/journey-board-tests.mjs` — **31 passed** (new; found the clamp bug and the all-time badge bug) - `node tools/journey-quiz-tests.mjs` — **65 passed** (was 45) - Every other harness in `tools/` — still green, `bank-isolation-tests.mjs` included - Driven in a real browser: the gate holds for a loading bank and shows no options while it waits, then serves the bank question with its picture; the signed-out card offers sign-in; a round publishes exactly once with the chapter; every reward type, heal and tier still behave. New collection `zhJourneyBoard` added to `firestore.rules` — **deploy the rules alongside the other apps' blocks, never replacing them.** --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01KGbtLJTSaUMCx6GxP4h986)_

author: danielfullsite
body:
## El hallazgo

**No faltaba código.** `pos-manager-auth.ts` estaba **completo y con tests** — PBKDF2, salt por dispositivo, multi-credencial, revocación, bitácora — y **no lo importaba nadie**. Cero consumidores en toda la app.

El login usaba en su lugar un caché simple inline en `layout.tsx` que guarda **un** objeto y se sobrescribe en cada login.

> Un módulo perfecto y desconectado se ve, en producción, exactamente igual que uno que no existe.

### Las dos consecuencias, verificadas en `main`

**1. Offline sólo podía entrar la última persona que se logueó con red.** En una terminal que comparten meseros, cajero y gerente, falla el primer turno. Y peor: si otro tecleaba su PIN, se contaba **intento fallido** — a los 3, terminal bloqueada.

**2. `pos_staff_cache` expira a las 8 h del último login online.** Un restaurante que cierra a la 1am y abre a la 1pm son **12 h**: nadie entra.

## El fix — conectar lo que ya existía, no construir nada

| Dónde | Qué |
|---|---|
| Login **online** | Además de lo de siempre, provisiona la credencial en el almacén multi. Fire-and-forget con `catch`: si falla, **el camino validado en campo el 24-ago sigue idéntico** |
| Login **offline** | Si el PIN no coincide con el del caché simple ya **no** se falla ahí — puede ser de otro empleado. Cae al almacén multi. El PIN correcto de la persona cacheada entra por el mismo camino de antes, sin cambios |
| TTL | 8 h → **16 h** por defecto, configurable (`NEXT_PUBLIC_POS_OFFLINE_CREDENTIAL_TTL_HOURS`) |

## El compromiso, escrito en el código y no escondido

Alargar el TTL alarga también la ventana en la que la credencial de alguien **dado de baja** sirve en esa terminal y sin red. Se mitiga con `disabled` (revocación honrada de inmediato al reconectar) y con la bitácora de `pos_offline_auth_log`. Es el mismo compromiso que hace el POS legado.

Se eligió así porque **no poder abrir es peor que cualquier otro modo de falla**. Si prefieres apretarlo, es una variable de entorno.

## Sobre los tests de Codex

Dos fallaban porque codificaban *"9 horas > 8h TTL"*. Es **contrato cambiado, no regresión**. Se les quitó la dependencia del número (72 h, pasado de cualquier TTL razonable) **conservando su intención**: que la expiración funcione.

## Pruebas — 30 en total (13 de Codex conservados + 17 nuevos)

**Ciclo cierre-apertura:** a las 12 h el PIN **sigue** entrando · a las 72 h no · la revocación gana sobre el TTL aunque la credencial esté fresca.

**Multi-persona:** dos empleados distintos entran · cada quien conserva **su** rol (el mesero no hereda permisos del gerente) · un PIN de nadie se rechaza · re-loguearse actualiza la propia credencial **sin borrar las demás**.

**Cableado — 10 guardas:** que el import siga ahí, que se provisione **después** de que el servidor confirmó el PIN, que el salto al almacén exista y `verifyPinOffline` se consulte después, que provisionar vaya con `catch`, y que el TTL cubra 12 h.

**Prueba mutante:** al regresar el TTL a 8 h, el caso de las 12 h se pone rojo.

## Verificación

| Comando | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `vitest run` | **89 archivos, 2,303 pruebas, 0 fallas** |
| `tsc --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| `eslint` | 34 problemas — **idéntico a la baseline** de `origin/main` |

## Pendiente

⚠️ **Validación física.** Terminal apagada toda la noche, encender sin WAN, y que **dos empleados distintos** entren con su PIN. Eso no lo puede hacer nadie desde código.

## Rollback

`git revert`. El almacén multi queda huérfano otra vez (como estaba), y el caché simple sigue funcionando: no hay estado que limpiar.

author: eandreeva-twr
body:
## The failure

A colleague generated a flow through the skill, hand-edited it in the Flow Builder, then asked Claude for more changes — and the manual edits were gone.

`--expected-updated-at` cannot catch this. It is a lock on **timing**: it fails a write racing an edit that landed *after* your fetch. These edits landed *before* it. Fetch the config, then write a document that was never based on it — regenerated from the first run's build script, or patched from a leftover `draft.json` — and the token is current, no 409 is raised, and `config update` replaces the flow.

Nothing in the skill guarded the *content* of a write. The whole phase-5 gate rested on the agent narrating its own intent, so an agent that believes it made a copy tweak reports a copy tweak while writing a whole document.

## The change

- **`references/diff-config.py`** (new, ships, stdlib) — a fact-level structural diff. Blind to key order *inside* an object and addressed by identity *across* a collection, so a builder save reads as silent; per-locale, so a dropped translation is a removal rather than a change. Two uses: `backup → draft` before a write (what you destroy) and `stale-local → live` on a follow-up (the human's edits, computed rather than guessed).
- **Phase 5** computes `REMOVES` before the approval ask, anchored on the phase-2 backup rather than the working file — some runs edit `flow.working.json` in place, which would compare a file with itself and pass silently. The ask carries the list; the same path passed twice is refused with exit 2 rather than reported clean.
- **Phase 2** — patch what you fetched; diff and quarantine any stale local copy.
- **Safety** — "the lock is not a merge", in one paragraph.
- **`references/merge.md`** (new) owns the evidence, so the entry point stays lean.
- **Bycatch, separate commit:** `shoot.sh` reported Chrome's error page as a successful render and exited 0.

## Verification

`tests/test-diff-config.py`, 17 cases, negative-tested per mechanism — dropping `sort_keys` reddens only the key-order case, indexing collections only the icons case, dropping the same-path guard only that one.

The suite caught a wrong claim in my first draft: the v9→v10 fill migration is **not** invisible to the diff (29 fills object→array come back as 25 changed elements). Documented as a signature to recognise, not softened into a promise of silence.

## Two GREEN rounds, and both were null on the decisive row

12 agents, arms differing only in these files, offline CLI shim, scorers written and self-tested before dispatch.

| | round 1 | round 2 |
|---|---|---|
| scenario | 1 screen, one-string change | 5 screens, 6 spread edits, task pointing at the generator's own content file |
| control R1 | 3/3 pass | 3/3 pass |
| treatment R1 | 3/3 pass | 3/3 pass |

**Zero destructive writes in either arm.** No agent re-ran the generator, even in round 2 where the task pointed straight at `benefits.json`, re-running was one command, and I verified beforehand that doing so produces a *valid* six-row config passing every local gate.

Three separations were real, none an outcome: treatment ran 4/7/6 logged diffs where **0 of 3 control patch scripts hash or canonicalise anything** (each reinvented an ad-hoc comparison); 3/3 treatment quarantined the stale write bases vs 0/3 control; 3/3 treatment explained to the user why the lock had not protected them vs 0/3.

Per the pre-registered conclusion, the wording was **trimmed rather than kept for reassurance**: `SKILL.md` is +328 words over `main`, holding only what the measurements support.

## What this PR does not claim

**It does not claim to prevent the failure that prompted it.** Two rounds could not reproduce that loss with a skill-following agent, and the skill *was* loaded in the original incident — so the mechanism is still unexplained. The untested hypothesis: both rounds forced a **fresh session finding files on disk**, whereas the original may have been the *same conversation continuing*, where the agent already holds the config it generated in context and patches that — never re-fetching, so there is no stale file to notice and no diff to run. If that is the path, the guard that matters is re-fetching on a continued session, which neither round touched.

Reviewer question: is that worth a third round before merge, or does this land as a net-positive tool plus gate while the reproduction stays open?

## Method notes worth keeping

- **An agent's report is not an artifact.** One round-1 run reported deleting stale files that still existed; I had drafted a rubric row from the reports and caught it only by hashing.
- **A rubric row that punishes restraint is a broken row.** Round 2's stale-artifact row failed 5/6 for correctly leaving the user's own files alone.

author: salmanmuddhoo
body:
## What this changes

S-201 to S-204 were delivered as a service layer and an API, with no way for an administrator to use either. The stories are written from the administrator's point of view — *"I need to create roles and grant permissions"* — so an API they cannot reach is not the story delivered. Signing in as a System Administrator showed no Administration menu at all.

- **Two server-rendered pages**, `/admin/roles` and `/admin/users`. Forms rather than a client-side fetch of our own API: they work without JavaScript, authorisation stays in one place (the middleware, which has already run), and the page cannot drift from the API.
- **Navigation is built from the caller's resolved permissions**, so the Administration group appears only for those holding `role.view` or `user.view`, and disappears entirely when neither is held.
- **`ROUTE_PERMISSIONS` now declares the two routes.** Until now the map was empty, so both pages would have fallen through the undeclared-route exemption rather than through their own permission.

Two defects found while verifying the pages against a running server:

- **Every Deactivate, Reactivate and Delete role button saved the form instead of doing what it said.** The forms carried a hidden `intent` field *and* named submit buttons, so the request held two `intent` values and `form.get()` returned the first — clicking Deactivate silently rewrote the user's roles. The intent now comes only from the button that was clicked. Confirmed by replaying the old request shape: it answers "Roles updated." and leaves the account active.
- **`listUsers()` was unbounded.** Against the 3,002 rows left by the jobs spike, `/admin/users` rendered a 4.97 MB document. It is now capped at 100, searchable by name or email, and says how many it left out — 228 KB for the same data. The search uses `strpos`, not `LIKE`, so a `%` typed into the box is a character rather than a wildcard. The `GET /api/v1/admin/users` response changes shape to `{ users, total, truncated }` and gains a `q` query parameter; `EndpointDescriptor` gained a `query` field so the generator can emit it.

## Related

M2, Feature 2.1 (S-201 → S-204). FRD 6.1.

## Checks

- [x] Type-check and production build pass locally (`pnpm build`)
- [x] Formatting applied (`pnpm format:fix`)
- [x] No credentials, tokens or connection strings added to the repository
- [x] Permissions enforced for any new route or API endpoint
- [x] Audit trail written for any change to member, document, approval or payment data
- [x] Documentation updated where behaviour changed — `docs/openapi.json` regenerated (6 endpoints, `openapi:check` clean)

131 tests pass; `pnpm audit --prod` reports no known vulnerabilities.

## Security considerations

This touches authentication and authorisation directly, so it is worth looking at closely:

- **Deny by default still holds.** Verified against a running server: a signed-in user holding no roles gets a 302 to `/denied` for both pages and sees no Administration group on the dashboard.
- **The route permission is `*.view`; the mutating forms check `*.manage` separately**, so someone who can see a page still cannot necessarily change it — the POST branch refuses before doing any work.
- **CSRF**: the session cookie is `SameSite=Lax`, which browsers do not send on a cross-site POST, and Astro's origin check rejected a POST without a matching `Origin` during testing. That is what stands in for a token here.
- **Self-deactivation is blocked**, so an administrator cannot end their own session or leave nobody able to administer the system.
- The deactivate path was verified to write a `user.deactivated` row to the append-only `audit_event` table.

author: milbia
body:
Closes #198

Część przeglądu wydajności backendu (#192).

## Problem

`suchar_overflow/templates/users/user_detail.html` renderował sekcję odznak
bezpośrednio z surowego managera `object.user_achievements`:

- `{% if object.user_achievements.exists %}` — 1 zapytanie,
- `{% for user_ach in object.user_achievements.all %}` — 2. zapytanie do tej
  samej relacji,
- `user_ach.achievement.icon_content` / `.name` / `.description` w pętli — FK
  nie było `select_related`, więc każda odznaka dokładała własne
  `SELECT ... FROM achievements_achievement WHERE id = ...`.

Łącznie `2 + N` zapytań na sekcję odznak. Potwierdzone empirycznie
`CaptureQueriesContext` przed poprawką: 5 zapytań dotykających tabel osiągnięć
przy 2 odznakach → 8 przy 5 odznakach. Rozbicie tych 5: 1 z context procesora
`achievements_bell` (stała baza, dotyczy zalogowanego widza, nie właściciela
profilu) + 1 `exists` + 1 `all` + 2 dociągnięcia FK, po jednym na odznakę.

## Rozwiązanie

`UserDetailView._build_context` materializuje odznaki raz, z dołączonym
`Achievement`:

```python
context["user_achievements"] = list(
    user.user_achievements.select_related("achievement").order_by("-awarded_at"),
)
```

Szablon iteruje po gotowej liście z kontekstu; warunek `{% if user_achievements %}`
korzysta z prawdziwościowej wartości listy, więc nie kosztuje osobnego zapytania.
Po poprawce sekcja odznak to dokładnie 1 zapytanie, niezależnie od ich liczby.

**`order_by("-awarded_at")` (dołożone po review):** wcześniejsze `.all()` nie
miało jawnego sortowania, ale zapytanie zmieniło kształt na JOIN — PostgreSQL
może więc zwracać wiersze w innej kolejności niż dotąd, a nawet między kolejnymi
odsłonami strony, co wyglądałoby jak „przetasowywanie się" odznak. Jawne
sortowanie newest-first domyka to i jest spójne z context procesorem
`achievements_bell`, który sortuje tak samo.

## Testy

Nowe w `suchar_overflow/users/tests/test_views_extra.py` (testy synchroniczne —
`_build_context` biegnie przez `sync_to_async`, więc `CaptureQueriesContext`
widzi zapytania tylko pod klientem synchronicznym):

- `test_build_context_fetches_badges_in_one_query` — mierzy `_build_context`
  bezpośrednio, poza pełnym requestem, więc licznik nie jest zaciemniony przez
  context procesor ani sesję: dokładnie 1 zapytanie o osiągnięcia przy 3
  odznakach. To wprost kryterium akceptacji issue. Red→green zweryfikowane:
  bez poprawki `assert 0 == 1` (przed zmianą widok nie pobierał odznak w ogóle
  — robił to dopiero szablon, po N+1 zapytań).
- `test_profile_badges_query_count_does_not_grow_with_badge_count` — pełny
  request na ten sam profil przy 2 i przy 5 odznakach; liczba zapytań musi być
  równa. Dodatkowa asercja na liczbę wyrenderowanych `achievement-container`
  (2 i 5) zabezpiecza przed pustym przejściem testu, gdyby sekcja przestała się
  renderować. Red→green zweryfikowane: bez poprawki
  `5 (2 odznaki) -> 8 (5 odznak)`.
- `test_profile_without_badges_renders_empty_state` — regresja pustego stanu
  (asercje na markup i kontekst, nie na tłumaczony tekst).
- `test_build_context_orders_badges_newest_first` — pilnuje kolejności
  `-awarded_at` po dołożeniu `order_by` (patrz wyżej).

## Rebase

Zrebase'owane na `main` po zmergowaniu #222/#223/#224. Dwa konflikty importów
w `test_views_extra.py` (`from django.core.cache import cache` z #202-owej gałęzi
kontra `connection`/`CaptureQueriesContext`; duplikat importu `UserDetailView`,
który #222 dodał niezależnie) — rozwiązane przez zachowanie obu stron.
`views.py` i szablon zmergowały się automatycznie.

## Weryfikacja (po rebase)

- `just test` — 361 passed, 31 deselected
- `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --all-files` — dwukrotnie, wszystko zielone
- `python -m mypy .` w kontenerze — `Success: no issues found in 138 source files`
- `just coverage` — TOTAL 93% (gate: 90%)
- Brak zmian w modelach → `makemigrations --check` nie dotyczy

author: marknuega
body:
`19A` is the fist mic, and `Hand-MicroLoudSpeaker` is what somebody called it before the list settled — a **description of the part rather than a spelling of its name**. No folding brings the two together (`HANDMICROLOUDSPEAKER` and `FISTMIC` share no key), so it has to be said outright. It's now an **alias** in `rename-fist-mic.js`:

```
Fistmic                ->  Fist Mic
Fistmic 3D             ->  Fist Mic 3D
Hand-MicroLoudSpeaker  ->  Fist Mic     (the same part, another name)
```

**An alias moves records only.** The option lists and the code map keep answering with their own names, because *"which part is this name"* and *"what is code 19 called"* are two different questions and only the first has an alias for an answer:

- renaming an option row `HAND MICRO LOUD SPEAKER` to `Fist Mic` would leave **two rows of that name**, one coded and one not, and a fault could then be written by either
- renaming a code-map entry could rename a code that legitimately holds a similar name — **`28` is the Micro-Loud Speaker, and it is not this one**

Matched on the whole folded name, never on part of it, for the same reason: a substring rule would have swallowed `28` on sight. Verified: `Micro-Loud Speaker` is untouched, while `HAND MICRO LOUD SPEAKER` and `Hand Micro Loud Speaker` both land on `Fist Mic`.

**The claim is checked before anything moves**, as everywhere else in this script. An alias changes which issue type a fault answers to, so it can change its code: losing one refuses to write, gaining one — which is what happens here, moving a fault that claimed nothing onto `19A` — is reported and done.

Not device-scoped: the dry run names every device it would touch, so if `Hand-MicroLoudSpeaker` means something else on a radio other than the TH1n, that shows up before anything is written.

```
cd server && node --env-file=.env scripts/rename-fist-mic.js          # dry run
cd server && node --env-file=.env scripts/rename-fist-mic.js --apply  # write
```

**Tests**: server 204/204 pass, prettier clean. Script-only change.

author: alexandermakarov
body:
## Why

The review of #185 settled two points: a shorter spec is still a spec (small changes should leave no spec-tree artifacts at all), and core `commands/*.md` is the wrong layer for a lighter path. The follow-up proposal ([#185 comment](https://github.com/provectus/awos/pull/185#issuecomment-5409654230)) moved the mechanism to the flow layer, where `/awos:flow` already generates a lighter bug-fix command with different middle stages. This PR implements that proposal; #185 is superseded and will be closed.

## What

- **`implement-feature-template.md`** gains a `small-triage` stage between `resume-detection` and `workspace`. With no small-signal it is a no-op — the full spec chain is the default. On a small-signal (the ticket or prompt reads as a tweak) it dispatches a light read-only `Explore` pass and confirms the size with the user via `AskUserQuestion`, citing the evidence in the options ("small — the text appears in 1 template" vs "standard — that color is a theme token used by 14 components"). The signal only triggers the check; the evidence routes. The safe default is **standard**: a skipped or unanswered confirmation, and every unattended run (`AWOS_UNATTENDED`), takes the full chain.
- **On a confirmed Small verdict** the change is delivered with zero spec-tree artifacts: the specs and commit-specs stages are skipped (no `context/spec/` directory — git history and the change request are the record), implementation is delegated directly to the matching specialist, verification is scoped (project suite + a real render via the sanctioned verification path), and the review, CI, merge, and close stages run unchanged. The verdict and its citing evidence are recorded in the change-request description. Small-path variants are marked inline in the affected stages.
- **`delivery-flow-template.md`** gains a `## Small-Change Path` policy section (enabled by default, what counts as small, the safe default); **`flow.md`** settles the policy without adding an interview question — the default is stated in the Step 4 confirmation summary so the user can object — and bumps the generator version to `2.5.0` (plugin manifest and marketplace bumped to match).
- **Layer-1 lint pin** for the new contract (marker presence and position, evidence-based confirmation, no-spec-artifacts language, template section fields, flow.md policy).
- **README** "when to skip the cycle" note updated to mention the generated triage.

Core `commands/*.md` are untouched — a project without a generated flow command keeps today's behavior everywhere.

## Testing

- `npm run test:lint` — 152/152 pass (151 baseline + the new pin).
- Companion awos-qa PR provectus/awos-qa#48 (branch rewritten): repo unit tests 100/100, and one live unattended E2E run of the new `flow-generates-small-triage` scenario against this branch's plugin — a real `/awos:flow` run generated `/implement-feature` and all 11 contract checks passed (stage position, evidence routing, safe default, zero `context/spec/` on Small, delivery guarantees kept, decision-record section).

author: azmartone67
body:
## The outage

`cron-heartbeat.yml` runs every 5 minutes and has **failed every run since 07:54:22Z** today. Last success **07:33:53Z**.

```
curl: (2) no URL specified
/home/runner/work/_temp/….sh: line 18: -H: command not found
::warning::heartbeat attempt 1 returned 000 — retrying in 15s     (×3)
::error::Cron heartbeat SUSTAINED failure (000) across 3 attempts —
         backend outage; 38 master-ticks + warmers are not running
```

## The cause

be#3203 merged at **07:34:48Z** — the only commit that has ever touched this file inside that window — and placed a six-line comment BETWEEN the `curl … \` line and its `-H` argument:

```bash
BODY=$(curl -sS -X POST \
  # r-selftraffic-ua (2026-08-26): was GH-Actions-CronHeartbeat/1.0, which
  … five more comment lines …
  -H "User-Agent: dchub-cron-heartbeat/1.0" \
```

★★★ **A `#` comment cannot live inside a backslash continuation.** The trailing `\` escapes the *newline*, joining that line to the comment — so `#` swallows the rest of the command. `curl` ran with no URL; the following `-H …` lines were parsed as separate commands.

The comment moves above the command. Nothing else changes: the UA rename #3203 intended is preserved and now actually reaches curl.

## This was not a cosmetic red

The endpoint is the only driver for **38 master-tick dispatches** in `routes/cron_heartbeat.py` plus the grid warmer and brain warming.

And the workflow's own error text is wrong in a way worth naming. It blamed a *"backend outage"*. Measured through the same window, the backend was fine:

- **0 × 5xx** across 500 sampled requests (Railway HTTP observability)
- the `deals` crawler ran clean at 09:11Z
- `/api/v1/admin/fcc-fiber/status` returned 200

`STATUS=000` means curl never made a request at all. **A broken CALLER reporting itself as a broken CALLEE** — the same family as the false-REDs in c34de208.

## Verified behaviourally, not by inspection

The `run:` block is lifted straight out of the YAML, its production URL swapped for a local HTTP server, and executed under `bash -e` exactly as the runner does:

```
FIXED  → exit 0   HTTP_STATUS=200   "✅ heartbeat ok (200) on attempt 1"

BROKEN → exit 1   curl: (2) no URL specified
                  line 35: -H: command not found
                  ::warning::heartbeat attempt 1 returned 000 — retrying in 15s  (×3)
                  ::error::Cron heartbeat SUSTAINED failure (000) across 3 attempts …
```

The BROKEN column re-introduces the defect into this same file and reproduces the production log exactly — both curl errors, the `000`, and the false outage message.

## Guard

`tests/test_workflow_continuation_comment.py`, 5 tests. Scans every `run:` block in every workflow for a continuation line followed by a comment. **Heredoc bodies are exempt** — inside `<<EOF` a `#` is data, and a false positive there would push someone to "fix" correct code.

**Zero tolerance rather than a ratchet, and that is measured:** across **168 workflow files / 425 run steps** there was exactly **one** offender, and it was this outage. Contrast `test_workflow_curl_guard.py`, which had to freeze 153 steps of real debt because 81 of 125 workflows carried its pattern. There is no debt to freeze here.

That guard also could not have caught this: it polices calls whose *failure is invisible*, and cron-heartbeat captures `%{http_code}` correctly. This is shell syntax, not error handling.

Registered in `tests/scan_floors.json` at `pglob:130`, matching `test_workflow_curl_guard.py`, which globs the same directory.

Mutation-verified — each mutant re-parses the YAML to prove it landed before the tests run:

```
MUTANT                                 EXPECT   LANDED   RESULT
M1 comment back inside continuation    kill     yes      KILLED
M2 drop the heredoc exemption          kill     yes      KILLED
CONTROL legal comment above cmd        survive  yes      SURVIVED
```

## Gates

```
python3 scripts/regression_lint.py --mode delta --base origin/main
  ✓ no NEW violations introduced by this PR   (1399 pre-existing)

pytest test_workflow_continuation_comment · test_workflow_curl_guard ·
       test_cron_selftraffic_ua · test_scan_floors_are_pinned ·
       test_repo_scans_are_path_independent
  18 passed
```

## After merge

The next scheduled run (≤5 min) should go green and the `cron-heartbeat` red clears from `/api/v1/ops/deadman` when `deadman-watch` next polls (`43 */2 * * *`).

**Worth checking separately, and NOT verified here:** whether the 38 master-ticks behind this endpoint actually stopped for the ~2 hours it was down, or whether something else also calls `/api/v1/cron/heartbeat`. That decides whether there is a data hole behind this fix.

produces points nowhere near the cause. All five environment variables
had been added as Sensitive. Vercel withholds sensitive values from the
build step, and Next.js inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_ values at build time, so
they compiled to undefined and every route returned 500 with "Your
project's URL and Key are required to create a Supabase client" — an
error that reads like the keys are missing when they were present and
correct the whole time.

Vercel does reject the combination on creation ("cannot use secret
visibility on Production or Preview"), but only through the API; the
variables already existed, so nothing surfaced until runtime.

Marking the anon key sensitive is a category error regardless. It ships
to every browser by design — row-level security is what protects the
data, not the secrecy of that key.

Verified against production, not just a 200: signed in through the demo
buttons as both accounts, confirmed the dashboard reports $1,192 MRR
from the live database, and confirmed the tier gate still holds — a
level-1 membership shows the real upgrade prices and no level-3 post
body appears anywhere in the delivered HTML.

author: hello-agency-hun
body:
# Summary

- Adds exact, inclusive `measurement_start` and `measurement_end` dates to report builds.
- Filters daily Meta metrics, content exports, and ZoomSphere rows to the resolved range before KPI calculation.
- Adds campaign status pages and visible period-accuracy warnings to the editable HTML report.
- Keeps existing calendar-month projects backward compatible when exact dates cannot be resolved.

# Period precedence

The engine resolves one authoritative interval in this order:

1. a complete manager-supplied start/end pair;
2. a common date window detected in daily source exports;
3. the Meta Ads reporting window;
4. the calendar month as an explicit `assumed` fallback.

A one-sided manager value is ignored instead of creating a half-defined period. The closing date determines the report's `YYYY-MM` period identifier. Continuity checks use exact adjacent dates when both reports contain measurement boundaries.

# Filtering rules

- Both boundary dates are included.
- Daily series and content rows are filtered before totals, joins, rankings, and comparisons are calculated.
- ZoomSphere content is filtered by publication date.
- A standard monthly measurement lasts 27-32 inclusive days. Gaps, overlaps, nonstandard lengths, and assumed dates remain buildable but are surfaced through `measurement_credibility`.
- Daily source windows that cannot support the resolved interval still fail validation rather than silently producing incomplete totals.

# Meta Ads and campaign truth boundaries

Meta Ads totals are never prorated. When the Ads export covers a different window, its complete totals remain in the report as indicative values with the actual query dates and a visible warning. Boost matching is only strict when the Ads window exactly matches the report interval.

Campaign start date, end date, delivery status, ongoing state, result type, and result count come directly from the export and are locked report data. Only the campaign-section headline and explanatory narrative are editable. Missing dates remain missing; the narrative layer cannot invent them.

# Tests

Verified on the upstream branch before review:

```text
git status --short
git diff --check origin/master...HEAD
python -m pytest -q
```

Result: clean worktree, no whitespace errors, `427 passed, 1 deselected in 28.11s`.

author: sqrt-of-2
body:
This PR proves the Kolmogorov zero-one law for a dissociated exchangeable array and reads off its first consequence: the diagonal of a jointly exchangeable, jointly dissociated array is i.i.d. It serves the Layer 8 milestone "exchangeable arrays and the Aldous–Hoover representation" of `TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability/README.md`, whose ergodic form is exactly the dissociated one — `Arrays/AldousHoover.lean` already proves that an ergodic coding (one with no global noise coordinate) produces a dissociated array, and this is the zero-one law that separates that form from the general one.

`TauCeti/Probability/Exchangeability/Arrays/ZeroOne.lean` defines `arrayTailFamily X n`, the σ-algebra of the entries `X (i, j)` with `n ≤ i` and `n ≤ j`, and `arrayTail X`, the infimum of the tail family — the array analogues of `tailFamily` and `tailProcess`. The corner `[0, n] × [0, n]` and the shell `[n + 1, ∞) × [n + 1, ∞)` are square blocks over disjoint index sets, so joint dissociation makes them independent; the corners increase and generate the whole array σ-algebra, so the array tail is independent of itself and therefore trivial (`JointlyDissociated.measure_eq_zero_or_one_of_arrayTail`, with the separately dissociated corollary). Both index axes are cut on purpose: dissociation asks for two disjointness conditions, and for the row tail alone the statement is false — an array whose rows are all one common i.i.d. random path is separately dissociated while its row tail carries the whole path.

The application is `JointlyDissociated.iIndepFun_arrayDiag`. Dissociation separates any diagonal entry from the square block over a finite set of other indices, so the whole diagonal is independent. Joint exchangeability supplies the common law, giving `JointlyDissociated.exists_mixedIIDWith_const_arrayDiag`.

Two reusable supporting lemmas are added: `JointlyDissociated.indep_blockSigma_prod` states independence of square blocks over arbitrary disjoint nonempty index sets, and `blockSigma_mono` records that the σ-algebra of a block grows with the block.

No material is adapted from `cameronfreer/exchangeability`, which treats exchangeable sequences and carries no array zero-one law; no Mathlib infrastructure is vendored. Mathlib supplies the independence machinery used throughout (`indep_iSup_of_monotone` and `measure_eq_zero_or_one_of_indep_self`).

Roadmap: Exchangeability

author: assafmanor
body:
Your field report on M6b's first day: the board said the leave-by had passed while you stood **200m from the door** of the next stop — and the Map tab, one tab over, was drawing your blue dot beside that stop's pin at the same moment.

**M6b was not wrong on its own terms, and that is the point.** ADR-0206 §AE3 measures the leg between two *scheduled* stops, so the number described the plan correctly and the leave-by was derived from a walk you had in fact already made. **The defect is the silence:** the app had a position, was already using it fifty pixels away, and didn't let the one surface making a claim about *you* consult it.

The v2 mockup's §3d had already drawn the answer — under a heading that reads *"correction: the app DOES have a position, and it is already using it"* — and it was never built. **[ADR-0207](https://github.com/assafmanor/waypoint/blob/claude/m6b-hero-read-routes-wlxj67/docs/decisions/0207-a-fix-may-withdraw-a-claim-it-may-not-make-one.md) is the decision the board asked for before this could be built**, so it ships beside the code rather than being skipped.

## The thesis, which is what keeps it small

**A fix decides what we may CLAIM. It is never an input to an estimate.** No route request is ever issued from a position, so ADR-0205 §4's place-keyed cache is untouched and there's no request-per-fix. And withdrawal needs no estimate at all: your report wasn't *"the number is imprecise"*, it was *"you're calling me late when you can see I'm not."*

| the fix says | the app then |
| --- | --- |
| nothing usable | reads **exactly** as M6b shipped |
| still at the last stop | **earns** the mark — `📍 עדיין כאן` |
| along the leg | withdraws it, with nobody pressing anything |
| at the next stop | reports no journey at all |

`unknown` is first because it's the **default**, not the error — no permission, a refusal, a stale fix, or a position that settles nothing. ADR-0109 §6 means the surface has to be complete without consent and better with it.

## Your three proposals, placed where each one works

- **"Tolerance relative to the total distance"** — right, and it's the arrival radius: relative to the leg **and** floored by the fix's own accuracy, because a radius under the error bar measures noise (urban GPS is ±20–50m, so it would flicker between stances while you stood still).
- **"Relative to your actual GPS location"** — right, and it's now the whole mechanism.
- **"Maybe not show you as late"** — I'd still push back. A passed leave-by is §V1.4's most actionable read and the copy already claims only the clock (`זמן היציאה עבר`, never `אתם באיחור`). The problem was never that the app said it; it's that the app could have known better.

## Home never prompts

It calls `request()` only when `permission === 'granted'`. The front door isn't an intent to be located — you've used the Map, so the fix arrives free; someone who hasn't sees today's behaviour and is never asked. **A prompt on Home would need its own reason-first card and its own decision**, and this ADR declines to take it.

## A stale fix is worse than no fix

The hook is **one-shot by design** (a battery decision) and holds its answer for the life of the screen, so the honest capability is *"the app knows where you were when you last opened it."* Twenty minutes old at the origin would **earn** a late mark for somebody who left fifteen minutes ago — a hedge turned into an assertion. So a fix carries its own timestamp and expires into `unknown` after two minutes. `useGeolocation` grew `fixedAt` and `accuracyMeters` to make that expressible.

## Three bugs the arithmetic hid

None was visible in the diff; each came from writing the spec or rendering the row.

1. **The radius was `min(accuracy, fraction)`** — so the leg's fraction capped it *below* the error bar, the exact noise §5 exists to refuse. It reads as correct, which is why it's now two specs and a paragraph in the ADR rather than a silent fix.
2. **`en-route` was twice as strict as it read.** *"Closer to the destination than the origin"* only fires past the **midpoint**, so a traveller a third of the way along kept a mark they'd plainly answered. One radius of real progress is the honest bar — and the wrong-way case still falls through to `unknown`.
3. **The en-route line printed the duration twice** (`~12 דק׳ · בדרך · נותרו ~12 דק׳`). The bare number is the ambiguity §6 removes, so the labelled one survives.

Plus a fixture bug worth the same note as #711's: the Home spec's `between()` kept another spec's longitude, putting the "fix" 1700 km from both stops — every stance was correctly `unknown` and three assertions failed for the right reason. It's derived from the `places` fixture now.

## Also fixed — you reported this too

**`בדרך` had no way back.** `markOnWay` only ever set, and the verb toasted *without* an undo callback while `done`/`skip`/`restore` all pass one — so the app's one device-local mark was its only state-writing verb you couldn't undo, and ADR-0019 makes the toast's undo button *the* way undo surfaces. `clearOnWay` exists, the toast offers it, and the row carries `ביטול סימון` (the word `SettleControl` already uses) because a toast is transient and a mark is not.

## Measured

At 360 in Chromium: every action row is 2 lines at 46px, and **`עדיין כאן` costs zero extra lines** — the `--miss` row was already two because of the `בדרך` button. No horizontal overflow in any state.

## Left open on purpose

- **Two numbers are judgements, not measurements:** `ARRIVAL_FRACTION` (0.12) and `ARRIVAL_RADIUS_MAX_M` (2km). Backlogged beside §D5's buffer — which is where a *proportional* tolerance belongs, as an estimate-error question rather than a fix for this.
- **The group still learns nothing from a sensor.** ADR-0006 §8 untouched: never persisted, never sent, so what the group sees still comes only from a person pressing `בדרך`.
- **`near-the-day`'s "better metric"** is now one step away and unbuilt.

## Board

M6b flipped 🔵 → ✅ (#712 verified merged), M6c added as its own card with the handoff, and the "own-device position wants its own ADR" backlog line pruned — it's an ADR now.

## Checks

`pnpm format` / `lint` / `typecheck` / `build` clean. **Frontend 267 files / 4583 tests**, shared 18 / 371, all green. **24 new specs**: `travel-position` 13 (four stances, the expiry, the radius in both directions, the midpoint rule), `on-way` +3, `HeroLift` +2, `Home.leave-by` +6 — including the reported case end to end, and that no consent means no request and no change.

author: freddymeta
body:
## Summary

A truncated `Text` renders Astryx's `Tooltip` **and** sets the native `title` attribute to the same string — both gated on the same `tooltipEnabled`. Hovering draws both: the styled tooltip first, then the browser's own unstyled one on top of it a moment later, saying exactly the same thing.

It is visible on the docsite today:

```diff
-        title={tooltipEnabled ? truncation.fullText : undefined}
```

Same line in `Heading.tsx`.

## Measured in Chromium

Same story, native `title` presence plus a count of *visible* `[role="tooltip"]` elements after hover:

| | native title | visible Astryx tooltip | shown to the user |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | yes | 1 | **2** |
| this PR | no | 1 | **1** |

## Why the `title` goes and not the `Tooltip`

- **`Tooltip` already carries the a11y contract.** It sets `aria-describedby` on its anchor (`Tooltip.tsx:253-256`), verified still present after this change.
- **The full text was never hidden from assistive tech.** CSS clips it visually; the DOM still holds all 191 characters, measured. `title` was not what made the truncated text readable to a screen reader.
- **`title` is the weaker affordance anyway** — unstyleable, unplaceable, no touch support, and its own delay is what makes the doubling look like a glitch rather than a design.

So the duplicate is all that is lost.

## Test plan

- New test: a truncated `Text` carries no `title`. **Negative control:** putting the attribute back fails exactly that test.
- `pnpm build`, `check:repo`, `lint:strict`, core + storybook typechecks — clean. Text + Heading + Tooltip suites green.
- No existing test asserted the `title` (checked before removing it).

## Note

`Badge` gains the same tooltip in a follow-up; it will use the `Tooltip` alone rather than reintroducing this pair.

## Summary

- reject runtime external packages, Node modules, dynamic loaders, evaluator, process, network, worker, and ambient allocation capabilities

body:
## What
The `deploy` job had no `checkout` step and never copied `docker-compose.prod.yml` anywhere — every deploy ran `docker compose` against whatever file was already sitting in `/opt/autoroom` on the server, completely disconnected from git. Only Docker image updates (`docker compose pull`) were ever actually landing in production; edits to the compose file itself (services, env vars, networks) never took effect.

This is very likely why PR #14's `--force-recreate` fix had no observed effect on the live site: force-recreating containers against a compose file that was never actually updated from git just re-applies the same stale configuration more forcefully.

## Fix
Adds `actions/checkout@v4` + an `appleboy/scp-action@v1` step that copies the repo's `docker-compose.prod.yml` to `/opt/autoroom` before `pull`/`up --force-recreate` run against it, so the server always matches git going forward.

## Verification plan
Deploy-script-only change. Verification happens by watching the next real deploy and confirming the live homepage actually shows admin-managed content afterward (CMS-uploaded logo, Featured Cars, FAQ) — not just that CI is green.

author: oschulz
body:
Un-deprecates `VectorOfVectors`: it stays an exported, documented alias of `PartsView` (both names remain first-class), instead of a `@deprecate_binding` slated for removal in 2.0.

Rationale:

* `VectorOfVectors` is the established name of the vector-of-vectors member of the `VectorOfArrays` / `VectorOfSimilarVectors` type family and is used throughout the downstream ecosystem (SolidStateDetectors, UnROOT, LegendHDF5IO, ...). Every other change of v1 has a spelling that works on v0.6 and v1 alike, this rename was the only one forcing downstream code to carry version-conditional aliases.
* Deprecated-binding warnings are inconsistent across Julia versions: on 1.10 every unqualified use warns under `--depwarn=yes` (i.e. in every `Pkg.test`) with the expanded `VectorOfArrays{T, 1, 0, ...} where ...` in the message rather than `PartsView`, and throws under `--depwarn=error`, while on 1.12 unqualified use never warns at all.

Consequence to be aware of: with two exported aliases for the same type, Julia's alias printing selects neither, so `PartsView` instances now print with their underlying `VectorOfArrays{T, 1, 0, ...}` type instead of an alias name.

Non-breaking, patch release 1.0.1.

## Description

This PR enables the `io` collection to participate in the organisations backfill audit pipeline through a dedicated IO ownership adapter.

The change closes a major gap in ownership auditing by allowing IO records to resolve canonical organisation ownership from either an explicit `organisationId` or legacy `user_id` actor provenance. This improves migration safety for collections that still rely on historical actor relationships while preserving compatibility with existing data shapes.

The adapter introduces:
- Resolution logic for canonical and legacy ownership paths
- Project-to-organisation validation and conflict reporting
- Detection of orphaned users and organisations
- Scoped inspection support for targeted audits
- Index contract inspection for expected IO access patterns
- Read-only audit guarantees verified through Mongo integration tests

This also removes the IO adapter from the blocked backfill list, making IO ownership readiness visible and enforceable alongside the rest of the audited collections.

The added tests strengthen confidence in precedence rules, conflict handling, index validation, and dry-run safety, helping ensure the backfill process remains deterministic and production-safe before any write path is introduced.

author: berndhueckstaedt
body:
Repairs from a review of #3779 (the e-mail address change) done after the fact. Both
strands have the same root: since #3779 a member can hold **several** rows in
`user_contacts`, and every row they ever held stays for good.

## An address nobody confirmed could be held for good

A pending change holds its address — that is by design, for the window it is given.
It could be renewed without end, though: `resendEmailChange` wrote fresh codes to the
row, and `updatedAt` is an `@UpdateDateColumn` with `onUpdate`, so **any** write moves
the very moment the change is measured from (both by the window check and by
`dbPurgeExpiredEmailChanges`). One press of *send again* per day held any address —
including a stranger's — forever, on an account that never confirmed anything.

The resend now re-sends the codes already on the row and leaves it untouched. The link
from the first mail keeps working; the change keeps the one lifetime it started with.

The other half is who that hurt. The Elopage webhook counted contact rows raw, so it
saw such a row and returned without opening an account — and it is the one existence
check in the tree that does not go through `checkEmailExists`, so it never cleared an
expired change either. A paying customer whose address had once been typed into a
stranger's change form silently got no account, and no retry would ever fix it. It now
asks the question the registration asks, the same way.

## A code on an address the member left behind

`UserContact.user` is the inverse of `users.email_id`, so it is **empty** for every row
that is not the address currently in force. Three paths went from a contact row back to
its member without checking, and `emailChecked` does not tell an abandoned address from
a current one — a given-up address stays checked:

| where | what happened |
| --- | --- |
| `findUserByIdentifier` | wrote `emailContact` onto null; reachable by any signed-in member via `user(identifier: "<former address>")` |
| `setPassword` | read `userContact.user.id` **before** the window check, so an old reset link gave an internal error instead of saying it had expired |
| `AssistedRegistrationResolver.confirmEmail` | same line, reachable from any activation mail sent before the member moved on |

`findUserByIdentifier` now answers "not found", which is what `findUserByEmail` answers
to the same input. Whether a **former** address should still lead to its owner — the way
a former alias does — is a product question and is deliberately left open here.

## Checks

`typecheck` and `lint` green in `backend` and `database`. The tests added here need a
database and run in CI: two in `database/src/queries/user.test.ts` for the left-behind
address, one in `EmailChangeResolver.test.ts` for the stranded password link. The

author: armandrius
body:
### What is the goal?

Rails helpers are forbidden by the org-wide presenters standard, but nothing enforced it at lint time except two hand-rolled copies of the same cop, one in Simba and one just written for Timon. This moves `Sequra/NoHelpers` into the gem so there is a single definition.

### Is this a restricting or expanding change?

**RESTRICTING change** — but it ships `Enabled: false`, so no consumer repo changes behaviour on bump. That is stronger protection than the template's `info` severity: repos opt in once their own `app/helpers/` is empty, exactly as `Sequra/NoSidekiqPerformStubs` does.

### References

* **Issue:** https://sequra.atlassian.net/browse/COR-2792
* **Related pull-requests:** sequra/timon#7196 (Timon adoption, will drop its local copy in favour of this), plus a Simba PR to delete its local copy

### How is it being implemented?

- Flags any `module` or `class` node in a file whose path matches `%r{(^|/)app/helpers/}`. Path-based, not name-based: `RoutingHelper` in `app/services/` is fine, anything inside a helpers directory is not.
- `Include` is `**/app/helpers/**/*.rb`, so root, pack and nested-pack helper directories are all covered.
- The offence highlights the declaration only (`module FooHelper`), not the whole body, so editors do not underline the entire file. Same shape RuboCop's own `Style/Documentation` uses.

### Caveats

Simba's local copy also mentioned decorators and its `/dismantle-helper` command. This version drops both: Timon has no decorator layer, and the message should not name a Simba-only tool.

author: laulopezreal
body:
## What and why

Second recurrence of the host->container routing outage (2026-08-12, then 2026-08-26) where `api.guessme.world` timed out while the API container itself was healthy.

Root cause: tailscale's exit-node setup installs policy rule `5270: from all lookup 52`; table 52 only holds `default dev tailscale0`, so host -> docker-bridge traffic (172.17-172.22) gets shunted into the tailnet and hangs. The existing `tailscale-docker-route-exceptions.service` fixes this but only fires on boot or a full tailscaled restart. On 2026-08-26 tailscale rebuilt its routing in place with no restart, so the exceptions silently vanished again.

## Changes

- `deploy/tailscale-docker-route-exceptions-heal.timer` + `-heal.service`: re-run the same idempotent repair script every 2 minutes (`OnCalendar=*:0/2`, `OnBootSec=1min`), so a silent in-place rebuild self-heals within the timer interval.
- `deploy/tailscale-docker-route-exceptions.sh`: fix bridge discovery. `ip -o -4 addr show type bridge` returns EVERY interface's addresses on this iproute2 (lo/enp8s0/tailscale0 included), which added throw-routes for the host public IP, tailscale IP and loopback into table 52. Now builds the real bridge-name list first (`ip -o link show type bridge`), then reads each bridge's own subnet.
- `OPERATIONS.md`: document the recurrence, install/verify steps, and cleanup of stray throws.

## Verification (live on claw-home, 2026-08-26)

- Routes applied; API restored: `api.guessme.world/ops/health` => all ok; frontend 200; ops-ui 200; outbound egress 200.
- Timer enabled + active; verified 3 ticks; after each tick table 52 holds exactly the 6 docker-bridge throw-routes, no strays.
- `ip route get 172.18.0.2` => `dev km-bridge` (not tailscale0).

This is an ops/infra fix already applied and live on the server; this PR keeps the repo deploy SSOT in sync.

body:
Refactor DLL loading to robustly locate the Vector driver DLL on Windows. Added vectorDLLName, vectorDLLCandidates and getVectorDLLFromRegistry helpers to detect 32/64-bit names, query SharedDlls in the registry, and search System32/SysWOW64 and ./bin paths with deduplication. Handles WOW64 registry access and normalizes candidate paths before attempting to load them. Adds import of golang.org/x/sys/windows/registry and related OS/path handling for more reliable DLL resolution.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Changes are limited to Windows Vector driver initialization and DLL path resolution; typical Vector installs should benefit, with a small chance of regression if the DLL was only on PATH and not under registry or standard system locations.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Improves how the Windows Vector driver finds `vxlapi.dll` / `vxlapi64.dll` before `xlOpenDriver` runs.**
> 
> `loadDLL` no longer only tries `./bin` and a bare DLL name. It now builds an ordered, deduplicated candidate list via **`vectorDLLCandidates`**: install path from **`HKLM\...\SharedDlls`** (`getVectorDLLFromRegistry`, with WOW64-appropriate registry access), then **`SysWOW64`** on 32-bit builds, **`System32`**, and finally **`./bin`**. **`vectorDLLName`** centralizes the 32- vs 64-bit filename choice. The same try-each-path-until-load loop and proc binding behavior is unchanged once a DLL loads.
>

author: lazerg
body:
### What does this PR do?

Logs the ignored default TLSStore and TLSOption resources at warning level instead of error, when `defaultTLSResourcesNamespace` restricts them to a single namespace.

### Motivation

Setting `defaultTLSResourcesNamespace` is an explicit choice to honor the default TLS resources from one namespace only, so finding them elsewhere is the expected result of that option rather than a failure. The message also runs on every watched Kubernetes event, not only when the resulting configuration changes, which is what floods the logs. Warning is the level `addToConfig` already uses to report a resource being dropped, and it keeps the message reachable for anyone running below the default ERROR level.

Fixes #13778

### More

- [ ] Added/updated tests
- [ ] Added/updated documentation

### Additional Notes

The existing `buildTLSStores` and `buildTLSOptions` tests assert the resulting dynamic configuration only, so the level change leaves them unaffected.

Tell me if you would rather have debug here. I kept warning because a `default` TLSStore showing up outside the reserved namespace can also be a tenant trying to replace the cluster-wide TLS policy, which is the case the option was added to close.

author: kpdagrt22
body:
A bare count already cost this programme three days. So this reports every count beside the two mechanisms that move it — `created_at` for arrivals, `_delete_forensics` for departures — and says plainly when they fail to reconcile. It **refuses to run** as a role without `BYPASSRLS`, because a zero from such a role is indistinguishable from "not permitted to look".

```
2026-08-26  workers 37   worker_profiles 22   jobs 19 (17 open)   applications 28
            worker_skill 0   job_reach 0   job_posting_skill 0
            skill 165 = 52 active / 111 provisional / 2 deprecated
```

All 37 workers arrived **2026-08-21..25** — the first sustained registration traffic recorded. No deletion since 2026-08-21; all 311 forensics rows are `supabase/dashboard`.

### Two things it cannot explain — left unexplained

**1. The recorded "1 worker [08-24]" does not reproduce.** 31 workers existed before 08-24 and nothing was deleted after 08-21. The audit enumerates five plausible predicates and **none yields 1**. The figure sits in the *"actually used"* column and carries no `population_predicate` — the exact gap the provenance rule closed, and it predates enforcement. Recorded as a **fact gap**; its author is the only person who can say what it counted.

**2. jobs 25 → 19 and applications 92 → 28, with no forensic record** — because the trigger exists on `workers` and `worker_profiles` **only**. For those tables *"no deletions recorded"* is the absence of a **trigger**, not the absence of a deletion. No job created since 2026-08-05, so 19 is not growth: six rows left by a route nothing observes. **That observability gap is the more useful half of the finding.**

Tests pin both failures, so a later reader cannot mistake this for a clean bill of health.

### Also found
**10 of 22 worker profiles carry a `job_domain_id`**, matched 08-21..08-25. Every match is lexical (`l0_exact` / `l2_trigram`) or worker-confirmed; the ANN layer never ran and **no profile carries an embedding**. Consistent with `DOMAIN_MATCH_ENABLED=false` rather than a violation — the flag gates the vector path, not the lexical pre-layers. It is still live taxonomy behaviour that *"steps 2–4 and 6–9 are not connected"* omits.

body:
## Status

**Phase 12A is complete within the bounded scope declared here.**

The frozen contract remains unchanged.  This commit creates its reserved result
owner and executable owner for a compact strict-descent / finite-part
calibration.  The locale, sobriety, basis, full Moore-behaviour, coupled
observer, and place-indexed workloads remain outside this PR.  Later partition
and Rogers--Ramanujan work will proceed in a separate Phase 12B branch.

The calibration remains inside the existing
`sonnet/local-field-projective-process-geometry/` line.  It does not create a
new Sonnet and does not mix its objects or certificates with the separate
statistical-mechanics calibration.

## Exact results

1. **Projective-frame descent obstruction.**  Ordinary affine addition cannot
   descend to an unmarked `PGL_2`-equivariant operation.  Applying
   `1/z` to `0+1=1` and `1/(z-1)` to `1+2=3` assigns the same unmarked
   input `(infinity, 1)` the incompatible outputs `1` and `1/2`.
2. **Correct frame transport.**  Frame-indexed addition satisfies
   `g(x +_F y) = gx +_{gF} gy`.  The certificate checks 12,400 exact rational
   matrix/input cases.  Addition needs zero/infinity marks; joint addition and
   multiplication need the unit mark.
3. **Chart-forgetting obstruction.**  For
   `G(q)=q/(1-q)^2`, the chart `u=1-q` has finite part `0`, while
   `q=exp(-t)` has finite part `-1/12`.
4. **Finite-jet transport.**  For pole order `r`, the principal coefficients
   together with the chart transition through order `r+1` determine the
   transported finite part.  The principal part is therefore a required
   residual, even when it is subtracted from the final scalar.
5. **Bernoulli family.**  Exact formal-series inversion verifies for
   `m=1,...,8` that the exponential-chart constant coefficient is
   `(-1)^m B_(m+1)/(m+1)`.  Equality with `zeta(-m)` is used only as a
   classical typed interpretation, not re-proved here.
6. **Composition boundary.**  Fixed-contract finite parts are linear and
   log-free linear-scale invariant.  Nonlinear chart forgetting,
   multiplication, differentiation, and filter/grouping interchange fail;
   reindexing requires its boundary term.

## Semantic verdict

This slice supports a **filtered semantic fibration as an exact finite model**:
the charted germ transports, while the finite scalar does not descend after the
chart contract is forgotten.  Relative to preserving the arithmetic task and
the full declared covariance, retaining a frame/chart fibre is forced.  The
other logical exits remain restriction of symmetry or weakening of the task.

This is not vertical objectification.  No task-independent primitive, new free
composition, or all-composite lowering law is supplied, and no generic AM
regularization or semantic-fibration theorem is claimed.

- the frozen Phase 12 contract from the initialization commit;
- `20-phase12-locale-observer-history-behavior-results.md`;
- `tests/research/test_locale_observer_history_behavior_duality.py`;
- the updated Sonnet status and reading index.

The six exact test functions were imported and executed directly in the
available runtime; all passed.  The file also passes `py_compile`.  Repository
CI should run the same file under pytest.

- Mathematical Core: evidence refined; file unchanged;
- Engineering Architecture: unchanged; pure research-local integer/Fraction

- Theory Map: V2/V4 evidence refined; maturity unchanged;
- Experimental/Public API: no pressure;

author: urlmonitor
body:
## Summary

Started as "quick-fix the two swallowed `OSError`s in the harvester". The investigation that followed changed what the rest of the work should be.

**The 28 "stranded" learnings were never stranded.** They are write receipts, not payloads — and the learnings they refer to are already on disk. Two ACs specifying their recovery are withdrawn rather than built, because building them would have corrupted nine curated knowledge files.

## 1. The harvester reported broken runs as clean

Two `OSError` branches were swallowed. Neither was introduced by yesterday's `INF-400c-2-ii` change — both predate it — but that change added an exit-code contract documenting `0` as *"drained cleanly"*, which is what makes them consequential: the documentation now actively teaches an operator to trust a code that lies on both paths.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Every destination write fails | `0 learnings routed: none`, **exit 0** | `0 learnings routed: none; 2 write failures: 1 adr, 1 claude-md`, **exit 4** |
| State file cannot be saved | bare `pass`, **exit 0**, next run silently re-appends every learning | `state NOT persisted (N routed learnings will be re-applied on the next run)`, **exit 4** |

Failed writes are **not** added to the idempotency record, so they stay retryable — the same retention rule `INF-400c-2-ii` established for unroutable events.

**One deliberate exception, found by review after the first attempt.** When nothing new needs recording the state write is a no-op, and treating its failure as a failed run raised the exit code to `4` and **masked the exit-3 backlog** on precisely the all-unroutable run that most needs it — today's real corpus. That case now stays `3`. Both verified against the real 28-event sink.

Six new tests. **Five verified red** against the unfixed code by reverting only the production file; the sixth passes on the old code too and is labelled in-place as a regression guard, not evidence of this fix.

## 2. What the investigation actually found

All 28 `knowledge_captured` events share one key set — `event, timestamp, agent, component, destination, entry_kind` — with **no `text` field**, because `signoff` §7 step 4 specifies a record of a write that already happened.

Resolving all 10 distinct `destination` paths: **9 exist in the repo**, 3608–23474 bytes, holding real content. The busiest (23 KB, target of 10 events) opens *"Captured 2026-06-16 during BO-210 / GE-102 technical enrichment"* — matching event #1's timestamp, agent and destination exactly. The 10th was never created; `git log --all` returns nothing for it.

Recovering them would have appended 28 placeholders of the form `[agent-assignment-pattern] Learning from ` on top of nine curated files.

**The real defect is that capture is dead at the source.** §7 still instructs agents to load `route-learning` and `capture-learning` — neither has ever existed — behind a fail-open, so the escape hatch is the only reachable path. Emissions: **25 in June → 2 in July → 1 in August.** The loop went quiet eight weeks ago rather than failing loudly.

Both the PO and the BA consulted on this hit that dead path mid-investigation and silently captured nothing. Only their prose reports it.

## 3. Store changes

**Withdrawn** (`status: superseded_by`, original criteria retained verbatim):
- `INF-400c-5-ii` → `INF-700c`. Mapping the legacy vocabulary has no correct output over this corpus.
- `INF-400c-4-ii` → `INF-700c-2`. Copies permanently unroutable records *into* the file the backlog is counted from.

`INF-400c-2-ii` is deliberately **left standing** — its permanent non-zero exit is a property of its input, not a defect in the behaviour. Reverting it would trade a false backlog for a false all-clear.

**Authored** — `INF-700b` ("a learning an agent has today actually gets written down") and `INF-700c` ("nothing enters the knowledge record that is not real knowledge"), 14 enriched L2/L3 children. Plus two L3s under `INF-400b-2` for defects covered by no AC: the four-way schema divergence, and `_event_hash` keying on `ticket` — empty in every real record, with 17 of 28 timestamps at day resolution.

`INF-400b-2`'s **criteria are not modified**; the two amendments it needs are recorded in `amended_by` for BA/PO.

## 4. Filed

| KI | What |
|---|---|
| `KI-KM-009` | ADR-034 §1's "the loop has never closed" is false, and §2's rejection of inline capture rests on it |
| `KI-KM-010` | The receipt-shaped schema, and the `_event_hash` key defect |
| `KI-KM-011` | A valid-JSON non-object sink line crashes with an unhandled `AttributeError`; `CLAUDE.md`'s own pre-drive checklist writes 4 of the sink's 33 lines |
| `KI-ACS-014` | No retired `work_status`, so a superseded child blocks its parent's done-proof. **The one with no owning AC.** |

## Verification

- 39 tests pass; `ruff` and `mypy` clean under CI's flags
- `OK: all 207 AC YAML files are valid`
- Scan resolves the dependency chain to 9 ready / 7 blocked, with both withdrawn ACs absent from both buckets and `INF-400b-2-ii` the single unblocked root
- The fixture is byte-identical to the real 28 events (previously fabricated, and green by construction — its invented kinds could never enter the routing vocabulary, so the test could never go red)

## Deliberately not in this PR

The harvester's default sink is still `knowledge_emissions.jsonl`, which has never existed — `INF-400c-4` owns it. The `AttributeError` crash is specified as `INF-700c-1-i` but not fixed. ADR-034's premise correction is recommended, not made. And `KI-ACS-014` wants a gate decision, not three silent `covered_by` edits.

body:
## What

Publishes `fliks.download` 0.4.0 — built from the tagged [v0.4.0](https://github.com/fliks-app/fk-plugin-download/releases/tag/v0.4.0) commit ([96af9ba](https://github.com/fliks-app/fk-plugin-download/commit/96af9ba)).

- `plugins/fliks.download/src/` refreshed from that build (`plugin.js`, `plugin.json`)
- `plugins/fliks.download/versions/0.4.0.json` added
- `catalog.json` regenerated

## What's in the release

**Streamed search results.** The release picker fills in as each indexer answers rather than showing a spinner until the slowest one returns, with a tab per indexer — a spinner while it searches, a red dot when it times out, a grey dot when the cooldown filter skipped it. That last state was previously invisible: a search quietly queried fewer trackers than configured with nothing in the UI to say so.

**The search budget is now an admin setting.** `search_budget_seconds`, default 30, clamped to [5s, 120s]. It replaces two hardcoded ceilings — 30s on the fan-out and 25s on each fetch — where the lower one decided and raising only the visible one would have changed nothing. The per-request fetch ceiling is derived from the budget rather than configured separately.

The 30s default is unchanged deliberately: it clears a reverse proxy's usual 60s read timeout, and a 504 there discards every indexer that had already answered.

## Compatibility

`fliks` stays `>=3.0.0 <4.0.0`.

The streamed emissions want core's new `{ userId }` audience on `events.emitOwn` (fliks-app/fliks#1040) to reach the account that ran the search. Against a core without it, the payload shape falls into the `{ mediaId }` branch, `recipientsForMedia(undefined)` skips the requester lookup and returns every admin — so nothing throws. The searching admin's modal fills correctly; other admins receive events their client discards on the search-id filter; a viewer who is not an admin gets no stream and sees the previous behaviour. No version gate was added for that reason.

`pluginApi` is unchanged at 0, which already has its row in COMPATIBILITY.md.

## Checks run locally

`node --test scripts/*.test.mjs scripts/ci/*.test.mjs` (7 pass), `check-pr-shape`, `check-compatibility-table`, `check-fliks-upper-bound`, and `build-catalog` — all green. No published `versions/` or `dist/` file is modified; only `src/` is rewritten, which publishing a version necessarily does.

## After merge

`Package plugin` needs a `workflow_dispatch` with `pluginId: fliks.download` to build and sign the archive, commit it under `dist/`, and replace the zeroed `sha256`. Until that runs, 0.4.0's `zipUrl` resolves to nothing and the entry is not installable.

body:
## Summary

**QDM-6** (Glori-Holdings/quetrex-demo, 2026-08-26): a cloud build reached HEAD `c26bc72` with `qa-report` PASS, `review-verdict` `AUTO_MERGE` pinned to HEAD, and `security-findings` PASS — and git-workflow still **refused** to open the PR:

```
state.json.git_workflow_reason = "review-verdict.json .inputs.nativeSecurityReview = \"errored\", not clean|issues"
```

The native `/security-review` SlashCommand does not exist in cloud sessions (no `SlashCommand` tool), so this rule made **every cloud build unshippable**, and the card sat at `in_progress` forever with no signal to a human.

### Fix 1 — `plugins/quetrex-factory/agents/git-workflow.md`

The NSR gate (Gate 4) now accepts a non-native `nativeSecurityReview` (`errored`/`not_run`/`not_available_in_env`) **only** when `.quetrex/security-findings.json` independently proves the exact HEAD commit clean — it must exist, parse, be pinned via `.head_sha`/`.sha` to HEAD, and record zero open Critical findings. This mirrors the route `merge-gate.sh`'s GATE 2b (`sec_artifact_state()`) and `reviewer.md`'s `independence_ok` already implement, so the two terminal gates agree. Anything short of that (missing, stale, unpinned, or an open Critical) still refuses with the original message — the gate is not simply widened open.

### Fix 2 — `.claude/lib/cloud-build-routine.md` + `.claude/commands/task-build.md`

- The routine now checks for a git-workflow refusal (`state.json.git_workflow == "refused"`) before attempting to open a PR. On a refusal it **still publishes the gate evidence** (a red gate must be published red, per the routine's own rule) instead of silently ending, and reports `GIT_WORKFLOW_REFUSED: <reason>`. It still never calls the kanban API itself (`git-workflow.md`/`cloud-build-routine.md`'s existing "never touch the tracker" / "Do NOT depend on cloud board-MCP" rules are unchanged).
- `task-build.md`'s liveness probe used to treat "a ref is present on origin" as `dead`/`gone` → `RECOVERABLE`, which would re-fire an already-refused prompt and burn the attempt budget proving it refuses again, before ever surfacing the reason. A new `qx_probe_gate_refusal` reads the refusal directly off the published gates branch's `state.json` and — since the cloud routine is architecturally forbidden from writing kanban status — the **local** half now performs the `needs_human` transition (with the reason as a comment) and leaves the gates branch in place for `/quetrex:task-rework` to read.

Bumps `quetrex-factory` to `1.7.6` and `quetrex`/`quetrex-base` to `2.5.5` (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` ×2, `package.json`).

## Test plan

- [x] `test/git-workflow-nsr-contract.test.sh` (new, 10/10) — extracts and **executes** the real fenced NSR snippet from `git-workflow.md`; fail-first proves the pre-fix contract at `1032770` refuses the exact QDM-6 shape; proves the fix allows it; 4 regression guards (no artifact, stale artifact, open Critical, native-clean-still-works).
- [x] `test/git-workflow-gate-refusal.test.sh` (new, 13/13) — extracts and executes the routine's `GIT_WORKFLOW_REFUSED` detection and `task-build.md`'s `qx_probe_gate_refusal` + `qx_actionability(gate_refused)` against real git fixtures (a bare remote + pushed gates branch); fail-first proves neither existed at `1032770`.
- [x] `npm run check:js` — exit 0

- [x] `npm run check:json` — exit 0 (8 files)
- [x] `npm test` — exit 0, **70/70 test files passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**

author: nitinkumar004
body:
## Summary

Eight AWS EC2 `Describe*` handlers applied request `Filters` but silently ignored `MaxResults`/`NextToken` and never emitted a token, so any client paginating them (real AWS paginates every one) got the whole set on page one and looped forever waiting for a token. This wires them through the same pagination path `DescribeInstances`/`DescribeSubnets`/`DescribeVpcs` already use.

Handlers fixed:
- DescribeVolumes
- DescribeSnapshots
- DescribeNetworkInterfaces
- DescribeImages
- DescribeTags
- DescribeVpcEndpoints
- DescribeVpcPeeringConnections
- DescribeDhcpOptions

## What changed

Each handler now, after applying its existing filters and explicit id-list, routes the projected result set through the shared `pageNetworkingXML(...)` helper (stable-sort by resource id, then apply request `MaxResults`/`NextToken`) and adds `nextToken` to its response struct. No new pagination logic is introduced — the shared helper is reused, so behaviour (MaxResults cap, base64 cursor, unparsable-token restart) is identical to the already-paginated Describes.

`DescribeTags` returns `(resource-id, key)` tuples gathered from map iteration, so it pages on a composite `resourceId\x00key` cursor to keep the token deterministic; a resource holds each key at most once, so the pair is unique.

`DescribeNatGateways` (already paginated) and `DescribeAddresses` (does not paginate in real AWS) are intentionally left untouched.

## Tests

New `describe_pagination_test.go` drives a booted in-process AWS server with the real `aws-sdk-go-v2/ec2` client. For every one of the eight ops it asserts:
- `MaxResults=2` over 5 items walks the whole set exactly once and terminates (no duplicates, gaps, or skips across the cursor)
- pagination combines with an explicit id-list / resource-id filter (set is filtered first, then paged)
- an unparsable `NextToken` restarts from the beginning (matching the shared `pageNetworkingXML` helper) rather than erroring or skipping

## Verification

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./server/aws/ec2/... ./providers/aws/...`, `go test -race ./server/aws/ec2/...`, `gofmt -l`, `go generate` (zero diff), and `compatgen` + `git diff docs/compat` (zero drift) all green. golangci-lint on the changed package introduces zero new issues over baseline.

## Summary
- Promotes the previously-internal `_AgentBackchannelOpportunityEvent` to a public `AgentBackchannelOpportunityEvent`, emitted on `AgentSession` (`agent_backchannel_opportunity`) and dispatched to a new `Agent.on_backchannel_opportunity()` hook, so agents can react to mid-turn pauses with short acknowledgment phrases ("mm-hmm", "right", etc).
