body:
### Motivation
- Production resume hits a phase-5 HOLD because account-credit approval packages were not built from the ledger’s durable per-coin selection, causing the validator to reject the package for coin 1267.  
- Root cause: phase-5 package generation only forwarded `--selected-earning-ids` when a confirmed-block payment-delay override was used, while validators always compared packages against `selected_work_by_coin`.  
- The change must preserve the 12-hour payment-delay gate, strict scope/checksum/guarded-apply validation, and the pre-wallet-send boundary while ensuring post-delay phase-5 uses the durable batch scope exactly.

### Description
- Always bind phase-5 account-credit approval packages to the ledger’s durable per-coin earning scope by passing `--selected-earning-ids=<durable ids>` derived from `selected_work_by_coin[coin_id].earning_ids` during package generation.  
- Remove the conditional that limited passing selected earning IDs to the override path so that normal post-delay runs and confirmed-block override runs share the same durable scope contract.  
- Add regression assertions to `tests/badpool_payment_batch_run_harness.php` and `tests/badpool_confirmed_block_payment_delay_override_harness.php` proving that normal post-delay phase-5 and override paths both generate account-credit packages with the exact durable earning IDs for coin 1267 and that wallet-send is not invoked.  
- Preserve all existing guarded-apply contracts, checksum validation, `packageWithinLedgerScope` checks, and payment-delay enforcement; no production operations were executed as part of this repair.

### Testing
- Ran PHP lint on `web/yaamp/core/backend/BadpoolPaymentBatchPhaseAdapter.php`, `web/yaamp/commands/BadpoolGuardCommand.php`, `web/yaamp/core/backend/BadpoolGuardContext.php`, and the focused harness scripts with no syntax errors.  
- Executed focused harnesses: `php tests/badpool_payment_batch_run_harness.php`, `php tests/badpool_confirmed_block_payment_delay_override_harness.php`, `php tests/badpool_account_credit_guard_harness.php`, and `php tests/badpool_approval_package_generator_harness.php` and observed them pass.  
- Ran the full safe PHP harness loop (`for f in tests/*.php; do php "$f"; done`) and observed `safe_php_harnesses_passed=27` and `safe_php_harnesses_failed=0`.  
- All automated checks and harnesses passed, demonstrating the post-delay phase-5 binding regression for coin 1267 is resolved and package scope validation remains strict.

author: adamtheturtle
body:
Fixes #1082.

Pool map and starmap results are homogeneous lists of callback results, so callable inference now accepts any signed literal index instead of treating the unknown-length result as a one-element sequence.

Verification:
- `cargo test --test resolver_edge_cases pool_map_results_preserve_callable_at_nonzero_indices -- --exact`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow change to Pool map subscript resolution in the callable inference path; regression test covers the new behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **#1082** by treating `multiprocessing.pool.Pool` `map` / `starmap` (and related async `.get()` results) as **homogeneous lists** of the callback return value, not a fixed one-element sequence.
> 
> When subscripting those results to call the element (e.g. `Pool(1).map(...)[1](1)` or `.get()[-2](1)`), the checker now requires only a **literal signed integer** index and still resolves through `pool_map_callable_fullname`, instead of using `literal_sequence_index` with length `1` (which effectively allowed only index `0`).
> 
> Adds `pool_map_results_preserve_callable_at_nonzero_indices` in `resolver_edge_cases` to lock in nonzero and negative indices.

author: go-to-k
body:
## Summary

cdkd carries orphaned copies of code that cdk-local actually runs. The copies are test-covered, comment-documented, and sit exactly where a grep lands — so a fix can be written into one, pass every gate, and ship as a no-op. That is not hypothetical: it happened to go-to-k/cdkd#2203 earlier today and was caught only by a security reviewer who booted the server.

Closes #2228.

## Module-level reachability would NOT have caught it

The obvious fence — "every `src/local/**` module must have a live importer" — is green on the exact defect. `vtl-engine.ts` HAS a live importer: `rest-v1-integrations.ts` imports it, and `local-start-api.ts` imports `warnSsrfRiskyUri` from that. ESM loads the module; not one of its five exports is ever reached.

So the critic is **symbol-level**, computed over the TS AST from the build entries (`src/index.ts`, `src/cli/index.ts`), handling dynamic `import()`, namespace imports, `extends` clauses and inline type imports under `verbatimModuleSyntax`.

## The audit — 57 modules

| class | n | notable |
|---|---|---|
| live (all exports reached) | 12 | incl. `ecs-task-runner`, `ecs-secrets-resolver` — fully live, correcting an earlier assumption |
| live-partial | 4 | `rie-client` 2/6 — `invokeRie` and `waitForRieReady` ARE live; only the streaming half is dead |
| loaded-only (zero exports called) | 2 | `vtl-engine` (a fork), `reload-orchestrator` (an orphan — no cdk-local equivalent) |
| unreferenced | 2 | `httpv2-service-integration`, `cfn-local-state-provider` — both forks |
| shim-consumed | 28 | `http-server`, `sigv4-verify`, … — legitimate re-exports |
| shim-unreferenced | 8 | re-exports with no body, so they cannot act as decoys |
| types-only | 1 | |

All 29 "dead" verdicts were cross-checked by grep; zero false positives.

## Why both an annotation AND a fence

An annotation alone is a comment asking the next reader to remember — which is what already failed here twice. A fence alone does not reach the author: the tree already contains orphans, so any check that is green today must tolerate them, and a tolerated orphan is invisible at the moment someone edits it.

So it runs in **both directions**: an unannotated unreachable symbol FAILS, and an annotation on a symbol that has become reachable FAILS as stale. 29 `@no-live-caller` / `@test-only-export` annotations were added — comments only, no logic changed in `src/`.

Shims are excluded **structurally**, not by allowlist: a file declaring no value symbols never enters the population. `http-server.ts` gets no special-casing.

## Probes, both directions

21 mutations of the checker: **20 RED**, plus one deliberate semantics-preserving control that stayed GREEN (proving the suite is not failing for an unrelated reason).

Worth stating plainly: **6 of those were GREEN on the first run.** One was passing for the wrong reason, so the fixture was rebuilt as a discriminating type-only-vs-value pair; four covered shapes absent from the current tree, so a self-probe corpus was added for them; one was unobservable, so a `CDKD_SELF_PROBE_FORCE_FAIL=1` seam now proves it in one spawn.

Must-not-fire direction: 28 consumed shims, 8 unconsumed shims, types-only, all 55 live symbols and every annotated orphan produce zero findings.

## Two byproducts the calibration surfaced

- `ecr-puller.ts`'s doc claimed `isImageInLocalCache` is reused by `docker-image-builder`'s `--no-build` path. That file is a shim; the reuse does not exist.
- `tests/integration/local-start-api/verify.sh:263` claimed cdkd's `invokeRieStreaming` parses the prelude. cdk-local's copy is what runs.

## Deliberately NOT in this PR

Deletion of the orphaned forks (~4.4k src + ~3.7k test lines) is go-to-k/cdkd#2277, and widening the critic's scope beyond `src/local` is go-to-k/cdkd#2276. Deleting a subsystem is a different review question ("was it really unreachable?") from adding a critic, and bundling them puts two unrelated risk judgements in one diff.

## Verification

`vp run test` **806 files / 16,608 tests**, all pass. `vp run check` 0 errors, `typecheck:test` 0, `build` 0. The CI step lands inside `check-build-test` (verified by parsing the YAML).

Note for merging: this touches `src/local/**` — comments only, but the `integ-local` gate is path-based, not content-based — so it needs a Docker `local-*` integ before it can merge.

body:
## Ownership claim

- Machine ID: `mbp-m5-max-128`
- Agent/session ID: `claude-c549c51b`
- Task: undate the pin comments
- Claimed paths: `docs/GENE_SCREEN.md`, `src/ai/advanced/gene_ledger.rs`
- Coordinated with: #2553, #2554
- Related issue/request: operator request ("fix all problems you see")

## What changed

**A comment I wrote this morning was falsified eight hours later by a tournament, and no test could have caught it.**

#2536 pinned nine genes on above the batch rule and documented *why* they were overrides by restating their columns: "all nine read `off` at clause 4 — each is positive in the two newest batches and negative in the third". True at 05:15Z. The 2,576-game batch published in #2551 rotated the columns, and **seven of the nine now read `on` by the rule itself**:

| gene | Last | Prior | Third | rule |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `army-target-weighs-enemy` | +5 | +9 | +31 | on |
| `buildings-before-projects` | +13 | +1 | +8 | on |
| `early-contact-window` | +10 | +17 | +2 | on |
| `founder-temple` | +1 | +8 | +6 | on |
| `lane-great-people` | −8 | +22 | +21 | on |
| `research-tier-premium` | +34 | +15 | +8 | on |
| `settler-screen` | +1 | +4 | +5 | on |
| `deals-for-our-gain` | +21 | −10 | +10 | off — mean exactly 7 |
| `idle-faith-patronage` | +1 | −18 | +17 | off |

(Read as evidence about the pins rather than as an argument for them: the batch that priced these is the first run in which the nine were on, so it is not a clean test of the same question.)

The fix is not to write the new numbers down. A column is a measurement that moves whenever a batch enters, so **any** prose restating one is wrong by the next tournament, silently, with nothing red. Both comments now state the invariant — a pin ships whatever the rule reads — and point at `rules.batch_decisions` and `batch_columns`, which are regenerated. Each keeps a short ⚠ recording the episode so the next writer does not reach for the same shortcut.

`docs/GENE_SCREEN.md` also gains a ⚠ under *Above the rule, the operator's pins* saying it in general terms, since that section is where someone writing the next directive will be reading.

The closing comment in `the_operator_pins_ship_above_the_rule` had the same problem and is replaced by what its assertion actually defends: no pin today is unpriced, and the day one is, that is worth noticing rather than discovering later from a genome nobody can explain.

**`tools/genes.py`'s `OPERATOR_DEFAULT_ON` comment carries the same stale sentence and is deliberately not touched here** — #2553 ("Set selected heuristic gene defaults") claims that file and is rewriting that exact block, so editing it would only manufacture a conflict. The finding is recorded on #2553 with the table above; if that PR lands without fixing it, the line is `tools/genes.py:519` and this PR is the template.

No behaviour change: comments only, plus one Markdown paragraph.

author: jerhaad
body:
The nightly implement job's stranded-work scan adopts any `~/wt/issue-*` tree with commits, no remote branch, and an open issue. It does not check whether the pipeline made it.

On a match it runs a `--yolo` agent in that tree, then `git add -A`, `git commit --amend`, a push, and a draft PR. A person's working checkout matching that glob gets their uncommitted work staged, their commit rewritten, and a PR opened from their branch — unattended, at 5am.

A marker in the worktree's gitdir claims trees the job created. Unmarked trees are skipped, so existing checkouts are never adopted.

Verified against real worktrees: three unmarked trees skip, adding the marker adopts, removing it returns to skip, and the marker is invisible to `git status` so a repair's `add -A` cannot stage it.

Also ignores `__pycache__`/`*.pyc`, which the same `add -A` will otherwise commit — one had already been staged into a commit this way.

- **`security.yml`** — commit-range gitleaks, blocking, same event-injection hygiene as open-pan-bpa''s gate. Job name `gitleaks (secret scan)` so it can join the main ruleset''s required checks.
- **`dependabot.yml`** — pip + github-actions, weekly.

author: hota1024
body:
`skills/kobune/SKILL.md` is the only instruction an agent gets, and several of
its claims did not match the CLI. The worst of them sat in the recovery an
agent reaches for first when a code change appears not to have worked.

Each claim below was checked against the source and against a binary built at
`b933523`.

## What was wrong

**`up`, `down` and `logs` name services positionally.** The Skill said to run
`kobune down --service api && kobune up --service api`. There is no such flag
on those commands, so clap rejects it outright:

```console
$ kobune down --service api
error: unexpected argument '--service' found
```

`docs/AGENT-RUN.md` §3 and `docs/DESIGN.md` §10 carried the same form.
`env ls` and `env get` are the two commands that really do take `--service`.

**`env` values expand, and a `command` expands nothing.** The Skill had both
backwards, and contradicted itself on the first forty lines further down.
`${NAME}` is expanded in an `env` value and a bare `$NAME` is not
(`crates/kobune-core/src/env.rs` `expand_value`), which is what the cache
advice rests on — `"$KOBUNE_CACHE_DIR/pnpm"` makes a directory of that name
inside the worktree. A `command` is split into argv by `shell_words::split`
and run directly (`apps/daemon/src/spec.rs:232`), so neither form expands
there without an explicit `sh -c`.

**The configuration layers were the wrong way up**, in the Skill and on the
reference page it sends agents off to read. `ConfigLayer::ORDER` is
`[Global, Project, Local]` with later layers winning, so
`~/.kobune/config.toml` merges *under* `kobune.toml` rather than over it.
`kobune.local.toml` is anchored on the main worktree, not on whichever
`kobune.toml` the search found — the distinction that only shows itself in a
worktree, which is all the Skill is about. And `kobune.toml` itself is
per-branch rather than one file every worktree shares.

**Smaller, and all of a kind.** `env ls` masks what you set, down to bullets
alone below five characters, and a secret stays a reference even under
`--reveal`. `env set` reaches three of the four layers, not four — `--scope
service` is refused on purpose. `unknown` was missing from the service states,
while `idle` is a state no runtime emits. And "do not write `.env`" named a
file that is not an env layer at all but the application's own, which
`[project] carry` exists to copy into a new worktree.

`DESIGN.md` §10 also listed `--from` for `--base`, a positional workspace for
`kobune rm`, a `--since` that does not exist, `init` doing the privileged
setup that is `kobune setup`, and none of `env get`, `daemon`, `skill` or
`update`. `kobune open` stays, marked as sketched and never built, because
`HomeSteps.vue` points at it for exactly that reason.

Two code comments went with them: `env.rs` and `environment.rs` both still
said three env layers, which is the number `DESIGN.md` was mirroring.

## Checked

- `node .claude/skills/prose/scripts/check.mjs` — 45 files, nothing to report
- `cd docs && pnpm build`
- `cargo build --bin kobune` — `SKILL.md` is `include_str!`d, so it ships with
  the binary and reaches users on the next build
- every command form now written in these files was run against the binary and
  parses

author: petturick
altecbx
body:
## The finding

> 613 names ranked · **24 had their option chain measured** · **0 qualified** · **76 skipped for earnings inside the option's life**

The sell board doesn't scan. It reads whatever the Premium Edge scan measured. And that scan's funnel scores like this:

```python
score = rvol_rank                    # 0-100
if 0 <= days_to_earnings <= 7:   score += 30
elif 0 <= days_to_earnings <= 21: score += 15
```

The sell board then **refuses every name with earnings inside the option's life.**

Both rules are correct for their own tab — the richest premium really does live around a report, and a hold-to-expiry seller really cannot underwrite one. `setup_board`'s docstring already noted the signs were opposed. What nobody caught is that **one of them was choosing the shopping list for both.**

So the funnel was buying chains for names the board was guaranteed to throw away, and the board reported it as *"nothing qualifies today"* — a claim about the market that was partly a claim about its own shopping list.

## The fix

Stage 1 now produces **two slates from one screen**:

| slate | size | contents |
|---|---|---|
| event | `stage2_n` = 24 | today's scoring, unchanged — Premium Edge's question |
| seller | `stage2_seller_n` = 10 | only names with **no** report inside `seller_horizon_days` = 47 |

47 = a 45-day option plus the board's own 2-day buffer. A test asserts it equals `45 + setup_board.EARNINGS_BUFFER_DAYS`, so the two can't drift apart again.

**The seller slate is additional, not taken out of the event slate** — fixing one tab by starving the other isn't a fix. A test asserts the event slate is bit-identical with the seller slate on and off.

### Ranked on evidence, not a proxy

The scan has been recording `iv30`, `erv30` and `vrp_ratio` per ticker per day all along. For a name it has already measured, there's no reason to rank by a *proxy for* richness when richness itself is on file.

- a reading counts only if it's **≤10 days old** — premium moves, and a fortnight-old number presented as current is worse than saying we don't know
- stale or future-dated → treated as **no** reading, not weak evidence
- no reading → falls back to the rvol proxy, which is also how new names keep entering
- store lookups bounded to **3× the slate size**, so a 600-name board never becomes 600 file opens

### A missing earnings date keeps a name out

Missing is not absent, and the board is going to trust this list.

## What this deliberately does NOT do

**The forecaster is untouched.** It was measured earlier to run ~24% high in the top realized-vol decile — but every correction tried traded bias for accuracy in the direction that costs a seller money. The honest fix was to stop concentrating the scan in that decile rather than bend the forecast toward the answer we wanted. The seller slate does that as a side effect.

**The `1.05×` floor stays**, and now says why in place. Before v4.65 the forecast read low, so the floor was quietly looser than it looked — nearer 1.02 in effect. Lowering it now would pay for that correction twice, and would move a risk preference in the same breath as a correctness fix, leaving no way to tell which one changed the board.

## Tests

Nine guards in `TestTheFunnelServesBothQuestions`, **each verified to fail against the previous funnel** (9 errors when `edge_scan.py` is reverted) — including the bounded-I/O check and the horizon-drift check.

**2,838 Python tests, 114 UI guards, 19 clock tests** green, checked by explicit exit code.

author: sonika-shah
body:
### Problem On a **recursive CSV import** (the whole-tree path the UI uses when importing at service/database/schema level), a table's **foreign-key relationship edge** (the `RELATED_TO` / ER graph link between the two tables) was **dropped** — even though the `tableConstraints` JSON on the table was preserved. This was flagged by greptile on #31863 (and its backport #32095). It's a **pre-existing** issue, not introduced by #31863: before that PR the recursive path dropped both the JSON and the edge; #31863 restored the JSON, leaving the edge drop exposed. ### Root cause The bulk relationship path for tables is asymmetric: - `clearEntitySpecificRelationshipsForMany` deletes **both** the schema `CONTAINS` edge **and** the FK `RELATED_TO` edge. - `storeEntitySpecificRelationshipsForMany` re-added **only** `CONTAINS`. The single-entity path is fine (`storeEntity` → `addConstraintRelationship`), which is why **non-recursive** imports (they re-PUT each table through the single path) keep the edge — only the recursive/bulk path drops it. ### Fix After the bulk `CONTAINS` insert, re-add the constraint `RELATED_TO` edges via `addConstraintRelationship`, mirroring the single-entity store path. (`addConstraintRelationship` only acts on constraints with `referredColumns`, i.e. foreign keys; PK/UNIQUE are no-ops.) ### Test `DatabaseServiceResourceIT#test_importExportRecursive_preservesTableConstraints` now also asserts the `RELATED_TO` edge survives a recursive round trip, reading it from the relationship DAO (deterministic — the search-backed ER endpoint is eventually consistent). **GREEN** with the fix (`Tests run: 1, Failures: 0`). Also verified before/after on a live stack (direct `entity_relationship` query): without the fix the FK edge is dropped by a recursive import; with the fix it survives, while the `tableConstraints` JSON is preserved in both cases. ### Scope Separate from the CSV constraint/custom-property PRs (#31863 and its backports #32095 / #32096) — this addresses only the ER relationship-edge gap greptile flagged. Backports to 1.13 / 2.0 to follow once this merges.

Greptile Summary

 This PR restores table foreign-key `RELATED_TO` edges during recursive and bulk relationship reconstruction. - Resolves referenced table FQNs in one batched lookup and inserts FK edges alongside containment relationships. - Extends the recursive CSV round-trip integration test to verify the persisted relationship edge directly through the relationship DAO.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 The PR appears safe to merge. No blocking failure remains.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | openmetadata-service/src/main/java/org/openmetadata/service/jdbi3/TableRepository.java | Rebuilds FK `RELATED_TO` relationships in the bulk table relationship-storage path using batched target resolution and insertion. | | openmetadata-integration-tests/src/test/java/org/openmetadata/it/tests/DatabaseServiceResourceIT.java | Verifies that a recursive CSV round trip preserves both foreign-key constraint metadata and its persisted relationship edge. |

Flowchart

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart LR A[Recursive CSV import] --> B[Persist table entities] B --> C[Clear table-specific relationships] C --> D[Rebuild schema CONTAINS edges] C --> E[Resolve FK target table FQNs] E --> F[Build RELATED_TO edges] D --> G[Bulk insert relationships] F --> G G --> H[Persisted table relationship graph] ```
Reviews (2): Last reviewed commit: ["perf(csv): batch FK edge restore; skip u..."](https://github.com/open-metadata/openmetadata/commit/4482fac6cd3e4b09c86ce544f79ad21bd0a5a45e) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=57080627) **Context used:** - Knowledge Base — [Metadata entity lifecycle](https://app.greptile.com/getcollate/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/open-metadata/openmetadata/-/docs/metadata-entity-lifecycle.md)

author: john-t-white
body:
Second of three pull requests for #32, and the compliance layer the issue puts
above the mechanics #33 landed. `tools/review-state/` already computes who owns
which thread, who owes a verdict, and what round each agent is on; it reports
that and nothing asserts it, which is why the skill's step 3 asked a reader to
notice a number had gone up. Severity's rule and the agent-definition
provenance follow in the third pull request, branched from `main` after this
merges.

## What changed

`tools/review-state/check.mjs` fails a round on an agent that did not post, a
thread its owner left unverdicted, a round not posted through
`tools/review-post/`, a finding with no anchor, two agents on one line with no
link between their threads, and a round over the minor-findings cap.
`review-state.mjs check --pr <n> --dispatched <spec>` runs it and exits 1.

## Judgement calls

**A subcommand on `review-state.mjs`, not a second tool.** The check consumes
exactly the payload that tool already fetches, calls the functions that already
compute most of it, and replaces a step that already re-ran that exact command.
A `tools/review-check/` would have carried a second copy of the GraphQL query
and the `gh` plumbing. The report path is unchanged and still the default.

**The dispatch comes in as an argument.** `--dispatched review-code=2,
review-security=3` is the agents the round actually ran and the round each was
told to run — which the skill has from step 1 and already puts in every
dispatch. Nothing is written between the two steps: the agents have no tool
that writes a file, and step 1 is deliberate about leaving nothing behind that
could go stale or collide on a second round. An agent left out of the round on
purpose is left out of the spec, which is what stops "nobody ran it" and "it
found nothing" from looking alike — the distinction the skill could previously
only ask for in prose.

**"Posted through the command" is checked, and two other checks then rest on
it.** `payload.mjs` writes the round record in one form, so a body that does
not parse is one an agent composed itself — and nothing then guarantees its
findings were prefixed, tagged, or anchored. Because that check establishes the
body is the command's own, the cap can be read straight off the count the
command wrote, with no need to attribute individual threads to rounds. The
anchor check works the same way: `review-post` tags a file-level finding
differently, so a thread with no line and no `file-level` marker is one the
command did not post.

**Only the round each agent was dispatched to run is checked for form.**
Earlier rounds predate `review-post` and could not be in its form. The
per-thread checks are not scoped that way: an unanchored finding or an unlinked
sibling stays wrong until it is fixed, whoever owns it, and re-failing until
then is the pressure working.

**`state.mjs` gains one `export` and nothing else.** #32 puts rewriting its
functions out of scope. `anchor` was already there, private; the check names
threads the same way the report does rather than carrying its own copy.

**The skill's `main`-copy block became a directory extract.** It copied two
named blobs and said what would break it:

> the day `main`'s `review-state.mjs` imports a third file, copying two blobs
> leaves `node` failing on the missing import

`check.mjs` is that third file. `git archive main tools/review-state | tar -x`
is not a file count that has to be maintained. The chaining and the
"must produce a report or nothing" property are kept.

**This pull request cannot be checked by its own check.** It touches
`tools/review-state/`, so `REVIEW.md`'s rule puts `main`'s copy in force for
its review — and `main`'s copy has no `check` subcommand. Same self-reference
#33 had; it takes effect from the merge.

## Test plan

### First commit — the check itself

`tests/tools/review-state/check.test.mjs` was written before `check.mjs`
existed and run first — one failing file:

    $ node --test tests/tools/review-state/
    # tests 43
    # pass 42
    # fail 1
    # Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../tools/review-state/check.mjs'

One case per failure the check has to catch, each stated as a round it must
reject, plus the rounds it must not: a verdict that answered an earlier commit,
a resolved thread, a file-level finding that says so, a thread nobody claimed,
a linked pair, one agent owning two threads on one line, two threads a line
apart, and a cap that held at three however many were summarized away. Writing
that first is what turned up two bugs in the cases themselves — a dispatched
agent given no round to post, and `no-round` doing duty for a double post,
which is now `extra-round`.

    $ node --test tests/tools/
    # tests 103
    # pass 103
    # fail 0

### Second commit — round 1's findings

Four cases added and six changed, each written before the fix it covers. Red
first, one case per finding:

    $ node --test tests/tools/review-state/check.test.mjs
    # tests 34
    # pass 28
    # fail 6
    not ok - is not a failure on a thread the round itself raised
    not ok - a round record numbering a different round is its own failure
    not ok - reads a round whose held-back summary contains a paren
    not ok - is a failure when the thread carries no severity tag
    not ok - is not a failure on two file-level threads in one file
    not ok - reports every one of them

The four new cases are the failures round 1 found, stated as rounds the check
must stop misjudging: a thread the round itself raised (no verdict is owed on
it), a thread raised in an earlier round (one is), two file-level threads in
one file (not a sibling pair), and a held-back summary containing a close paren
(a body the command itself wrote). The six changed cases follow the two kinds
that split — `hand-posted` into `wrong-round`, `unanchored` into `untagged` —
and the round records that now carry a timestamp.

Green after the fixes, with the existing suite unchanged:

    $ node --test tests/tools/
    # tests 107
    # pass 107
    # fail 0

The fixture `pr-29.json` is not reused: it predates `review-post`, so its round
bodies are the old form and its findings carry no severity tag. The new cases
build their payloads locally, in the style `state.test.mjs` uses.

### Third commit — round 2's blocking finding

Two cases added and the test helper changed, both written before the fix. Red
first:

    $ node --test tests/tools/review-state/check.test.mjs
    # tests 36
    # pass 34
    # fail 2
    not ok - is not a failure on a thread that has merely gone outdated
    not ok - is a failure on two outdated threads that shared a line

The helper now takes `subjectType` and `originalLine`, because a null `line`
was carrying two meanings and the cases have to be able to say which they
mean. The three existing file-level cases became explicit about being
file-level; nothing else about them changed.

    $ node --test tests/tools/
    # tests 109
    # pass 109
    # fail 0

### Fourth commit — round 3's findings

One case, written first, for the false pair `review-code` reproduced:

    $ node --test tests/tools/review-state/check.test.mjs
    # tests 37
    # pass 36
    # fail 1
    not ok - does not pair a live thread with an outdated one at the same number

    $ node --test tests/tools/
    # tests 110
    # pass 110
    # fail 0

The orphaned doc block in the same commit has nothing to run: it is a comment
moved back onto the function it describes, checked by reading the file.

### Checked by hand, against the live API

- `check` with no `--dispatched`, with `review-everything=1`, and with
  `review-code=x` each exited 2 before any fetch was made.
- `check --pr 29 --dispatched review-code=3,review-security=2` — the true
  dispatch for that pull request — exited 1 with
  `did not post through tools/review-post/` for both, which is correct: #29's
  rounds predate the command.
- `check --pr 29 --dispatched review-code=9` exited 1 w

author: roccobot
body:
## Che cosa cambia

Il tracciato viene dal secondo giro delle proposte, quello **H**: due tessere con 3dp di
stacco, quella dietro tagliata a elle perché l'altra le sta davanti, e la scacchiera sulla
tessera davanti. Scelta dell'utente **come segnaposto**, non come icona definitiva.

## Segue il tema su entrambi i livelli, non solo sul fondo

Il colore del glifo è una risorsa come quello dello sfondo, quindi `values/` e `values-night/`
ne dànno due versioni intere. Flippare solo il fondo avrebbe lasciato un glifo chiaro su fondo
chiaro in uno dei due temi.

| tema | fondo | glifo | contrasto |
|---|---|---|---|
| chiaro | `#E7EEF3` | `#1B5A86` | **6,28** |
| scuro | `#12222E` | `#7FC0F0` | **8,27** |

Misurate, non scelte a occhio, contro il **3:1** che serve a una grafica. Stessa famiglia di
tinta nelle due, perché l'icona deve leggersi come la stessa app e non come due.

⚠️ **Quale delle due compare la risolve il launcher** con la configurazione di sistema, quindi
segue il tema del dispositivo; ma i launcher tengono in cache le icone con una certa
insistenza, e il cambio può arrivare in ritardo. Da Android 13 c'è anche la strada delle icone
a tema, che tinge il livello `monochrome`.

## Due difetti trovati prima di scrivere il file

Nessuno dei due si vedeva a schermo, ed è la ragione per cui vale scriverli:

- **Le due tessere sono disgiunte.** Con i contorni sovrapposti la somma `evenOdd` spezzava
  quella davanti in due pezzi separati da una fascia vuota, e il risultato reso non somigliava
  a quello che c'era scritto nella proposta. Lo stacco di 3dp è quello che si legge come 'sta
  davanti', e non ha bisogno di nessuna sovrapposizione.
- **Il braccio della elle non regge una coppia qualsiasi di raggi.** 9 fuori più 4 di raccordo
  non stanno nei suoi 12dp: il tratto verticale tornava **indietro di un'unità** e il contorno
  si sovrapponeva a sé stesso. Succede su un segmento diritto, quindi si vede solo leggendo il
  path generato, non guardando l'icona. Il raccordo scende a 3 e i due tratti diventano di
  lunghezza zero.

Il punto più lontano dal centro è a **31,6** dei 33 ammessi dal cerchio sicuro da 66dp.

## `monochrome`

Riusa questo stesso file. Il sistema ne tiene solo l'alfa e mette la propria tinta, quindi una
forma piatta a un colore è esattamente quello che gli serve, e un secondo file divergerebbe dal
primo al primo ritocco.

## Versione

`versionName` **0.12**, e `versionCode` passa a **2**. Non è un dettaglio: la 0.11 è uscita col
numero 1, e senza crescere Android rifiuta l'aggiornamento come se fosse un ritorno indietro.
Nessuno lo controlla, quindi nessuno lo ricorderebbe.

⚠️ **Il merge non pubblica**: la pubblicazione la fa il tag `v0.12`, che va creato dall'utente.

body:
This fixes a bug in multi-shelf search results where pressing or swiping up (and/or left/right with a grid keyboard depending on the language) would always switch focus to the tvOS native keyboard instead of focusing on another search item.

The fix is a bit unexpected: make `-shouldUpdateFocusInContext:` in CobaltSearchResultsController always deny requests to switch focus away from the web contents view. This makes everything work as expected.

But, contrary to expected, this does not make it impossible to ever focus the native keyboard: when reaching the end of the results (i.e. there is nothing else to focus up/left/right), Kabuki eventually calls `OnScreenKeyboard.focus()` which disables user interaction in the web contents view and forces a focus update. Under this circumstance, `-shouldUpdateFocusInContext:` ends up not being called and CobaltSearchResultsController just receives the notification that a focus change has happened in
`-didUpdateFocusInContext:withAnimationCoordinator`.

Tested on the device (running tvOS 26.6) with Linear and Grid keyboards in English (LTR) and Arabic (RTL).

Fixed: 546217920

author: mobeenabdullah
body:
Next piece of the class-usage write path. The filter that decides which collections the hook does anything for.

## Why it reads live configuration

The write path registers ONE hook for every collection, so most calls reach it with nothing to do. Reading a list captured when the plugin was wired would miss a collection created afterwards, and a blocks field added to an existing one — both of which happen through the Schema Builder at runtime.

## Why most of the tests are about malformed input

Configuration reaches a hook as whatever the host wrote, including from untyped JavaScript and from the Schema Builder's stored JSON payloads. Each case below is a way the filter can be wrong in a direction that is invisible afterwards:

- **A string `"true"` reads as NOT localized.** JSON carries strings; a truthiness check would read this as localized, file one document's classes under every language, and leave the `""` subject — the one a read actually resolves — holding none. The document's classes would then be invisible to the count that decides whether a class is safe to delete.
- **A field with no usable name is skipped, not defaulted.** The name IS the `field` column every row is keyed by, so an empty one collects every unnamed field's rows into a single subject — and the reconciler then deletes each field's rows on behalf of the others.
- **A duplicate name yields ONE subject.** Reconciling the same rows twice in one pass makes the second pass read the first's inserts as rows the document no longer justifies, so a correct document ends with its own classes deleted.

## The scope limit, and why it is deliberate rather than pending

**Top-level fields only.** A blocks field nested inside a group or repeater is not indexed — because the rebuild reads `item[field]` and cannot resolve a nested path either. Indexing one here would create rows that no rebuild could ever reconcile or sweep, which is the permanently-stranded state.

The two halves have to agree about what a subject IS, and the cheapest way to keep them agreeing is for both to look in the same place. Widening them is one change, not two. This also settles the nested-paths thread declined on #1221: the answer is symmetry, not deferral.

## Test plan

Eight cases. Three properties break-verified individually, **each break confirmed to compile against a clean baseline**:

| break | test killed |
| --- | --- |
| truthiness instead of a strict boolean | `reads a STRING "true" as not localized` |
| accept an empty field name | `skips a field with no usable name` |
| stop de-duplicating names | `yields ONE subject rather than two` |

The baseline was NOT clean on the first attempt — `BlocksField.tsx` could not resolve `@nextlyhq/builder/shell` exports because this branch was cut from a newer `main` without rebuilding. A red that appears with and without the change is evidence of nothing, so the breaks were re-run after `pnpm --filter <pkg>... build`.

Gates, each exit status read separately: build 0 · vitest 0 (384 passing) · check-types 0 · lint 0 · root eslint 0 · fallow `verdict: pass` with all four `*_introduced` at 0.

## Pre-existing failure, flagged rather than silenced

`node scripts/check-comment-convention.mjs` exits 1, on files this PR does not touch:

- `.github/workflows/code-hygiene.yml` — 3 offences
- `packages/builder/src/breakpoint-action-styles.test.ts` — 1 offence

**Established as pre-existing with a control:** the same script exits 1 on `origin/main` itself. This PR's diff is exactly two new files, neither of them these. The allowlist may only shrink and an entry must not be added to silence a comment, so these want rewriting by whoever owns them rather than suppressing here.

## Changeset

Skipped — the module is internal, not exported from the package entry, and adds no API a host can call. The changeset lands with the hook that consumes it, where the behaviour becomes user-facing.

author: chokobole
body:
## Description

Slice 1 of #324.

**These four rows wrap in-tree oracles, which is what makes them removable
without losing coverage.** `HostKeccak256` wraps `keccak.testing.reference.sponge`,
`HostGrostl256` wraps `grostl.testing.reference.grostl256`, and likewise for
Ascon and RIPEMD-160. So what their sweeps assert is the device kernel against
that oracle, across every padding boundary, batched — and `HostRow` contributes
only the per-row loop to that. The sweeps therefore stay and call the oracle
directly.

Test counts are unchanged on every family: grostl 39, ascon 54, ripemd160 35,
keccak256 15. Same lengths, same values, same batch-equals-per-message claim.

**#243's precondition turns out not to be one.** It asked for out-of-tree golden
vectors at Keccak-256's absorb boundaries *before* deleting that row, because no
published vector fills a 136-byte rate block and it read the boundary sweep as
dying with the row. Keeping the sweep against the same `reference.sponge` the
row wrapped makes this deletion coverage-neutral instead.

That freeze is still worth doing on its own terms, and this PR does not do it:
`reference_test` anchors the sponge against `hashlib` on SHA3-256 and SHAKE —
which carries the permutation, the absorb, the multi-rate padding and the
squeeze — but the domain byte that makes it Keccak rather than SHA-3 still rests
on the published vectors alone. Strengthening that is a separate change, and
#243 can stay open for it.

Verified rather than asserted: wiring the Keccak oracle to `SHA3_SUFFIX` fails
all six boundary lengths, so the new comparison is live and not a tautology.

#243's open question — whether to retire the category or only Keccak-256's row —
is answered by #324: the category.

## Related Issues/PRs

Part of #324. Closes nothing on its own; #243 stays open for the golden-vector
strengthening described above.

author: daniloleonecarneiro
body:
## Problema

Salvar um contato novo pela tela leva o usuário para `/contacts/undefined` e dispara `GET /api/v1/contacts/undefined?include_contact_inboxes=true`. O contato é criado no banco; o que quebra é a navegação logo depois.

A causa é uma divergência de formato entre os verbos do mesmo recurso. Medido contra o backend rodando:

| rota | `data` contém |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/contacts` | `{ contact: {...}, contact_inbox: {...} }` — aninhado |
| `GET /api/v1/contacts/:id` | `{ id, name, email, ... }` — na raiz |
| `PATCH /api/v1/contacts/:id` | `{ id, name, email, ... }` — na raiz |

`createContact` devolvia `extractData<Contact>(response)`, e o `extractData` desembrulha um nível só (retorna `response.data.data`). No POST isso entrega o envelope `{ contact, contact_inbox }`, não o contato — então `.id` é `undefined`. O cast `as T` impede o TypeScript de acusar a diferença.

## Mudança

O desembrulho fica num helper aplicado aos **dois** ramos do create — o de `FormData` (com avatar) e o de JSON. O helper aceita a forma plana como fallback, então se o backend um dia normalizar o POST para responder igual ao GET, o front continua funcionando sem deploy casado.

`updateContact` não foi tocado: o PATCH já responde na raiz, então ele nunca teve o problema.

## Por que no frontend e não no backend

Achatar a resposta do POST seria quebra de contrato de API, e o `contact_inbox` que vem junto precisaria de outro lugar. O consumidor sabe desembrulhar; a API mantém o que já publicou.

## Como validar

```
npx vitest run src/services/contacts/contactsService.createContact.spec.ts
```

3 exemplos: o shape aninhado do POST, o mesmo pelo ramo de avatar, e o fallback para a forma plana. Com o fix revertido, 2 dos 3 falham. `tsc --noEmit` limpo.

## Summary by Sourcery

Corrija o retorno da criação de contatos para lidar com os diferentes formatos de resposta da API.

Bug Fixes:
- Corrija a criação de contatos para retornar corretamente o contato quando a resposta do POST vier aninhada, evitando navegação para `/contacts/undefined`.
- Mantenha compatibilidade com respostas planas do backend e aplique a correção tanto à criação com JSON quanto à criação com avatar.

Tests:
- Adicione testes para respostas aninhadas nos fluxos JSON e FormData, além do fallback para respostas planas.

author: chaxus
body:
The first version concatenated the markup by hand, on the assumption that
`ranui/builder` needs a browser DOM and this is a node build script. That
assumption was never checked, and it is wrong: the builder falls back to ranui's
own DOM mock when there is no `document`, so the ecosystem rule -- construct DOM
with the builder, not by hand -- applies here exactly as it does in the browser.

Using `View()`/`Div()` directly then ran into a second thing. They pick between
the mock and `document.createElement` by environment, and this file renders the
same pages in two: node for the real build, jsdom under vitest. A real document
lowercases the attribute names of an element made with `createElement`, so
`viewBox` came back as `viewbox` -- SVG reads it case-sensitively, so the icon
would not have rendered -- and the two environments produced different bytes for
the same page, which fails `check()` (the test that a fresh render would not
change a committed page) permanently.

So this uses `HTMLElementMock`, which `ranui/builder` exports, through two small
helpers. Same behaviour in both environments, and attributes and text are
escaped on the way out -- the part hand-written HTML gets wrong quietly. What
the rule is actually after is intact: no concatenated markup, no hand-rolled
`escapeHtml` at each interpolation.

It also turned up a real gap upstream: the builders have no `createElementNS`
path at all (`utils/builder/core.ts` only calls `document.createElement`), so in
a real browser they cannot construct SVG -- `View('svg')` yields an
`HTMLUnknownElement` with lowercased attributes. Anyone using them for an icon
will hit it. Noted in the exploration for a follow-up in chaxus/ran.

2870 unit tests and the language-menu e2e pass; the generated `viewBox` keeps
its casing, and the jsdom render now matches the committed page byte for byte.

author: take-cheeze
body:
## Summary

Ports **AWQ** (Lin et al., 2023, ["AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00978)) -- an onnxsim-native reimplementation of the *algorithm*, not any framework's code.

## Why this, and not a `pytorch/ao`/MSLK integration

Following up on `pytorch/ao` (torchao) as a possible next vendor target: research into torchao itself, and into `meta-pytorch/MSLK` (the closed-form kernel library torchao's own int4 path delegates to), both turned up **no real ONNX interop point**. Both quantize live PyTorch `nn.Module`s with runtime-only tensor subclasses/CUDA kernels, with no ONNX export path (a related `pytorch/ao` issue asking for one was closed "not planned"; MSLK has zero "onnx" hits anywhere in its repo).

AWQ's *algorithm* itself, unlike either framework's implementation, needs nothing but a weight tensor, a round-to-nearest block-wise integer quantizer, and real calibration activations -- exactly `quantize_weight_only_int4`'s own scheme and `adaround.py`'s own "post-hoc adjustment from real activations" style. So it ports cleanly on that basis alone, independent of whether the frameworks that popularized it have any ONNX story.

## How it works

AWQ's key empirical observation: not every weight element matters equally to a layer's output -- a weight column feeding a large-magnitude *activation* channel dominates that channel's contribution to the output, so quantization error there costs more than an equal-sized error on a column whose activation is small. Round-to-nearest treats every element identically regardless of this, and AdaRound's per-element rounding optimization never touches a weight's own magnitude, only which quantization bin it lands in -- both a different lever than what AWQ pulls.

AWQ instead rescales entire input-channel columns of the weight upward in proportion to that channel's own average activation magnitude before quantizing -- inflating a salient column's share of its block's dynamic range so round-to-nearest's fixed per-block step size costs it proportionally less -- and applies the exact inverse scale to the activation via a new `Mul` node inserted right before the layer, so the transformation is a no-op on the *unquantized* function.

Implemented as a pure-Python post-hoc pass (`onnxsim/awq.py`), reusing `adaround.py`'s own MatMul/Gemm candidate-matching and INT4 packing helpers (same target scheme). For every `quantize_weight_only_int4`-quantized layer: grid-searches a scalar exponent `alpha` (matching the AWQ paper's own grid search, not a closed-form guarantee) for the per-channel scale, re-quantizing the rescaled weight from scratch at each candidate and measuring real reconstruction error. `alpha=0` (plain round-to-nearest) is always a candidate, so a layer AWQ can't improve keeps its original quantization untouched with no inserted node at all.

## Verification

- A dedicated test builds a deliberately salient-channel calibration scenario (a few input channels carrying much larger activation magnitude than the rest -- AWQ's own motivating case) and confirms AWQ's measured reconstruction error is strictly lower than plain round-to-nearest's on the same data.
- A second test uses uniform activation magnitude (no channel more salient than any other) and confirms the `alpha=0` no-op path produces a **byte-identical** model to plain `quantize_weight_only_int4`, with no `Mul` inserted -- proving AWQ never makes things worse when there's nothing to gain.
- Further tests cover `Gemm` with `transB=1`, codes staying within the scheme's `[-7, 7]` range, and end-to-end `onnxruntime` execution.
- Full regression sweep: `tests/` (excluding torch/timm-dependent modules not installed in this environment) -- **449 passed, 68 skipped, 0 failed**.
- `ruff format` / `ruff check` / `mypy` clean.

## New files

- `onnxsim/awq.py`
- `tests/test_awq.py` -- 6 tests

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_awq.py -v`
- [x] `pytest tests/test_adaround.py tests/test_bias_correction.py tests/test_weight_only_quantize_int4.py -q`
- [x] Full `tests/` sweep (torch/timm-dependent modules excluded, not installed in this environment)
- [x] `ruff format` / `ruff check` / `mypy`

author: ruel225
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #130059 — a late provider status callback (e.g. a delayed "completed"/"initiated" webhook) arriving after `finalizeCall` removed the call from the active maps births a **phantom zero-duration call record under the default agent** (`main`), and (per ClawSweeper P1 review) a late inbound `call.initiated` on such a record would also queue `answerCall` for an already-ended call.

Root cause: `findCall` (`extensions/voice-call/src/manager/lookup.ts`) only consults the in-memory active maps. `finalizeCall` (`lifecycle.ts:65-66`) removes the record from `activeCalls` and `providerCallIdMap`, and records no dedupe key for the provider's eventual terminal callback (`rememberManagerReplayKey` is only called for `call.ended`/`call.error` in `processEvent`). So when the provider's late terminal callback arrives:

1. Its dedupe key is fresh → passes the dedupe gate.
2. `findCall` misses (the record is gone from the active maps).
3. The auto-register branch (`events.ts:182`) fabricates a fresh record via `createWebhookCall` — new callId, `agentId="main"` (default), `ringing`→`completed`, zero duration.

Result: wrong agent attribution (the real owner, e.g. `agent-sales`, is replaced by `main`) and duplicate call-history entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

Producer-first repair at the birth site, in three parts:

**Part A — consult the store before fabricating.** Before fabricating, consult the persistent store by `providerCallId`; if a record already owns this id, fold the event into it instead of birthing a phantom.

- `store.ts`: add `findCallByProviderCallIdInStore` — a sync helper reusing `readCallHistoryFromStore`'s scan (the webhook event path is sync and cannot await the existing async `findCallMatchesInStore`).
- `events.ts` auto-register branch: query the store before `createWebhookCall`; fold into an existing owner when found.

**Part B — fence terminal records from live side effects (ClawSweeper P1).** Folding a terminal record is not enough: the event then fell through to the normal `switch (event.type)`, so a late inbound `call.initiated` on an ended call queued `answerCall` (an answer action to the carrier for a dead call), and `call.answered` would arm a duration timer + fire `onCallAnswered`. When the fold resolves a **terminal** record, absorb the echo instead — persist + record the dedupe key and return without running live side effects. `transitionState` is already a no-op on terminal records, so the only behavioral change is suppressing the provider/timer/callback effects that should never run on an ended call.

**Part C — resolve a Plivo provider alias to the newest snapshot (ClawSweeper P1 finding 2).** Plivo transitions a call's `providerCallId` from `request_uuid` (at outbound creation, `plivo.ts:392`) to `CallUUID` (on later callbacks, `plivo.ts:284`), and the store appends a snapshot per event rather than upserting — so one logical call is retained under both ids. `findCallByProviderCallIdInStore`/`findCallMatchesInStore` matched only the **stale pre-terminal snapshot** when a late status callback carried the old `request_uuid` alias, so the fold resolved a non-terminal record and the late callback re-ran live side effects on a dead call. `resolveNewestByProviderCallId` (shared by the sync webhook helper and the async inspect helper) resolves the alias match to the newest snapshot for the logical call. A no-op for telnyx/twilio, which use one stable id. The `providerCallId` mutation in the try block is also guarded with `!foldedTerminalRecord` so a folded terminal echo does not downgrade the canonical id (`CallUUID`) back to the stale alias.

Sibling providers (telnyx/plivo) share this provider-agnostic `processEvent` path, so all parts cover them too.

Part 1 (persist `providerCallId` as early as possible) is already satisfied on `main` — the field is persisted on the live record throughout its lifecycle, so the store lookup finds it. Part 3 (an orphan marker) is optional defense-in-depth, not needed for the root cause.

## User Impact

Operators no longer see phantom zero-duration calls attributed to `main` in their call history when a provider's status callback is delayed past local finalization, and a late inbound status echo no longer triggers a spurious answer action to the carrier for an ended call. For Plivo, a late status callback carrying the original `request_uuid` no longer re-runs side effects against a stale pre-terminal snapshot. Call history and agent attribution stay accurate. No behavior change for the normal (non-late) callback path.

## Evidence

- **Reproduction test** (`events.test.ts`): a finalized call (`agent-sales`, `answered`) receives a late `call.ended` (reason `completed`, direction `outbound`). Pre-fix: a phantom UUID record is birthed under `main` — test fails (`owner.callId` is a fresh UUID, not `call-real-agent`). Post-fix: the event folds into the existing record (`owner.callId === "call-real-agent"`, `agentId === "agent-sales"`, no duplicate in history).
- **Inbound sibling regression** (`events.test.ts`): a finalized **inbound** call receives a late `call.initiated`. Pre-fix: `answerCall` is invoked on the provider spy (`answerCalls.length === 1`) — test fails. Post-fix: no answer request (`answerCalls.length === 0`) and no phantom. This is the ClawSweeper P1 gap — the original test only covered outbound.
- **Plivo alias regression** (`store.test.ts` + `events.test.ts`, Part C): persisted snapshots under `request_uuid` (pre-terminal) and `CallUUID` (terminal) for one logical call. Pre-fix: `findCallByProviderCallIdInStore("request-uuid")` returns the stale `initiated` snapshot (`expected 'initiated' to be 'completed'`), and a late `call.initiated` carrying the alias re-runs and queues `answerCall` (`answerCalls.length` 1, expected 0). Post-fix: the alias resolves to the terminal snapshot (state `completed`, `providerCallId === "CallUUID"`), the late callback absorbs, no `answerCall`, no canonical-id downgrade.
- **`restore.test.ts`**: updated the "restores dedupe keys from terminal persisted calls" assertion — a replayed webhook on a terminal record now folds (`result.kind === "processed"`, 0 active calls) instead of birthing a phantom.
- Suite: `extensions/voice-call` **723/723 pass** (63 files, 0 failures).
- CS-listed commands:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/manager/events.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/manager/events.inbound.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/manager/restore.test.ts` → green.
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <touched files>` → all guards pass (format, plugin boundaries, dead export, coercion, etc.); the only failure is a **pre-existing** tsgo error in `packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.ts:744` (stale `@google/genai`), an untouched file not part of this PR — deferred to CI.
- `oxfmt` clean, `oxlint` clean (direct `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint`; the `run-oxlint.mjs` wrapper times out locally — known issue).

### Production LOC

- `store.ts` +20/-4: `resolveNewestByProviderCallId` helper (shared by the sync webhook-path lookup and the async inspect lookup) replacing the two inline `findLast`-by-`providerCallId` scans that shared the same alias-resolution invariant.
- `events.ts` +9/-1 (this commit): the `!foldedTerminalRecord` guard on the `providerCallId` mutation, preventing a folded terminal echo from downgrading the canonical id to the stale alias.
- Prior Part A/B (`events.ts` +34/-9): fold branch + terminal-record absorb.
- Net prod (this PR) ≈ **+52** across two commits. Exceeds the bug-fix net-≤0 default for three distinct safety invariants at the same birth site: (1) phantom record = wrong-agent attribution + duplicate state, (2) dead-call side effects = spurious carrier answer/timer, and (3) Plivo alias = stale-snapshot side effects on a dead call + canonical-id downgrade. All three are producer-side realities a consumer guard can only mask, not prevent — the birth site must consult the store, fe

author: gregochr
body:
Docs only. The final prompt in the colour-scale series — Stage 7 flips the default and adds the one-time notice.

## The difficulty is not the flip

Reading the API Stage 6 actually shipped, the hard part is a distinction **three earlier stages were built to preserve**, and which one line could destroy.

**"Never chosen" and "invalid" both land on `verdict` today.** `setMode(m)` is `MODE = m === 'temp' ? 'temp' : 'verdict'`, and that fallback is Stage 5a's **safety guard** — *"an unrecognised value must never silently select the not-yet-shipped ramp"* — **not** the product default.

`V147` stores `map_colour_scale` nullable with no `DEFAULT`, and `UserSettingsResponse` passes it through raw rather than defaulting, *precisely* so this stage can tell a null apart from an explicit `'verdict'`. That was the whole point of following `V136`'s precedent, and the plan says so at both ends.

After the flip the two must diverge: **null → `temp`**, while a corrupt value still resolves deliberately rather than inheriting the new default by accident. And ⚠️ **a migration that backfills the column destroys the distinction permanently** — someone who explicitly chose `verdict` must keep it.

## Three places resolve the default today

`setMode`'s fallback, `App.jsx`'s `setMode(s?.mapColourScale)`, and `UserSettingsModal.jsx`'s pre-load `useState('verdict')`.

Flip one and the settings screen shows "Verdict" selected while the map paints temperature — the same class of disagreement cross-cutting rule 1 exists to prevent, this time between the map and its own settings page. The prompt calls for one `resolveMode` used by both, leaving `setMode` as the low-level setter with its guard intact.

## The notice

*"Colours now run cold to hot."* It is the only part of this work that reaches the person who was misreading the old map — the preference does not, because they will never open Settings to discover they were wrong. **It is not a setting; it is a sentence.**

⚠️ `MapView`'s existing fail-soft `localStorage` helpers are mandatory rather than stylistic: several of those reads happen inside `useState` initialisers, i.e. during render, where a storage-denied browser's `SecurityError` crashes **the whole app**, not just the map. That convention is already documented in the file.

## Also

Marks Stage 6 landed (#650), and notes that Stage 7 is the first stage since 5b to change what every reader sees — so browser verification applies in full, with an explicit instruction to say which states were seen and which the local DB could not produce.

## Testing

Docs only. No code, no tests affected.

author: pampeanodev
body:
🚨 **Hotfix — production is down.** #50 broke the app on load; this restores it. One line of config.

## Symptom

```
TypeError: (0 , v$.default) is not a function or its return value is not iterable
  at y$ (index-CA-E9kPY.js:300:45551)
```

Whole app dead behind react-router's error boundary. Reproduced locally byte-for-byte — the local build produced the *same bundle hash* as the deployed one.

## Root cause

Vite 8 swapped Rollup for Rolldown and aligned CommonJS interop to Node semantics — the ["Consistent CommonJS Interop"](https://vite.dev/guide/migration) breaking change I missed in #50.

Under Node ESM rules, `import x from <cjs>` resolves to `module.exports` and the `__esModule` marker is **ignored**. Because this package declares `"type": "module"`, the importer counts as real ESM, so Rolldown emitted the node-interop form `__toESM(mod, 1)`. That flag forces the first branch of the helper:

```js
r || !n || !n.__esModule || !a.call(n, `default`)
  ? t(o, `default`, { value: n, enumerable: !0 })   // r=1 → always this
  : o
```

→ `default` = the entire exports object.

`use-local-storage` is CJS-only and sets `exports.default = useLocalStorage`, so the default import landed on `{ __esModule: true, default: fn }` — an object. Then `App.tsx` line 13:

```js
const [userTheme, setUserTheme] = useLocalStorage("theme", ...)
```

...destructures a non-function. Exactly the error.

**Blast radius: 1 of 35 interop sites** in the bundle used the node form. Every other CJS dep lives inside an ESM package and never takes that path — which is why only this one broke.

## Fix

`legacy.inconsistentCjsInterop: true` — the opt-out Vite documents for this change. Smallest change that restores exact pre-upgrade behavior. The rebuilt bundle has **0** node-interop sites.

## Why this slipped through #50

`tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest` and `vite build` **all passed** while the app was fully broken. This is a bundler interop failure: it only exists in the built output, at runtime. The repo's 2 test files cover calculator services only — nothing renders a component. I flagged that gap when merging #50 but shipped anyway; I should have loaded the build in a browser first.

## Verification — in a real browser, against a production build

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| App loads, no console errors | ✅ |
| Live BTC price fetch (`$78,040.38`) | ✅ |
| Theme toggle round-trips through `localStorage` | ✅ *(the exact path that threw)* |
| Chart view + Table view render | ✅ |
| Donate popover opens with on-chain QR | ✅ |
| `tsc` / `eslint` / `vitest` / `pnpm audit` | 0 / 0 / 4-4 / **0 vulns** |

## Follow-up

`use-local-storage` is CJS-only, unmaintained (3.0.0 is latest), and used in exactly one place for one string. Replacing it with a ~30-line local hook removes the dependency and lets this legacy flag — which Vite will eventually delete — go away.

author: meziantou
body:
Stacked on #2006 → #2005 → #2004, because the startup warning needs the logger from #2006.

With no certificate configured — the default, and what the readme's first example shows — the server answers PRELOGIN with `NOT_SUPPORTED`. `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient` with the common `Encrypt=Optional` then proceeds unencrypted, and the LOGIN7 password arrives protected only by TDS's nibble-swap-and-XOR-`0xA5` obfuscation, which `TdsLoginParser.ReadPassword` reverses in six lines. The readme's quickstart then compares that password against a literal.

That is a library default that transmits credentials recoverable by anyone on the network path, and someone following the readme end to end ships exactly that.

This is spec-conformant SQL Server behaviour and interop demands it, so the behaviour is unchanged. What changes is that the risk is no longer silent:

- A warning is logged at startup when no certificate is configured — on the standalone `TdsServer` path and on the Kestrel `TdsTcpConnectionHandler` path.
- `RequireEncryption` gets a `<remarks>` saying what leaving it `false` actually means.
- The readme gets a short security section before the quickstart, and says outright that the quickstart's credential check is only meaningful on loopback.

Tests cover the warning firing without a certificate and staying quiet with one.

Found by a review of `src/Meziantou.Framework.TdsServer`.

author: iongpt
body:
Closes #124

## Feature

Optional auto-add filter: set a minimum **weekend gross** (USD) and only movies at or above it are auto-added. Modeled on the existing rating filter (enabled checkbox + value input), off by default — existing behavior is unchanged until enabled.

## Design decisions

- **Weekend gross**, not total: matches the issue's own example ("4 out of the top 10 grossed more than \$2 million"), and it's the figure BOM reports most reliably.
- **USD everywhere**: verified live — Box Office Mojo reports every regional chart in USD, so no currency handling is needed (the issue's premise about matching the region's currency turned out not to apply).
- **Fails open on unknown gross**: `weekend_gross` is only missing when the chart couldn't be parsed; failing closed would silently disable all auto-adds exactly when the parser is degraded. The movie is added with an INFO log instead.
- **Ordering**: runs after the `auto_add_limit` trim (preserves "Maximum Movies to Add" = top X by rank) and **before** the Radarr/TMDB lookup — a filtered movie costs zero HTTP requests. The gate lives inside `auto_add_missing_movies`, covering both the scheduler run and `POST /api/scheduler/update-week`.
- **Non-destructive**: below-threshold movies keep their card and manual "Add to Radarr" button on the weekly page (that path bypasses auto-add filters by design). A too-aggressive threshold costs a click, not a movie.
- **Save carry-over**: a client that omits the threshold field keeps the stored value (`boxoffice_timeout` pattern), so a stale setup page can't zero it.
- The number input uses `step="any"` — a coarse step would make non-multiples (like the \$56K thresholds relevant for small markets) fail HTML5 validation and abort the save, silently when the section is collapsed.
- Dashboard "Filters active" only advertises the filter when enabled **and** > 0.

Helper text warns that sensible values are region-dependent (small markets gross orders of magnitude less than Domestic) and that regenerating old weeks compares historical grosses against today's threshold.

## Tests

333 passing (was 306): helper semantics (above/equal/below/None/disabled/zero-threshold), gate ordering asserted via mock call counts (below-threshold movie triggers no `search_movie`; limit trims before the gate), YAML round-trip, save carry-over incl. explicit-zero and 422 on negatives, setup render, dashboard advertise/stay-quiet (mutation-checked).

body:
## Purpose

Adds an authenticated `me()` method to the existing `userProfile` endpoint so any client can discover **its own identity**: whether the caller holds a global platform admin role and which business memberships it has. This is the server-side discovery primitive for opening the public **gewerber-mcp** integration tooling up to regular users — a client first asks "who am I and what can I touch?" instead of guessing.

Data isolation is unchanged: everything stays server-side, only the caller's own rows are ever read (`session.authUserId`).

## Contract

```dart
Future<MyIdentity> me(Session session) // requireLogin = true (endpoint default)
```

New class-only serializable models (no database tables):

- `MyIdentity { UuidValue userId; AdminRole? globalRole; List<MyMembershipInfo> memberships; }`
- `MyMembershipInfo { int businessId; String businessName; MembershipRole role; }`

Existing enums are reused: `AdminRole` (core/admin allowlist) and `MembershipRole` (business module).

- `globalRole` is resolved through the existing `AdminRoleResolver` abstraction (DB allowlist `admin_user`, re-read per request) via getIt/injectable — no ad-hoc table access in the endpoint.
- `memberships` contains all membership rows of the caller joined with business names, deterministically ordered by ascending `businessId`; an empty list is valid.

## Notes for gewerber-mcp

During development gewerber-mcp consumes this via its gitignored `pubspec_overrides.yaml` path dependency to the local backend checkouts; once merged it resolves through the published client protocol as usual.

## Checklist

- [x] `.spy.yaml` models follow repo conventions (enums byName/lowercase reused, no new tables)
- [x] `serverpod generate` (server + client protocol + test tools)
- [x] DI config regenerated via build_runner (`GetMyIdentityUseCase` registered)
- [x] **No DB migration required** — class-only models; `serverpod create-migration` reports *"No changes detected"*
- [x] `dart analyze` clean
- [x] `dart format .` clean
- [x] `dart test`: 274 tests pass (incl. 5 new integration tests covering plain user / admin / moderator / zero memberships / unauthenticated)

## Summary
This PR implements the complete feature set for Phases 3-8 of the financial app roadmap, adding patrimonio (assets/liabilities), currency management, receipt processing, security/backup, and household expense attribution.

## Key Changes

### Patrimonio Management (Phase 3)
- Added `Asset` and `Liability` domain models with repository implementations
- Created `PatrimonioScreen` and `PatrimonioViewModel` for managing assets, liabilities, and financial snapshots
- Implemented `FinancialSnapshot` tracking for net worth history
- Added database entities and DAOs for assets, liabilities, and snapshots

### Currency & Inflation (Phase 4)
- Implemented `ExchangeRate` and `InflationRate` domain models with repositories
- Created `CurrencyScreen` for managing exchange rates and inflation data
- Added `CurrencyViewModel` with use cases for rate refresh and conversion
- Integrated `DolarApiClient` and `InflacionApiClient` for fetching live rates
- Implemented `CurrencyConverter` for multi-currency calculations
- Added `InflationAdjuster` for inflation-adjusted value calculations

### Receipt Processing (Phase 5)
- Created `ReceiptsScreen` and `ReceiptViewModel` for receipt management
- Implemented `ReceiptProcessor` with ML Kit integration for text/barcode recognition
- Added `AfipQrParser` for parsing Argentine AFIP receipt QR codes
- Created `ReceiptImageStore` for secure image storage
- Added `Receipt` domain model and repository

### Security & Backup (Phase 6)
- Implemented `AppLockManager` with biometric authentication support
- Created `AppLockGate` composable for app-level security
- Implemented `BackupManager` with encrypted backup/restore functionality
- Added `PasswordEncryption` using AES-GCM with PBKDF2
- Created `SecurePrefs` for encrypted shared preferences
- Added `DatabasePassphraseProvider` for SQLCipher integration

### Household Expense Attribution (Phase 7)
- Added `ownerMemberId` field to `EngineTransaction` for transaction attribution
- Implemented `MemberAttributionCalculator` for expense attribution logic
- Created `HouseholdSettlementCalculator` for debt calculations between members
- Added `HouseholdReportScreen` and `HouseholdReportViewModel`
- Implemented `GetHouseholdReportUseCase` for generating household reports
- Added `TransactionBeneficiary` entity for tracking expense splits

### Cash Flow Projection (Phase 8)
- Implemented `CashFlowProjectionCalculator` for future balance projections
- Created `CashFlowScreen` and `CommittedScreen` for viewing projections
- Added `CashFlowViewModel` and `CommittedViewModel`
- Implemented `GetCashFlowProjectionUseCase` for calculating upcoming commitments

### Supporting Infrastructure
- Added comprehensive test coverage for all calculators and use cases
- Updated database schema with new entities and migrations
- Extended `EngineModels` with new enums for receipt sources and rate sources
- Added network clients for public APIs (DolarApi, InflacionApi)
- Integrated ML Kit for receipt OCR and barcode scanning
- Added SQLCipher for encrypted database storage
- Updated navigation and routing for new screens
- Enhanced string resources with Spanish labels for all new features

## Notable Implementation Details
- All network operations use simple HTTP clients (no external HTTP library) to minimize dependencies
- Receipt images stored in private app storage only (no external storage permissions)
- Backup encryption uses industry-standard AES-GCM with PBKDF2 key derivation
- Household settlement calculations handle multi-currency scenarios
- Cash flow projections account for recurring transactions and committed expenses
- Biometric authentication gracefully falls back to PIN if unavailable

author: amirfr3
body:
## Purpose

GPU KV-cache capacity is observable — `num_gpu_blocks` and `kv_cache_size_tokens`
are labels on `vllm:cache_config_info`. The CPU offload tier exports only usage
(`vllm:kv_offload_cpu_cache_usage_perc` and the read/write variants) and no
capacity. The size is not recoverable externally either: it depends on
`blocks_per_chunk`, page alignment, and whether a replicated layout deduplicates
per-worker copies — all connector-internal.

This adds `vllm:kv_offload_cpu_config_info`, a gauge pinned to `1` whose labels
carry the capacity and the factors needed to interpret it:

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `num_blocks` | slot count (chunks, not GPU blocks) |
| `blocks_per_chunk` | GPU blocks per chunk — the slot-to-block conversion factor |
| `kv_bytes_per_chunk` | page-aligned bytes per chunk; with `num_blocks`, the tier's exact size in bytes |
| `capacity_tokens` | token capacity, or `"None"` when a slot count does not convert to a token count |

Per-engine; sum across the `engine` label for the instance total. The Info shape is
the extensible container #49307's reviewers asked for.

### `capacity_tokens = num_blocks * blocks_per_chunk * tokens_per_block`

The tier is content-addressed (`OffloadKey = block_hash + group_idx`), so there is
no per-request allocation to divide by and no analogue of GPU's `max_concurrency`.
This means `capacity_tokens` is not the same quantity as GPU's
`kv_cache_size_tokens`, which is addressable context rather than stored KV. It is
`None` in three cases:

- **More than one group.** With more than one group a token's KV may be stored on
  CPU for only some of its layers, so the naive product does not hold. Carries a
  `TODO` — an estimate could be added later.
- **Blocks that don't hold tokens.** A `MambaSpec` block holds one recurrent state
  regardless of `block_size`, so `tokens_per_block` there means something else.
  The gate is `OffloadingGroupConfig.blocks_hold_tokens`, an
  `isinstance(spec, AttentionSpec) and not isinstance(spec, HiddenStateCacheSpec)`
  allowlist evaluated per layer over `iter_layer_specs`.
- **No KV cache group at all.**

Zero chunks reports `0`, not `None`: zero slots hold exactly zero tokens.
Multi-group operators still get an exact capacity in bytes —
`num_blocks × kv_bytes_per_chunk` is partition-invariant because every slot is the
same byte size. The tier is uniform in bytes, non-uniform in tokens.

### Relation to #49307 and #51615

**#49307 (@yanburman)** became this same metric after review (@orozery: bundle
static tier information into one Info metric following `vllm:cache_config_info`),
emitted once at engine startup. That needed a new public `get_config_info()`
connector API, an `EngineCoreReadyResponse` field, a runtime-populated
`KVTransferConfig` side-channel and a `record_config_info()` chain — all of which
edit code outside `kv_offload/` + `offloading/`, which reviewers objected to.
**#51615 (@nilig, draft)** emits `vllm:kv_offload_cpu_capacity_tokens` through the
existing connector-stats path.

This PR takes #49307's metric shape and #51615's emission mechanism. The cost is
that the metric is absent (no series, never `0`) until the first scheduler step.

### `multiprocess_mode="mostrecent"` (second commit)

`_create_metric` never passed `multiprocess_mode`, so every offloading gauge took
`Gauge`'s default `sum`. Stats attach to one client's outputs per step, so under
`--api-server-count > 1` `sum` multiplies a per-engine constant by the number of
participating frontends. Added as a default on `OffloadingGaugeMetadata`, which is
`Gauge`-only, so it cannot be set on a counter or histogram. Counters and histograms
are unchanged: their deltas reach exactly one frontend per step, so summing is already
correct. This also corrects the seven existing offloading gauges, all of them per-engine
snapshots.

## Test Plan

- **Unit tests** — 15 tests across the four layers the metric passes through: the
  sizing arithmetic in `_build_tier_info`, the `blocks_hold_tokens` classification,
  the manager's stats payload, and the Prometheus label binding. Split that way so
  a break is localized rather than surfacing only as a wrong exported number. Each
  was mutation-checked: the guarded line broken, the test confirmed to fail, the
  source restored and verified byte-identical.

  ```bash
  # the four test files this PR changes
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
    tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py \
    tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_metrics.py -q

  # the H200 CI job's scope, minus the nixl/moriio/bidirectional suites (16 files);
  # 7 of them import ray, which is not installed locally
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload tests/v1/kv_connector/unit -q \
    --ignore-glob='*moriio*' --ignore-glob='*nixl*' --ignore-glob='*bidirectional*'
  ```

- **Lint** — `pre-commit run --all-files` and
  `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual`, as CI runs it.

- **Model evaluations: not applicable.** Metrics-only. `get_stats()` appends one
  pre-rendered label tuple to a payload the scheduler already emits each step, and
  `blocks_hold_tokens` is read only by `_build_tier_info`. No scheduling, KV-cache
  placement, transfer behaviour or model output is touched.

- **Not verified locally.** The development environment is macOS without CUDA, so
  the worker path, `SharedOffloadRegion`, an end-to-end `/metrics` scrape, DP>1, a
  real hybrid/Mamba model reaching `blocks_hold_tokens=False`, and the
  multi-frontend `mostrecent` merge are untested here. The H200 job covers the
  first two; the rest need a GPU run.

## Test Result

**The four changed test files**, on `40152c529`:
`154 passed`. All 15 added tests pass, plus the pre-existing tests in those files.

**Control comparison for the wider CI scope.** The local environment is macOS
without CUDA, which fails a fixed set of GPU-path tests, so the run was repeated
against a clean checkout of the merge-base (`6a5e8f597`):

| | branch | merge-base |
|---|---|---|
| failed | 67 | 67 |
| passed | 1209 | 1185 |
| skipped | 24 | 24 |

**The 67 failing node IDs are identical on both sides.**

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code): the test suite, the mutation-checking
of each added test, and this description. All code and reasoning have been reviewed
line by line by the submitter, who can defend the design and its trade-offs.

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
      No docs change: no file under `docs/` enumerates KV-offload metric names
      (`grep -rn "vllm:kv_offload" docs/` returns nothing).
