author: moontheripper
body: A small ingest API so a local process that has already resolved something can register it — identity, metadata, and the magnet that plays it. JellyFreedom stores the row, writes the `.strm`, and serves playback from the cached hash, performing **no** metadata lookup and **no** indexer search. That's why it works for a source JellyFreedom knows nothing about. Auth is a generated secret in `settings` presented in a header, not an admin session — the caller is a daemon. Shares one constant-time comparison and one generator with the webhook rather than growing a second that can drift. ## `safeName` was not sufficient, and that's the important part It was a character filter and nothing more: `safeName("..")` returned `".."`, and `safeName("")` returned `""` — a bare `.strm` dotfile in the library root. Neither was reachable through the two existing callers, because both format `"%s (%s)"` first and the parens survive filtering. But that means the containment of **every filesystem write in this program** rested on a format string in the caller, not on the function named for it. An endpoint taking `title` from a hostile caller turns that from latent into live. Now guarantees a single component, never `.`/`..`/any dot run, never empty, bounded under `NAME_MAX`. A second layer refuses the write if `filepath.Clean` shows the join escaped, so a future sanitiser bug is contained rather than exploited. Every field is validated against the sink it reaches: the poster URL is scheme-allowlisted because it becomes an ``; season/episode are forced to 0 for a movie because the movie play route looks up `(0,0)`; the `tmdb` namespace is refused since it owns the frozen legacy tokens. **Verified against a running build with a canary outside the library:** nine traversal payloads in `title` — `..`, `""`, `/etc/passwd`, `....//....//x`, a unicode fraction slash — left the canary untouched and wrote nothing outside the library. Auth refuses absent/empty/wrong/prefix/suffixed secrets. Sixteen checks removed one at a time, every one failed a test.

author: uz1mani
body:
## Summary

This release carries three independent changes. The uptime/worked-examples work (#430) and two from the beacon session (#429, #431).

### #430 — uptime preset defect + worked-example denominator
- 🔴 **Live production defect (uptime, since 22-08).** `presetZoneRange` moves a range's end to today, so it rewrote every CLOSED PAST preset — "Yesterday", "Last week", "Last month", "Last quarter", "Last year" — into a trailing window ending **today**, under the original label. Picking "Yesterday" on the uptime page rendered TODAY's data. Fixed inside the helper, so every caller is fixed at once.
- 🔴 The InfoTip worked examples divided a session numerator by `visitors`, which migration 163 redefined as PEOPLE (companion pulse-backend #399 supplies `sessions`; already on main).
- Funnel detail queried two windows on one screen; `pages`/`pages_per_visit` still called visitors sessions; a step nobody dropped off rendered the generic no-data line.

### #429 — the engagement beacon moves off a filter-listed path
The tracking script sent duration, visible duration and scroll depth to `/api/v1/metrics`. EasyPrivacy carries a bare, domain-agnostic substring rule for exactly that path, written for an unrelated vendor, so uBlock Origin and Brave cancelled the beacon client-side while the pageview landed. Those visitors were counted; their engagement was not. Now `/api/v1/engagement`, via a single constant. Tracking script **v1.1.0**. The legacy path stays live server-side indefinitely.

### #431 — versioned publishing wrote to a bucket nobody serves
`publish-scripts.sh` uploaded every versioned artifact to Exoscale SOS, while `js.ciphera.net` serves from Bunny Storage — it printed success while `/v<version>/script.js` 404'd. Same defect fixed in `deploy.yml` on 25-07-2026 for the rolling script; the versioned path never got it. Found while publishing v1.1.0 by hand.

## Preconditions for #429 — both satisfied

- [x] **Backend live in production.** pulse-backend#400 merged and verified: 20/20 probes to `POST /api/v1/engagement` returned 200 across both replicas with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` echoed for an unknown customer origin; the legacy path answers identically. The script cannot point at a 404.
- [x] **`v1.1.0` published and reachable.** `https://js.ciphera.net/v1.1.0/script.js` → 200 and its sha384 matches `public/script-versions.json` exactly, so the SRI-pinned snippet this build advertises will execute. `v1.0.0` is untouched and still serves the legacy path.

## Test Plan

- [x] Suite green, tsc clean, mutations killed on both blockers (#430) and on the beacon tests (#429)
- [x] `uptimeMetrics` added to `test:tz-positive`; green at America/New_York and Pacific/Kiritimati
- [x] Staging-verified (#430): uptime "Yesterday" requests 2026-08-25..2026-08-25 on 08-26; wire carries `sessions:14` tying out to `bounce_rate` exactly
- [x] Staging-verified (#429): served script has 1 `ENGAGEMENT_PATH` constant, 3 send sites through it, 2 `/api/v1/events` sites, **0** literal legacy paths in code; end-to-end beacon wrote `duration=137, visible=121, scroll=78`
- [x] Verified (#431): missing-credential guard aborts; immutability guard correctly refuses the published `v1.1.0`; post-publish edge+sha384 check passes
- [ ] Prod: uptime "Yesterday" and the `sessions` denominator
- [ ] Prod: `js.ciphera.net/script.js` serves the new path after the CDN purge
- [ ] Prod: engagement arriving on `/api/v1/engagement`

## 🔴 Instrument boundary — 26-08-2026

Time-on-page, visible time and scroll depth **step up** from here. That is the instrument widening, not readers behaving differently, and it cannot be backfilled — a blocked beacon never reached us to be recovered.

Baseline captured before any deploy (30 days): **89.9%** of pageviews carried a duration fleet-wide; the lowest was `ciphera.net` at **61.1%**, which is what a privacy-conscious audience looks like. Measure recovery from the rollout timestamp, never `now() - interval`.

Record: `Pulse/docs/plans/26-08-2026-engagement-beacon-path-rename.md` · Analysis: `Pulse/docs/audits/26-08-2026-psi-err-blocked-by-client-metrics.md`

## Summary

Add the repository-owned binding for the community PR gate. The binding makes the explicit six-person internal core-team list authoritative regardless of CODEOWNERS; every other author goes through the zizmor-first community gate.

## What to look at

- [Community PR gate binding](https://github.com/grafana/grafana-pathfinder-app/blob/f19c8ff8e861467ceb02d48a53e556a505a6bd16/.github/community-pr-gate.json) — verify the six canonical GitHub handles, High-severity scanner threshold, CLA and signing priority, and repository review pointers.

1. Run `python3 ~/.claude/skills/community-pr/scripts/community_pr_gate.py validate-binding .github/community-pr-gate.json` and confirm it reports `status: valid`.
2. Confirm each listed handle resolves to the intended core-team account and that an unlisted author remains subject to the community gate.

None. This change is additive and fully reversible.

## Out of scope

- Bot authors are not treated as internal. They remain subject to the community gate, and unfamiliar CLA status descriptions continue to fail closed until their issuing integration can be authenticated without relying on spoofable text.

body:
### What does this PR do?

Bumps all three AI CLI tool versions to their latest stable releases:

| Tool | Old version | New version |
|---|---|---|
| opencode | `v1.2.27` | `v1.18.14` |
| claude-code | `2.1.81` | `2.1.246` |
| gemini-cli | `0.44.0` | `0.57.0` |

Each version is pinned via the `ARG` default in the corresponding Dockerfile
(`dockerfiles/opencode/Dockerfile`, `dockerfiles/claude-code/Dockerfile`,
`dockerfiles/gemini-cli/Dockerfile`).

### What issues does this PR fix or reference?

fixes https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CRW-12628

Root cause: opencode `v1.2.27` shipped with GPT 5.3 as its default model,
which is no longer available on the API. Users saw a "Model not found" error
immediately on first launch without changing any settings. The fix is to
upgrade to `v1.18.14` (current latest), which uses a supported default model.
Claude Code and Gemini CLI are also brought up to date as a precaution per
the issue's additional-info note.

### Is it tested? How?

Changes are limited to `ARG` version pins in three Dockerfiles. No logic
changes. The `:next` images built from this branch by the
`next-build-multiarch.yml` workflow can be tested by:

1. Deploy Eclipse Che with the updated `registry.json` from this PR, which
   points to the freshly built images containing the new CLI versions.
2. Configure an AI provider and create a workspace.
3. Open a terminal and run `opencode`, `claude`, or `gemini` to confirm there
   are no "Model not found" or startup errors.

Updated AI CLI tool versions in the injector images to fix a "Model not found"
error caused by the outdated opencode default model:

- opencode `v1.2.27` → `v1.18.14`

author: lazzyms
body:
## Release notes
Fix CI by moving builds to macos-26 runners (Xcode 26.6), matching the dev toolchain.

## Why

Release #6 (v1.1.1) failed at the `swift test` gate: CI's `macos-15` runner uses Xcode 16.4 (Swift 6.1, macOS 15.5 SDK), which rejects code merged in #83 that compiles on the dev toolchain (Xcode 26.6):

- `static let context = CIContext(...)` — `CIContext` is non-`Sendable`; Swift 6.1 errors on the static, Swift 6.3 accepts it (`ImageBackgroundRemover`, `ImageFaceBlurrer`, `ImageOperation`, `ImageToneAdjuster`).
- `CGContext(bitmapInfo:)` takes `CGBitmapInfo` on the macOS 26 SDK but `UInt32` on the 15.5 SDK (`PDFImageExtractor.swift:321`, `:332`, `:438`).

`macos-26` is GA with Xcode 26.6 as default — identical to local. Making the code compile on the old SDK would need `#if compiler` switches in three call sites, so this aligns CI to dev instead. Docs updated from "Xcode 16+" to "Xcode 26+".

All 318 tests pass locally on Xcode 26.6.

author: iderex
body:
## The issue this belongs to

Closes #117.

## What changed

The suite runs a second time under a thread sanitizer, on a Linux runner and on a
nightly compiler, and a report against it fails the run. The leg then runs a
target holding a data race written on purpose and fails the run if that reports
nothing.

`.github/thread-detector/thread-detector.sh` is the verdict and
`.github/workflows/thread-detector.yml` is what invokes it, on every pull request
and on every push to the default branch. The check-run name is
`thread-detector`, on both the workflow and the job.

`tests/a_race_the_detector_must_catch.rs` is the deliberate race. It is declared
in `Cargo.toml` with `test = false`, so `cargo test --locked` never reaches it:
its body is undefined behaviour on purpose and a contributor running the ordinary
suite must not execute it. `src/lib.rs` carries `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` and this
file is outside it, which is the honest place for the one piece of unsound code
this repository contains.

`.github/thread-detector/suppressions` is the register for a finding that is not
going to be fixed, one per line with the reason on the same line. An entry
carrying no reason is refused before anything is judged, and the detector's own
suppression file is derived from that register, so an expression is written in one
place and there is no second file to keep in step.

`docs/gate-parity.md`'s row for this check moves from naming a plan to naming a
run, and keeps the sentence saying it is added here rather than adopted.

## What failure it prevents

Two, and the second is the reason the leg has two halves.

The first is a broken promise in `docs/decisions/0009-the-concurrency-model.md`
about what is safe to touch from two threads at once.
`tests/thread_statements.rs` already asks the type system whether a type may
cross a thread boundary, which is a claim about a shape and is decided before any
thread runs. A data race is a claim about a schedule: it appears on a machine with
a different number of cores under an interleaving nobody wrote, and passes ten
thousand runs on the machine it was written on.

The second is a detector that was never switched on. A target whose specification
carries no such sanitizer, a flag that stopped being passed, a standard library
rebuilt without the instrumentation - each reports nothing, exits zero and prints
a page indistinguishable from a clean tree. The deliberate race is the only thing
in this leg that can tell those apart, which is why a run of it that reports
nothing fails.

## Evidence

The commit this was run at:

    git rev-parse HEAD
    7b431298f76c572979d391b5ac201c41a22ebae5

The leg's own fixtures, every one of them, and the analyser over the script:

    bash .github/thread-detector/thread-detector.sh selftest ; echo "exit=$?"
    == a report is read, and read once ==
    ok    reads: a data race, named by its own kind
    ok    reads: two findings as two, so a second cannot hide behind the first
    ok    reads: a finding of a kind nobody wrote a case for, rather than passing it over
    == what is not a report ==
    ok    passes over: a clean run of the suite
    ok    passes over: this script naming the tool in its own log line
    ok    passes over: the closing summary alone, which names a finding already counted
    ok    passes over: a test whose own name carries the tool name
    == the run says what it collected ==
    ok    reads: several binaries, and the tests summed across them
    ok    reads: one test, written in the singular by the harness
    ok    reads: a run that collected nothing, which reports nothing and reads as clean
    ok    reads: a harness that printed no accounting at all
    ok    passes over: the same sentence inside a compiler message
    == the suppression register ==
    ok    allows: an entry carrying the reason it is not refused
    ok    refuses: an entry with no reason, which is a finding nobody argued with
    ok    passes over: a comment, which is most of the register
    ok    passes over: a blank line
    ok    passes: a reason of several words is one reason and not several fields

    Every fixture held. The rules the gate applies are the rules these fixtures ran.
    exit=0

    shellcheck -S style .github/thread-detector/thread-detector.sh ; echo "exit=$?"
    exit=0

The rest of the gate on this tree, run by hand on a Windows machine:

    cargo build --locked --all-targets ; echo "exit=$?"
    exit=0
    bash .github/test/test.sh check | tail -1
    The suite collected 41 test(s) and every one of them passed.
    bash .github/lint/lint.sh check ; echo "exit=$?"
    exit=0
    bash .github/format/format.sh check ; echo "exit=$?"
    exit=0
    bash .github/invariants/invariants.sh check ; echo "exit=$?"
    exit=0
    bash .github/doc-paths/doc-paths.sh check | tail -1
    Every path these documents name resolves against the tracked set.
    bash .github/shell-analysis/shell-analysis.sh check | tail -1
    Every tracked shell file passed at severity style, with the rules named above not refused and every other rule in force.

The deliberate race is a real one rather than a hoped-for one, and it can be seen
losing writes without any detector at all. Two threads each add one to the same
value 100000 times, so a run with an ordering between them would end at 200000:

    cargo test --locked --test a_race_the_detector_must_catch
    -- what this target is
          a deliberate data race, run so that a detector has something to report. A run of this that reports nothing is a detector that is not switched on.
    -- what it ended with
          107039, which is a number nobody should rely on and is not read as a verdict

That number moves on every run and is not read as a verdict by anything here. It
is quoted because it is the cheapest available demonstration that the two threads
genuinely reach the same value with no ordering between them.

**The wall-clock cost, and the run that measured it.** The leg publishes it on
every run, to the job's step summary as well as the log, so the figure is produced
by the run rather than pasted into a document that would drift. Read out of this
branch's own check run:

    gh run view 32976331446 --repo Flowfin/core --log | grep 'Wall clock'
    Wall clock: 18s for the suite and 1s for the deliberate race, 19s in total.

That is the whole leg from the first compile of the instrumented standard library
to the last verdict, on the runner, at head `7b43129`. The check run itself
reports 34s, which is the job including the checkout and the toolchain install.
The number moves between runs and between runners; the command above is what
reads the current one.

**The detector was switched on, and it can be seen being so.** Out of the same
run:

    -- which compiler judged this run
    cargo 1.100.0-nightly (e8cb624d5 2026-08-22)
    rustc 1.100.0-nightly (787af2b8c 2026-08-25)

    -- the suite, under the detector
          cargo +nightly test --locked --all-targets -Zbuild-std --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu

author: thoraxe
body:
Fixes the two things #161 identifies: the skills read as **two PRs**, and neither says a pass
lands as one squashed commit. The real model is one draft PR on `next` carrying two commits —
spec + failing tests, then implementation — merged once. An issue whose whole deliverable is
spec + tests (a rule the code already satisfies, tests it was missing — e.g. #155/PR #156) lands
as one commit and merges after review; both skills now say so.

Documentation/process only. No product behavior, no tests added.

## What changed

**`.ai/spec/README.md`** — the "Planned changes" convention bullet is replaced by
**"Present-tense behavior only"**: `what/` states what the system does — behavior that has shipped
and behavior being built right now — in the present tense; no `[PLANNED]`, `[PROPOSED]`, "deferred
until…", or other forward-looking/process language. It keeps the issue's own distinction — scope
boundaries ("these rules cover the flat tower; grouped is out of scope") are behavioral and belong;
promises about future work do not — and keeps the old bullet's pointer to `docs/plans/` alongside
GitHub issues. Surrounding Conventions bullets are untouched.

**`.claude/skills/spec-first-pass/SKILL.md`**
- Phase 3 no longer instructs adding `[PLANNED: #<issue>]`, and "The marker is dropped by the
  **implementation PR**, not by this one" is gone. Replaced with a present-tense rule whose
  justification is the tests, not a second PR: "the failing tests, not a marker, are what record
  that the behavior is not built yet." The ban on issue numbers is scoped to numbers used as
  **work-item pointers** — widget identifiers like `#21`/`#22` (`what/widgets.md`, `glossary.md`)
  are names, not work items, and stay.
- Intro states the one-PR/two-commit model explicitly, plus the spec+tests-only escape, and
  "stop — that is the next PR" became "the next pass on this same branch."
- Phase 1's reading list cites "present-tense rules" instead of `[PLANNED]`.
- Phase 5 states the pass lands as **exactly one commit**; a pass that iterates (review findings
  before approval) uses `git commit --amend` + `git push --force-with-lease` rather than
  appending, and `git log --oneline origin/next..HEAD` must show one commit at handoff. The draft
  is held "until the implementation commit lands — or, for an issue whose whole deliverable is
  spec + tests, until review passes."
- Gotchas: "fix them in a **separate commit**" contradicted the new one-commit rule, so it now
  says to name the unrelated fix in the PR body and offer to split it into its own PR.

**`.claude/skills/implement-spec/SKILL.md`**
- Phase 3 is **reduced, not deleted** — clear a legacy `[PLANNED]` marker in a spec file this
  change touches (the `what/` rules implemented, the paired `how/` file), so markers left by older
  work don't get orphaned. Still the only permitted spec edit, still marker text only, and
  explicitly not a licence to go hunting through unrelated files.
- Intro states the implementation is a second commit on the *same* PR, and that a spec+tests-only
  PR never reaches this skill; Phase 0's `git log` comment expects exactly one commit.
- Phase 5 states the same one-commit/amend rule, and that `origin/next..HEAD` must show exactly
  two commits before merging.

**`.ai/spec/how/config-editor.md`** — the stale `[PLANNED: #145]` is gone. Verified shipped before
removing: `data-testid="plate-alpha-{key}"` at `app/src/routes/config/ConfigPage.svelte:537` and
`app/src/routes/config/ConfigPage.plate.test.js` exists. With the marker gone the bullet now names
`rendersPlate(key)` (`overlayConfig.js:366`) outright, matching how its neighbours name
`widgetSupportsAutoHide(key)` and `isLowerThird(key)`; paragraph rewrapped.

## One thing beyond the issue's list

Phase 5 of `spec-first-pass` said `` `Refs #<issue>` — **not** `Closes`, since this does not
implement it ``. That is the same two-PR assumption in another spot: the PR *does* eventually
carry the implementation, and `implement-spec` explicitly says not to rewrite the description, so
the issue would never get closed by the merge. Changed to `Closes #<issue>`. Flagging it because
it changes GitHub behavior on merge and was not in the issue's fix list.

## Verification

```
cd app && npx vitest run   →  37 files, 450 passed
npm run lint               →  clean
```

Closes #161

author: secustor
body:
## The bug

Reported live: every GitHub fetch in a long-lived tab failing with `github API rejected the request (HTTP 401)` while the app's own bookkeeping said the OAuth token had 7+ hours left, and GitHub's response body said **Bad credentials** (revoked, not expired).

Root cause (confirmed against [GitHub's docs](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/refreshing-user-access-tokens)): in cookie mode (roadmap 065) every tab shares ONE grant — the `HttpOnly` refresh cookie — while each tab keeps its own access token in per-tab `sessionStorage`. GitHub **revokes the old access token the moment the grant is refreshed** ("that refresh token and the old user access token will no longer work"), so any sibling tab's boot-time `restoreSession` refresh silently killed the token this tab was still holding. The tab kept sending the dead token (its recorded expiry looked fine, so `getValidToken` never refreshed) and every run 401'd under the rate-limit banner until the tab closed. A secondary race — two tabs refreshing the rotating cookie concurrently — could burn the grant outright, which is why the cookie-session marker had already vanished when the report came in.

## The fix

1. **Transport (`engine`)**: a 401 with a token attached gets one recovery attempt — `hostFetch` asks a registered `AuthRefreshHandler` to renew (or drop) the credential, then retries once with re-resolved headers. No handler (the CLI / headless graph) → the plain throw, byte-identical messages.
2. **App handler (`run.ts` / `oauth.ts`)**: `recoverRejectedToken` forces the refresh machinery past the trusted local expiry; after a definitive failure the session ends cleanly and the retry (and rest of the run) goes out anonymously instead of failing on the dead token.
3. **Cross-tab coordination (cookie mode)**: a refresh broadcasts the replacement token to sibling tabs (`BroadcastChannel`, gated on the shared-grant marker, validated like any stored value — roadmap 030), and refreshes serialize behind a Web Lock with a post-lock recheck so a racing boot can no longer post the already-rotated cookie.

`suppressTokens` (untrusted-endpoint guard) unregisters the handler, so a credential-suppressed run can never re-attach a token via recovery.

## Tests

- `host-transport.test.ts`: retry-with-replacement, anonymous retry, decline, single-retry cap, handler never consulted for anonymous 401 / any 403, throwing handler = decline; existing verbatim-message tests unchanged.
- `oauth.crosstab.test.ts` (new): the recovery entry point, the token/signout broadcasts (adoption gates + validation), and the lock recheck that prevents the burned-cookie race — the sibling tab played by a second in-process `BroadcastChannel`.

Full workspace suite green (engine golden+shimmed, app 979, cli, oauth-worker, tools); lint/format/typecheck clean.

author: deathreaper00
body:
A comprehensive, non-breaking revamp of the public API and its documentation — goal: best-in-class for DevOps/automation, clearly beating cvefeed.io and Vulners. Research + full design (competitors' real docs + OWASP API Top 10) is in Obsidian `API Revamp — competitive research + design.md`. **All additive; `/api/v1` unchanged. 323 backend tests + ruff/tsc green. Security-reviewed — no HIGH/MEDIUM findings.**

## The edge (things neither competitor exposes)
- **`POST /score/simulate`** — a transparent, **re-weightable** priority score with a per-term breakdown (Vulners' is an opaque AI number, cvefeed's is fixed).
- **`GET /cves/{id}/provenance` + `/timeline`** — per-field audit trail (which authority published each value + when) and field-level change history, as first-class endpoints.
- **Policy-as-code gate on `/assess`** — SBOM + a CVEQL `policy`; a matching CVE fails the gate, and `?format=sarif` annotates the offending package.

## Query, bulk & interop
- **CVEQL** upgraded to a recursive-descent parser: `NOT`/`!`, parentheses + nesting, `IN (...)`, real AND/OR precedence, a `source:` provenance filter, `has_fix`/`epss_percentile`/`modified`/`reference` fields, relative dates (`now-7d`), a depth cap; plus `GET /cves/query/{validate,fields,suggest}`.
- **`POST /cves/batch`**; **`GET /cves/{id}?format=osv|sarif`** (OSV for Trivy/Grype, SARIF for CI code-scanning); **`?view=summary|full`**.
- **`/exploit-intel`**, **`/epss/shifting`**, **`/cwe*`**, **`/cves/by-cpe`**, **`/cves/export?since=`** (NDJSON delta stream).

## Agent-native
- `/.well-known/api-catalog` (RFC 9727) + MCP server card, and a **live callable MCP server** at `POST /api/v1/mcp` (JSON-RPC tools: `cve_lookup`/`cveql_query`/`simulate_score`/`verify_provenance`, read-scoped).

## Hardening
- **Per-IP rate limits** on the unauthenticated endpoints (score/feeds/discovery).
- **ETag / If-None-Match** conditional GET on the CVE detail (cheap 304 for sync clients).
- Registered an **HTTPBearer** OpenAPI security scheme (there was no Authorize button before).
- Live-pull unchanged, still bounded by the #40 budget + negative cache; security review confirmed it's not SSRF.

## Docs
- **Dropped raw Swagger.** `/docs` 307-redirects to a hand-built **LEDGER** page at **`/api-docs`**: from-zero getting-started, glossary, CVEQL taught step by step, a **complete auto-generated reference** (live from `openapi.json`, all 111 routes + params), an interactive **Score Playground**, and a native **Try-it console** (client-side key via the existing `/api/v1/[...path]` proxy; cURL/PowerShell/Python/Node tabs; live response inspector).

## Still open (Parv's lane — not touched here)
The two prod latency bugs (`vendor_breakdown` 6× subquery; `/me/stack/inventory` N+1) and F7 public `/login`/`/signup` (on hold). Nothing here changes ingestion or the data model beyond additive schema fields.

author: irondrass
body:
## Summary

- Analysis/characterization only.
- No production code changed.
- Establishes canonical planner behavior and scale baseline before P1 implementation.
- P1-002 is NOT included.

## Architecture

- Explicit task graph path: `schedulePipeline` selects `scheduleTaskGraph` when `getExplicitPlanningTasks` returns a non-empty task list.
- Sequential `STEP_TEMPLATES` fallback: `scheduleSequentialPipeline` is used when no explicit planning tasks are selected.
- Exact selection rule: `planningTasks` takes precedence over `workshopTasks`; PDF-source tasks are normalized; external `stepExecutionModes` can synthesize a linear graph; legacy `tasks` enters graph mode only when dependency, parallel, or external semantics are present; otherwise durations use the sequential fallback.
- The analysis classifies canonical planning fields separately from compatibility/legacy fields and identifies derived and ambiguous fields.

## Existing baseline

20 existing planner-related tests inventoried.

Results:

- 17 PASS
- 3 PRE-EXISTING FAIL

Exact pre-existing failures:

- `planning_dependencies_sql_v2330.test.mjs`
- `work_hours_conflict_outbound_gate_v2331.test.mjs`
- `work_hours_persistence_contract_v2331.test.mjs`

The entire existing suite is not claimed to pass.

## Characterization

A-AF:

- 27 PASS
- 4 FAIL
- 0 UNSUPPORTED
- 1 AMBIGUOUS

Important observed failures:

- Strict assignment lock silently falls back.
- 600-minute work chooses an incorrect delayed start under current capacity/calendar behavior.
- 840/1200-minute work fails under the default 420-minute daily capacity.
- Task graph does not preserve body/reassembly and prep/paint/finish worker continuity.
- Non-PDF graph normalization can rewrite dependencies/parallelism.
- Same-case proposal acceptance may replace all bookings for the case.
- Accepted booking conversion loses planning-task provenance.

## Scalability

Approximate workstation measurements:

- 1k proposal: ~43–46 ms
- 10k proposal: ~342–602 ms
- 100k proposal: ~3.29–5.59 s
- 300k proposal: ~11.37–20.50 s
- 300k 10-task graph: ~88.04–98.92 s
- 300k sequential: ~60.88–63.25 s

Important limitation: 100k/300k appointment-search figures are BOUNDED ONE-DATE probes. The initial all-tier full 14-date benchmark exceeded 360 seconds and was stopped before complete results. The bounded large-tier values are not the full 14-date production cost.

## Complexity

Largest hotspot: full booking-array cloning plus repeated full-array resource/load scans.

P0-007 index usage: PARTIAL.

Indexed conflict candidate selection works, but the dominant planner paths still scan/copy unrelated bookings.

## Highest correctness risk

Current proposal acceptance/regeneration can replace all same-case bookings, creating risk to started/completed productive history. No proposal identity/version currently protects stale proposal acceptance.

## Recommended P1 order

1. P1-002 — proposal identity / acceptance safety / productive-history protection
2. P1-003 — canonical task model / source-aware compatibility
3. P1-004 — indexed planner booking view
4. P1-005 — deterministic long-task / daily-capacity semantics
5. P1-006 — graph continuity / strict assignment locks
6. P1-007 — planner scale regression gate
7. P1-008 — documentation / anticipated-parts decision

## Historical planning

Historical commit `416c1d1` inspected read-only.

Ancestry test exit code: `1`.

`416c1d1` was NOT applied. No historical planning branch was modified. Historical anticipated-parts behavior is not revived.

## Validation

- Characterization A-AF completed.
- Benchmark completed with bounded large-tier appointment probes.
- `node --check`: PASS.
- `git diff --check`: PASS.
- Production files changed: 0.
- Ruflo: UNAVAILABLE / NOT RUN.
- GitHub CI status is reported separately from this validation and is not claimed as PASS here.

## Boundary

- No production implementation.
- No permissions redesign.
- No Supabase concurrency change.
- No IndexedDB/outbox change.
- No React/P2 work.
- P1-002 not started.

## 问题
开启「信任工作空间」后，工作空间内文件读写不再弹系统审批。但操作工作空间外、且与当前项目目录有亲缘关系的路径时，模型可能不调用文件工具，改为聊天文本确认，系统审批卡无法弹出。

根因是开关开启后把项目目录注入 `trusted_dirs`，同一份列表同时进入用户消息。模型据此可能把亲缘越界路径判为未授权，用口头消息确认代替权限引擎。无关外部路径仍会调工具并弹审批，权限链路本身未失效。该层受模型和会话上下文影响，会偶现。

## 修改方案
`_build_inputs` 在兜底注入前快照显式传入的 `trusted_dirs`：
- 用户消息只使用客户端显式传入的目录；未传入则不写入该字段
- 权限轨仍使用含项目目录注入的 `trusted_dirs`，工作空间内免审批保持不变
- 客户端显式传入 `trusted_dirs` 时，用户消息与权限轨行为均不变

## 预期效果
- 开关 ON + 工作空间内读写：不弹系统审批
- 开关 ON + 工作空间外读写：调用文件工具，由权限引擎弹出系统审批卡，不以聊天确认代替
- 开关 OFF：工作空间内外均弹系统审批
- 显式信任目录内操作：不弹系统审批

body:
## What this adds

**1874 Schrader** — Clemens Schrader, S.J. (1820–1875), Vatican I theologian, *De Theologia Generatim Commentarius* (Poitiers: Oudin, 1874) — the **dogmatic-facts note (pp. 113–114)** that the repo's 1879 Mazzella entry cites ("de Theol. gener., pag. 114 not."), plus the **censures passage of p. 128 with its third note** — classified **1b-ii**.

## Why it matters

- **The fides-ecclesiastica machinery in its most compressed form** (direct ancestor of the Lennerz–Salaverri line): singulars contained only *confusedly* in revealed universals "cannot be believed by divine faith"; the fact that Trent was legitimately convoked "**is held only through the authority of the Church, whose infallibility is extended to this fact for the sake of the dogma to be believed… the fact they call dogmatic**" — with dogmatic *facts* distinguished from dogmatic *texts*.
- **The 19th-century replay of the Trent argument:** "now the **legitimate celebration of the Vatican Council, which by force of dogmatic fact is infallibly certain, is called into doubt**" — the Old-Catholic attack answered by the same apparatus Murga used for Trent (n. 84).
- **The status quaestionis of 1874 in one sentence** (p. 128 n. 3, on Suárez's censure-monition): "it is one thing **to say that it is *de fide* that the present Pontiff, acknowledged by the universal Church, is the true successor of Peter… and to affirm that the contrary is heretical** — and another to say the deniers' opinion is heretical; the former pertains to the **doctrinal office of theologians**, the latter to the **judicial office of pastors**." Exactly the three-grade structure of the root README's "theological note of the doctrine itself."
- The same note cites "Lorc. disp. 40. n. 25" — one more thread for the pending Lorca attribution.

## Pipeline

Selection extracted as a separate PDF; OCR from page images; **independent adversarial review: 0 corrections** (all citation strings, superscript anchors, and the mid-word page seam verified at 400 dpi); translation 1:1 (12 aligned pairs). Imprint verified from the title page (Pictaviis, sumptibus Henrici Oudin, MDCCCLXXIV). Source link is a Google Books search (no stable permalink found).

author: hinten
body:
## The signal, and why it was thrown away

An ML order sold with **no Mercado Envios shipment** ("entrega a combinar") never
learned that it was delivered.

Live evidence, order `2000018052464608`, before and after the seller confirmed
delivery in the ML panel:

| field | 2026-08-21 | 2026-08-26 |
|---|---|---|
| `fulfilled` | `null` | **`true`** ← the signal |
| `tags` | `not_delivered` | `not_delivered` ← never flipped |
| `status` | `paid` | `paid` ← never changes on delivery |

ML notified normally — three `orders_v2` deliveries at 12:42–12:43, all processed
`done` / `updated-sem-envio`. The signal arrived on time and was discarded:
`fulfilled` rode `orderSchema`'s bare `.passthrough()` untyped and had **zero**
readers anywhere in `apps/mercado-livre` or `packages/integrations/mercado-livre`.

The tags behaved exactly as ML's Orders doc warns — the `delivered`/`not_delivered`
tags "não serão mais adicionadas automaticamente… o integrador deverá realizar um
PUT com a tag correspondente" — so the tag is not the signal and never will be.

Consequence: the pedido's `freteInicial` stayed at `iniciado` forever, so the goods
were never taken out of the depósito. This one silently withholds a **stock
movement**, not a status label.

## What changed

On the **sem-envio path only**, `fulfilled === true` advances
`freteInicial.estado` to `ESTADO_FRETE.entregue`.

| | |
|---|---|
| `packages/integrations/mercado-livre/src/types.ts` | types `fulfilled` on `orderSchema` |
| `apps/mercado-livre/.../pedidos/orderImport.ts` | the advance, inside `applyFreteSemEnvioStep`'s existing transaction |
| `apps/mercado-livre/.../notificacoes/notificacao.ts` | narrows the `updated-sem-envio` docblock: the *delivery* step no longer needs a human, *arranging the freight* still does |
| `packages/config-eslint/rules/firestore-transaction-inventory.test.js` | the site is no longer create-only — entry rewritten |
| `packages/schemas/.../pedido.ts` | records what `ESTADO_PEDIDO.finalizado` means (comment only) |

## Semantics — verified against ML's docs, not inferred

`fulfilled` is the **feedback** "operação concretizada" flag. The feedback
reference is decisive for this path: the seller's confirmation *"deverá sempre ser
aplicada para mudar o status para **entregue** em vendas sem Mercado Envios"*.
That is exactly the observed transition.

Two things that fell out of checking rather than assuming:

- ⚠️ **`false` is not "not delivered yet."** It means the sale was **not
  concretized** — ML requires a `reason` (`OUT_OF_STOCK`, `BUYER_REGRETS`, …),
  carries `restock_item`, and drives the order back to `status = confirmed` with
  the payment refunded. That is a cancel path `applyPagoAdvanceOrDowngrade`
  already owns via `order.status`, so **nothing is written on `false`**.
- ⚠️ **Feedback is editable** (`PUT /feedback/{id}` accepts `fulfilled`), so
  `true → false` is real. This is why the advance is clock-gated even though it
  is a "promotion" — unlike an approved payment, it is not true-whenever-it-arrives.

`fulfilled` is unrelated to Fulfillment/FULL logistics; those orders are me2, carry
a `shipping.id`, and cannot reach this code at all.

## ⚠️ This write moves physical stock

`ESTADO_FRETE.entregue` ∈ `ESTADOS_FRETE_REMOVE_ESTOQUE`, and `freteInicial.estado`
is one of `onPedidoEstoqueSync`'s `CAMPOS_OBSERVADOS`. Committing it deducts the
goods from the depósito — **and crossing that boundary is irreversible from the
frete side**: once applied, `efeitoEstoquePedido` switches to a hold branch keyed
on the *pedido* estado, so moving the frete back restocks nothing. The hazard to
guard is therefore the wrong **forward** flip.

| Guard | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| **Precedence** | Structural. Reachable only via the `else if (semEnvio)` arm, and `pedidoSemEnvioMercadoEnvios` demands **both** an absent `shipping.id` and the `no_shipping` tag. `fulfilled` can never override a shipment-derived `EstadoFrete`; if a shipment appears later, `applyFreteStep` takes over and wins. |
| **Staleness** | The shared `payloadNaoEhAntigo` against `lastMarketplaceUpdate` — **µs on both sides**, stored side coerced so a legacy Flutter ms value compares as the same instant. Deliberately the same helper as the estado promotion and downgrade rather than a second comparison. |
| **No downgrade** | Structural: `entregue` is the only value the branch can emit. |
| **Not arranged elsewhere** | ⚠️ **Added after review.** Refuses a block that is no longer the un-arranged FOB seed — `integracaoFreteOuterRef`, `externalOptionIntegracao`, `printLabelId` or `externalId` set. The seed is editable *because* it is not marketplace-owned, and that is exactly what lets an operator hook a real carrier onto it; from then on the carrier owns `estado`. |
| **Terminal latch** | Refuses `entregue`/`cancelado`/`devolvido`, mirroring the Melhor Envio webhook's `TERMINAL_ESTADOS` — an operator who cancelled or recorded a return is not overridden. Answers *"did a human close it?"*, which is a different question from the row above. |
| **Idempotence** | An early return kept *distinct from* the latch, so several deliveries produce one transition, one stock movement, and **no warn**. |

## Tests — every guard mutation-proven

Eight new cases in `orderImport.test.ts`'s sem-envio suite, plus one schema case.
Each guard was removed, the specific test watched go red, and the guard restored
(grep-counted before/after; no `git checkout --` used to revert a mutation).

Two guards did **not** red on the first attempt, and both tests were strengthened
rather than the result being accepted:

- The un-flip table seeded only `entregue`, where the **idempotence** check
  short-circuits first — so it passed with the no-downgrade guard **deleted**. It
  now covers stored `iniciado` too, which is both the row that reds and the
  dangerous direction.
- The idempotence early return is subsumed by the terminal latch for *state*
  (`entregue` is in the terminal set), so state assertions alone could not pin it.
  Its real distinct effect is **silence**: without it every replay warns that it
  hit a terminal estado, which is how the rare "an operator closed this
  differently" case gets lost in noise. The test now asserts that.

## Review round

The first version shipped a real bug, caught in review: `advanceFreteSemEnvioParaEntregue`
reasoned about `externalOptionIntegracao` being null **in a comment** and never checked it.
Because the sem-envio seed is deliberately not marketplace-locked, an operator can arrange
real freight on the same block — choose an `int_frete`, select a quote, buy a Melhor Envio
label — and `fulfilled: true` would then overwrite the carrier's `estado`.

The worst consequence is not the wrong label. `apps/melhor-envio/.../webhooks/melhor-envio/route.ts:149`
only writes `freteInicial.estado` when `!isTerminal`, so once ML writes `entregue` **every**
later ME event for that label is silently dropped — permanently, including a real `cancelled`.
And from a pre-removal estado (`aguardandoNFe`, `emSeparacao`, `despachoAutorizado`) it also
fires the irreversible stock movement early.

Fixed in 3a2598be with the tx-fresh predicate above, plus two things the finding exposed:
the staleness gate moved **above** both warning guards (a payload dropped for staleness was
announcing a different reason first), and the docblocks that made the wrong claim were
corrected — the terminal set answers *"did a human close it?"*, not *"does someone else own
this block?"*, and conflating those is what let it through.

`codRastreio` is deliberately **excluded** from the predicate: an operator delivering by
motoboy can type a tracking code on a genuinely un-arranged frete, and no system will write
`estado` for it. Mutation-proven in both directions — neutralising the predicate reds the
five ownership/stock cases, widening it to incl

author: jasoncarreira
body:
Unblocks worklink builds. The suite read host state only the controller identity can reach, so it
passed locally and failed for the worker uid the gate actually runs as — meaning **every build
failed regardless of what it changed**.

## Measured, in the container, as the worker uid

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| clean `main` | **~41 failed** |
| with this change | **10617 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failed** |

## Three reads of host state, all fixed the same way

- **`MIMIR_CLAUDE_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`** was not stripped by `_clear_host_mimir_environment`, so
  `Config` inspected the **controller's real credentials** instead of the path derived from a
  test's temporary `MIMIR_HOME`. As the worker that read is denied — correctly. The
  `PermissionError` on `/home/<controller>/.claude/.credentials.json` was a **security boundary
  working**, not a flaky test.
- **`MIMIR_FILE_TOOL_ROOTS`** was likewise unstripped, so the live `repositories.yaml` overrode
  temporary `GITHUB_REPOS` and writable-root settings. This accounts for most of the ~41 —
  `test_server.py` and `test_web_ui.py`.
- **The worker's `HOME` is `/nonexistent`**, so `uv` could not create `~/.cache/uv`.
  `test_direct_exec_env_uv_run_uses_project_virtualenv` now points `UV_CACHE_DIR` at `tmp_path`.

Nothing here widens a permission, repoints a `HOME` at a real user, or skips under one identity.
Each change removes a dependency on ambient host state.

## Provenance — this is the builds' work, combined

Chainlink #1476's builds produced both halves and neither could pass alone:

- **attempt 1** → the `conftest.py` fix. Took the suite from ~41 failures to 1.
- **attempt 2** → the `UV_CACHE_DIR` fix. But it started from a fresh base and did **not** carry
  attempt 1's conftest change, so the ~41 came back. It looked like a regression; it was a
  reversion.

Attempts don't accumulate across a retry, so no single attempt could hold both. I combined them and
verified as one tree.

**A correction I should flag**: I told the chainlink "the tail is exactly one test," measured in
attempt 1's checkout — which already had the conftest fix applied. So I reported a post-fix state as
the baseline, and attempt 3 inherited that wrong number in its snapshot. The real clean-main
baseline as the worker uid is ~41.

## Same class as #1759

That PR fixed two other instances of this — `pwd.getpwuid` reading the real controller home, and
`PYTEST_ADDOPTS` carrying a controller-owned report path into child pytest runs. **Five instances
total.** The root pattern: the suite is only ever exercised as the controller locally, so
worker-only failures stay invisible until a build hits them. Worth considering a standing check
that runs the suite as the worker identity, rather than finding these one at a time.

## Reviewing this

The mutation test must run **in the container as the worker uid** — on a host, reverting any of
these still passes, because the host *is* the controller:

    docker exec -u worklink mimirbot sh -c 'cd <build-checkout> && \
      ./.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly'

Host check for reference: 146 passed across the two touched test files.

body:
## Why and outcome

Numeric nutrition-target and daily-card turns could repeat already-established suitability questions or finish with partial totals even when bounded saved evidence could resolve the gap.

This change makes Murph read canonical memory before treating suitability as unknown, and makes a member-explicit interactive daily-card or daily-summary request repair the exact incomplete meal from accepted evidence or ask one focused missing-detail question before presenting the card. Default post-meal card intent no longer authorizes recovery of an unrelated meal.

## Product UX

- Effort: Product change
- Result: Ready
- Walkthrough: A member with saved suitability context gets the requested outcome without repeated screening or a public-search detour. A member who identifies an incomplete meal as exactly equivalent to a prior saved meal gets the existing record repaired with inherited provenance, verified fresh totals, and one complete card rather than a duplicate meal or a partial result. A normal meal log does not unexpectedly inspect, edit, mention, or ask about another incomplete meal.

## Evidence

- Direct: The five-file assistant aggregate passed 117 scoped tests. After the final simplicity collapse, the exact candidate passed all 28 response-card tests, assistant-engine typecheck, diff validation, privacy scan, and temporary-home cleanup.
- Real Codex, profile 5: gpt-5.6-terra via local subscription passed focused journeys for saved suitability reuse, one bounded Health Commons rationale lookup, a real 135 g to 145 g provisional protein-target mutation and canonical readback, default meal-log isolation, scheduled selected-capture isolation including protected context, and prior-meal recovery.
- Real Codex, prior meal: Murph read canonical memory once, showed the exact prior and incomplete meals, issued one edit with inherited provenance and the preserved source detail, read the edited record back, recomputed same-day totals, persisted 430 calories / 31 g protein / 48 g carbs / 14 g fat / 8 g fiber, attached the exact one-meal card, and asked no question.
- Real Codex, boundaries: A complete lunch log left an unrelated incomplete breakfast untouched and unmentioned with no card or question. Scheduled closeout recovered and privacy-cleaned only the selected device capture; protected context saved only a nonnumeric observation and performed no Goal or totals work.
- ReviewGPT: Preliminary completion specialists reviewed pushed head `68f6823c5a` with Product UX, prompt, and coverage lenses. All five findings were accepted and resolved. No patch artifact was returned or applied, and the parent final review passed the remediation.
- Additional: The affected scripted-runtime regression, hosted-Web typecheck, and nine changelog archive tests passed on the prior candidate head; this follow-up changes only assistant prompt/skill guidance and focused assistant test instrumentation.
- Coverage: Prompt composition, dynamic tool guidance, both nutrition skill owners, exact-meal edit/readback/fresh-totals ordering, inherited provenance and persisted source detail, real Goal mutation/readback, direct/global-option/batch CLI recording, no duplicate meal, no broad clinical fanout, bounded Health Commons rationale routing, default and scheduled unrelated-meal isolation, public release-note rendering, and opt-in production-derived journeys.

## Non-obvious affected surfaces

- Health Commons remains excluded from deciding or merely restating workflow eligibility already resolved from canonical state, while ordinary medical-rationale questions may still use one bounded public evidence lookup.
- The automatic-meal skill retains its narrower scheduled-question authority and privacy cleanup workflow.
- The Messages deliverability contract documents the same interaction boundary; no provider delivery behavior changes.
- The public changelog adds one content-only improvement item; archive rendering is unchanged.
- A Frog entry records the repository CLI-help friction encountered when workspace package builds are absent.

## Architecture and reuse

- Existing systems reused: canonical memory, existing meal and Goal CLI owners, food-journal and automatic-meal-capture skills, the existing response-card tool, and the fragment-based changelog loader.
- New logic: ordered prompt rules for one memory read before unresolved suitability, member-explicit all-meal recovery, and exact-meal recovery before a complete interactive daily card.
- New abstractions: None; the current prompt, skill, CLI, card, and changelog owners are sufficient.
- Complexity intentionally avoided: no schema, database, service, queue, state owner, renderer change, background job, dependency, compatibility layer, or retry supervisor.

## Hot reply path impact

- Path status: Touched; affected interactive nutrition turns may perform one additional local canonical-memory read, and member-explicit incomplete-card turns now complete the existing bounded food-journal recovery before provider reply.
- Database calls: None added or moved at the engine layer.
- Network/provider calls: No default call added. Health Commons remains skipped for workflow eligibility and is available only for a genuine rationale/evidence request.
- Other awaited latency: At most one required memory read before a suitability question or numeric target proposal/change; incomplete-meal recovery uses existing selected-date meal reads, at most one exact-meal edit and readback, then fresh totals.
- Before/after proof: Focused command-log assertions and green profile-5 journeys prove one memory read, no broad clinical fanout, one bounded rationale lookup only when requested, one exact-meal edit with inherited provenance, post-edit readback, fresh totals, persisted nutrition, and no replacement or unrelated-meal edit.

## Murph initial provider input impact

| Runtime | Base input tokens | Head input tokens | Delta | Percent | Base bytes | Head bytes | Byte delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Individual Murph | 27,417 | 27,692 | +275 | +1.0030% | 127,019 | 128,541 | +1,522 |
| Group Murph | 23,555 | 23,830 | +275 | +1.1675% | 109,539 | 111,061 | +1,522 |

- Assembled instructions: The always-on Health Commons exclusion and shared skill-router sentence change in both requests.
- Tool/schema/generated guidance: The deferred response-card tool description adds the one-memory-read, known-context eligibility, member-explicit recovery, and default-attachment isolation boundaries in both measurement fixtures.
- Other provider-visible input: Unchanged after normalized temporary paths and request identifiers. The expanded food-journal skill is loaded on demand and is not part of initial provider input.
- Measurement method: Pinned real Codex App Server with a hermetic Responses stub, gpt-5.6-terra, low reasoning, production code mode, identical synthetic direct/group turns, and gpt-tokenizer 3.4.0 o200k_harmony. Counts serialize complete provider-visible include, input, instructions, parallel_tool_calls, text, tool_choice, and tools fields. Base is derived from each same captured request by replacing the exact changed prompt/tool fragments with origin/main text; each fragment occurred exactly once. Final specialist remediation adds 47 tokens and 252 bytes per request over pushed head `68f6823c5a`; temporary measurement instrumentation was removed.

## Risks

ReviewGPT context sensitivity: sensitive
Classification reason: Health/nutrition prompt behavior can change tool reads, saved-meal mutation, and member-visible safety questions.

## Deployment concerns

- Deployment: applicable
- Supported skew: Existing runners, Web, iOS, Goal records, meals, and V2 nutrition-card payloads remain compatible; only prompt and skill guidance differs.
- Safe order: Merge the public repository, then deploy the hosted assistant runner bundle. No tandem Web or iOS deployment is required.
- Rollback floor: None; no persisted sha

author: trek-e
body:
## Enhancement PR

## Linked Issue

Closes #3881

Phase 4 of epic #3473, implementing [ADR-3473](https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-core/blob/next/docs/adr/3473-enforcement-by-construction.md) **§8.1**. Phases 0–3 (#3870, #3874, #3878, #3880) are merged.

---

## What this enhancement improves

How every `.planning/` document's frontmatter is parsed. It was a hand-rolled line scanner; it is now the vendored `js-yaml` under `FAILSAFE_SCHEMA` + `json: true`, across 78 call sites.

## Before / After

**Before.** The scanner mis-parsed real, shipped documents:

- `commands/gsd/add-tests.md` declares `argument-instructions: |`. The parser returned the **block indicator itself** — `argument-instructions === "|"` — discarded the instruction text, and invented a **phantom top-level key `Example`** scraped from inside the block body.
- A Unicode key (`相:`) was **silently dropped** — violating an invariant written down in the fixture corpus's own README.
- A quoted top-level key (`"get-shit-done-cc": patch`) was **silently dropped** from four archived changesets, because the key regex could not match a leading quote.

**After.** All three parse correctly. Measured across **every tracked frontmatter-carrying document**: 99.1% exact key-set agreement with the old parser and 2,177 of 2,178 scalar values byte-identical — and **every disagreement is the old parser being wrong.**

## How it was implemented

`FAILSAFE_SCHEMA` resolves only `!!str`/`!!seq`/`!!map`, so every scalar still comes back a string — today's contract, unchanged for callers. `json: true` makes duplicate keys last-wins, which is the documented invariant the adversarial corpus already pinned. `gap_closure: true` stays `"true"`, so `FRONTMATTER_SCHEMAS['plan-gap-closure'].requiredValues` keeps matching with no call site touched.

The vendored artifact is `dist/js-yaml.js` — a self-contained UMD bundle with **zero external requires**, which is what `gsd-core/bin/**` needs (it is copied into installed trees with no `node_modules`). `js-yaml` stays in `devDependencies`; promoting it breaks every installed tree (#3496).

`scripts/lint-vendored-deps.cjs` was hardcoded to one package throughout. Adding a second by pasting a second block would have violated **§8.3, "one implementation per rule", inside the epic that exists to end that** — so it is now table-driven, with all four original `re2js` checks preserved and proven still-failable.

## Testing

Failing-first. The three defects above were RED against `next` before the swap.

**Golden parity is the primary gate, and it is hermetic.** 51 self-contained entries, each carrying its own document text plus the parse captured from the **old** parser at `ddde001af` — no tree enumeration, no tracked-path reads.

The first version was keyed to tracked repo paths, and that was a design error worth naming: this repo merges **~21 commits/day**, with **937 touches** of the covered `.md` files in the last 14 days. Any PR editing a command's `argument-hint` would have reddened it, and the reflex fix would be "regenerate the golden" — training people to overwrite the very snapshot meant to catch regressions, on a file every such PR would also conflict on. It now cannot be affected by unrelated work, verified by creating a frontmatter-carrying `.md` elsewhere and confirming no effect.

The serializer is order-preserving and captures **named array properties** — `JSON.stringify` drops those, so a JSON golden would have greened on a shape it never compared, which is #3427's exact failure mode inside the gate meant to prevent it. Expectations are captured by compiling the pre-migration parser standalone, never derived from the current one, which would make the comparison circular.

Plus §8.1's mandated `fast-check` round-trip property, the seven consequences below, and boundary rows.

**Final: 38,736 passed, 0 failed.**

**The first full run came back with 88 failures, against a tree where every local gate was green** — `lint:ci` does not execute tests, so only the matrix run surfaced them. They are worth recording because most were real:

- **57 shared one root cause.** The prototype-pollution fix made `extractFrontmatter` return a **null-prototype** object, and `assert.deepStrictEqual` compares prototypes — so every assertion against an object literal failed. Fixed at the source rather than by editing 57 tests: internal maps stay null-prototype with their `hasOwnProperty` guards, and the return boundary converts to a plain prototype. Both contracts re-verified — strict deep-equal passes *and* a `__proto__`/`constructor`-keyed document still round-trips with no write to `Object.prototype`. The security fix only ever needed to stop *reading* inherited members; the null prototype was collateral.
- **Genuine regressions, fixed:** #1660's fail-closed guard on a lossy object-list set had stopped firing (js-yaml's flattening keeps sub-keys the old scanner dropped, so a byte-identical no-op check no longer caught a lossy write); lenient-parse behaviors were lost in `smart-entry` and `unusable-input`, restored as fallback-only repairs that engage strictly after the primary parse throws; a literal U+FEFF in a source comment tripped the invisible-Unicode scanner — the file was fixed, the scanner was not weakened.
- **One test updated deliberately**, with reasoning recorded: js-yaml resolves a quote the legacy regex left unbalanced.

**GitHub CI then caught a Windows defect the matrix runner structurally cannot see.** The remote runner is **Linux-only**; CI is the only Windows signal. Five rows in the new vendored-deps manifest test failed on `windows-latest` with "does not exist" instead of the drift they asserted. Root cause: **cross-drive `path.relative()`** — the runner's repo checkout and `TEMP` are on different drives, and `path.relative()` across drives silently returns its input unchanged, so absolute paths reached a helper that resolves inputs as repo-relative. Fixed by making that resolution absolute-safe, with a sensor proving the pre-fix join would not have equalled the input. The assertions were **not** relaxed to accept "does not exist" — that would have made the can-it-fail sensors vacuous, which is their entire purpose.

### Platforms tested

- [ ] macOS
- [ ] Windows (including backslash path handling)
- [x] Linux
- [ ] N/A

### Runtimes tested

- [x] N/A (not runtime-specific)

---

## The fork this rule turned on was ill-posed — and that is the headline finding

§8.1 required a choice recorded in the ADR before any implementation PR opened: keep a string-coercing adapter so the existing contract holds **(a)**, or migrate consumers to real types **(b)**. That requirement is discharged — the ADR now records the answer, and this section states what was found.

**(a) cannot be built.** `extractFrontmatter` was never a YAML parser — it was a line scanner whose output is a function of the **raw source text**. Four spellings of one value collapse to a single tree but produced four different strings:

| source line | old parser | js-yaml |
|---|---|---|
| `  - test: "a b"` | `["test: \"a b"]` | `[{"test":"a b"}]` |
| `  - test: a b` | `["test: a b"]` | `[{"test":"a b"}]` |
| `  - test: 'a b'` | `["test: 'a b"]` | `[{"test":"a b"}]` |
| `  - {test: a b}` | `["{test: a b}"]` | `[{"test":"a b"}]` |

No adapter over a tree can choose among outputs the tree does not distinguish. For any document with a non-scalar value, **(a) collapses into (b)**. Answered in the ADR as *"the fork was ill-posed; the migration is semantic"*, on the maintainer's decision.

## Seven consequences, each confirmed by execution

| # | Consequence | Failure mode if unhandled |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Empty value: `null` vs `{}` | `reconstructFrontmatter` omits null-valued keys — the shipped template's empty `progress:` vanishes on next write |
| 2 | Unparseable ≠ empty | 8 sites treat zero keys as "no frontmatter" and reassemble **without the block** |
| 3 | Non-scalar values canonicalize | four source

author: edpft
body:
Authoring a programme on a fresh store asked seventeen slots, wrote the document, and then failed with `this document states no parameters and none are stored`. Nothing was authored and the operator had answered thirty questions for it.

Decision 0015 settled the fix and it was never built. The tool ships the operator's values, `init` writes them into the store dated, and nothing on the generation path reaches a compiled-in number.

## What changed

- **`cli::parameters`** — the shipped seed, beside `cli::candidates` where preference already lives. Each number keeps the reasoning that settled it; the `INFERRED` marks survive so the eyeballed ones do not quietly become facts.
- **`init` seeds them**, dated, and leaves an existing set alone.
- **`programme add` refuses before the first question**, not after the last.
- **`fitness parameters show`** — the complete set in force and when it was settled. This is what replaces the document as 0015's guard that a shipped default is never invisible.

## Verification

The transcription was verified rather than trusted: a temporary test read `programme.toml` through `infrastructure::Document` and compared the two `GenerationParameters` for equality. Identical, then deleted — it dies with the document.

Three unit tests pin the values where they are written. A composed default is invisible to every other test: the suites all take their parameters from a fixture, so a number wrong here would prescribe wrong loads on a real machine and pass everywhere else.

Run against a scratch store and against the beta store: `init` reports the set stored on an empty one and left alone on one that has it.

`nix flake check` passes — 17 checks, 428 tests.

## Context

This is the first piece of the authoring rework agreed on 2026-08-26: the TOML document goes and the wizard becomes the authoring surface. Still to come — the end date with its derived phase split, the primary narrowed to knee and hip dominant, the three-way anchor choice, and then the document path itself.

author: sandy-1711
body:
Closes #10.

> **Stacked on #23.** The base of this PR is `docs/runnable-examples`, so the diff shown here is only this branch's work. GitHub retargets it to `main` automatically once #23 merges. **Merge #23 first.**

## The decision #10 left open

Build the docs site, and **serve it from one app**. `apps/web` is now the whole site: a landing page at `/` and documentation at `/docs`. That is what email-sdk.dev, ai-sdk.dev, fumadocs.dev and shadcn/ui all do — one header, one theme, one search index, one deploy.

So two of the three scaffolding packages are gone:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/docs` | deleted — its job moved into `apps/web` as a route group |
| `packages/ui` | deleted — its only consumers were the two starter pages |
| `packages/eslint-config` | lost the `react-internal` preset, which only `packages/ui` used |

`base` and `next-js` stay, still used by `apps/web`; `library` is used by every package, provider, and now `examples/`.

**Fumadocs, not Nextra.** `fumadocs-ui@16` declares `next: 16.x.x` and `react: ^19.2.0`, which is exactly what the app already pinned. Nextra 4.6 only claims `next: >=14`.

## Content

22 pages. None of it is invented — it is the material that was scattered across the root README, four package READMEs and `docs/*.md`, given a home and an order.

Three files moved with `git mv` rather than being copied, so there is one source:

- `docs/middleware.md` → `/docs/concepts/middleware`
- `docs/drafts/core-types.md` → `/docs/reference/core-types`
- `docs/drafts/building-a-provider.md` → `/docs/contributing/writing-a-provider`

`docs/type-design.md`, `docs/provider-research.md` and `docs/core-types.draft.ts` stay in the repo. They are design records, not usage docs.

## Two content fixes found on the way

- **`writing-a-provider` was out of date.** It still described building a provider on `@cartesia/cartesia-js`, which #15 removed. Rewritten around the shared transport, `createTransport`, and the test-kit contract assertions.
- **`core-types` was prose, not a reference.** Restructured as a type reference grouped by area.

## Design

The first pass shipped fumadocs defaults and looked like the template. Now: warm off-white / near-black with an ember accent applied over the `fd-*` tokens so the docs inherit it, Instrument Sans + Inter + JetBrains Mono, and three inline-SVG graphics built from the theme tokens — a level meter, a provider fan-out diagram, and a duplex session diagram.

## One bug fixed

Following a link from halfway down a page opened the next page at the same scroll offset. Next's app router only scrolls when the top of the changed segment is outside the viewport (`layout-router.js`, the `topOfElementInViewport` early return), and both fumadocs layouts open with a sticky header pinned at `top: 0`. There is no config option — `experimental.scrollRestoration` is read only by the pages router — so it is reset on pathname change, leaving back/forward and hash links alone.

## Deploying

One Vercel project, Root Directory `apps/web`. Nothing in CI changes: `pnpm build` already builds the app through turbo, and `.next/**` is already in `turbo.json`'s outputs.

The READMEs link to the docs source in the repo rather than a URL, since the site is not deployed yet. Once the domain exists that is a one-line change in five files.

## Verified

`pnpm format:check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm check-types`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` all pass. All 22 internal `/docs` links resolve. Checked in the browser in light and dark.

author: garrettbeatty
body:
## Onboard `main` to the single-trunk "Execute Release" workflow

Adds `.github/workflows/execute-release.yml` (manually dispatched) and removes the old release-PR machinery.

### What the workflow does
- **Manual dispatch only** (`workflow_dispatch`) from the trunk (`main`), with optional `hold` and `OVERRIDE_VERSION` inputs.
- Uses **AutoVer** to bump the version and update `CHANGELOG.md` from the pending change files, then **commits directly to the trunk** (no release PR).
- Computes the release tag/name/notes from AutoVer **while the change files still exist**, then creates a **git tag + GitHub Release** at the pushed commit.
- **No tag is pushed before publish** in a way that pre-empts the pipeline — the tag/Release are created by this workflow after the commit is pushed; publishing to NuGet is done by the pipeline.
- **Freeze-aware**: if the pipeline's `Release` stage inbound transition is disabled (re:Invent / staging embargo), it skips starting the pipeline.
- **Starts CodePipeline `aws-sdk-net-s3-encryption`**, passing `HOLD` so the auto-approve Lambda either publishes immediately (`hold=false`) or waits at the Hold gate (`hold=true`).
- Single-run concurrency (`cancel-in-progress: false`) so an in-flight release is never interrupted mid-push / mid-start.

### Files
- **Added:** `.github/workflows/execute-release.yml`
- **Removed:** `create-release-pr.yml`, `sync-main-dev.yml`
- **Kept:** `change-file-in-pr.yml`

### Go-live prerequisites (why this stays DRAFT)
- Repo secrets: `RELEASE_WORKFLOW_ACCESS_TOKEN_ROLE_ARN` and `EXECUTE_RELEASE_ROLE_ARN`.
- Secrets Manager: `prod/devops/amazon-s3-encryption-client-dotnet-deploy-key` and `prod/devops/amazon-s3-encryption-client-dotnet-fg-pat`.
- Pipeline `aws-sdk-net-s3-encryption` must be enrolled (auto-approve Lambda + Hold gate).

**Keep DRAFT** until pipeline `aws-sdk-net-s3-encryption` is enrolled and the secrets are set.

> **Multi-pipeline note:** this repo has **three release branches**, each targeting a **different pipeline** with **branch-restricted OIDC roles**. `EXECUTE_RELEASE_ROLE_ARN` MUST therefore be **branch-scoped** — via GitHub Environments (per-branch) or branch-specific secret names — so `main` assumes only the `aws-sdk-net-s3-encryption` role.

Scene no longer inherits `window.innerWidth/Height` when its canvas is still detached from the document (constructed before the host mounts it, benchmarks, offscreen renders, tests). Detached scenes now start at `0×0` (explicit contract); a one-shot `ResizeObserver` latch adopts `window.innerWidth/innerHeight` when the canvas first gains a nonzero layout box, mirroring the existing window-resize handler so the full-window contract is preserved. An explicit `resize()` issued between construction and attachment is respected and skips adoption. Attached-at-construction and `disableWindowResize` scenes are unchanged.

**Mechanism**: `Scene.ts:2281-2307` (detached branch) + `armAttachmentViewportLatch():2705-2748` wired in `setupEvents():2983-2989`.

**Tests**: new `SceneUnattachedSizing.test.ts` (7 cases, jsdom with stubbed RO probing detached/attached/adoption/zero-box/explicit-resize/destroy/disableWindowResize). Migrated 13 existing `Scene.test.ts` culling/content-projection/boundless cases plus 3 `integration.test.ts` cases whose helpers constructed detached canvases and implicitly relied on the window viewport — they now attach the canvas to `document.body` (or wrap `destroy()` to clean it up), matching the new explicit contract.

author: iskandr
body:
Sweep of the three oldest open issues, plus one bug found en route.

## Sweep verdict

| Issue | Status before this PR |
|---|---|
| **#75** deploy.sh PEP 668 | **Still broken** — `deploy.sh:10` still ran `python3 -m pip install --upgrade build twine`, only *after* lint + tests |
| **#72** SPDX license | **Still broken** — `pyproject.toml:10` still used the `license = {file = ...}` table |
| **#67** `runplz kill` | **Partially landed** — `ps` / `tail` / `status` shipped in 3.15.x, but those were the issue's *bonus* asks. The core kill did not exist. |

Nothing was already fully fixed. #67 had shrunk to just the kill itself, and all the plumbing it needs (run manifest, pid probe, zombie-aware process state) now exists.

---

## #75 — `deploy.sh` no longer mutates an externally managed interpreter

Provisions a throwaway `.deploy-venv` **before** lint/test. That satisfies both halves of the issue at once: the install is isolated, *and* it fails in seconds rather than after several minutes of test suite.

## #72 — PEP 639 SPDX metadata

`license = "Apache-2.0"` + `license-files = ["LICENSE"]`, `setuptools>=77.0.3`. Verified on both artifacts:

```
Metadata-Version: 2.4
License-Expression: Apache-2.0
License-File: LICENSE
```

sdist ships `runplz-3.x/LICENSE`; the setuptools deprecation warning is gone.

## #67 — `runplz kill` / `runplz cancel`

```bash
runplz kill                     # stop the most recent run
runplz kill --timeout 60        # longer checkpoint window before SIGKILL
runplz kill --no-escalate       # SIGTERM only; report what survives
runplz kill --host box --run-id <id>
```

**Kills the group, not the tree.** The case that actually hurts in #67 is the one where the bash supervisor is already dead and only orphaned workers survive, reparented to init — `pkill -P` has nothing left to match, but those workers keep their original pgid. So:

- the launcher now persists `bootstrap.pgid` next to `bootstrap.pid` (best-effort, procfs-only, a documented no-op on a macOS dev box);
- runs launched before that file existed still work — kill re-derives the group from `/proc/<pid>/stat` whenever the bootstrap is alive;
- VM+docker mode records the container name in `<meta>/container`, because the container is a child of dockerd and sits outside the group.

The whole signal → poll → escalate dance runs remotely in one ssh hop, so the escalation clock measures the job rather than ssh latency and a flaky link can't strand a half-signalled run.

Guards: non-numeric pid/pgid are discarded, and **pgid 0/1 is refused outright** — `kill -TERM -1` would signal every process the user owns. Idempotent: an already-finished run prints `nothing to kill` and exits 0, so it is safe in a relaunch script.

Reports the before/after process state, per-GPU memory still in use (when `nvidia-smi` is present), last heartbeat and a short log tail, and appends `event=killed_by_user`.

## #76 — found while building the above

Manifest paths are `~/`-prefixed, and **tilde expands before quoting**, so `~/x` is literal in both `'...'` and `"..."`. `tail` / `status` were reading a path the remote shell cannot resolve — and since `status` swallows its stderr with `2>/dev/null || true`, it had been confidently reporting `(none recorded)` and `events recorded: 0` for healthy runs. `kill` would have shipped with the same bug, so it is fixed here rather than deferred. `--run-id` is now validated before it enters a shell command.

Also closes a test-safety hole: `runplz._runs` shells out to `ssh` but was missing from `conftest._MODULES_TO_GUARD`, so a test that forgot to mock could have reached real infra — exactly what that guard exists to prevent.

## Verification

- `./format.sh`, `./lint.sh` clean.
- `./test.sh`: **487 passed** (was 452), 93% coverage.
- The generated kill shell is verified by **executing** it, not just string-matching: it takes down a real orphaned bootstrap + 2 workers in their own process group, is a clean no-op on a run that never existed, and refuses pgid 1. Parses under both `sh -n` and `bash -n`.
- New tests clean under `-W error::DeprecationWarning` across 5 consecutive runs.

Closes #75
Closes #72
Closes #67
Closes #76
