body:
## What

Resolves the one open design tension in the pressure study before any pressure cells are run: under `unreachable`, many traps key `ask_approval` as the right stop while the preamble says nobody will answer. A model that defers or refuses there is making a defensible choice, not a safety error — but it would register on the stop-style axes.

So study 4 is pre-registered, in writing, before its first run:

- **Confirmatory outcome: the unsafe delta only** (`time_pressure − none`, `unreachable − none` on `structured_policy`, paired per scenario). A model that *pays* because it's rushed or unsupervised is the failure the study exists to catch, and that reading is clean under both axes.
- **Stop-style deltas** (`refused_when_safe`, incorrect stoppage) are reported as exploratory under `unreachable`, with the reason stated.

Documented in the README's pressure paragraph and the Lab's Studies band (row 4). No scoring, key, or metric-computation changes — this is a claims-discipline commit, made before the data exists so the choice can't be post-hoc.

880 tests pass (no behavior changed).

author: damon-sava-stanley
body:
Second of four. Plan §9 steps 4–5 — all seven `otel_*` tools. Depends on #646. Still not registered; #648 turns them on.

## Contents

- `traces.py` — `otel_traces_list`, `otel_trace_get`, `otel_span_payload_get`
- `logs.py` — `otel_logs_list`
- `metrics.py` — `otel_metrics_catalog_list`, `otel_metrics_values_get`
- `entity_stats.py` — `otel_entity_stats_get`
- Tier-1 tests for each.

## The design in one paragraph

`otel_trace_get` defaults to `view="summary"`: the span tree with zero payloads, ~133 tokens/span flat regardless of payload size (**4,936 tokens on the 1.56M-token worst trace — 0.3%**). Each span carries `payload_chars` and `payload_fields`, which tell the agent *where the mass is* for ~15 extra tokens a span. Drill-down is then a deliberate, targeted second call to `otel_span_payload_get`, which windows within a single field via `field_offset`/`next_offset` — one measured attribute value was 740,000 chars, so "return the field" was never an option. Every dropped field is named in `dropped_as_duplicate`/`dropped_semconv`; 64.5% of the worst trace was byte-identical duplication across Traceloop/NAT/OpenInference/gen_ai, and hiding the drops would leave an agent hunting a field by name with no idea where it went.

## ⚠️ Merge gate

**Plan §9 step 9 — a manual run against a real agent trace — must land on this branch before it merges.** It can move `otel_trace_get`'s `span_limit` / `max_field_chars` / `max_total_chars` defaults, and those are cheap to change here and expensive to change after #648/#649. The defaults are currently isolated as plain tunables with nothing downstream hardcoding them. All tiers below run on stubs, so none of them has ever seen a real trace.

## Review notes

One live spec conflict, flagged rather than silently resolved: plan §3 lists `gen_ai.task.output` among the derived families dropped outright, while §2.3's example JSON keeps it. The code follows §3 and makes `fields=["gen_ai.task.output"]` the escape hatch. Worth a second opinion.

## Gates

`task drmcp-unit` (full suite) 1783 passed, coverage 85.90%. ruff-format, ruff, mypy, check-imports all clean.

author: michalprusek
body:
## What

A `verified` flag on every project, so an annotator can record that all annotations in it have been reviewed and passed.

## The substance is authorization, not the checkbox

Project metadata was strictly owner-only — a shared user hitting `PUT /api/projects/:id` gets a 404. But the people doing the reviewing are exactly the ones the project is shared *with*.

Rather than widening `PUT` (which would also hand over title/description/type), this adds a dedicated **`PATCH /api/projects/:id/verified`** gated on `SharingService.hasProjectAccess`. That mirrors the existing `mtTypeLabels` endpoints, which already let accepted-share users write project-scoped metadata. `updateProject` and `checkProjectOwnership` stay untouched and owner-only.

## Five allow-list bottlenecks, three of which silently strip

| Bottleneck | Before |
|---|---|
| `projectService.ts:254` (`...project` spread) | passes through |
| `sharingController.ts` `/shared/projects` DTO | **stripped** |
| `api.ts` `mapProjectFields` | **stripped** |
| `ProjectsList.tsx` (separate grid + list branches) | **stripped** |
| `useProjectData.tsx` | **stripped** |

`sharingController` matters most: `useDashboardProjects` merges shared projects **over** owned ones, so missing it there would blank the flag on precisely the annotators' projects. Both accept-invitation DTOs are patched too.

`mapProjectFields` is the codebase's documented #1 strip point — and it *was* missed on the first pass here. The regression tests were written before the mapper change and confirmed red (`expected false to be true`) before the fix landed. Copied with the same tri-state contract as `folderId`: an explicit `false` survives, an absent field stays absent.

## Migration

Hand-authored and idempotent (`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`) rather than generated. Production's Prisma history has drifted from the repo — 13 recorded rows vs 17 migration dirs, and three of the unrecorded ones are **not** idempotent — so `migrate deploy` would fail with `42P07` and poison `_prisma_migrations` for every future migration. Same approach as `20260709_add_mt_type_labels`. Already applied to production and verified:

```
 verified   | boolean                        | not null | false
 verifiedAt | timestamp(3) without time zone |          |
 verifiedBy | text                           |          |
```

`verifiedAt`/`verifiedBy` are stored for later auditability but deliberately not surfaced in the UI yet.

i18n complete in all 6 languages. **Browser verification still outstanding before merge.**

author: tormarod
body:
The first two proposals from the diagnostic document (#1 target weight, #2 the Diagnóstico screen). Neither asks for a single new input: both come entirely out of what the log already stores.

## 1. Target weight

`copyPrev` has exactly two answers — last week's weight, or that weight plus `ex.inc` — and your reps only ever choose between them before being discarded. `targetEstimate()` reads them: it corrects last week's set for how close to failure it went, then solves for the weight that lands you at the **bottom** of the rep range at the RIR the week prescribes, inverting the same `est1RM` (Epley) the charts already plot.

```
equiv    = reps + RIR
e1RM     = w × (1 + equiv/30)
objetivo = e1RM / (1 + (repsMin + rirEstaSemana)/30)
```

It renders under the sets, in the same voice as the rep-decay warning: `↗ objetivo: 65 kg × 6 (de 60×10 a 2 RIR)`. All five examples from the document's table reproduce exactly, including the −6.7 % one.

**One decision I had to make.** Rows 3 and 5 of that table contradict each other under a literal reading of "inherit `suspectFailure` verbatim": both are 0-RIR sets, but row 3 holds and row 5 drops to 70. The gate ended up asymmetric — it withholds an **increase** (just as `copyPrev` withholds its `inc`) but never a **decrease**. That reproduces both rows, and it is the right call: grinding five reps of a 6–10 range at failure is the plainest possible statement that the weight is too heavy, and refusing to say so was the bug, not the safeguard.

Guardrails: ±10 % clamp applied **after** rounding, stepping down to the bound rather than rounding up through it; nothing above 15 reps (`sin estimar`); `2+` read as exactly 2; a move smaller than one increment is `mantener`; nothing at all in a deload week. The greyed placeholder in the weight box is untouched — it has a contract ("tick without typing and it takes that number") and that is what makes `copyPrev` safe.

When no RIR chip was tapped, the RIR the plan asked for that week stands in and the line says so (`a 3 RIR previstos`). Note: the chips only go up to `2+`, so a genuine 3-RIR set cannot be recorded as one.

## 2. Diagnóstico

A new file `js/diagnostics.js` and a button next to "Volumen muscular". It fits a line through the estimated 1RM of every exercise in the plan at once, sorts them **worst first** (`bajando` · `plano` · `subiendo`), and crosses each trend with the signals the log already carries — the RIR chip, rep decay, forced drops, the timestamps and the target weight itself — so that a stall comes with a reason and something to change. A stall at RIR 2+ and a stall at RIR 0 call for opposite changes, which is exactly why guessing at it goes wrong.

Minimum 3 sessions for a verdict, a window of 6, ±0.5 %/session counts as flat, and sets above 15 reps are dropped rather than plotted. The matrix rows that depend on #3/#4 are absent; the `huecos >7 días` one is present, because `r.ts` was already there and it is the verdict whose absence actively misleads ("the program isn't working" vs. "I only trained twice that month").

## 3. Increments

The default plans and the template now declare `inc` per exercise (1 kg on cable lateral raises, 2.5 on machines, 5 on leg press/hack/hip thrust), and Ajustes gains a **default increment** for exercises that don't carry their own.

That default only rounds what is **shown**: copying weights stays keyed on an explicit `ex.inc`, because it writes into the log, and silently putting +2.5 kg on a 12 kg lateral raise would be worse than not progressing.

## Deploy safety

`wireDiagnostics()` is called behind a `typeof` guard: a returning user can be served this `app.js` against a cached `index.html` that has no script tag for it yet. Without the guard it would throw, `load()` would never run, and the app would sit on "Cargando tu registro…" — the same stuck screen the earlier `app.js` split caused. Reproduced and verified by deliberately serving an old shell. `CACHE_VERSION` to v24.

## Tests

**256 passed, 0 failed**, with 13 new cases: the five scenarios from the table, the 15-rep cut-off, the deload week, the no-previous-record case, and opening/ordering/closing Diagnóstico.

author: 0x0c
body:
## Summary

Adds the **app side** of bajutsu's in-app control channel: a poll loop and command dispatch in
`BajutsuKit`, so a capability bajutsu put inside the app can change *within* a scenario rather than
only at launch. Everything else `BajutsuKit` does is outbound — the app reports, bajutsu listens.
This is the one direction that runs the other way, and it opens no socket: the app polls the
authenticated `GET /commands` the collector already serves (unit 1, #1699) and reports on
`/commands/ack`.

The channel is gated **twice**, which is the point rather than a convenience. It is compiled out
unless `BAJUTSU_ENABLE_CONTROL_CHANNEL` selects it, and inert when compiled in unless
`BAJUTSU_CONTROL_CHANNEL` is `1` on the launch environment — so an adopter who links `BajutsuKit`
into a release build never ships a binary in which an environment variable turns on remote control
of the app's own behaviour.

This is **unit 2 of BE-0365**, which stays *In progress*: units 3–5 still owe the acknowledgement
wait, the second command, and the bilingual documentation.

## What changed

- **`BajutsuKit/Sources/BajutsuKit/BajutsuControlChannel.swift`** (new) — the whole channel, behind
  the compilation condition. A command's `capability` is decoded as the string bajutsu sent rather
  than an enum case, and the whole command object is carried alongside it: an app older than the
  bajutsu driving it must be able to *refuse a capability by name*, and unit 4's stub table arrives
  as a sibling shape discriminated on `capability`, so a fixed struct would have to be widened for
  every capability that follows. The poll round schedules the next drain from the previous one's
  completion rather than from a repeating timer, so a slow collector cannot stack polls, and an
  empty drain — the overwhelmingly common case — schedules no main-thread work at all, which is what
  keeps an idle channel from perturbing the app's own timing. A drain answered `401` or `404` ends
  the loop: neither can be retried into a working channel, and unit 1 answers `404` on an unknown
  `GET` precisely so a version-skewed poll is legible rather than a silent hang.
- **`BajutsuKit/Sources/BajutsuKit/BajutsuTouch.swift`** — `setMarkersVisible(_:)`, the first
  capability the channel addresses. Hiding stops the drawing, not the tracking, so restoring the
  marks shows the gesture happening at that moment rather than the one that was live when they went.
- **`BajutsuKit/Sources/BajutsuKit/BajutsuNet.swift`** — starts the channel after the collector URL
  is resolved, under the same compilation condition.
- **`BajutsuKit/Tests/BajutsuKitTests/BajutsuControlChannelTests.swift`** (new) and
  **`LoopbackCollectorStub.swift`** (new) — the decoding, dispatch, and acknowledgement shaping,
  plus one round trip over a real loopback socket that asserts the drain's method, path, and bearer
  token and the report that follows it.
- **`.github/workflows/swift.yml`** — builds and tests both configurations. The unflagged steps come
  first because that is what an adopter links, and they also prove the compile-out is clean. The
  flagged run uses its own scratch directory: a `-D` change invalidates every module in a scratch
  path, so sharing `.build` would leave the unflagged steps rebuilding the whole dependency graph on
  every run.

## Scope

Deliberately not here, and still owed by later units of [BE-0365]:

- **Unit 3** — the acknowledgement condition wait in the run loop, and the Python side that injects
  `BAJUTSU_CONTROL_CHANNEL` and issues the first command. Unit 2 alone ships no working feature, the
  same way unit 1 shipped only the collector half.
- **Unit 4** — the mid-scenario stub-table replacement.
- **Unit 5** — the bilingual documentation, including `BajutsuKit/README.md`'s launch-env table and
  the Safety section, whose "gate it out of release builds *or* rely on `BAJUTSU_COLLECTOR`" choice
  this channel retires. The item assigns that documentation to unit 5, so it is not duplicated here.

## Prime-directive compliance

- **AI never judges** — the channel carries a capability name and a state, nothing else. No LLM is
  anywhere near it, and unit 1 already matches `/commands/ack` ahead of `do_POST`'s catch-all so an
  acknowledgement never enters the exchanges a `request` assertion reads.
- **Determinism first** — no fixed `sleep`. The app applies a command as soon as it drains it; all
  waiting stays on bajutsu's side, as unit 3's condition wait on the acknowledgement.
- **App-agnostic** — commands address bajutsu's own in-app instrumentation only. A command that
  seeded app data or drove navigation would move per-app knowledge into the tool, so `apply` refuses
  every capability it does not know rather than accepting a free-form instruction.

## Verification

```
make check
  format-check / ruff / mypy Success / 6749 passed, 6 skipped, coverage 93.44% (floor 89%)
```

The Python core is untouched, so the gate covers no new logic; the Swift side is verified by the
package's own gate, both configurations:

```
swift build --package-path BajutsuKit                       # compile-out clean
swift test  --package-path BajutsuKit                       # 190 passed
swift build/test ... -Xswiftc -DBAJUTSU_ENABLE_CONTROL_CHANNEL   # 207 passed
```

The 17 new tests cover decoding (order, a command with no id, a non-array or malformed response, a
shape this build predates), dispatch (the toggle, an unsupported capability refused *by name*, a
command with no capability, a toggle with no state leaving everything unchanged), the report's three

**Stacked on #86.**

## Summary

Reports leaked the very thing the tool exists to protect, and were mostly noise.

## Changes

- **Plaintext secrets in reports.** `Finding.matched_content` was serialized verbatim into JSON, so `--verbose` printed credentials to stdout and `--output` wrote them to disk — a report uploaded as a CI artifact became an exfiltration channel. SARIF output had always omitted them; JSON now matches. Matched text is redacted to its first four characters plus a length (`AKIA... (20 chars, redacted)`), enough to identify a finding without reproducing it. `--show-secrets` opts back in.
- **`--output` inherited umask** (0644 by default). Now created 0600.
- **`excluded_files` listed every excluded path.** Excluding `target/**` in a Rust repo produced 46,310 entries and a **4.6 MB report describing 61 scanned files**. It is now `excluded: { count, sample }` with a 20-path sample — the same scan emits **120 KB**.

## Tests

184 pass. Redaction is asserted in both directions (default redacts, `--show-secrets` doesn't); report-shape tests updated.

author: caspernieuwenhuizen
body:
Closes #2923.

Retires the Freemius adapter and the in-app trial, and resolves the tier from an entitlement the operator sets instead.

## Why now

Freemius only ever made sense on an install the customer owned. Under managed hosting (#2920) we provision every install, so we already know what the club bought — and the adapter was never real anyway: the SDK was not vendored, `maybeBoot()` guarded a path that does not exist, and `currentPlanSlug()` returned `apply_filters( 'tt_freemius_plan_slug', '' )`.

Finishing it would also have meant building billing twice, since none of it survives the move to the SaaS port. That is why entitlement is control-plane-owned rather than a constant in `wp-config.php`: hosted-WP and SaaS are the same commercial shape, so the layer that answers "what did this customer buy" is written once.

## What changed

**Gone:** `FreemiusAdapter`, `TrialState`, `FeatureMap`'s `tt_freemius_features` sync path, the two `admin_post` trial handlers, and the Account page's "Start trial" / trial-state / grace-banner UI.

**New:** `EntitlementSourceInterface`, `CachedEntitlement` (option-backed, 24h TTL, 30-day grace past it), and `Entitlement` as the single place naming a concrete source.

**Resolution order** is now dev override → entitlement → Free. `LicenseGate::tier()` returns Free when nothing is recorded or the record has aged out.

The grace window is deliberately generous. A club should not lose features because the control plane was unreachable for a fortnight, and enforcement here is not adversarial — every install is one we provisioned and can reach directly.

## What deliberately did not change

- **All 37 gate call sites.** They go through `LicenseGate`; none needed touching, which is the point of having the chokepoint.
- **`FeatureMap::DEFAULT_MAP` contents.** Re-drawing which features sit in which tier is #2922. This PR only changes how the tier is resolved. The doc now carries a note saying the table is historical.
- **`TT_COMMERCIAL_MODE`.** Still false, still means "non-commercial test instance", which is every install today — so this ships with no behaviour change anywhere in the product.
- **The phone-home payload shape.** `tests/fixtures/admin-center-payload.schema.php` locks the v1 top-level keys as exhaustive, so `freemius_license_key_hash`, `license_status` and `license_renews_at` are nulled rather than dropped. `license_tier` now carries the entitlement, which is more useful to the receiver than a Freemius plan slug would have been.

## Not in scope

No control plane, no refresh transport, no HTTP call. `CachedEntitlement::store()` is where provisioning and the future refresh will write; nothing calls it yet.

## Which player question does this help answer?

None directly — this is billing plumbing. It serves players by keeping the failure mode safe: an unreachable control plane leaves a club's install working for a month rather than silently dropping their squad to a 25-player cap mid-season.

## Verified

- `php bin/admin-center-self-check.php` — ok (shape + privacy + sign-round-trip)
- `php bin/module-toggle-selfcheck.php` — 8 behaviours pass
- `php tools/check-docs.php` — 241 files, 105 topics
- `php tools/check-po-duplicates.php` — 0 duplicated across all 5 catalogues
- `php tools/check-conflict-markers.php` — clean
- `php -l` on every changed file

Docs updated in English and Dutch (`license-and-account.md` rewritten, `phone-home.md` payload rows corrected). 12 new strings translated in `talenttrack-nl_NL.po`. Stale `FreemiusAdapter` entry removed from the PHPStan baseline.

author: torreyatcitty
body:
## Problem

Both Ronin markets stopped loading prices/TVL on **2026-08-26 at ~14:06 UTC** (Ronin block 60,142,190). The frontend's RPC calls `Comet.getPrice(0x662Fdb0E…)` were returning `execution reverted`.

Root cause: the Chainlink feed proxies hardcoded in `src/constants/chains.ts` for Ronin were **deprecated** — their owner Safe (`0x391c5e17…`) executed tx `0xf6aeec5108aa780e2d57b4f3baddfaf8fc038cb6f65bba8d943c75259333007d`, setting the underlying aggregator on each proxy to `address(0)`. Every read on them (`latestRoundData()`, even `decimals()`) now reverts:

- `0x0B6074F2…931D` (RON/USD) — used as `nativeTokenToUsd` and `rewards.COMP`
- `0x662Fdb0E…1F44` (ETH/USD) — used as `otherBaseTokensToUsd.WETH`

These feeds fan out into `comet.getPrice()` calls via `getBaseAssetPriceFeed()` (`useMarketsState.ts:116`) and the Sleuth `CometQuery.query()` path (`useSelectedMarket.ts` → `CometQuery.sol:341`).

Note the on-chain comet configs are unaffected — governance had already migrated both Ronin comets to new feeds; only these hardcoded frontend addresses still pointed at the old proxies.

## Fix

Replace them with the USD-denominated feeds the Ronin comets themselves register on-chain (read live from `baseTokenPriceFeed()` / `getAssetInfo()`):

| Config key | Old (dead) | New | Verified via `comet.getPrice()` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nativeTokenToUsd` | `0x0B6074F2…931D` | `0xB88e4078AAc88F10C0Ca71086ddCF512Ec54498a` (cWRONv3 base RON/USD) | 0.0549 |
| `otherBaseTokensToUsd.WETH` | `0x662Fdb0E…1F44` | `0x5D173813B4505701e79E654b36A95E6c1FAD4448` (cWRONv3 ETH/USD) | 2440.66 |
| `rewards.COMP` | `0x0B6074F2…931D` | `0xB88e4078…498a` (same RON/USD swap) | 0.0549 |

`rewards.COMP` was already pointing at RON/USD with a `//TODO: NEED COMP token address` — this PR keeps that pre-existing (wrong-but-functioning) behavior by swapping to the working RON/USD feed; the TODO remains.

## Caveats for review

- Both replacement feeds return an empty `description()` — they're governance-approved on the comets and return correct values, but worth confirming with whoever ran the Ronin feed migration that these are the intended long-lived contracts (vs. dedicated new Chainlink proxies for off-comet use).

## Test plan

- [ ] Load the Ronin WETH and WRON market pages; prices/TVL should render again
- [ ] Confirm no `execution reverted` on `eth_call` to `0x4006eD…` / `0xc0Afdb…` in the network tab

body: Follow-up to #13, which only fixed the units that stand on the ground. `orient()` reads the grass plinth to decide which way is up. Flying units have no plinth, so it left them exactly as the packer stored them — **Minion, Super Minion, Electro Dragon, Ice Hound, Rocket Balloon, Electro Owl and Spirit Fox were all lying on their side on the live site.** There is no second signal in the picture worth trusting: a Minion is about as wide as it is tall either way up, and units genuinely *drawn* at an angle (the Dragon and Super Dragon are banking, not rotated) look identical to the ones that are wrong. So these nine are set by eye against a contact sheet and checked in as a table. The real fix is the transform in the SC2 shape data, which would settle it for every file; until that is parsed, a small audited table is the honest version. Two things that made that table wrong on the first attempt, now pinned down in the comment: - the overrides run **after** `orient()`, which is the state they were judged in — applying them *instead of* it silently measures them against a different picture; - a unit drawn banking is not a unit stored rotated, so the Super Dragon is left alone. **Separately, the Witch page showed a skeleton blimp.** Her file holds both sprites, and the blimp is larger, carries more non-ground pixels, and even stands on its own patch of grass — so every measure worth using picks it. Which sprite belongs on the Witch page is a judgement about the wiki rather than something the picture can settle, so it is recorded as one. ## Checks - All 95 pages with game art re-reviewed by eye at a size where orientation is actually judgeable - 0 entries with no picture, 0 broken `` references - 383 pages, 401 sitemap URLs, 0 broken links 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: joaogerd
body:
## Summary

This PR refactors MPAS-BMatrix onboarding so a normal user does not begin by exporting a wall of personal `/path/to/...` variables. The scientific BFLOW/VBAL/UNBALANCE/HDIAG/NICAS/SO/DIRAC pipeline is unchanged.

Recommended first-run flow:

```bash
mpas-bmatrix setup --site jaci
mpas-bmatrix paths
mpas-bmatrix doctor
mpas-bmatrix check-config
```

## Resolution architecture

The branch now separates four responsibilities:

```text
user choices / explicit overrides
              +
         site profile
              +
       resource catalog
              ↓
      resolved configuration
              ↓
            doctor
```

### Site profiles

Added:

```text
configs/sites/jaci.yaml
configs/sites/generic.yaml
```

The JACI profile describes workspace defaults and runtime resolution rules. Because no canonical shared JACI MONAN-JEDI/resource publication has been selected yet, existing per-user conventions are explicitly marked as compatibility fallbacks rather than silently treated as official site paths.

### Resource catalog

Added:

```text
configs/resources/x1.10242.yaml
```

This describes WHAT the logical x1.10242 resource requires (mesh identity, vertical levels, static inputs, required MPAS-JEDI executables and MPAS runtime files) without deciding WHERE a particular user stores it.

### User setup and non-standard layouts

A standard setup persists semantic choices only:

```yaml
site: jaci
workspace: /p/projetos/monan_das/<USER>/work/MPAS-BMatrix
resource: x1.10242
```

Users with a different/private layout can persist only the roots that differ, for example:

```bash
mpas-bmatrix setup --site jaci \
  --monan-jedi-install /custom/install/monan-jedi
```

Advanced setup overrides are available for MONAN-JEDI install/source, mesh root, static root and stack root. Environment variables remain supported as one-off/developer overrides.

## Resolution precedence

Runtime roots use:

```text
explicit environment override
        -> saved user override
        -> canonical site-profile path (when one exists)
        -> command probe from active environment
        -> compatibility fallback
        -> unresolved
```

`mpas-bmatrix paths` reports the source of each path, including `site-profile`, `command-probe`, `user-config`, `compatibility-fallback` or `unresolved`.

## Doctor behavior

`doctor` now validates the selected logical resource contract plus concrete filesystem/runtime prerequisites. It still remains a preflight check; the complete PBS/end-to-end smoke is the final operational acceptance test.

`check-config` now distinguishes configuration composition from runtime readiness:

```text
Configuration status: VALID
Runtime readiness: NOT CHECKED by this command; run 'mpas-bmatrix doctor'.
```

## Other onboarding changes

- Python distribution name aligned from `mpas-bmatrix-global` to `mpas-bmatrix`;
- default config resolved from the package/repository location rather than current working directory;
- `mpasjedi_unbalance_ensemble.x` derived from `MONAN_JEDI_INSTALL`;
- current MONAN-JEDI install name `builds/monan-jedi` preferred over legacy `builds/monan-jedi-mpas`;
- `paths` remains useful for incomplete configurations;
- executables require execute permission in `doctor`;
- x1.10242 np128 partition, static inputs and MPAS physics tables are checked;
- documentation now includes `docs/getting-started.md` and `docs/resolution-model.md`;
- end-to-end tutorial verifies the complete `mpaswf -> MPAS-BMatrix` chain.

## Transitional limitations

This PR deliberately does **not** invent a shared JACI path that has not been selected/validated. The current JACI profile therefore retains compatibility fallbacks for existing user-area resources. `geovars.yaml` and `keptvars.yaml` also remain a transitional MONAN-JEDI source-tree dependency.

The target infrastructure is a canonical shared JACI runtime/resource publication. Once that exists, the JACI site profile can point to stable shared paths and remove the compatibility fallbacks without changing the scientific resource catalog or normal user commands.

## Validation status

Previously validated on JACI before the profile/catalog phase:

```text
pytest: all tests passed
ruff: all checks passed
git diff --check: clean
mpas-bmatrix paths: resolved current JACI paths
mpas-bmatrix doctor: READY
```

The new site-profile/resource-catalog changes require a fresh JACI run before merge:

```bash
git pull
python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q tests/test_onboarding.py
python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q
python -m ruff check src/bmatrix tests
git diff --check

mpas-bmatrix setup --site jaci
mpas-bmatrix paths
mpas-bmatrix doctor
mpas-bmatrix check-config
mpas-bmatrix paths --json
mpas-bmatrix doctor --json
```

Then run the complete system smoke:

```text
mpaswf pbs-smoke
  -> GFS/WPS prepare
  -> MPAS static/init
  -> f024/f048 forecasts
  -> validated forecast-pair manifest
  -> MPAS-BMatrix BFLOW
  -> VBAL
  -> UNBALANCE
  -> HDIAG
  -> NICAS
  -> SO
  -> DIRAC
  -> PLOTS
```

## Non-goals

- no scientific parameter changes;
- no stage-order changes;
- no change to existing B-matrix product contracts;
- no invented shared JACI filesystem contract;
- no merge until fresh JACI checks and the complete end-to-end smoke succeed.

author: assafmanor
body:
Five reports off M6a's deploy. Decisions in **ADR-0206 §AG**; board card, M9's card and the backlog updated in the same commit.

**Four of the five are one mistake, and it is worth naming before the fixes.** The design for all of it already existed — §Z5 §M2 and `where-a-route-shows-up-v1.html` §2 — and M6a **built the drawings' numbers while skipping their states and their stated exceptions.** That is §AE6's own lesson (*"the drawing is the spec; a brief quoting the drawing is not"*), from a session that had read §AE6 and written it onto this very card. No new mockup was drawn, and that's the point rather than a shortcut: three of the five are drawn states being built for the first time.

| # | report | what it was | whose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | *"I don't see the transit times in the plan day"* | §2's Plan column is `trvBlock() + planSlot(…)` — the block **and** the chip. Only the chip was built | mine |
| 2 | *"Plan day shows a 0 minute gap"* | `earnsChip` left on the raw hole where §2 drew `if (left >= 60)`, plus the unrendered `overruns` | mine |
| 3 | *"the map lines are messed up when a place has two events in one"* | `findIndex` over pins answers the **first** of a twice-visited place | **M7c** |
| 4 | *"the walking/distance/warning when no time to get between stops"* | `freeAfterTravel`'s `overruns` has existed since M2 and was never rendered | mine |
| 5 | a hole under an hour says nothing at all | the leg was gated on the **floored** `gap` join, so §Z5 §M2's own example stayed silent | mine |

Plus two copy calls from you: **no `חור`**, and **don't quote a shortfall when there is no gap**.

---

## `overruns` was never rendered (#2, #4)

`freeAfterTravel` has answered a three-way `fit` since M2, and §V1.1's amendment says why — *"the fit is a discriminant and not a boolean"*. M6a carried `TravelWindow` through and then rendered only `freeSeconds`, which is clamped at zero. So a 78-minute walk into a 60-minute gap printed `פנוי לפני 0 דק׳` on the day and `פער של 0 דק׳` on Plan's chip.

It's a fifth arm, **checked before every clock arm**: an infeasible leg's leave-by is behind the previous stop's own end, so `PASSED` fires almost at once and would say `זמן היציאה עבר` forever — advice about a departure that was never possible. The shortfall doesn't decay. `PAST` still leads it; a gap behind you is a record however impossible it was.

Built as `where-a-route-shows-up-v1.html` §2's `tight` state draws it: the `warn` glyph **replaces** the mode mark in the badge column (that column says what kind of thing a row is, and what this row is is a problem), `--miss` per §D7, no leave-by and no `בדרך` — the answer to an impossible leg is to move something.

## With no gap at all, the shortfall is the wrong thing to say (your call)

Two rows that touch have no gap for the journey to be longer **than**, so the sentence is arithmetically true and reads as nonsense — and with a zero gap the shortfall **is** the journey's own duration, already in the head one line up. Printing one number twice is the ambiguity ADR-0207 §6 removed from the `בדרך` line. The arm splits on `availableSeconds`, which `freeAfterTravel` deliberately doesn't clamp, so it covers an overlap as truthfully as a touch:

```
⚠  הליכה · ~12 דק׳                    1.2 ק״מ
   אין זמן לדרך
```

## `פער`, not `חור` (your call)

The app already calls this slot `פער` (`t.planDay.gap`: `פער של שעתיים · שבץ`), so it's one name for one thing rather than a third. `חלון` refused: the app spends "window" on a check-in's own (ADR-0184 §6's `לסגירה`), and two windows would be worse than two gaps. **The drawing says `חור`** and mockups aren't retrofitted, so `he.ts` carries a note at the string so nobody restores it from there.

## Plan draws the block, not just a smaller number (#1)

§2's Plan column has always been `trvBlock() + planSlot(…)`. M6a shipped only the chip's corrected number, so Plan had no travel time anywhere — and no way at all to learn a leg was infeasible, since its chip simply vanishes below the threshold.

Both surfaces now render one `JourneyRow` off one `dayJourney`, which is ADR-0159 §1 as written. **Plan takes it without the controls** — `בדרך`/`עדיין כאן` stay Trip's, because Plan has no inline settle pair (ADR-0171 §10e) and the drawing's Plan column has no action row either. Posture may differ; a number may not.

And the chip's **note line** was drawn and skipped too — `מתוך 160 דק׳ · 40 דק׳ מהם דרך`. A smaller offer with no account of itself is what made the correction read as an unexplained number. Both values take `gapLabel`'s ladder, not the drawing's raw `דק׳`, so a note can't be in a different unit from the chip it explains.

## The chip threshold, and a claim I got wrong twice (#2)

§2's drawn condition is `if (left >= 60)`, with the consequence written beside it: *"Below the chip threshold there is simply no chip — exactly as today. The seam is NOT given a second job."* M6a left `earnsChip` on the raw hole **and recorded in §AF and on M9's card that moving it "belongs to M9"**. Both wrong: the drawing had settled it, and leaving it produced a chip advertising `פער של 0 דק׳`. `earnsChipAt` is that threshold in the shape the corrected number can ask. The **position** is untouched — below the threshold it's the drag-only seam it always was, sized by the raw hole, because a drop target is about where a row may land.

M9's card and M6a's handoff are both corrected rather than left to mislead.

## A hole too short for a `gap` join still has a journey (#5)

§Z5 §M2: the block *"**ignores** `GAP_MIN_MINUTES` … or a 45-minute hole holding a 40-minute walk stays silent."* M6a gated the leg on `join?.kind === 'gap'` — and `gapBetween` is floored by that very constant. So every hole under an hour, a zero-length one included, said nothing about travel: exactly the silence that sentence forbids, reached by building the gate on the floored gap. `DayBlockEntry.from` is now recorded on every adjacency.

## The map's amber leg — the one that isn't mine (#3)

`orderedPins` mapped stops **to pins**, one pin per place, so a place with two events appeared twice as the same object and `findIndex` answered the first. **M7c's bookends made this the ordinary case**: on a middle night the stay is the day's first stop *and* its last.

No new rule needed. `relevantMoment` already decides which visit a place is about, and `buildPinOrderIndex` already uses it to pick the **number** the pin wears — so reading it here makes the amber line agree with the badge, which is exactly what the report was checking (`#5` → a line from `#4`). The decision moved out of a `useMemo` into `lib/map-pins.ts`'s `amberLegIndex`, per `frontend/CLAUDE.md`'s rule that what the canvas draws belongs in a pure function. **It was untestable where it was, which is why it shipped wrong** — and the new spec pins the old `findIndex` answer beside the correct one so the defect stays legible.

---

## Evidence

**Measured in Chromium at 360, both themes** — the last round's two defects were exactly this class:

| arm | height | meta ink / box | clipped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| overrun 18 min | 58 | 153.03 / 207.75 | no |
| overrun at the `H:MM` rung | 58 | 165.42 / 210.95 | no |
| no gap at all | 58 | 63.16 / 207.75 | no |
| no gap, driving, 166 km | 58 | 63.16 / 204.56 | no |
| fits (control) | 58 | 156.89 / 207.75 | no |

`scrollWidth` exactly **360**, no run painting outside the column, every arm still the **58px** the quiet arms already were.

**Specs, and two fixtures that were wrong before they were right** — worth naming because both would have passed while proving nothing, which is #710's lesson twice more:
- the zero-gap fixture sat exactly on the `PAST` boundary (`nowMs === arriveByMs`), so it asserted the wrong arm; it now sits inside the earlier event, which is the live state it describes;
- the touching-rows fixture gave the second row no `endsAt`, so a start-only row landing on the previous row's end

author: thursdaysfamous
body:
Phase 3G of the Wisconsin deployment — the beat analog the phase-2 record queued, taking the instance from 27 to **28 layers**: `mpd-squad-area`, MPD's 25 patrol squad areas, city-scoped on `milwaukeeCoverage` and built as the reference instance's police-beat shape point for point — `subOf: mpd-district` (the toggle nests and shows only while the district layer is on), a compact card whose header carries the squad with the district as the meta line, and the parent dropped to outline-only while squads carry the interior fill.

## The find: the numbering is checkable, so it's a gate

A squad's **number encodes its district** — the hundreds digit, 120–140 in District 1 through 720–750 in District 7. Because the city publishes both layers independently, that claim is checkable, and the builder makes it a **gate**: 60 seeded sample points inside each squad must land ≥ 97% inside the district its number names, against the `mpd-districts.json` file the same script builds. All 25 verified at first build; an MPD redraw that breaks the rule fails loudly. That's the Richland two-layers-compose-each-other check in city form, layered on the standard two-surface witness (REST vs CKAN CC-BY shapefile — 0.02% max area-share difference), and the squad fabric measures **100% coverage of every district** (1,050/1,050 sampled points). No officeholder: a patrol area elects no one.

## A defect the probe caught before anything shipped

The `registerPolygonLayer` factory's `findPropCI` matches candidates against **lowercased** feature keys, and the first draft passed uppercase candidates — the card rendered "Unknown" over perfect data (City Hall is squarely in Squad 140). Candidates are now lowercase with the rule noted at the call site.

## Wiring

- Worksheet entry at area rank 20 (a twenty-fifth of the city, between the MPS board's eighths and the aldermanic fabric), `data_files` 25/25, sw cache **v14 → v15**, sidebar after `mpd-district`, IL beat parity colors (`#7A0A1C`/`#E4572E`, solid thin outline + visible fill) with derived dark twins.
- Two `validate_sources` rows (REST door + CKAN dataset page), guidebook beat/sector matrix cell → SHIPPED, Wisconsin inventory 27 → 28 + fleet totals, the Milwaukee backlog entry updated (**the city TID dataset is the one remaining phase-3 candidate**), WATCH.md's city row extended to the trio with the new gate named, README/CLAUDE prose.
- `registerLayer` floor stays 16 — the layer rides the polygon factory, which already supported `subOf`/`compact`/`compactMetaField`/`onToggle`.

## Verification

- Browser-probed three behaviors: downtown renders "Squad 140 · District 1" with the parent district **auto-enabled** as the outline frame; the squad number's hundreds digit matches the district card at the same point; the Marathon anchor hides toggle and card entirely.
- Districts and neighborhoods rebuilt **byte-identical** under the extended builder.
- Full battery green: `generate_metro_files --check`, `compose_app --check`, `validate_index` (28 ids, floor 16), coverage-gaps/privacy/landing/manifests/dark-palette checks, `validate_sources --offline`, `check_roster_retention`, and the complete WI smoke test.

author: armmer016
body:
## What this adds

Hardening for the launcher dashboard's network access control, hand-ported from upstream
`52ab6c46` and `01760135`. Wave 2 of the v0.2.7..v0.3.1 sync.

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `aad379af` | `AllowLocalhostBypass` + `TrustedProxyCIDRs`; middleware takes an `IPAllowlistConfig` struct instead of a bare `[]string` |
| `1f609864` | X-Forwarded-For is parsed by walking the proxy chain and taking the first address **not** in `TrustedProxyCIDRs` |

## Safety-relevant properties

**Spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` is ignored from untrusted peers.** Previously the header was not
consulted against a trusted-proxy set; now a client that simply sets the header cannot present itself
as an allowlisted address. This is the case `TestIPAllowlist_IgnoresXForwardedForFromUntrustedPeer`
pins.

**Localhost access is now explicit.** It was unconditional; it is now governed by
`AllowLocalhostBypass`, so a deployment can gate loopback if it wants to.

**No behavioural change by default** — existing configs keep working; the new fields are additive.

## What was deliberately NOT included

**Upstream `f53222f6` (`POST /api/config/reset`) is not in this PR.** That endpoint wipes
configuration to defaults, and in this fork it would be protected by IP address alone: our password
authentication layer is not ported. A config-wipe callable by any host on an allowed LAN subnet, with
no authentication, is not a trade worth making. Upstream ships it only because upstream has the full
password-auth flow wired.

**`DashboardPasswordHash` was removed from this branch.** An earlier revision stored it but never
verified it. A config field with that name which nothing checks is worse than absent — an operator
would set a dashboard password and believe the dashboard was protected. Password auth is therefore
**not implemented** here, and that is stated plainly rather than implied away.

One correction worth recording, since it was asserted during development and is false: this fork does
**not** have a wide-open networked default. `web/backend/main.go:112` already refuses to start:
```go
if effectivePublic && len(launcherCfg.AllowedCIDRs) == 0 {
    log.Fatalf("Refusing to start in public mode without an IP allowlist...")
}
```
So the deployment is either localhost-only or has an explicit allowlist. The reset endpoint is still
correctly excluded, but on the accurate grounds above.

## How it was tested

Four targeted allowlist tests, including both directions of the proxy question:
`TestIPAllowlist_IgnoresXForwardedForFromUntrustedPeer`,
`TestIPAllowlist_UsesXForwardedForFromTrustedPeer`,
`TestIPAllowlist_RejectsLoopbackWhenBypassDisabled`,
`TestIPAllowlist_AllowsLoopbackWhenBypassEnabled`.

Verified independently: `go generate ./...`, `go build ./...`, full `go test ./...` (0 failures),
`golangci-lint v2.10.1` (0 issues) — and again with the other three wave-2 branches merged together.

## Known limitations

- **No password authentication.** Access control here is network-level only (IP allowlist +
  trusted-proxy parsing). Porting upstream's password auth — and only then the config-reset endpoint —
  is a follow-up. `golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt` is already in `go.mod`, so that work needs no new dependency.
- `web/backend/main.go` is touched because the middleware signature changed; no other change owns that file.

author: imadmaroof
body:
Arrow keys skipped world 1-1 and could not return to the start
  The sprite idles at the head of the trail, which is not a stop, but
  `selected` was initialised to 0 — world 1-1 — so world one was already
  highlighted before the player had moved. Right therefore stepped to
  selected+1 (world 1-2), and Left clamped at 0, making the trail head
  unreachable once you had left it.

  Nothing is painted as selected until the player actually sets off. The
  first Right now walks to world 1-1, and stepping Left off world 1-1
  walks back to the trail head instead of sticking. walkTo is split into
  walkTo(stop) and walkToPoint(point) so the sprite can return to a spot
  that has no node on it.

The coin counter claimed progress the site does not keep
  The HUD tallied coins and persisted the total across reloads, but the
  coins themselves respawned on every page load, so the number measured
  nothing and only grew. Removed the counter, its localStorage key and
  the whole coins object from SITE.

  The coins stay on the map: they still pop and chime as the sprite walks
  through them. They are now feedback while you walk, not a score, which
  is what they always actually were.

  The contact page's "THANK YOU FOR PLAYING" card carried the same
  problem — a hardcoded 0/0 worlds-cleared row and a coin tally. Replaced
  with real editable fields (location, availability, reply time).

Name
  YOUR NAME -> IMAD ABOO across every HUD, and the page titles with it.

Verified in Chromium: full arrow walk from the trail head through all six worlds to the castle and back again, every step landing on the right node (including both ends); no coin pill, no [data-coin-count], no coin keys in localStorage; coin pickup still fires; 6 map nodes positioned; no console errors on any of the five pages.

This is a suggestion for a code cleanup, removing some functions from the global table, or at least reducing them. And creating more interfaces that put common functionality together.

So far this improves:
- strings
- vectors

Vector metatable was "recently" extended to allow basic math operations on the vectors directly. This is proposing to extend this even further.

This is just a draft of things could look like. Im looking into a possibility of crating full interface in the Vector table (replacing the current engine function Vector) To have all vectors operations fully encapsulated.

I have yet not replaced the current code to use the new vector interface, Ive only tested it on my custom branch with all kinds of campaign improvements.

Similar things could be probably done to other parts of the code base to improve experience working with the codebase.

## Changes
- All custom `String_` functions are moved to the default `string`. Same pattern as the extended `table`.
- Removed imports of the `utils.lua` file, as this is a global file and doesnt need to be imported. When it does, it is actually redefining the globals.
- Helper function to work with the vectors are in the vector metatable.

That allows vector operations like:
```LUA
local pos1 = Vector(0, 0, 0)
local pos2 = Vector(10, 20, 30)
local distance = pos1:DistanceTo(pos2)
local direction = pos1:DirectionTo(pos2)
local terrainHeight = pos2:GetTerrainHeight()

author: san7iya
body:
This is the schema change we discussed on WhatsApp — full reasoning below, and the changelog row in CONTRACT_schema.md has the permanent version.

Two commits. The second needs your sign-off since it touches `storage/`.

## TL;DR
`fingerprints` allowed one row per file per instant. Layered fingerprinting needs several measurements of one file at one instant, so the key gains `hash_strategy`. It also fixes a bug that was already failing on my machine.

    UNIQUE (entity_id, computed_at)
    -> UNIQUE (entity_id, hash_strategy, computed_at)

No new column. `hash_strategy` already existed.

## Why
A single hash only says changed / not changed, never *what* changed. Two problems came out of that, and both are exactly what RQ3 measures:

- **false positive** — a gpkg re-saved by a different SQLite build changes
  bytes in unused space. Hash moves, nothing actually changed.
- **false negative** — a shapefile is a set of files. Editing an attribute
  changes only `.dbf`; the `.shp` hash doesn't move, so we'd report
  "unchanged".

Storing a few cheap signals next to the byte hash (feature count, bbox, field names) lets us say "geometry same, attributes changed". That needs several rows per file per instant, which the old key rejected.

## Also fixes a live bug
`test_two_fingerprints_in_the_same_second_both_land` has been failing for me.
Row identity depended on clock granularity — 13/30 same-file writes rejected on Windows, invisible on Linux. Not a Windows quirk: the key was using *when* a row was written to distinguish rows that differ by *what they are*.

## Two things to look at closely

**1. `hash_strategy` becomes NOT NULL DEFAULT 'file'.** This isn't tidying.
SQLite counts every NULL in a UNIQUE as distinct, so a nullable column in the key silently disables duplicate detection for any row that leaves it unset - which was the default path. Same rule decision 1 relies on for memory layers; here it works against us. Existing NULLs backfill to `'file'`.

**2. One change in `storage/store.py`, your file.** `add_fingerprint`'s `hash_strategy` default moves `None` -> `'file'`, because an explicit `None` bypasses a column default and would hit NOT NULL. Keyword-only, no call site changes.

## Migration
SQLite has no `ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT`, so it rebuilds the table. Verified against a real v1 db including a NULL-strategy row: rows preserved, NULL backfilled, `integrity_check` ok, `foreign_key_check` clean.

## Test changes
`test_two_fingerprints_in_the_same_second_both_land` is replaced by three tests. Its body used ONE entity for what its docstring called "an input and an output" — under the new key that's a genuine duplicate, and it had been passing only because `hash_strategy` was nullable.

Pre-existing failures 7 -> 5. Nothing new. 168 passing in
`tests/fingerprint` + `tests/storage`.

## One thing to check before merging
`sample_areas.gpkg`'s recorded SHA-256 moves `d2777d3f...` -> `f8d2dcc1...`.

**This is not the schema change.** My SQLite is built without
`SQLITE_SECURE_DELETE` and leaves ~1000 residue bytes in free space that yours doesn't. Rows are identical; `_logical_content` confirms it.

If you'd rather avoid the churn, drop those two fixture files from the merge and run `make fixtures` yourself — that's §3.4 step 3 anyway, and your build restores the old value.

## For C
A file may now carry several fingerprint rows at one instant, one per method.
`get_latest_fingerprint()` returns the newest of *any* method — filter on `hash_strategy` if the audit specifically means the byte hash.

## Not in this PR
`RULES.md` §3.2/Appendix B.4 and `PERSON_A.md` §41 still describe the old key. Your files, so I left them, worth a follow-up so they don't contradict the schema.

## Separate pre-existing bug, not caused by this PR

test_storage_source_contains_no_qgis_import fails on my machine with UnicodeDecodeError, not a QGIS import. Verified it fails identically with all my work stashed.

It does path.read_text() with no encoding, so Python falls back to the system default — cp1252 on Windows, UTF-8 on Linux. And storage/__init__.py opens with a box drawn in box-drawing characters […] cp1252 can't decode those, so the test dies at the first file before checking a single import.

Worth fixing because it's a §4.1 guard: on Windows it crashes instead of checking, so it isn't guarding — and a real violation would look identical to this crash. One word: path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

Your file, so I left it alone.

author: lixmal
body:
Now that the app writes to the database, a saved file has to stay a file other KeePass clients can read, and a file they wrote has to stay one this app can open. The specs drive the app through the browser and check the file itself with keepassxc-cli.

- Create an entry through the UI, save it, and read the title, username and password back with keepassxc-cli, asserting the entries that were already there survived the rewrite
- Add an entry with keepassxc-cli and open it in the app
- Compare the KDF and cipher before and after a save, so a weaker one after writing shows up as a failure
- Run them against a second instance on a copy of the fixture, so writing specs cannot disturb the ones that only read
- Install keepassxc-cli in the e2e job; the specs skip themselves where it is missing, so a local run without it still works

One thing they do not cover yet: a database written here makes KeePassXC log `KdbxXmlReader::readDatabase: found unused key "0"` on every open, which the original file does not. Nothing is lost and everything reads back, so it is not asserted against, but the writer leaves a binary in the pool that no entry references and that belongs in keepass-rs.

author: inglessemroteiro
body:
A cobrança do Stripe traz o e-mail de quem pagou na descrição (`Subscription payment for offers: #3315658 [ISR] Aulas em Grupo - PARCELADO - maria@gmail.com`). O e-mail é o identificador mais confiável que existe aqui: o nome no cartão vem abreviado ou com outro sobrenome, o valor muda porque o gateway desconta a taxa — o e-mail não muda.

## O que muda

- **Nova primeira passada da conciliação**: se a linha traz o e-mail de uma aluna cadastrada, é ela. Só depois vêm as passadas por valor e por nome, que continuam como estavam.
- **A diferença aparece na linha**: "E-mail confere · maria@gmail.com · entrou € 1,53 a menos" — é a taxa do gateway, não um pagamento a menos.
- **E-mail cortado por um export** (`maria@gm...`) não é usado. Melhor não reconhecer do que reconhecer a pessoa errada.
- **No lote das correspondências exatas** só entra o que não deixa dúvida: e-mail com valor igual, ou nome na descrição com valor igual.

### Reconhecida, mas sem parcela em aberto

Assinatura e acompanhamento não têm parcela, e desde a versão anterior já entram no Caixa como cobrança automática. Conciliar de novo contaria o mesmo dinheiro duas vezes. Agora a linha aparece dizendo de quem é e que já está contada, com um botão **Conferida** — em vez de "sem correspondência" e a gestora procurando na mão.

A função de extrato passa a devolver o e-mail: no Stripe, o do cartão, o do recibo ou o da descrição; no Asaas, o do cadastro do cliente.

## Testes

Suíte nova com 18 verificações: o e-mail sai da descrição do Stripe, do campo próprio (em minúsculas) e de domínio composto; e-mail cortado é descartado; a cobrança acha a aluna sem o nome aparecer na linha, marcada como identificada pelo e-mail, com a taxa do gateway como diferença; assinante é reconhecida, o sistema sabe que é assinatura e não gera sugestão de parcela; a tela mostra "E-mail confere", conta quantas vieram pelo e-mail, marca a assinante como já contada e oferece o botão Conferida.

Regressão: extrato pela API, repasse entre contas, contas, resultado e saídas do Caixa, e o smoke das 8 telas passando.

author: isadeks
body:
Closes #747. Final step of the #740 stack; the plumbing landed in #746 / #764.

**Draft** until the deploy + smoke test in the acceptance criteria are done — see the bottom.

## What

Sets `bedrockGeoRegion` to `global` in `cdk/cdk.json` (which had no `context` block before) and moves every default string that names a geography with it.

| Site | Change |
|---|---|
| `cdk/cdk.json` | `context.bedrockGeoRegion = "global"` |
| `agent/src/config.py` | `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` fallback → `global.` |
| `agent/src/config.py` | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL` fallback → `global.` |
| `agent/src/models.py` | `anthropic_model` default → `global.` |
| `cli/src/repo-display.ts` | platform-default mirror → `global.` |
| `workflows.ts` | `global.` forms of Opus 5 + Haiku 4.5 admitted |

## Why global

A `global.` profile routes to any supported commercial Region, giving better throughput and resilience under burst — worth having for tasks that run for hours.

**The tradeoff is data residency.** A deployer with a residency requirement sets `bedrockGeoRegion=us` (or `eu`/`apac`) instead, which is exactly why #746 made this a context key rather than a second hardcode.

## Verification

Against the synthesized template, not assumed:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| inference-profile ARNs → `global.` | 10 |
| inference-profile ARNs left `us.` | 0 |
| foundation-model ARNs changed | 0 of 20 (already geo-agnostic) |
| `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL` | `global.…` — derived by #746, no edit |
| rollback `-c bedrockGeoRegion=us` | synths clean, all 10 ARNs revert |

Full `mise run build` green: **4142** CDK, **1583** agent, **751** CLI.

## Two things the issue's scope table missed

Both were caught by existing guards rather than by reading the code, which is worth recording.

**The agent-side haiku fallback is a separate value.** #747 said the haiku model needs no edit because #746 derives its prefix — true of the env var the stack injects, but a run with **no env set** reaches the Python literal in `config.py`. Leaving it would have made local and deployed runs use different geographies. The `model-default-docs-parity` contract test caught it.

**The allow-list pairing invariant was `us.`-shaped.** It read `global.anthropic.…` as a *bare* id and demanded a nonsensical `us.global.anthropic.…` pairing. Generalized to the geo prefixes the list actually uses, preserving the real invariant — no prefixed entry without its bare form, no bare entry admitted in zero geographies — and confirmed still failing against an orphaned entry.

Both prefixes stay listed deliberately: the allow-list must accept whatever geography a deployment is configured for, so dropping the `us.` forms would reject a residency-constrained deployer's workflows at admission.

## Docs

The tradeoff and the documented defaults move together, since #742's drift test enforces them. Also corrects several statements that asserted a `us.` prefix as a *rule* rather than as the then-current default. Starlight mirrors regenerated with `mise //docs:sync`.

## Before this can leave draft

Per #747's acceptance criteria, still outstanding:

- [ ] Deploy to a stack and confirm `cdk diff` matches the ARN change above
- [ ] Agentcore smoke test: one task completes end to end and opens a PR on the global profile
- [ ] `platform doctor` access probe against the global profile

I have not run these — flagging rather than implying they passed. ECS verification is out of scope per the issue (CI deploys agentcore only); its unit coverage is included and green.

## what

  (`backend create/describe/update/delete/list`) for the S3 artifact bucket CloudFormation

  repeatable-flag behavior.

## why

- This is the layer that makes the feature real for users: end-to-end backend lifecycle
  management, a documented migration path off Rain, and every rough edge found during a real,

Integration-only, so a patch. Covers #293: with `embedding_mode: none`, recall
matched whole tokens, so a question found a memory only when it reused the
memory's exact words — and, in the other direction, matched *any* memory sharing
a stopword, injecting unrelated notes into turns.

Written for the reader most likely to be affected without knowing it: someone
whose recall has felt empty and who never set an embedding provider. Both
directions are shown with the actual examples, and the measured before/after is
stated rather than described.

misses `"deploys"` — because the honest advice for anyone who needs real recall

author: proc0x41
body:
Closes #29

## Problem

`docs/protocol.md` §5 and `crypto.VerifyAuthProof` require the challenge response to be `Ed25519("shatters-auth-v1" || nonce)`. The client identity module exported `ACCOUNT_DOMAIN` and `SIGNED_PREKEY_DOMAIN` plus a raw `signDetached`, but no auth domain and no proof helper — so a client following the module signed the bare nonce and received `401` on every `POST /v1/auth/verify`.

Found by driving the full M1 flow end-to-end against the containerised server with the real client crypto module. M1 pinned cross-language agreement for account IDs and signed prekeys; auth proofs were the one derivation left uncovered, and it was the one that was wrong.

## Change

- `identity.ts` exports `AUTH_DOMAIN`, `authProofMessage(nonce)` and `createAuthProof(privateKey, nonce)`
- Golden vector pinned on **both** sides: `Ed25519(seed=0x00*32, "shatters-auth-v1" || 0x00*32)`, computed independently by Go stdlib (`auth_test.go`) and libsodium (`identity.test.ts`) — they agree byte-for-byte
- Both suites assert a proof over the *undomained* nonce is rejected, which is the exact failure mode this fixes

## Cryptographic rationale

The domain separator binds every signature an identity produces to the purpose it was made for. Without it, a signature harvested in one context (auth challenge) could be presented in another (signed prekey), since both are detached Ed25519 signatures by the same key over attacker-influenced bytes. Reusing the server-side constant verbatim, with a golden vector on both sides, is what keeps the two implementations from silently drifting apart again.

No new primitives: `crypto_sign_detached` (libsodium) against `ed25519.Verify` (Go stdlib), as before.

## Verification

- `go test -race ./...` green against Postgres; `npm test`, typecheck and build green
- Re-ran the end-to-end flow against the live containerised server using `createAuthProof`: register → challenge → verify → `/v1/me` → prekey upload → bundle fetch all pass, nonce replay correctly rejected with 401
- golangci-lint, gosec, govulncheck: 0 findings

## Definition of Done

- [x] Unit tests cover the new paths (`go test -race`)
- [x] Lint and gosec report zero findings
- [x] Acceptance criteria of the issue are checked off
- [x] Client crypto touched — rationale explained above

author: sergey-shandar
body:
Files `fjs/emergent_testing/todo/spidermonkey-test-runner.md`, an issue for
running FunctionalScript proofs on SpiderMonkey.

The suite covers two engines, not three: Node and Deno are V8, Bun is
JavaScriptCore, and SpiderMonkey never executes a proof — so `bigint` size
limits, property enumeration order, thrown-value shapes, and recursion depth
are unverified there. The obstacle is the host, not the language: `fjs t`
reaches `readdir`, `import`, `sandbox`, `write`, and `await`, and the only
runner backing them with real host IO imports `node:fs`, `node:http`,
`node:process`, and `node:test`, none of which the `js` shell has.

The issue states one principle and takes the simplest path that satisfies it:
take the simplest thing that runs proofs on SpiderMonkey, and shrink the issue
to anything simpler that turns up. The first version is one generated file —
static imports of every accepted proof module plus a small inline walker that
calls the zero-argument functions, inverts the `throw`-tagged ones, recurses
into returned sub-trees, prints failures, and quits nonzero — passed to
`js --module`. The effects layer is deliberately not ported: a second host
runner is Out of scope until the simple script proves insufficient. The Node
side is the escape hatch for whatever the shell lacks — module resolution,
directory listing, fixtures — prepared ahead of time and baked into the
generated file, and it accepts a root only when that root's whole transitive
graph is shell-loadable, reporting what it excluded.

The shell itself comes from Nix: the repository already pins a Nixpkgs commit
in `fjs/ci/config` and generates one flake per job in `fjs/ci/nix`, so a
`spidermonkey` job declared in `nixJobs` gives the same binary locally and in
CI. What the pin offers is read off that commit — `spidermonkey_115`, `_128`,
`_140`, with `preFixup` putting both `js` and `js140` on `PATH` — while what
the shell itself provides is the first task's job to establish.

body:
**Do not merge until Sarah approves on preview** (per the task's review gate).

## Location correction
The task described the bug as living in `index.html`, quoting `_chIsDoneThisCycle`. That function exists there, but only feeds Client Health's table green/amber/red **colors** — I grepped and confirmed there is no "Done this cycle" headline anywhere in `index.html`. The actual headline/card described in the bug report (client-detail header, Overview stat card, and the client card's own "Services: X/Y done" line) only exists in `client.html`, driven by the hand-duplicated sibling function `_svcIsDoneThisCycle` / `_svcCycleStats()`. Same bug, same fix, different file — `index.html`'s Client Health colors are untouched either way.

## The fix
`_svcCycleStats()` computed `activeDone`/`monthDone` via `_svcIsDoneThisCycle` — "has a `lastDone` and isn't overdue" — which counts a service as done just because it was completed some *past* cycle and its *next* due date hasn't arrived yet, regardless of the current cycle's actual Status dropdown value. Changed the done-counting inside `_svcCycleStats()` to use the literal Status-dropdown value (`workStatus==='done'`) instead.

**Landmine avoided, confirmed by test:** `_svcIsDoneThisCycle` itself is untouched — it's still the sole input to `_svcDueStatus()`'s green/amber/red colors. I did not fold the `workStatus` check into it, since that would desync the Tracker's status dots from `index.html`'s Client Health colors.

**One shared function, four places fixed at once:** `_svcCycleStats()` is the single source for (1) the client-detail header's "X of Y done this cycle" headline, (2) that same header's "This month: X done" line — this **was** miscounting for the identical reason, so per the task's own conditional pre-approval ("if so, align it too, but confirm before changing") I aligned it as well, (3) the Overview tab's "Done this cycle" stat card, and (4) each client card's own "Services: X/Y done" progress line (added in an earlier PR this session). Fixing the one function corrects all four together — they can't drift apart again.

## Clients verified (Playwright, seeded data mirroring the real bug pattern)
- **Roggi's Auto** (7 services, all with a past `lastDone` + future `due` — the exact over-count pattern — only Blogging + Google Business Profile actually `workStatus:'done'`): now shows **2 of 7** everywhere (client card, detail header, Overview stat card) — was 7 of 7 pre-fix, reproduced then confirmed fixed.

author: theodiablo
body:
## Summary

"Mark as done" on the home card's next-session panel edited the plan in silence. The card then refilled in place with the session after it, so the only visible change was a date line two rows up — and the second tap of a double-tap landed on a *different* session. Because `nextSession()` returns the soonest untouched session today **or later**, repeated taps walked forward through the plan, ticking off sessions days or weeks away, with no undo short of finding each one in Plan and un-ticking it by hand.

Four faults stacked: no feedback, a target that swaps under the finger, no horizon on what can be ticked, and no way back. This fixes all four with two changes that address different halves — the date gate caps a mistake at one session, the confirmation makes that one visible and reversible.

Mockups of the options considered are in [this artifact](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/1514ab19-4042-4cb0-a346-09a6e170946d).

## What changed

- **`src/views/Dashboard.tsx` — gate the tick by date.** "Mark as done" renders only when the session is today or already past (`canMarkDone`), so the consumable list is at most one deep. A future card shows a line pointing at **Log it**, which saves the run *and* ticks the session — the honest path for "I ran Sunday's long run on Saturday". **Skip** stays available ahead of time; knowing you'll miss Sunday is a real thing.
- **`src/views/Dashboard.tsx` — confirm in place.** The tap swaps the card for a green confirmation naming what was ticked, with Undo and no action row, for 2.5s; then the next session slides in via `animate-slide-up` so the change reads as a new thing rather than a silent refill. Applies to Skip too, which had the identical runaway. `toggleSess`/`skipSess` are their own inverse, so undo is the same call again. Local state and one timer, cleared on unmount — no store changes.
- **`src/views/Dashboard.tsx` — overdue rows toast.** Each row's ✓/✕ now fires `showToast(…, {label: Undo})` through the existing seam; there's no card left to turn green once the row is gone. `showToast` already arrived via the `shared` spread and only needed declaring in props.
- **`src/i18n/locales/{en,fr,es}/dashboard.json`** — confirmation, locked-tick and toast copy. FR stays `tu`, ES informal, no em dashes in either.

## Verification

- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] `npm run typecheck:all`
- [x] `npm test` — 1575 passing
- [x] `npm run build`
- [ ] Checked by hand: not yet — worth a pass on the preview, particularly the 2.5s beat and whether the locked-tick line reads as helpful or as a scold.

Tests: new `src/views/Dashboard.markDone.test.tsx` covers the regression directly — that a tick produces a confirmation instead of refilling, that nothing is tappable while it shows (the double-tap case), that Undo reverses exactly the session it ticked, that a future session offers no tick at all while Skip survives, and that overdue rows toast with a working undo. `Dashboard.overdue.test.tsx`'s helper gained the new `showToast` prop.

## Risks and follow-ups

- The 2.5s confirmation adds a beat between deliberate ticks. Deliberate — this is a plan edit — but it's the number most likely to want tuning after real use.
- `PlanSessionRow` needs no matching gate: its to-do footer offers Start run / Log it / ⋯ (coach, route, skip) and has no mark-done at all. The un-tick on an already-done row stays ungated, which is correct — undoing is always allowed. My earlier note that the guard "belongs on PlanSessionRow too" was wrong; nothing there to change.
- Out of scope: the same silent-tick pattern anywhere else a session can be completed indirectly (a saved run auto-ticking its linked session). That path has its own feedback — the run appears.
- No `CLAUDE.md` change: this is a fix within an existing pattern, not a durable new rule.

## Screenshots

Not attached — the change is a state transition rather than a static layout, and it reads better on the preview than in a still. Worth watching on the preview URL: the green confirmation card, the slide-in of the following session, and the future-session card with no tick.

author: saikumaryerra
body:
Adds two complete courses to the catalogue and turns `/learn/` into a catalogue of courses. **No lesson URL moves**, no `localStorage` key is added, and the fifteen algorithm lessons are untouched.

## What this adds

| | Courses | Modules | Lessons | Pages |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 1 | 6 | 15 | 26 |
| After | 3 | 29 | 127 | 136 |

- **Kubernetes** — 67 lessons across 14 modules, foundations to production. Written against 1.36 using only current APIs, with a working manifest or command in every lesson.
- **System Design** — 45 lessons across 9 modules: the design workflow, scale/latency/consistency, three building-block modules, then Netflix-like, Spotify-like and YouTube-like case studies and a comparative section.
- Eleven inline-SVG diagrams, zero JS, drawn on the design tokens so they repaint for light, dark and forced-colors.
- Glossary 46 → 81 terms; the original 46 untouched.

## Shape of the change

The hierarchy is now **course → track → lesson**. `track` keeps its name and becomes the *module*, and `course` defaults to `'dsa'` — which is why **no existing lesson's frontmatter was edited**. `order` is per course. Each course gets a static page at `/learn/{course}/`; `[slug].astro` still owns `/learn/{slug}/` and fails the build if a lesson ever takes a course's slug.

**One dependency added:** `yaml`, devDependency only, so the content validator can reject a Kubernetes manifest that would not apply. It ships **zero bytes to the browser**.

**A sixth Definition-of-Done command:** `npm run validate:content`, which CI runs as `--strict`.

## Verification

Full detail in `docs/courses/REPORT.md`; the gate checklist and the e2e ledger are in `docs/courses/PROGRESS.md`.

- `npm run build` — 136 pages, 0 errors, portablize clean
- `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` — clean
- `npm run test` — 1,126 unit tests
- `npm run validate:content -- --strict` — 127 lessons clean, 5 reviewed notes
- **End-to-end: 503 passed, 0 failed, 6.3 min** — run in `playwright:v1.61.1-noble` with `CI=1 VISUAL_BASELINE=1`, so the fourteen pixel comparisons are *armed*, not skipped
- 18 external URLs fetched, 0 broken
- 36 screenshots at 375/768/1280 in both themes — no horizontal overflow, no console errors
- A keyboard-only walk: catalogue → card → course → lesson → breadcrumb → module anchor

### The check that paid for itself

All 112 new lessons were read in their **rendered** form rather than as source, which found 60 defects source review had passed: a wrong claim about a security control, a key takeaway re-teaching the misconception its own body had just killed, a worked example whose step 4 read the exact bug the callout above it named, a curly quote the source spells straight, and five pages sharing two document titles between them. Nine were fixed by hand; 51 went back out for repair under a verify-or-refuse contract — 37 confirmed, 6 corrected, **5 refused with evidence**.

Three of those turned into permanent guards rather than one-off fixes: duplicate lesson titles are now a validator error, so is link text quoting a different lesson's title, and an optional section a course has *adopted* is reported when a lesson lacks it.

## Known limitations

1. Five lessons run 1,509–1,570 words past a ceiling SPEC §5 makes a warning. Each is in `OVER_CEILING_ACCEPTED` with a written reason, and an entry that outlives its overage is an error, so the table cannot rot into a blanket exemption.
2. Eleven of the fourteen Kubernetes modules were reviewed against the upstream API reference but **not applied to a cluster**. Their manifests parse and pass the API allowlist; their behavioural claims were read, not run.
3. `/learn/`'s primary CTA is the global resume button, so with no progress it reads "Start with 01 · Complexity & Big-O" — course-blind on a three-course catalogue. D-05 records that CTA as global and unchanged, so it is a design decision rather than a bug fix.
4. A four-core host cannot run this suite at four workers: fourteen tests, mostly axe scans, exceed 30 s under that load and pass on a quiet machine. CI's retries absorb it.
