author: oleksii-debug
agourakis82
body:
`hessian_of(atan(x), 0, 0)` answered a confident **0.0**. Now **-0.640000** at x=0.5 and **-0.160000** at x=2.0 — the analytic values of `-2x/(1+x²)²` at both points.

This is the third attempt. The two before it were reverted for producing wrong numbers, and **both failed for the same reason, which no amount of black-box probing could show**.

## What the IR dump showed

`let d2 = fo_emit_f64_binop(nx, OpDiv, u2)`, with `nx` in r22 and `u2` in r21, emitted:

```
NV2_IR i=45 binop dst=21 src1=20 src2=20    u2 = u*u
NV2_IR i=47 binop dst=22 src1=17 src2=6     nx = -2*argv
NV2_IR i=49 binop dst=23 src1=22 src2=22    d2 = nx * nx   <-- u2 never read
```

**Both operand slots hold `nx`.** Register 21 is computed and then referenced by nothing. Reading `u2.1` *after* the `nx` tuple had been bound returned **nx's** `.1`.

## That one fact explains every earlier observation

Including the ones that refuted my own hypotheses, one after another:

- the **first** derivative was always right — it is used immediately
- `negtwo * argv` alone was right, same reason
- `one / u` alone was right, so "division is broken" was **false**
- rewriting every quotient as reciprocal-and-multiply changed nothing, because the problem was never the division
- `-2 * 0.25 * 0.64 = -0.32` was a **stale read**, not x² substituted for x — I had read that arithmetic as naming a clobbered argument register, and it did not
- emitting both derivatives in one pass broke the **first** order too, because it lengthened the chain of live tuples

Five hypotheses, five refutations, and the real cause was invisible in every one of them. It took reading the emitted instructions.

## The fix

Mechanical, and applied to all five: extract `.1` on the line after each call, and never read `<tuple>.1` later. The emitter is rewritten that way throughout, with the reason recorded in place so it does not get "tidied" back.

## Measured

| | value | |
|---|---:|---|
| `hessian_of(atan(x))`, x=0.5 | **-0.640000** | exact |
| `hessian_of(atan(x))`, x=2.0 | **-0.160000** | exact |
| `variance_of(atan(x))` | 0.006400 / 0.000400 | unchanged |
| `variance_of(sin(x))` | 0.007702 | control |
| `hessian_of(sin(x))` | -0.479426 | control |
| `variance_of(exp(x))` | 0.027183 | control |
| `hessian_of(exp(x))` | 1.648721 | control |

`madaros_fixed_point_gate.sh` reports `MADAROS_FIXED_POINT_OK`.

Full Madaros suite A/B against `main`, compared **per test**: **zero new failures**. Five tests left the list — the four `test_gri30_h2*` and `test_eisa_backend_v1`, the timing-sensitive integration tests that time out identically on both arms when the arms share the cluster. Not claimed.

## What is deliberately still restricted

The second-order path keeps kind 6's restriction: it applies **only when the argument carries no Hessian of its own**. With a compound inner the chain rule reads `s_g²` where `H_g` belongs, and that case still clears to `0.0` rather than answering plausibly.

## Tests

Two regression tests, **at two points each**, because a single point cannot separate a correct answer from a stale or passed-through value — which is exactly how the first attempt fooled me. They are separate files because the two measurements live in different channels, and `hessian_of(expr, 0, 0)` about a value carried by channel 1 correctly returns 0.0; that cost me a wrong reading once and the comment says so.

Closes the remaining half of #2164.

## AI disclosure

Implemented and verified by an AI coding assistant (Claude), on the third attempt. The first two were reverted rather than shipped. Every figure is measured from a build of this base, and the IR excerpt above is verbatim from `SOUNIO_NV2_IR_TRACE=1`.

author: patrickrb
body:
Carries the #78 fix to `staging` so the release that failed at 19:30 can actually complete.

## Why this is needed

The previous promotion (#76) merged fine, but its staging build died at **Compute version and release tag**:

```
.github/scripts/android-next-version.sh: Permission denied
exit code 126
```

Everything downstream was skipped, so **no AAB was built and nothing was uploaded to Play** — which is why the Play Console shows no new draft:

```
success   Generate release notes and semver bump with Claude
failure   Compute version and release tag
skipped   Build APK & AAB
skipped   Create GitHub Release
skipped   Publish AAB to Play
```

#78 fixed it on `dev`, but the release lane runs from `staging`, and `staging` still has the broken mode:

| Branch | `android-next-version.sh` mode |
|---|---|
| `dev` | `100755` ✅ |
| `staging` | `100644` ❌ |

## What this carries

Two commits, nothing else:

- `d1ab316` — CI: fix "Permission denied" on android-next-version.sh
- `d94916a` — merge of #78

The fix records the executable bit in git *and* invokes the script via `bash` at both call sites, so the release lane no longer depends on a mode bit surviving a Windows checkout.

## What should happen on merge

The staging build re-runs from the top and this time gets past the version step:

- **Version** — Claude already chose `minor` on the failed run, off baseline `0.1` → expect **`0.2.0-dev.<run#>`**
- **GitHub Release** — `android-dev.<run#>`, flagged **prerelease** (not a draft — this pipeline never creates drafts)
- **Play** — AAB uploaded to the **internal** track, which is where the draft will appear

The AI step is not cached, so it will re-run and may word the notes slightly differently. Last run produced:

> New: 7 more analog SSTV modes (Scottie DX, Martin 3/4, PD 160/180/240/290), plus WeFax and digital SSTV. Send pictures straight from the camera, add an optional CW ID tail, and use VOX pre-tone for HTs on audio cables. RX and TX now show band and time remaining. Gallery gains search, notes, date grouping, quality grades and partial-decode badges. Logbook search, tablet layout, new icon.

Worth noting that mentions digital SSTV as new. It compiles and is tested as of #77, but nothing in `sstvaf/` references it yet, so it isn't user-selectable — you may want to edit the published notes.

## Note on the source gate

`Staging branch source gate` will not run on this PR either, for the same reason as #76: `staging` carries the old `pull_request` trigger while `dev` has `pull_request_target`, so neither event fires. This PR puts the new trigger on `staging`, so the gate starts working from the next promotion onward. Don't add it to required checks until after this merges.

body:
## Proposed Changes

`flox develop` no longer falls back to `flox activate` when no package is named. With no `<package>` argument, it now resolves the project's Nix expression builds directly: exactly one build in `.flox/pkgs/` and that build is entered; more than one and every candidate is listed so you can name one; none and the command explains where to add one. `<package>` is now optional rather than required.

The prior behavior — bare `flox develop` silently running `flox activate` — created an asymmetry with `flox build`: in a project with a single Nix expression build, bare `flox build` builds it while bare `flox develop` activated the environment instead of developing it. That alias has been unadvertised for about three years, so rather than deprecate it, this removes it outright and gives `flox develop` the same bare-invocation convention `flox build` already has.

Be suspicious of the "multiple candidates" error message: the candidate list comes from a `HashMap` with no inherent order, so it is sorted by name before being joined into the message — dropping that sort would make the error text (and any test asserting on it) flaky across runs. Not covered by this PR: `allow` and `deny` becoming ordinary package names again is a consequence of removing the alias, not a change anyone had to make by hand, so there's no dedicated guard against those two names anywhere in the resolution path.

<details>
<summary>What the parser looked like, and what it looks like now</summary>

`Develop` was a two-branch enum: a `Package(DevelopOptions)` branch for the new command, and a hidden `DeprecatedActivate(activate::Activate)` branch that the parser fell through to whenever the package branch failed to parse. Because bpaf's alternation prefers whichever branch fails with an "uncatchable" error over one that fails "catchably," the package positional carried `.non_strict()` (to keep `-- <cmd>` off the package branch) and a custom `.parse()` step that turned a missing positional into an uncatchable failure (to make the package branch's own error win over the fallback's whenever both branches genuinely failed on the same input, e.g. `flox develop --stability stable` with no package).

With the fallback branch gone, none of that arbitration is needed. `Develop` is now a single struct — matching how `Build` is already modeled as a single struct with its own subcommand enum inside, rather than the top-level command itself being a two-branch enum — and the package field is a plain `Option<String>` positional; bpaf's derive macro applies `.optional()` automatically for `Option<T>` fields, so no custom parser function remains. `allow`/`deny` no longer need special-casing: they were reserved words only because the fallback branch's nested auto-activation subcommands (`activate::allow`/`activate::deny`) could otherwise capture them.

`Develop::handle` also drops the `config: Config` parameter it only needed to hand off to the `activate` branch, and the `deprecated_alias` metrics field goes with it — `flox develop` now reports simply as `develop`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Test strategy</summary>

Unit tests: `resolve_target` — the private function now driving bare-invocation resolution — gets one test per branch (sole build resolved, multiple builds refused by name, zero builds refused, a manifest-only project also refused since manifest builds are never bare-invocation candidates, and a named package still resolved correctly regardless of how many expression builds exist). Each was verified non-vacuous by temporarily breaking the corresponding branch and confirming the matching test fails. The dispatch-level `mod.rs` tests that used to assert the fallback branch's wire names (`activate`, `activate::allow`, `activate::deny`) are replaced with tests asserting `develop` is reported and that `allow`/`deny` parse as ordinary package names.

Integration tests (`cli/tests/develop.bats`): the two deprecated-alias tests (bare invocation warning, `-- <cmd>` delegation) are removed, replaced with three bats tests for the new bare-invocation behavior — zero, multiple, and exactly one Nix expression build, the last of which runs the real shell-entry path end to end. All three pass alongside the existing package-name-based tests in the same file.

</details>

## Release Notes

**Breaking change.** `flox develop` with no package argument no longer runs `flox activate`; it now develops the project's sole Nix expression build if there is exactly one, and refuses (naming candidates, or explaining how to add one) otherwise. `<package>` is optional. `allow` and `deny` are usable as package names again.

author: antonioalwan
body:
## Summary

Advances the `MSAL/IdentityCore` submodule pointer from `6eb0fef5c` to `1681d9900` to pick up the fix that stops the broker-internal `external_key_pop` marker from being sent to the `/token` endpoint.

This is a submodule pointer bump only. No MSAL source changes.

## What this pulls in

Only the commits from AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-common-for-objc#1949:

```
1681d9900 [patch] [bugfix]: Do not send external_key_pop to the /token endpoint (#1949)
405fb3f26 Address review feedback on tokenEndpointParameters
3924eeea7 Return an immutable copy from tokenEndpointParameters
808720398 [patch] [bugfix]: Do not send external_key_pop to the /token endpoint
```

Nothing else has landed in IdentityCore between the two pins, so the bump is scoped entirely to this fix.

## Why

`external_key_pop` is a client-internal marker used to tell the broker that the PoP key was supplied by the caller. It is consumed by the broker and is not a valid `/token` parameter, but `MSIDTokenRequest` merged `authScheme.schemeParameters` into the request body wholesale, so the marker was forwarded to eSTS.

The fix introduces `tokenEndpointParameters` on `MSIDAuthenticationScheme`, with a PoP override that strips the marker:

```objc
- (NSDictionary *)tokenEndpointParameters
{
    // external_key_pop is a client-internal marker consumed by the broker, not a '/token' parameter.
    NSMutableDictionary *parameters = [self.schemeParameters mutableCopy];
    [parameters removeObjectForKey:MSID_OAUTH2_EXTERNAL_KEY_POP];
    return [parameters copy];
}
```

`MSIDTokenRequest` now consumes `tokenEndpointParameters` instead of `schemeParameters`, so the invariant holds for every request type that builds on it rather than being enforced per request class.

## Related

- Fix: AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-common-for-objc#1949
- Feature this hardens: AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-common-for-objc#1934 (caller-provided keys for AT PoP)
- Downstream consumer: AzureAD/azure-activedirectory-tokenbroker-for-objc#2590, which needs this pin so the marker is stripped on the authorization-code grant path, not just in `ADBrokerAADV2TokenRequest`

## Testing

Covered by the tests that shipped with the IdentityCore fix (`MSIDAuthenticationSchemePopTest`, `MSIDAuthenticationSchemeTest`, `MSIDAuthenticationSchemeSshCertTest`), which assert the marker is absent from `tokenEndpointParameters` for PoP and that Bearer and SSH-cert schemes are unaffected.

## Changelog

No entry added, matching the precedent for pointer-only bumps such as #3080 ("Update IdentityCore to pick up the OneAuth duplicate-symbol fix").

author: agreenspan
body:
## The defect

`cache()` single-flights concurrent misses behind a Redis lock, but it *reimplemented* the lock `createLock` already provides — an ownership token, `RENEW_OWN_LOCK`/`RELEASE_OWN_LOCK` Lua, and a `setInterval` heartbeat — and its waiter loop broke out of the poll the moment the lease lapsed. Because every waiter polls independently at 50ms, a lapsed lease (a holder killed mid-compute, or an event-loop stall) sent **all** waiters off to recompute at once — a stampede, not the "one waiter computes alongside" the comment claimed. Measured: 4 waiters behind a lapsed lock ran the producer 4 times.

## The fix

Compose on the primitive instead of reimplementing it. Single-flight now builds on `createLock`:

- **Holder** — `acquire()` → compute → write → `release()`. The heartbeat-renewed lease, the ownership token, and the fenced release are all `createLock`'s job now.
- **Waiter** — polls for the value, and re-`acquire()`s on a lapsed lease. Whoever wins recomputes; the rest keep polling. That single `acquire()` *is* the re-election, so exactly one waiter recomputes rather than every waiter stampeding the producer.

The redis-error → compute-ourselves fallback is preserved (a throwing `acquire()` degrades to computing, as the initial lock failure does).

## Verification

- `bun test packages/db/src/redis/cache.test.ts` — 22 pass (in-memory Redis mock). Repointed the raw-lock-key failure-mode tests to `createLock`'s key; added a mutation-checked re-election test.
- **Mutation-checked**: restoring the old break-on-lapse makes the new test fail with `calls=4` (the measured stampede).
- 46 pass across `cache` + `createLock` + `lanes`; `tsc` clean; biome clean.

Retires the duplicated lock code (which Macroscope's reimplementation/primitive checks flag downstream in the Zealot port) and closes the stampede.

author: gitjanerik
body:
## Hvorfor skogen manglet

Ikke datamengde. `--typer` sto på sin default `myr`, og `bygg-n50-areal.yml` hadde **ingen input for flagget** — det fantes ingen vei fra Actions-fanen til skogen, uansett hvor mange ganger jobben ble kjørt. Alt annet var klart fra v5.24.0: klassifiseringen kjente `Skog`, flis-formatet hadde plass, klienten hadde taggen, og `arealMerge` sto ferdig til å la OSM-skogen vike. Manifestet sa ærlig `typer:["myr"]` hele veien.

En default som representerer et ferdig avklart mellomsteg er en felle, og denne sto i to leveranser.

## Målt, ikke gjettet

Buskerud, kjøring [32941787745](https://github.com/gitjanerik/lende/actions/runs/32941787745):

| type | flater | km² | forkastet |
|---|---|---|---|
| myr | 42 120 | 895 | 12 682 |
| skog | 6 339 | 8 500 | 5 663 |
| isbre | 53 | 4 | 1 |

14 fliser, **6,0 MB** (5,4 gzip), største flis 1314 KB, 3 isbre-navn. Myr alene var 3,1 MB i v5.25.0 — skog og isbre dobler det. Nasjonalt var myr 57,9 MB, så alle tre peker mot **~110–120 MB**. Innenfor det `public/` bærer, uten R2.

## Endringer

- **`typer`-input i workflowen**, og scriptets default snudd til `myr,skog,isbre`. Man må be om mindre, ikke om mer.
- **Skruene er per type** (`--toleranse myr=4,skog=8`, `--minareal myr=2500,skog=5000`). En skogteig er kilometervis av kant der ingen meter er synlig i 1:10 000; en myr bæres av hvert knekkpunkt. Myrens tall står urørt, så de 206 eksisterende flisene ikke skrives på nytt.
- **Isbre er ny kode 410** — ikke ISOM, siden ISOM 2017-2 ikke har bre (sportskart tegnes ikke på is). Norsk turkart-konvensjon: hvit flate med svak blågrå kant. Kanten er ikke pynt — hvitt mot lys åpen mark har nesten ingen flate-kontrast. Eget «Isbre»-lag, farge i alle elleve temaer, egen post i tegnforklaringen.
- **Bre-navn er PUNKTER**, ikke tagger på flatene: N50 Arealdekke har ingen navn, og Jostedalsbreen ville uansett fått ett navn der kartet trenger armenes. Bakes fra `N50_Stedsnavn_tekstplassering` til `isbrenavn.json`; `arealMerge` lar i tillegg navngitte OSM-breer overleve undertrykkingen.
- **Høyfjellet skiller seg fra granskogen.** `mapBuilder` setter `data-areal="skog"` når arket faktisk bærer N50-skog, og arkets eget stilark bytter da `--bg` til temaets nye `--bg-apen`. Gaten står på **arket, ikke temaet**: `n50ArealFetcher` feiler aldri hardt, så «ingen fliser» ser ut som «ingen skog her», og et tema-nivå-bytte ville gitt nøyaktig det tomme arket Turkart finnes for å unngå.
- `TYPER` utvides **bakerst** (rekkefølgen er kodingen), og en ukjent type droppes nå i stedet for å falle tilbake på myr — ellers maler en gammel klient Jostedalsbreen som myr.

## To feilspor som er verdt å kjenne

**Jeg leste «The operation was canceled» som at kjøringene døde**, bygget en OOM-hypotese på det og hevet heap-taket. Jobbene gikk helt fint — jeg avbrøt dem selv, fordi sandkassens klokke og GitHubs klokke gikk i utakt. Hevingen er tatt ut igjen, og kommentaren i workflowen er skrevet om så neste person ikke arver en lærdom som er feil. Målingen avgjorde det: rss 0,5 GB, 91,8 GB ledig disk. Den strømmende forenklingen står, men av andre grunner enn først oppgitt.

**Bre-navnene ga først 0 treff.** «0» kunne bety tre ting, så telleren ble delt i tre — og svaret kom på én kjøring: `3 traff regelen, 0 uten navnestreng, 3 uten brukbart punkt`. `N50_Stedsnavn_tekstplassering` er et annotasjons-lag, og `ogr2ogr -nlt POINT` får ikke punkt ut av det. Geometrien leses nå som den er og punktet regnes selv. Verifisert: `→ 3 beholdt`, uten at ett eneste annet tall flyttet seg.

## Gater

2 584 tester (34 nye), `npm run build`, `npm run boot:workers`, `npm run mcp:protokoll`, `npm run navnediff`, `npm run royk` (15 sjekker, ingen JS-feil). Kontrast-testene er verifisert i **begge retninger** — grønne på riktig kode, røde når `backgroundApen` settes tilbake til den grønne tonen.

## Flisene er IKKE bakt i denne PR-en

Koden er klar. Kjør «Bygg N50-arealdekke» uten `bare mål` etter merge — regn ~110–120 MB og en drøy halvtime. Fram til den kjøringen står `typer:["myr"]` i manifestet, og kartet oppfører seg nøyaktig som før. Det er hele poenget med at merkelappen står på arket.

author: serina-mcfall
body:
## Summary

Adds `launchpad/docs/corpus/standards/diagrams.md`, the canonical policy node for diagrams
inside corpus nodes: what form one may take, when a node carries one, what evidence it
owes, and what enforces it. The shape is forced by measurement rather than taste — a
corpus diagram cannot be an image file, because `validate.py` rejects every non-`.md` file
under the corpus root including one placed under `generated/`. Nine sections, 31 evidence
entries, no other corpus file touched.

### Related issue

Closes #1312. Part of #605.

### Issue type

Task

---

### Agent provenance

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Harness / provider | Claude Code |
| Model | claude-opus-5[1m] |
| Session reference | N/A - harness does not expose a run id |
| Initiating human | @serina-mcfall |

### Objective

One hand-authored corpus node at `launchpad/docs/corpus/standards/diagrams.md` stating the
diagram policy for the documentation corpus.

### Impacted components

```
launchpad/docs/corpus/standards/diagrams.md          (new — the deliverable)
launchpad/plans/2026-08-26-issue-1312-corpus-standard-diagrams.md   (new — the plan)
```

No other file is touched. `validate.py`, `node.schema.json`, the ADRs and
`launchpad/docs/corpus/AGENTS.md` are all unchanged, per the issue's out-of-scope list.

### Approach and rejected alternatives

**The question the task turns on:** a diagram asserts relationships, relationships are
substantive claims, and substantive claims need ledger entries — but the body is discarded
before anything is checked, so a claim whose only home is a diagram is unevidenced by
construction.

**Chosen:** a diagram projects what the node already establishes, and is never the only
place a claim appears. It gets no ledger entry of its own.

**Rejected — one ledger entry per drawn edge.** It invents a granularity the schema does
not describe (the schema says one entry per *claim* and gives diagrams no hook), and it
does not survive contact with the checker, which cannot tell the two versions apart.
Between two unenforced rules, the one worth having keeps every claim on the surface that
*is* checked. Section 5 states plainly that this is a choice rather than a fact and defers
to #1314 if the evidence standard settles it otherwise.

**Also rejected — citing `launchpad/docs/corpus/AGENTS.md`,** the instruction node that
governs this work. It has not merged, so a bare-path citation to it resolves on this branch
and hard-fails on `launchpad`. That is open bug #1473. Every claim is sourced to a primary
file that exists on the merge target instead; section 9 records the cost.

### Verification

Command run:
```
python3 launchpad/project-intelligence/corpus/validate.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s launchpad/project-intelligence/corpus/tests -p "test_*.py"
python3 -m unittest discover -s launchpad/docs/corpus/schema/tests -p "test_*.py"

# merge-target proof: origin/launchpad tree with ONLY this node added
git archive origin/launchpad | tar -x -C $MT
cp launchpad/docs/corpus/standards/diagrams.md $MT/launchpad/docs/corpus/standards/
cd $MT && git init -q && python3 launchpad/project-intelligence/corpus/validate.py

# negative control: same tree, plus a node citing the unmerged AGENTS.md
cd $MT && python3 launchpad/project-intelligence/corpus/validate.py
```

Raw output:
```
UNVERIFIED  corpus-agents: evidence entry 1, citation 1: is a commit reference, which names no openable file
UNVERIFIED  corpus-standard-diagrams: evidence entry 1, citation 1: is a commit reference, which names no openable file
UNVERIFIED  corpus-standard-diagrams: evidence entry 16, citation 1: is a graph-edge or tool-result citation, which names no openable file
UNVERIFIED  corpus-standard-diagrams: evidence entry 16, citation 2: is a graph-edge or tool-result citation, which names no openable file
UNVERIFIED  corpus-standard-diagrams: evidence entry 20, citation 2: is a graph-edge or tool-result citation, which names no openable file
PASS  corpus validation found no errors; 5 item(s) reported unverified
EXIT=0

Ran 79 tests in 0.298s
OK

Ran 27 tests in 0.032s
OK

--- merge-target proof (origin/launchpad + this node only) ---
UNVERIFIED  corpus-standard-diagrams: evidence entry 1, citation 1: is a commit reference, which names no openable file
UNVERIFIED  corpus-standard-diagrams: evidence entry 16, citation 1: is a graph-edge or tool-result citation, which names no openable file
UNVERIFIED  corpus-standard-diagrams: evidence entry 16, citation 2: is a graph-edge or tool-result citation, which names no openable file
UNVERIFIED  corpus-standard-diagrams: evidence entry 20, citation 2: is a graph-edge or tool-result citation, which names no openable file
PASS  corpus validation found no errors; 4 item(s) reported unverified
EXIT=0

--- negative control: same tree + a node citing the unmerged AGENTS.md ---
FAIL  control-node: evidence entry 1, citation 1: does not resolve to a real file in the repository
FAIL  1 corpus validation error(s)
EXIT=1
```

The merge-target run is the one that matters, and the negative control is why it is worth
anything: it proves the check can actually fail rather than passing vacuously. The
cross-model reviewer reproduced that probe independently and got the same result.

The two `FAIL` messages quoted in section 3 of the node are verbatim output of the same
validator against a scratch corpus containing `generated/arch.png` and `topology.svg`.

- [x] Tests or checks were run and the raw output is pasted above
- [x] The diff is confined to the scope of the linked issue
- [x] No secrets, keys, tokens or hostnames were added to tracked files

### Not verified

- **The mandatory cross-model review gate is NOT discharged.** Codex recovered from #1467
  and a real pass ran — it reproduced the merge-target probe and independently confirmed
  one finding — but it **ran out of credits mid-review and never reached a verdict**. The
  gate was genuinely attempted and genuinely did not complete. This PR is a draft for that
  reason.
- **Nothing establishes that a Mermaid fence renders for any consumer of this corpus.** No
  CI step, config or statement in the tree says so. The node's preference for Mermaid rests
  on reviewability in a PR diff, which is verified, not on rendering, which is not.
- **The knowledge crate's rendering capability was not inspected.** It is the question most
  likely to change the node's preference between fence languages.
- **Image rejection was measured with `--root` against scratch corpora**, not by committing
  a knowingly-invalid file into this branch's history.
- **One FACT rests only on `UNVERIFIED` tool-result citations** — the measured diagram
  counts (1 Mermaid fence, 20 box-drawing files). Disclosed in section 9, since no check
  holds that convention.
- **`.superpowers/` step ledger is gitignored**, so it records the build locally only; the
  durable record of the merge-target check is this PR body.

### Security implications

None. The change adds two Markdown documents and no executable path, no dependency, no
configuration and no network surface. Nothing in the diff is read by any runtime component;
the only consumer is `validate.py` in CI, which parses front matter and never executes it.

### Escalations

Two review findings are filed rather than fixed, because they concern other artefacts:

- **#1488** — three defects in `AGENTS.md`'s create procedure, found by following it
  literally as this task's plan required. One is the procedure gap that *causes* #1473 and
  was filed nowhere; ten sibling branches are following that procedure now.
- **#1489** — the authored-`relationships` backfill. Every standards node in the batch
  ships an empty array for a reason that expires the day the batch merges, and nothing
  tracked going back.

Six further findings from `review-final` were fixed in `d3e737f` rather than deferred,
because each was a defect inside this deliverable: four issue-ownership claims asserted in
the body with no ledg

author: jamesbhobbs
body:
## Summary

- add `deepnote_toolkit.streamlit` helpers for reading `.deepnote` sources and snapshots, rendering input blocks, and normalizing notebook outputs
- add local-sidecar and public-runs API clients for dynamic Streamlit apps
- authenticate hosted cloud runs as the current viewer by exchanging the opaque `streamlit-token` cookie for a short-lived, viewer-scoped public API bearer on every request
- explicitly request detached cloud execution and normalize sanitized `snapshotBlocks` returned to hosted app viewers
- keep explicit `token`, `token_provider`, and `DEEPNOTE_TOKEN` support for local development

This moves the Python helper package out of [deepnote/deepnote#466](https://github.com/deepnote/deepnote/pull/466), so it ships as part of Deepnote Toolkit rather than requiring a separate PyPI package and Toolkit dependency.

## Hosted authentication

The hosted runner derives the app UUID from `x-original-host` (falling back to `host`) and calls `POST /api/streamlit-apps/{appId}/api-token` with the current session's opaque `streamlit-token` in the `StreamlitToken` header. The returned token is sent to the returned `apiOrigin` using the same `Authorization: Bearer` public API contract as CLI/API runs.

Credentials are resolved per request and are never cached globally or in Streamlit session state. A hosted request also never falls back to a process-wide `DEEPNOTE_TOKEN`.

## Hosted run contract

`DeepnoteCloudRunner` submits `POST /v2/runs` with:

```json
{
  "notebookId": "<notebook-id>",
  "detached": true,
  "inputs": {}
}
```

Detached execution keeps viewer-triggered work out of the shared project session and is required by the scoped app token. When polling completes, hosted viewers receive sanitized `snapshotBlocks`: the executed notebook's block IDs, types, metadata, and outputs, without raw project `snapshotContent`. Toolkit converts those blocks into the same `RunResult.outputs` model used by snapshots and the local sidecar.

Normal API-key clients remain compatible: inline `snapshotContent` is still parsed when the public API returns it.

## Dependencies

- Depends on [deepnote/deepnote-internal#20682](https://github.com/deepnote/deepnote-internal/pull/20682) for the short-lived Streamlit viewer API-token exchange, detached public-v2 run authorization, and sanitized `snapshotBlocks` response.
- [deepnote/deepnote#466](https://github.com/deepnote/deepnote/pull/466) is updated to consume this Toolkit module and retain only the examples and cross-repository smoke tests.

## Testing

- 53 targeted tests passed (new Streamlit suite plus the existing `streamlit_data_apps` tests)
- targeted Black, isort, Flake8, and MyPy checks passed
- Toolkit-backed example smoke tests in `deepnote/deepnote`: 3 passed
- local cross-repository HTTP smoke passed: the Python Toolkit client called the TypeScript sidecar, which launched the real local Deepnote kernel and returned the executed code output (`kernel received count=9`)
- full unit collection was attempted locally but could not start because the available environment lacks the repository dev dependencies `polars`, `pyspark`, `responses`, and `parameterized`

The repository-wide Black/Flake8 checks still report pre-existing formatting differences and F824 warnings in unrelated files; all files changed by this follow-up pass their targeted checks.



<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added tools for building Streamlit apps from Deepnote notebooks.
  - Added support for local and hosted notebook execution with per-viewer authentication.
  - Added automatic rendering for common input types, including text, selections, sliders, dates, and checkboxes.
  - Added structured handling for notebook text, images, dataframes, agent output, and snapshots.
  - Exposed public authentication, runner, document, and widget utilities.

- **Documentation**
  - Added guidance for building, authenticating, deploying, and synchronizing Deepnote-powered Streamlit apps.

author: erikdarlingdata
body:
Closes #2655.

## The defect

PostgreSQL 18 removed `op_bytes` from `pg_stat_io`. `PgIoStatsCollector` already guarded that — it
substitutes NULL so a collection cannot fail on "column does not exist" — but **both** byte figures
`get_pg_io_stats` serves were derived from it:

```csharp
block_bytes = r.OpBytes > 0 ? r.OpBytes : (long?)null,
read_bytes  = r.OpBytes > 0 ? r.Reads * r.OpBytes : (long?)null,
```

So on 18 both came back `null` with no note, no status, and nothing to separate a version change from a
collector that had stopped.

## What 18 replaced it with is better than what was lost

`op_bytes` was the per-operation **block size**, which the read multiplies by a count to *estimate* volume.
`read_bytes` / `write_bytes` / `extend_bytes` are **measured totals**. 18 also introduced vectored reads, so
one entry in `reads` can cover several blocks and the old estimate undercounts.

Measured through the running service against a real 18.6 target — not reasoned about:

| combination | reads | measured bytes | old estimate | undercount |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `background worker/bulkread` | 6,862 | 565,723,136 | 56,213,504 | **10.1×** |
| `client backend/bulkread` | 4,742 | 448,724,992 | 38,846,464 | **11.6×** |
| `autovacuum worker/vacuum` | 2,797 | 362,037,248 | 22,913,024 | **15.8×** |

An order of magnitude, not a rounding difference. That is why the column was removed rather than renamed,
and why the two quantities must never share a name without saying which is which.

## The change

- **V101** adds `read_bytes` / `write_bytes` / `extend_bytes` as **`numeric`** — what PostgreSQL declares
  them, verified on 18.6, beside counts it declares `bigint`. Nullable, no default, no backfill.
- **The collector** selects them on 18+ and `NULL::numeric` below, appended to the SELECT so no existing
  ordinal moves. Declared `Decimal(28, 0)`: whole bytes, and 28 rather than 38 because C# `decimal` tops out
  near 29 significant digits and a declared width the runtime type cannot carry is a promise broken at the
  reader.
- **The reader** differences them like every other cumulative counter here — a plain SUM would report the
  total since `stats_reset` rather than the window.
- **The read** serves `bytes_source` per row and on the envelope: `measured`, `estimated_from_block_size`,
  or `unavailable`, plus a `bytes_note` saying the two are not comparable.

`byte_counters_tracked` is what stops a pre-18 zero reading as a measurement — `GREATEST(NULL, 0)` is `0`
and the outer `coalesce` would flatten it anyway, so without the flag a pre-18 server reports a perfectly
credible zero bytes. Same guarantee `write_counters_tracked` already gives Aurora's write side. **It probes
`read_bytes`, not `extend_bytes`**: WAL rows legitimately report no `extend_bytes` (verified on 18.6), so
probing that column would answer "bytes are not measured here" for a row that simply does not extend, and
the read would serve a measured server as an unmeasured one.

## Verification

Two live targets at once — 17.11 and 18.6 — through the real service, not fixtures:

- the registry stamped both majors (`17` and `18`) via #2653's column
- the store split cleanly: **7,910** rows on 17 all carrying `op_bytes` and no `read_bytes`; **79** rows on
  18 with **56** carrying `read_bytes` and none carrying `op_bytes`
- `get_pg_io_stats` returned `estimated_from_block_size` with `block_bytes: 8192` for the 17 target, and
  `measured` with `block_bytes: null` for the 18 target

Worth noting the empty case is already right and stayed right: before load, the 18 target answered
`no_io_activity` with an accurate explanation rather than a bare empty list.

## Tests

`Pg18IoBytesTests` pins the rung, that the columns are `numeric` and never `bigint`, that all three are
differenced rather than summed as levels, and that the tracked flag probes `read_bytes` specifically — that
last one is the assertion with a real failure behind it. `PgIoStatsCollectorDefinitionTests` now pins both
arms of the version exchange: 18 loses `op_bytes` and gains the three, 17 and below the reverse, same shape
either way.

author: santiagovargasve
body:
## T064 — Expense form: the common case in under fifteen seconds

### What changed

- **`ExpenseForm`** — title, amount, currency, date, and the two collapsed lines ("Pagado por: tú",
  "Dividido: entre todos") that open editors when tapped. Amount gets initial focus on open, per
  frontend/CLAUDE.md's "the expense form... a full sheet with the amount field focused on open."
  Reuses T004's existing `Dialog` (already full-screen below 768px, unchanged here).
- **`PayerEditor`** — collapsed by default; expands into member checkboxes on tap. With one payer
  checked, no amount field is shown (it's implicitly the full total — nothing to enter). With 2+,
  each gets a `<MoneyField>` and a live remainder ("Faltan $X" / "Sobran $X" / "Balanceado"). Save
  stays disabled until it balances exactly, so `PAYERS_DO_NOT_BALANCE` is a backstop the happy path
  never reaches.
- **`AddExpenseFab`** now mounts the real form (T063 shipped it as a placeholder).
- **`page.tsx`** fetches group detail (members, default currency) alongside the feed and `/me`, all
  three in parallel — the form needs both before it can even render its defaults.
- Split editing itself is out of scope (T065) — this form only ever sends `{ strategy: "equal" }`,
  with a static line where T065 mounts its own editor.

### Never optimistic

On success the form re-fetches the created expense via `GET /api/expenses/:id` — the same shape
the feed already renders (api-contract.md § *Reading a list or a single expense*) — and hands that
confirmed record to the feed, rather than reconstructing one from the `POST` response plus its own
local state. Also invalidates `["group", groupId, "expenses"]` and `["group", groupId, "balances"]`
— the feed itself doesn't read from the TanStack Query cache (T063 built it with plain state), but
this is forward-compatible with T066's balances view, which will.

### A real bug caught during manual verification

The multi-payer amount fields originally defaulted to `"0"` — meaning typing `120000` into an
untouched field produced `0120000` → `$0.120.000`, since the pre-filled zero wasn't cleared first.
Fixed to default to an empty string until a real amount is entered. Screenshots below are from
*after* the fix.

### Deviation

Currency selector is limited to `KNOWN_CURRENCIES` (the static COP/USD/EUR table `format.ts`
already knows how to render — see T061/T062), not the literal deployed `SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES` env
var, which isn't available client-side. Same reasoning and same choice T062's `CreateGroupDialog`
already made for its own currency picker.

### Infra: PointerEvent polyfill

`vitest.setup.ts` gets a `PointerEvent` polyfill — jsdom has no `PointerEvent` constructor, and
Base UI's `Checkbox` dispatches one internally on click, so any test clicking a `Checkbox` (the
payer editor's, here) throws `ownerWindow(...).PointerEvent is not a constructor` without it. First
hit by this task's tests; needed by every future one that exercises `Checkbox` (T065's
`equal_subset`, most likely).

### How verified

- `npm run test:ci` (lint, typecheck, test with coverage, build) — all green.
  `src/server/services` and `src/lib/money/**` unaffected, still comfortably above their gates.
- Manually in the browser, twice end to end (registered two users, one real group): submitted the
  untouched default path (amount + title only) and watched the row land correctly with the right
  "your share"; then submitted a real two-payer split ($200.000 as $120.000 + $80.000), watched the
  live remainder go from "Faltan $80.000" to "Balanceado," and watched the row land with "Pagado
  por 2 personas." Caught and fixed the leading-zero bug above in the process. Verified the feed at
  375px (layout, not the dialog interaction — see below). Cleaned up all test fixtures from the DB
  afterward.
- **Not independently verified**: the dialog's open/submit interaction specifically at the 375px
  viewport — the browser-automation tool couldn't reliably click through it in that viewport this
  session (repeated timeouts unrelated to any server error or console error I could find). The
  static 375px layout is confirmed correct, and the `Dialog` component's full-screen-sheet behavior
  below 768px is existing, already-verified T004 infrastructure this task doesn't touch — but
  flagging the gap rather than claiming a mobile interaction check I couldn't actually complete.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run test:ci` passes
- [x] Manual verification in-browser at desktop width, both the default and multi-payer paths
- [ ] Mobile-viewport dialog interaction — not completed this session, see note above

author: fnlich
body:
`examples/sample_challenges/` has held five problems from the subnet all along — two Python, three Rust, each a page of prose with its edge cases stated rather than shown — and `run.py` there grades a solution you wrote by hand. Nothing pointed the **miner** at them. The built-in samples are toys beside these, and a miner that answers a toy correctly has proved very little.

```bash
python -m solvers.rehearse --challenge all
python -m solvers.rehearse --challenge extent-journal
python -m solvers.rehearse --challenge sparse-circular-array reactive-stat-board
```

Each challenge becomes a `TaskRequest` — `PROBLEM.md` as the statement, `cases.json` for the language, entrypoint and public cases — and goes through the same path a validator's request takes: signed, through `CustomMiner`'s HTTP handler, archived by the miner's own `save_solution`, then graded with the validator's executor.

## How many cases the model is shown

The decision that makes any of this mean something, so it is a flag rather than a default nobody reads.

Each challenge ships three public cases. Show the model all three and grade it on all three and the result is **circular**: `VerifyingSolver` repairs its answer until the public examples pass, so the grade at the end can only agree with a check already made — it would report a success it was incapable of failing.

So the model is shown a subset and graded on everything: two of three by default.

```bash
python -m solvers.rehearse --challenge all --examples 0
```

`--examples 0` shows none at all. That is not a handicap — on the run this miner was built for, no public examples shipped with any task and the entire repair loop was dead code. It is the condition worth measuring against, and the hardest one.

Asking for all three anyway is allowed, and the report then admits what it is: *"every one of which the model was shown — so this grade cannot fail"*.

## Batch behaviour

One fleet for the whole batch, opened once and closed at the end. Opening browsers per challenge would spend a minute of sign-in-warm page loads five times over, and the tabs are built to be reused — that is what a miner does for its whole life.

It ends in one table, because several hundred lines of per-challenge output scroll away before anyone reads them:

```
[rehearse] summary
  FAIL  asset-rebuild-planner        python  passed 0/3 — plan_rebuild(*[{'a': 'A'...
  PASS  extent-journal               python  passed all 3 test(s)
  ????  reactive-stat-board          rust    it compiles locally; the tests could...
  PASS  revocable-verification-gate  rust    passed all 3 test(s)
  FAIL  sparse-circular-array        rust    it does not compile: error[E0308]: mi...

  2/5 would have scored
```

A mixed run exits on the worst outcome in it — a run with one wrong answer is not a passing run.

Rust without a Docker daemon still reports whether each answer **compiles**, which is the difference between a zero and a maybe; the table says `it compiles locally` rather than claiming a pass, and a non-compiling answer is a definite `FAIL` rather than an unknown.

## Practical notes for a real run

`--timeout 300` is capped by `glm_request_timeout_s` (default 280), so the effective per-challenge budget is 280s and `--challenge all` is roughly a 23-minute run at worst.

## Verification

Six mutations, all caught. Two survived a first pass, and in both cases the **tests** were wrong rather than the code:

- the path-traversal guard was never exercised, because the hostile names resolved to directories with no `cases.json` in them either way — the test now plants a real challenge just outside the directory and requires `../elsewhere` not to reach it;
- the summary-width test checked the helper rather than the printed line, which then showed the width budget belonged to the whole row and not to the detail alone, since the name column is as wide as the longest challenge name.

260 tests pass, pyflakes clean. All five challenges verified loading and running end to end against a stub model, with the archive written per challenge (`<name>.py`/`<name>.rs` plus the exchange `.json` beside it).

author: jidmirzyah
body:
## What was wrong

`skills/.usage.json` is telemetry, and `bump_use` **deliberately** records any
name handed to it — its docstring calls usage tracking *"pure observability …
orthogonal to whether a skill is ever curated"*, which is why bundles and
hub-installed skills get counted too. **That permissiveness is correct.** The
cost is that a name nothing can resolve still accumulates a record, and nothing
notices.

**It happened.** `vault-governance` held **51 recorded uses with no `SKILL.md`
anywhere** — and its record read `curator_managed: True`, so the one entry the
curator would eventually have acted on was the one that did not exist. Its last
recorded use was **2026-08-15, two days after a prior audit concluded there was
no separate live entry by that name**.

Drift ran the other way simultaneously: **18 skills installed in a single batch
on 2026-08-10 had no record at all**, leaving them invisible to the curator.

Between the two directions, **every usage-based count was wrong** — *"58 of 105
skills have zero uses"* was unusable as evidence for anything.

## Not urgent, and that was checked rather than assumed

- Nothing has ever been archived — every record `state: active`,
  `archived_at: null`, and `~/.hermes/skills/.archive/` **does not exist**.
- The last curator run (2026-08-20) reported `checked: 84, archived: 0,
  marked_stale: 0`.
- Thresholds are **30 days to stale, 90 to archive**; the oldest inactivity on
  the system is **25 days**.
- Nothing anywhere referenced the dead name — checked `SOUL.md`, memories,
  `config.yaml`, `jobs.json`, every vault instruction file, and every other
  skill.

**But the failure mode was invisibility, not damage.** Waiting for the threshold
to arrive is exactly how it stayed unnoticed for two weeks.

## Reports, does not repair

The fix for a dead record is `forget()`; for a missing one it is
`seed_record_if_missing()`, which anchors the inactivity clock **without**
enrolling the skill for archival — `adopt_skill()` would, and that is a policy
choice rather than a cleanup.

Which is right depends on *why* the drift appeared, so it stays a judgement call.
**Both alert texts name the repair** rather than leaving the reader to find it.

## Verification

- **7 tests, all failing on the unpatched tree** — including that the check never
  modifies either side, that both directions are reported separately, and that an
  unreadable registry is reported rather than swallowed.
- `tests/scripts/` + `tests/cron/` — **1052 passed, 1 skipped**.
- `ruff` clean; footgun scan clean.
- Against the live system, after its records were repaired: **no drift**.

author: bmethod
body:
Part A of the 2026-08-26 harness posture directive. kendex now commits its own render, the same posture the eight consumer repos already run.

## Why

kendex carries packages that exist in no marketplace: app-deploy, kendex-issues, decider, dev, orch and the rest of the repo skills. Their renders were ignored twice over, in `.gitignore` and in `.git/info/exclude`, so a clone of this repo got no working harness until someone ran the CLI on it.

## What changed

| Surface | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `.gitignore` | Harness rows removed. `/.kendex-lock.json` stays, on the row `kendex refresh` writes itself (`crates/core/src/engine/posture.rs`). |
| `.git/info/exclude` | Harness rows stripped. Machine-local rows kept: `.cache`, `tmp`, `.env.local`, `agent-memory-local`, `first-run`, `assistant-daemon-state.json`, `.claude/worktrees/`, `settings.local.json`. |
| Render | 862 files under `.agents`, `.claude`, `.codex`, `.pi`. |
| `tools/guard` | Byte-ceiling, oversized-file and TODO lanes skip the render. The source under `skills/`, `agents/`, `hooks/` stays governed. |
| `tools/byte-ceiling-excludes` | New. Four oversized rendered files, named one by one, each with the reason. |
| `tools/size-ratchet-excludes`, `tools/suppression-ban-excludes` | Render rows, so the mirror is not judged twice. |

Guard excludes name `.agents/*` and the individual large rendered files. No `hooks/*` wildcard, so a repo-own hook still gets checked.

## Proof

Fresh clone of the branch to a scratch dir, then deleted:

- `.agents/skills/{app-deploy,decider,dev,github,orch}/SKILL.md` present.
- `.claude/skills/<same>` resolves through `../../.agents/skills/<same>` and `SKILL.md` reads.
- 19 links, 0 dangling, 0 absolute.

Other checks:

- `kendex refresh` re-run on the committed trees is a no-op, so the render is idempotent.
- No machine paths in the committed trees. The two hits are `/home/me/...` test fixtures in `.agents/skills/orch/tests`. `.claude/settings.local.json` and `.kendex-lock.json` stay ignored.
- No credential-shaped values (token prefixes, private keys, JWTs).
- Full `tools/guard` chain green.

Hook scripts render without the exec bit on purpose. Every caller invokes them as `bash <path>`.

## Review round 1

- `size-ratchet` was never declared for this repo, so a clone got a dev-implement validation step calling a path that did not exist. Declared in `kendex-local.toml`; the render and the `.claude` link follow.
- `kendex-issues` named its own source as `~/dev/kendex/...`. Fixed in the source this repo owns, `.kendex-local/skills/kendex-issues/SKILL.md`, so the render follows on refresh. The path is now relative to the checkout root, with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` named as the way to find it.
- Same defect in the `[skill-instructions] orch` block of `kendex-local.toml`, which claimed the orch-drill rig was already at `~/dev/orch-drill`. It is a separate repository, so the text now says to clone `bmethod/orch-drill`.

Clone proof re-run after the fixes: `size-ratchet` present and executable, its link resolves, 20 links with 0 dangling and 0 absolute, and both machine paths gone outside the test fixtures.

**Why this outranks the backlog top.** It is the close-out of three merged packages, and `AGENTS.md`'s session-continuity rule asks for it before a session ends. Untracked files have no history; leaving it uncommitted risks losing the only record of what was measured.

**One concern:** the session record. No code.

### What it carries for the next session

- **B2 (streaming) is the only unbuilt item** of the transport plan, and the paired measurement that justifies it: `openai/gpt-4o-mini` max inter-chunk gap **22.440 / 25.055 s non-streamed** against **0.478 / 0.208 s streamed**, same model, same endpoint.
- Two upstream facts settled at `$0`: `usage` arrives in a stream's final chunk with **no opt-in**, and keep-alive frames exist — but their **cadence is not settled** (1, 16, 16, 21 per call, no regular spacing), so any figure quoting a fixed interval is unsupported.
- The warning that **keep-alives will defeat the per-`recv` timeout** once streaming lands, which is why the call budget had to land first.
- **B1's premise correction**: "classify in-band SSE errors" was already satisfied by accident, so the obvious bite-proof passes on `main` before the code exists. B2 must not re-litigate it.

### And the things that went wrong

- The three defects an adversarial reviewer found in this session's own code, each written as a pattern rather than an incident.
- Numbers that were wrong in inherited documents: "8 of 8 exceed on wall clock" is **7 of 8**; and the per-`recv` timeout's bite is a property of the **model**, not of OpenRouter.
- Five traps that cost real time, including that **`pytest-timeout` is not installed** — so a mutation run passing `--timeout` reports every mutant killed while testing nothing.

### Verification

`make validate` exit 0; 97 doc-gate tests pass (`test_doc_gate_consistency`, `test_cited_paths_resolve`, `test_session_handoff_narrative_pointer`, `test_session_handoff_claims`, `test_session_handoff_live_state`, `test_docs_numbering_no_collisions`). `make handoff` regenerated `docs/session-handoff.md`, which now points at the dated narrative and marks it `(today)`.

## Summary

Seeds this repo with its first skill, `android-e2e-demo-recording`: it runs an Android app's unit and
instrumented (Compose) tests on a Devin box and records one continuous side-by-side video of the
emulator and the terminal, with each test's name burned into the frame. The skill was developed and
re-recorded eight times against `nowinandroid`
([EvangelosG/nowinandroid#3](https://github.com/EvangelosG/nowinandroid/pull/3)); this copy is the
portable template — drop `.agents/skills/android-e2e-demo-recording/` into any Android repo and edit
`config.env`.

Nothing about the app is written down. `config.env` holds five values (`APP_MODULE`, `VARIANT`,
`UNIT_TASKS`, `PAUSE_ARG`, `AVD`), all with derive-it defaults (`:app`, `Debug`,
`<app>:test<Variant>UnitTest`, the first installed AVD). Everything else — where the result XMLs are,
which tests ran, how many, and what to draw over which second of video — is discovered at runtime from
Gradle, the XMLs and `adb logcat -v epoch`.

Because those five values are the one thing an operator can get wrong, a wrong one answers itself
rather than dumping a Gradle trace after a ten-minute configure:

```
* What went wrong:
Cannot locate tasks that match ':core:domain:testNopeUnitTest' as task 'testNopeUnitTest' not found ...

test* tasks that exist in :core:domain:
  :core:domain:testDemoDebugUnitTest
  :core:domain:testProdDebugUnitTest

Set APP_MODULE / VARIANT / UNIT_TASKS to match, in:
  .../android-e2e-demo-recording/config.env
```

`explain_gradle_failure` parses the failing task spec out of the log, then lists that project's tasks
sharing the verb prefix — or the build's modules if the *project* was the wrong part, and nothing at
all when Gradle already printed `Candidates are:`. It also reprints the `* What went wrong:` block,
which the on-camera output filter otherwise swallows. Same idea in `boot_emulator.sh` (unknown `AVD`
fails before launching the emulator, listing the installed ones) and `verify_evidence.sh` (missing
result XMLs list the module directories that do have results).

Three traps the SKILL.md exists to prevent, all learned the expensive way:

- the screen recorder time lapses its own `*-edited.mp4` (200s becomes ~18s), so `finalize_recording.sh`
  re-encodes the raw `*-raw-*.mkv` chunks instead and `verify_evidence.sh --video` fails a take whose
  duration does not match the run;
- label timing must come from the first raw chunk's creation epoch, not from when a human started
  recording, or every name sits ~5s early;
- the default take has no pauses and is evidence a suite ran green, not something to watch — a reviewer
  who has to read the screens wants `--pause-ms 400`/`800`, which only does anything once a test class
  in the app repo reads the `demoPauseMs` instrumentation argument.

Verified on this box against `nowinandroid` with `REPO_ROOT` pointed at it: green full run (12
instrumented / 1 ignored, 11 unit), plus deliberately wrong variant, unknown task, unknown module,
unknown AVD and wrong result paths. `shellcheck -S warning` is clean.


Link to Devin session: https://outpostai.devinenterprise.com/sessions/c43d19d89fca421786cf8df7edf24be7
Requested by: @EvangelosG

## Cross-scope note (CLAUDE.md)

Touches `driver/`, `rom/bench/`, and `refemu/` — docs plus two live
defaults in `refemu/scripts/gen_reference_trace.py`. Team-lead sign-off
per the human owner's direct instruction to close this inside the sprint
(#199) rather than defer it.

## Summary

Closes #199. #198 (R_DrawColumn/R_DrawSpan unroll, `PINNED_HASH
9a6a47d0…`) correctly updated the live consumers of the milestone icount
(15,653,137 → 15,393,136) in `justfile`, `driver/test_render.sh`,
`driver/gen_frame_fixture.py`'s CLI default, `rom/bench/canonical_throughput/run.sh`'s
window label, and `scripts/run_milestone.sh`'s call site — but missed
docs and two comment blocks in files it otherwise touched, plus two live
defaults in a file it didn't touch at all.

**This PR's five items** (found by grepping the whole repo for the old
value after #198 landed, not by trusting any single file's changed-lines
list):

1. `driver/README.md:27` — the milestone icount cited in the fixture
   validation section.
2. `rom/bench/canonical_throughput/README.md:26` — the boot-phase window
   boundary table; `run.sh` itself was updated in #198, its README
   wasn't.
3. `driver/gen_frame_fixture.py`'s pre-increment/post-increment
   explanation comment — cited the old value twice, describing the exact
   mechanism #198/rom-2 fixed elsewhere.
4. `rom/bench/canonical_throughput/run.sh`'s header window-table comment
   and `scripts/run_milestone.sh`'s checkpoint-cadence illustrative
   example — both separate from the lines #198 already updated in the
   same two files.
5. **`refemu/scripts/gen_reference_trace.py`'s two `--expect-*-icount`
   defaults — live, not docs.** `--expect-init-graphics-icount`
   (11,016,543 → 11,014,966, value taken from rom-2's #200 review, not
   re-derived here) and `--expect-frame-commit-icount` (15,653,137 →
   15,393,136). `--expect-frame-commit-fbhash`'s default is unchanged —
   the ROM's rendering didn't change, only its instruction count.
   #200's one-off regeneration passed `--no-expect`, routing around
   these stale defaults and masking them; `justfile`'s
   `gen-reference-trace` recipe calls the script with no flags, so the
   next real run would have hit a spurious cross-check failure on a
   correct trace — a gate that fails on good input trains people to pass
   `--no-expect` reflexively, disabling it permanently. Also updated the
   adjacent comment explaining why `max_instructions=15_728_640` still
   doesn't need to move (15,393,136 still falls in
   `[14, 15) × RAM_HASH_INTERVAL`, verified) and the fbhash-unchanged
   comment to mention both #127 and #175.

## Deliberately NOT touched

`refemu/reference_traces/README.md` and the committed
`demo-boot-to-first-frame.eabb12ed4f18.tsv`/`.json` trace files it
describes. That section documents an **existing, still-current artifact**
generated against the pre-#175 ROM — the committed trace files still
reflect the old hash's data. Updating the cited icount there without
regenerating the actual trace would make the prose wrong in a *new* way
(claiming a number the committed file doesn't contain), not fix it.
refemu-2's trace regeneration — the sprint's last remaining item — is
what makes that section's numbers current; this PR doesn't get ahead of
it.

`SPEC.md`'s own reference is similarly left alone, per team lead's note
(CODEOWNERS-gated, human owner's call).

## Verification

- `python3 -m py_compile driver/gen_frame_fixture.py refemu/scripts/gen_reference_trace.py` — clean.
- `bash -n` + `shellcheck` on both touched `.sh` files — clean.
- Repo-wide grep for the old values (`15653137`/`15,653,137`/`11016543`/`11,016,543`)
  after this diff: every remaining hit is either an intentional "was X
  before" historical note (already correct, from #198's own sweep),
  `SPEC.md` (left for the human owner), or
  `refemu/reference_traces/README.md` (deliberately unchanged, see
  above).

## Purity declaration

- [x] No computation moved outside SQL
- [x] Driver changes: comment/doc/default-value only, no new logic
- [x] No wall-clock/randomness on any computation path

author: ibetitsmike
body:
## Summary

Fixes nested PTC (kernel-mode) bash rows rendering an empty red exit-code pill and `took —` after a workspace reload, and makes failed reconstructed nested calls report "failed" instead of "✓ completed".

## Background

`code_execution` persists rich `nestedCalls` (full outputs) on the tool part during live streaming, and those take precedence on history replay. When they are absent (older histories, interrupted or truncated streams, compaction), the UI reconstructs nested calls from the compact `result.toolCalls` records; RLM kernel-mode compact records (r12) carry only `{ok, bytes}` with the real result suppressed. That fallback reconstruction previously fed placeholder data into `BashToolCall`:

- `wall_duration_ms` undefined → `took —`
- `exitCode` undefined is not `0`, so `ExitCodeBadge` took the red `bg-danger` styling with empty content → the empty error pill
- an `ok: false` record still showed "✓ completed" as its status

Untouched current-format histories are unaffected: rich `nestedCalls` persist and keep full duration and exit-code detail after reload. This PR hardens the fallback path.

## Implementation

- `displayedMessageBuilder.ts`: reconstruction emits no synthetic output for kernel compact records. Failure travels out-of-band via the existing nested-call `failed` flag, so a real tool output can never be mistaken for a reconstruction stand-in (Codex review round 1).
- `toolUtils.tsx`: `getNestedToolStatus` honors an explicit `failed` flag over shape-derived detection.
- `BashToolCall.tsx` / `bashCollapsedSummary.ts`: render `took …` and the exit-code badge only when those fields exist.
- Error records reconstruct as `{success: false, error}` so failure text stays visible in bash's ErrorBox after reload.

## Validation

- Red-green verified: each mechanism's regression test fails with that mechanism reverted
- Remote UAT (coder-agents): live rendering, untouched current-format reload, fallback compact-record reload, failure statuses, plain non-kernel bash regression, and 390px width, with no empty pill or `took —` in any scenario

## Risks

Low, display-layer only. Affects nested tool rendering inside `code_execution` cards; full live results are guarded by a test asserting duration and exit-code badge still render, and real outputs that structurally resemble reconstruction records are passed through untouched.

author: ryancinsight
body:
`Heavy Validation (kuznetsov)` was killed at its 15-minute bound on #655. The log accounts for the time exactly:

```
19:40:31  Fetching the repository        ← starts
19:53:51  Fetching the repository        ← ends, 13m20s
19:55:13  Compiling proc-macro2 ...      ← compile begins
19:55:44  Terminate orphan process (rustc)
```

The job spent 13m20s of a 15-minute budget fetching, then was killed 31 seconds into the compile. It never reached a test.

## Cause

Nine checkouts carried `fetch-depth: 0` — every commit, every branch. Nothing reads any of it. No workflow runs `git log`, `describe`, `blame`, `merge-base` or `rev-list`, and neither does anything under `scripts/` or `xtask/` that CI calls. They now take the default shallow fetch.

## Not a bound change

The 15-minute budgets are untouched. The same job finishes in 8–9 minutes on main, so the bound was never the problem — the fetch time is, and it varies enough to leave the three heavy jobs one slow fetch away from failing on work that is perfectly fine. #655 is the current casualty and needs this to land first.

I looked at this expecting to find that #655's lockfile change had busted a cache. It hadn't; the timing said otherwise.

Item: KW-CI-FULL-HISTORY-CHECKOUT

<!-- RECURSEML_SUMMARY:START -->
## High-level PR Summary
This PR removes unnecessary full git history fetching (`fetch-depth: 0`) from all CI checkout steps, switching to shallow clones instead. The change addresses a critical performance issue where the `Heavy Validation (kuznetsov)` job spent 13 minutes and 20 seconds of its 15-minute timeout just fetching git history, leaving insufficient time for actual compilation and testing. Since no CI workflows or scripts actually use git history commands, the full history fetch was wasteful. The backlog entry documents this issue as `KW-CI-FULL-HISTORY-CHECKOUT`.

author: estparcae
body:
Añade `/[locale]/dashboard`: el panel que usan los participantes durante las 12 horas. Busqué "dashboard" en el repo y salían 0 coincidencias — `participant/[number]` es la ficha pública, no un panel autenticado.

Va **en draft** porque hay dos cosas sin terminar (abajo) y porque las decisiones de modelo de datos conviene revisarlas antes de mergear.

## Qué incluye

| Ruta | Qué resuelve |
| --- | --- |
| `/dashboard` | Countdown al code freeze, progreso de las 12 h, equipo, validador de entrega, checklist de 7 pasos y las cinco sedes. |
| `/dashboard/agenda` | Los 9 bloques canónicos con filtro por tipo, «solo mi agenda» y estado ahora/pasado/próximo. |
| `/dashboard/badge` | Muestra el badge que ya generó el Badge Studio, su estado, y a qué perfil lleva su QR. |
| `/dashboard/tracks` | Los 3 tracks con sus ideas para arrancar, más premios y perks. Selección en borrador → confirmación. |
| `/dashboard/mentors` | Las 4 mesas de las comunidades organizadoras: mesa de planta del equipo + turnos de 25 min (11:00–13:00). |
| `/dashboard/credits` + `/[partner]` | Los 8 partners. Código oculto hasta canjear, y una página por partner. |
| `/dashboard/support` | WhatsApp, etiqueta de soporte y plantilla copiable con sede/mesa/track ya rellenados. |

## Decisiones que quiero que miren

**El contenido canónico no se duplica.** Agenda, tracks, premios y perks se leen de `src/messages/{es,en}.json`. `src/lib/dashboard/content.ts` solo aporta lo que la landing no necesita: hora de fin, lugar, tipo de bloque, audiencia y el catálogo de partners. Si cambian la agenda en los mensajes, el dashboard la sigue.

**Seis tablas nuevas, ninguna existente tocada.** Todas con prefijo `dashboard_`; los equipos cuelgan de `badge_participants`. Migración `0006_absent_blob.sql`.

**Sin transacciones.** El driver es `neon-http`, así que la reserva de turno (`where team_id is null`) y el cupo de cada mesa (subconsulta dentro del `UPDATE`) se resuelven en una sola sentencia para que dos equipos no pisen la última plaza.

**El badge no se duplica.** `/dashboard/badge` no genera nada: lee `getBadgeStudioState`, pinta el PNG que ya existe con `participantBadgeImagePath` y enlaza al Studio para crear o reemplazar. El QR sigue siendo el que el Studio escribe hacia el perfil público.

**Mentorías = mesas por organización, no personas.** El brand book prohíbe inventar datos fuera del contenido canónico y el sitio solo dice "Mentorías con Crafter Station", así que las mesas son Crafter Station, AI Labs, Nucleo Labs y Open2.

**Soporte es WhatsApp**, no Discord: es el canal que ya usa el evento.

**Reutiliza el sistema visual existente** — `.keycap`, `.pixel-heading`, `.scanlines`, `.cursor` de `globals.css`. No añade tokens, fuentes ni dependencias.

## Lo que falta antes de mergear

1. **Sembrar las mesas de mentoría.** `seedMentorTables()` está escrita y es idempotente, pero no hay quién la llame — falta decidir si va en un cron, en el arranque o a mano.
2. **Creación de equipos.** Se leen y se muestran, pero no hay UI para crearlos ni para unirse. Probablemente deba engancharse al flujo de WhatsApp que ya existe.

## Verificado

- `next build` en verde, con las 7 rutas.
- `biome check` limpio sobre todo lo nuevo.
- TypeScript sin errores.
- **No probado contra una base de datos real**: no tengo credenciales. La migración está generada pero sin aplicar.

author: wkjarosz
body:
## The bug

Building a consumer with `-fsanitize=undefined` reports every access to `m_thread_index` as a null dereference:

```
smallthreadpool.h:384:28: runtime error: load of null pointer of type 'int'
smallthreadpool.h:386:43: runtime error: store to null pointer of type 'int'
```

**The pointer is never actually null.** The thread_locals were defined out-of-line in whichever TU provides `SMALL_THREADPOOL_IMPLEMENTATION`, so every *other* TU reached them through the Itanium ABI's TLS wrapper, which guards the access on a weak `_ZTH…` initialization symbol. These variables are constant-initialized, so no init function is ever emitted and that symbol resolves to zero. GCC 13.3 then computes the address with `lea` — which sets no flags — and emits no test of its own, so the sanitizer's null branch consumes the *guard's* flags:

```asm
cmpq $0x0, <GOT slot for _ZTHN3stp10ThreadPool14m_thread_indexE>   ; ZF=1: no init fn exists
je   skip_call                                                     ; taken
mov  %fs:0x0,%rax
lea  -0x270(%rax),%rax        ; lea sets NO flags
je   <ubsan report>           ; consumes the stale ZF above -> always taken
mov  %esi,%fs:(%rax)          ; the real store: %fs:-0x270, perfectly valid
jne  <normal path>            ; same stale flags
xor  %esi,%esi                ; pointer argument = literal 0
call __ubsan_handle_type_mismatch_v1
```

There is no `test %rax,%rax` anywhere. The access itself is a valid `%fs`-relative store, which is why nothing ever crashed — the diagnostic fires and the program runs correctly. GCC 16.1 emitted a flags-setting `addq` for the same line in the one TU I checked, so this looks version-dependent.

## The fix

Define all three statics in-class (C++17 `inline static` data members). That removes the cross-TU reference, so there is no wrapper and no guard to confuse the null check, and it drops an indirection on every access.

## Second, independent issue in the same lines

`m_next_guest_thread_index` was a plain `int` incremented with `++` from arbitrary guest threads entering the pool concurrently — a data race that could hand two threads the same index. It is now `std::atomic<int>` bumped with a relaxed `fetch_add`; nothing is published through the counter, so relaxed suffices. `max_thread_index()` carried a second copy of that same read-modify-write and now calls `get_or_assign_thread_index()` instead.

## Verification

Against a consumer's (HDRView's) full suite under ASan+UBSan on Ubuntu 24.04 / GCC 13.3, Release:

|  | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Affected tests, `halt_on_error=1` | fail with the report above | pass |
| Full suite | — | 74/74 |
| `_ZTH…` guard references in binary | present | 0 |

Header also builds and runs warning-free on GCC and Clang, C++17 and C++20.

author: sindredg
body:
Plan section 1.

## The measurement changed the fix

The request was to put the place selector nearer the top. Measured first, on a
375px viewport:

| | |
|---|---|
| Page height | **2144px**, over three screens |
| Moon section | 1.6 screens down |
| Eclipses | 2.4 screens down |
| Selector | visible at 210px, then gone |

The selector was never hidden at the top. It was gone for the other two thirds
of the page, so changing place meant scrolling back up. That makes this a
**sticky** problem rather than a position one.

## After

Measured from 1616px down the page, at both 375px and 1280px:

- the control bar pins at `top: 0`
- the selector sits 38px into the viewport, reachable without scrolling back
- the background is opaque, so content does not show through
- the theme button does not overlap the bar

The masthead also shrank on narrow screens, moving the selector from 210px to
189px. That is the smaller half.

## One note

Content never enters the body gutters, so a plain `background: var(--paper)`
covers everything scrolling under the bar. No negative margin or full bleed
trick was needed.

## On the test

One assertion added: **if the bar is sticky, it must have a background.** A
transparent sticky bar shows the page scrolling through itself, which is a bug.

Whether the bar is sticky at all is a decision, not a fault, so that is not
asserted. Same rule as #39.

## Verified

138 pass, `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.

author: vjpixel
body:
## #6317 — `unclaim-issue`

`session-registry.ts` tinha `claim-issue` e nenhum inverso — a única forma de soltar uma issue era `end`, que encerra a sessão inteira e solta TODAS. Evidência ao vivo colhida nesta sessão: `unclaim-issue --issue 6328` foi tentado logo após o merge do PR #6333 e o CLI respondeu com a lista de verbos disponíveis — o subcomando não existia. As claims de #6328/#6326 seguiram presas mesmo com as issues já `CLOSED`.

Implementado:
- `unclaimIssue()` em `scripts/lib/session-registry.ts` — check-and-set escopado à PRÓPRIA sessão (`kind`+`tag`+`sessionId`); nunca mexe na claim de outra sessão (mesma disciplina de `releaseMergeLock`). Três desfechos: `unclaimed`, `no-op-not-claimed` (issue não estava reivindicada — nunca finge sucesso, mesmo padrão do `end` pós-#5797), `no-op-session-missing`.
- Subcomando CLI `unclaim-issue --issue N`.
- `.claude/hooks/inject-session-id.mjs` — `unclaim-issue` entra em `INJECTABLE_SUBCOMMANDS` (precisa de `--session-id` pra saber DE QUEM remover).
- Call sites documentados em `.claude/skills/diaria-develop/SKILL.md` e `.claude/skills/diaria-overnight/SKILL.md`: (1) logo após merge confirmado via `gh issue view --json state`; (2) ao gravar status terminal `deixado-para-o-helios`/`nao-tentada` — segurar uma claim que o próprio status diz "não é meu" é contraditório.

Fora de escopo (conforme a issue): chamar `unclaim` a partir de um hook (não sabe se o merge foi *confirmado*); GC de claim de issue fechada (o call site certo resolve na origem).

## #6327 — heartbeat de sessão coordenadora depende do beacon

`grep -c "session-registry.ts heartbeat"` mostra 0 em `diaria-develop`/`diaria-overnight`, mas a medição ao vivo mostrou `lastHeartbeat` fresco mesmo assim (develop com 171min de vida e heartbeat de 0min). Causa: o beacon (`PreToolUse`, #6303) enriquece o registro coordenador EXISTENTE a cada chamada de ferramenta — garantia real, mas implícita e não documentada em lugar nenhum; uma docstring antiga (#6160) ainda afirmava o contrário.

Implementado (opção (a) da issue, recomendada pelo editor):
- Docstring de `heartbeat()` em `session-registry.ts` documenta a dependência, corrige o texto desatualizado do #6160/#5474, e nomeia o contra-argumento honesto (acoplamento observabilidade↔correção, hook fail-open engolindo exceção).
- Teste novo em `test/session-beacon-hook.test.ts` (`#6327`) — spawna o hook real via stdin contra um registro `overnight-*` pré-existente e trava que `lastHeartbeat` avança sem criar `interactive-*` paralelo.
- `.claude/skills/diaria-{develop,overnight}/SKILL.md` registram a dependência no ponto de `register --kind {develop|overnight}`.
- **Decisão registrada (critério de aceite 4):** sessão coordenadora rodando de worktree vinculado (o beacon pula esse caso, #6303) — aceitável ficar stale, sem heartbeat por caminho alternativo. Justificativa completa na docstring de `heartbeat()`: por convenção do repo, worktree é sempre do subagente implementador, nunca da coordenadora; o fallback `SOFT_STALE_MS` já existe e é seguro; adicionar um call site só pra esse caso reabriria o padrão "depende de skill lembrar" que o beacon existe pra eliminar.

## Disciplina

- `npx tsc --noEmit` limpo.
- `npx tsx --test test/session-registry.test.ts test/session-beacon-hook.test.ts test/inject-session-id-hook.test.ts test/lib-boundary.test.ts` — 1 falha pré-existente (`checkSessionsScanHealth` ILEGÍVEL, `chmod` não restringe leitura de diretório no Windows), confirmada não-relacionada via `git stash` contra o mesmo commit base.
- `test/skill-chained-session-command-guard-6232.test.ts` atualizado (regex duplicada de `INJECTABLE_SUBCOMMANDS`) e verde — as chamadas `unclaim-issue` novas nas SKILL.md são standalone.
- `npx knip --reporter compact` limpo.

Closes #6317
Closes #6327

### ✨ Description

The `shiki-langs-*.js` build chunk was 5.2 MB (968 kB gzip) — Shiki's entire on-demand grammar registry (~215 non-pre-registered languages) collapsed into a single lazy chunk by `ui/plugins/consolidateChunks.js`, so highlighting one code fence in an unusual language downloaded every language's grammar.

`KsMarkdown` pre-registers 29 grammars statically (`shikiHighlighter.ts`) and falls back to `shiki/langs`'s full bundle for anything else. The chunk-group `name` is changed from a constant `"shiki-langs"` to a function that names each grammar its own chunk (`shiki-lang-<name>`), plus one small chunk for the registry index that maps a language to its module. Pre-registered grammars are unaffected — they stay bundled into the `markdown` chunk as before.

Verified with a full `npm run build`: largest chunk dropped from 5.2 MB to 780 kB (`emacs-lisp`, 198 kB gzip), 214 grammar chunks + 1 registry chunk emitted, and the existing build-time invariants in `consolidateChunks.js` (no static edge into a lazy toolchain, no import cycle, no static edge into an on-demand grammar chunk) all held without changes to their logic — only their naming pattern was widened from `shiki-langs` to `shiki-lang(-|s-registry)`.

### 🎨 Frontend Checklist

- [x] Type checking passes (`npm run check:types`)
- [x] Code builds without errors (`npm run build`)
- [x] Unit tests pass (`npm run test:unit` — ran the full `KsMarkdown` suite, including the on-demand-grammar test)
- [ ] Translations are complete if `en.json` changed — not applicable, no translation keys touched
- [ ] Screenshots or video recordings attached showing the `UI` changes — not applicable, build-output-only change with no rendered UI difference; verified via build output file sizes instead

### 📝 Additional Notes

This trades one large file for ~215 small ones in the served `assets/` directory (and in the shipped jar). If that file-count cost is unwanted, an equally small change buckets grammars into a handful of chunks instead of one-per-grammar — happy to switch if preferred.

### 🤖 AI Authors

This PR was raised by an AI. Why did the cat sit on the shiki chunk? Because it wanted to load *purr*-grammar on demand, one byte at a time. 🐱
