body:
## Summary

`harumi-cli` was the only repo without the review workflow that `harumi-platform`, `harumi-api`, and `frontend` all run — so no automated review comments on PRs here. This adds it.

Two deliberate differences from a straight copy of harumi-platform's version:

**1. This repo is public; the other three are private.** A `pull_request` from a fork gets a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN` and no access to the AWS role, so the job would *fail on every outside contribution* rather than review it. Forks are skipped via:

```yaml
if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
```

`pull_request_target` would grant the needed permissions, but it checks out untrusted code *with* them — the documented privilege-escalation footgun. Not a trade worth making for a repo whose PRs all currently come from `harumi-io` branches (verified across all 20 PRs to date).

**2. The prompt targets this codebase**, not React/TanStack. Each item was checked against the actual source rather than assumed:

- `requires-python = ">=3.9"` (`pyproject.toml:10`) — no 3.10+ syntax or stdlib.
- `~/.harumi` credential handling and the 0600 mode (`config.py:92`), and tokens leaking into `git remote -v` / shell history — `git.py:146`'s `_authenticated_url` already documents an escaping hazard here, so it's worth watching.
- Regenerating `cli-surface.json` when the command tree changes, since `test_every_command_builds` enforces it and harumi-docs' weekly drift check (harumi-io/harumi-docs#12) reads it.
- Flags are a public interface shipped to users' laptops and can't be hot-fixed server-side.
- Partial failure in multi-step commands — `projects create` and `import` create a project, then provision a repo, then push.

It also encodes the class of bug behind #20: `X-Organization` scopes harumi-api's *read* endpoints while creation reads `customer_id` from the body, so a setting that scopes reads does not necessarily scope writes. That's the kind of cross-repo mismatch a reviewer looking only at this diff would miss.

## Infrastructure

Uses the shared org-wide CI/CD role by ARN (`harumi-us-east-2-github-cicd-role`), the same pattern harumi-platform uses since neither repo has an `AWS_ROLE_TO_ASSUME` secret. That role's trust policy already covers `repo:harumi-io/*` and grants `bedrock:InvokeModel`, so **no new secret or IAM change is required**.

`--max-turns 80` matches harumi-platform rather than harumi-api's 30: the action fails the job when turns exceed the ceiling even if the review posted successfully.

## Test plan

- [x] Workflow YAML parses; permissions, triggers, fork guard, and step order verified.
- [x] Confirmed `PROMPT_SIMPLE` retains the `{LAST_COMMIT}` placeholder the bash substitution depends on.
- [x] Verified every repo-specific claim in the prompt against the source (3.9 floor, `0o600` chmod, `_authenticated_url`, `cli-surface.json` regeneration).
- [x] Confirmed all 20 existing PRs originate from `harumi-io` branches, so the fork guard doesn't disable review in practice.
- [ ] **Real validation is this PR itself** — if a review comment appears below, the workflow works end to end. Worth confirming before merge.

author: jstar269
body:
## What

`jalr rd, rs` and a non-`$ra` `jr rs` must read their target register **at** the
transfer. MIPS orders it `temp <- GPR[rs]`, then `GPR[rd] <- return_addr`, then the
delay slot — so neither the link write nor the slot can change where control goes.

`tools/codegen.py` emitted the target read after both:

```c
sr_begin(...); s->r[rd] = ret; sr_end(...);
<delay slot>
{ uint32_t _t = s->r[rs]; dispatch(s, _t); }
```

Two independent defects fall out, and one reordering fixes both:

| shape | pre-fix behavior |
| --- | --- |
| slot writes `$rs` (`jr $t9` tail-call preceded by a reload of `$t9`) | dispatches to whatever the slot left behind |
| `jalr $rX, $rX` — no delay slot needed | link lands first, so the target becomes the call's own return address |

`jr $ra` is deliberately untouched: it IS the host return under the AOT frame model,
it reads `$ra` at the transfer by construction, and turning it into a computed
dispatch would double-execute the caller's continuation.

## Evidence

**Failing-before / passing-after, executable.** The defect was found by an
AOT/interpreter cosimulation gate that ran the same source-owned guest bytes through
both execution lanes. With `tools/codegen.py` reverted to `af5c4f4` on an otherwise
identical tree:

```
cosim: 17 comparison cases, 4 divergence report(s)      cosim: FAIL
  cell=jrslot  trace diverges at step 9:
      AOT     op=0x240300b2   (entered leaf B — the value the slot wrote)
      INTERP  op=0x240300a1   (entered leaf A — the architecturally correct callee)
  cell=jrslot  architectural field r2: AOT=0x00001000 INTERP=0x00000010
  cell=jrtail  same divergence via the `jr $rs` emission path
```

With the fix: `17 comparison cases, 0 divergence report(s)`.

That gate is a separate change (it is a ~2.5k-line framework and deserves its own
review). This PR carries the production fix plus source-shape regressions so the
emission order cannot regress without the gate.

**4 of the 7 tests fail against the pre-fix generator** — both aliasing forms, the
computed `jr`, and the no-link `jalr $zero, $rs`. Verified by running the new test
module against a pristine `af5c4f4` worktree:

```
FAILED (failures=4)
  test_jalr_aliasing_its_own_link_register_still_reaches_the_callee
      AssertionError: 273 not less than 156 : jalr read its target after writing the link
  test_computed_jr_reads_target_before_its_delay_slot
  test_jalr_reads_target_before_its_delay_slot
  test_jalr_with_a_zero_link_register_writes_no_link
```

The other three are boundary pins that must NOT change: the `jr $ra` host return, the
link-before-slot ordering, and the branch-before-slot trace order.

## Scope

Only the target-latching fix, its regressions, and the metadata those require. No
unrelated codegen cleanup.

`jr rs` and `jalr rd, rs` are the **only** register-dependent transfer targets in the
generator — direct `j`/`jal` and every conditional branch compute PC-relative or
encoded targets, and branch conditions were already read before the slot.

## Local validation

- `tools/test_codegen_transfer_target_timing.py` — 7 tests, OK
- `python -m unittest discover -s tools -p "test_*.py"` — 1506 tests, 1 failure:
  `test_build_truth::test_M1_...`, which fails **identically on pristine `af5c4f4`**
  (the mutant invokes `ver` through MSYS `sh`, which has no such command). Unrelated
  and pre-existing; tracked separately.
- `production-smoke`, `production-smoke-gap`, `dispatch-selftest`,
  `dispatch-isolation-selftest`, `src/ref` selftest — PASS
- `publish_audit --tracked-only --provenance-self-consistency` — OK on **both** the
  index and `--worktree` legs (640 tracked files)
- `pre-commit run --all-files` — all 15 hooks pass

## Provenance

One added path (`tools/test_codegen_transfer_target_timing.py`), classified
`synthetic_fixture` by the deterministic `tools/test_*` path-shape rule — mechanically
derivable, no private record needed, nothing hand-attested. Metadata digests refreshed
from final bytes in the same commit.

author: snokvist
body:
> **Blocked on a waybeam_venc merge decision.** This is the consumer half of the
> frame-SHM ring v2 break. A v2 producer will not serve a v1 consumer and vice
> versa, so this must land together with the venc change (`OpenIPC/waybeam_venc#116`),
> not before it. Opened now so the diff is reviewable while that decision is made.

## What changed and why

venc 0.69.0 removes its frame-SHM ring-fill bitrate clamp. On a `frame-shm://`
craft **we** are the rate controller: co-located on the same SoC, already
reading the egress ring as a §9.9 TX-local backpressure signal, already owning
`video0.bitrate` under §9.6. The producer-side clamp was a second controller on
the same input signal, and its only actuator (`MI_VENC_SetChnAttr`) emits an IDR
on every real rate change.

Ring header offset 88 therefore carries the signal the clamp was reacting to
instead of the clamp's own output, and offset 96 adds the drop counter that was
previously invisible to us:

| off | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| 88 | `throttle_permille` (u16, `1000` = healthy) | `low_water_slots` (u16, `<= 1` = healthy) |
| 96 | — | `other_drops` (u64) |

**The polarity at offset 88 inverts, which is why this is a version bump and not
a rename.** A same-layout, opposite-polarity field is the one change a
byte-offset consumer cannot detect for itself: unrebuilt, we would read a
near-empty ring as catastrophic clamping and a full ring as perfectly healthy —
the dangerous direction reading as healthy. `attach()` already refuses a version
mismatch (`io/src/frame_shm.cpp:226`), so the break is loud.

**Slots, not a fraction of `slot_count`.** The healthy band is `<= 1`, because
the producer samples immediately after writing — a consumer that is keeping up
still leaves one frame queued, which is why the clamp recovered at `<= 1` slot
and engaged at `>= 2`. A permille encoding cannot carry that: at a 16-slot ring
one slot is 62.5 permille, truncates to 62, and converts back to 0 —
indistinguishable from a drained ring.

**`other_drops` is kept strictly apart from `full_drops`** because the two call
for opposite reactions from §9: `full_drops` is congestion this node is causing
and slowing down helps; `other_drops` is a frame the producer could not build
(oversize, or a malformed encoder packet table) and slowing down fixes nothing.
Folding them would make a craft-side packet-table fault read as a link problem
and drive the selector down for no reason.

## Evidence

The measurement that motivated removing the clamp, from @vertexodessa on a
Star6E at 720p120, ~11 Mbps commanded (`OpenIPC/waybeam_venc#116`):

| | clamp on | clamp off | reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| IDR rate at receiver | 6.5 /sec | 0.2 /sec (the 4 s GOP) | craft-side count |
| glass-to-glass | ~100–143 ms | **~15–37 ms** | operator measurement |
| ring read latency (`rw`) | 40–120 ms | **1–9 ms** | `rw` sample |

**Control — unchanged by this PR:** every offset except 88 and 96, pinned by
`tests/frame_shm_test.cpp` (`kFrHdrHealthMagic` 76, `kFrHdrFullDrops` 80,
`kFrameRingHeaderSize` 192). The header size does not move and no field
relocates; only the *meaning* of 88 changes and 96 is taken from producer pad.
`shm_full_drops` semantics are untouched, and the §15.3 egress column is
unaffected — we do not publish producer health on rings we create.

Method caveat: the latency numbers above are the craft author's, taken on
hardware this branch has not been run on. **No RF trial has been run for this
change** — see Verification.

## Verification

- Build: `scripts/gates.sh` with `WBLINK_SSC338Q_TOOLCHAIN` and
  `WBLINK_ANDROID_NDK` set — **35 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, on a wiped
  `build/`. That includes `ssc338q{,-au,-eu}` (the `.232` vehicle) and
  `android-arm64`, which is the only preset building `WBLINK_FRAME_SHM=OFF` and
  therefore the one that proves the rename is consistent across the ifdef
  boundary. Warnings introduced: none.
- Tests: `ctest dev` 84/84. `frame_shm_test` 168 checks, 0 failures — it pins
  the new offsets and asserts `other_drops` is a delta that rebases *together*
  with `full_drops` (they come from one producer, so rebasing only the counter
  that happened to decrease would leave the survivor reporting the old
  producer's lifetime total as a delta).
- Hardware: **none run.** This branch produces and consumes a v2 ring, so a
  device trial needs the matching venc build; that run is gated on the merge
  decision above. Nothing here has been on RF.

## Blast radius

- `io/src/frame_shm.cpp:459` is the only site that ever read offset 88; the
  rename is mechanical from there through `FrameShmStats` →
  `StreamStats::shm_low_water_slots` → the §15.3 JSON key.
- §15.3 consumers see two renamed/new keys: `shm_throttle_permille` →
  `shm_low_water_slots`, plus `shm_other_drops`. `tools/link_monitor.html` is
  updated in this change; `tests/link_monitor_test.py` pins the key list.
- §9 decisions: **nothing.** PROTOCOL.md already states these fields are
  observability-only and do not feed selection. The one place the old field
  appeared in a *rule* is the §9.3a Pass 111 clean-rung criterion, restated here
  from `shm_throttle_permille == 1000` to `shm_low_water_slots <= 1` — the same
  verdict on the raw signal instead of on a controller's response to it, and the
  same threshold, since the clamp recovered at `<= 1` and engaged at `>= 2`. The
  rung-4 calibration record keeps the field names it was taken with, annotated.
- Other frame-SHM consumers, out of tree: `waybeam-hub` and `radeon-vrx` need
  the same version bump (one constant each — neither ever read offset 88).
  `Waybeam-android` is **unaffected**: it builds `WBLINK_FRAME_SHM=OFF`
  (`wifi/src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt:47`) and `frame_shm.cpp` is only compiled
  when that is ON (`CMakeLists.txt:422`), so its vendored copy never compiles an
  attach path.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched off main — nothing committed or pushed to it directly.
- [x] Spec/protocol docs updated in this change (§15.4 layout, §15.3 fields and
      the `health_valid` rule, §9.3a criterion).
- [x] Comments and docs match the code as merged — no `permille` naming or
      "0 = drained" wording survives.
- [x] Deliberately left out and named: the §3.9 mid-stream re-arm (separate
      change), and any device trial (gated on the venc merge).

body:
## Проблема / задача
Candidate 01 exterior source is contract-validated and pinned, but Scene Factory did not yet load, compile, measure, or reproduce it as part of the approved Candidate GLB. The current media-surface phase also needed to remain an immutable historical baseline while the candidate pin advanced.

## Возможные варианты решения
- Compile the four project-authored exterior objects together with the approved architecture and components, while retaining runtime media surfaces as a separate manifest.
- Fold media planes into the Blender GLB, which would conflict with their platform-runtime-plane representation and the established phase boundary.
- Publish generated room outputs directly, or stage them internally and publish with exclusive no-clobber links.

## Обоснование выбора
Compiling architecture, components, and exterior together preserves the exact project-owned geometry contract and produces a directly measurable 61-mesh GLB without changing media ownership. Internal temporary outputs plus exclusive hard-link publication prevent partial or foreign-file overwrite during concurrent runs. Historical architecture, component, and media baselines remain explicit, so advancing the Candidate commit cannot silently rewrite previous evidence.

## Реализованное решение
- Pinned Candidate commit 380098d4b7cbc1d57498b059466f095ae3568929 and all seven source blobs by Git OID, raw SHA-256, and size.
- Added approved exterior source loading, phase-isolation validation, Blender compilation, GLB contract inspection, two-run reproducibility verification, CLI commands, and CI coverage.
- Added deterministic beveled-box exterior geometry with contract-derived names, materials, transforms, support metadata, and no parented objects or media planes.
- Recorded measured evidence for the 61-mesh, 8-material GLB: SHA-256 eb74ca5e90b7dd09ad137c2127a53988491a557eb1d634093dd2b5eee6456b92, 614784 bytes, byte-identical across two runs, and Khronos validation with zero errors and warnings.
- Added atomic no-clobber output publication and deterministic replacement-race coverage.
- Preserved architecture, component, and media-surface historical baselines and kept lighting, final Candidate, release, and publication boundaries false.
- Local repository validation passed; the full exact-Blender suite passed 723/723.

author: gunnjake
body:
Documentation sweep after the 2026-08-25 batch. Not cosmetic — three of these would cause real damage if followed.

### ⚠️ Three docs still described the migration approval gate as current
`README.md`, `database/migrations/README.md`, and a comment in `ci.yml` that read literally **`# required reviewers here = manual approval gate`** — an instruction to re-add it.

That gate **caused a production outage**: the approval held the *migration* while Vercel deployed the *code* independently, so new code ran against the old schema. All three now record why it must never come back, plus the rule that replaced it — **sequence the deploy, not the migration**: migration-only commit to prod first, then the code.

### ⚠️ DEPLOYMENT.md would have pointed production at the dev database
It listed the **dev** project ref as the prod value, left over from when the split was mid-flight. Replaced with placeholders and a warning rather than substituting a ref that can't be verified from the repo.

### ⚠️ The stack claimed Alembic
No dependency, no `alembic.ini`, no `alembic/`. Migrations are hand-written SQL — and `database/migrations/README.md` already said so, so the repo contradicted itself.

### Also
- **"Endpoints (current)" listed 3 endpoints**; there are 19 routers. Replaced with a pointer to the generated schema, plus the note that prod 404s `/docs` and `/openapi.json` **by design** — so it stops being reported as an outage and nobody aims the type generator at it.
- **`## Tests` said `pytest`.** Bare `pytest` picks up the repo `.env`, talks to a real database, and fails ~17 survey tests. Now documents `DATABASE_URL=""` and why "passes in CI, fails locally" is usually this.
- **Back-merge instructions recommended a push that is always rejected** by the ruleset. The PR is now the instruction, with the verification commands.
- Removed the `board-in-review.yml` job row and workflow reference — deleted from both repos 2026-07-03; board moves are manual.
- Database split is done (2026-07-09); dropped the "in progress" notes.
- `NEXT_STEPS.md` bannered as historical — the board is the tracker.
- Documented the `Migrate database (dev)` job, which existed but appeared nowhere.

Docs and one workflow **comment** only — no behaviour change. Companion PR in fa-web-app.

author: dcoyier
body: Quail now speaks **only** MCP 2026-07-28. Handshake-era HTTP cannot be represented on a product server: - `initialize` / `notifications/initialized` and other handshake JSON-RPC return `-32022` - `GET` / `DELETE` `/mcp` return `405 Allow: POST` (no standalone SSE session) - Allowed POSTs are stamped `mcp-protocol-version: 2026-07-28` so the SDK cannot take its 2025 entry - Clerk sticky keys are `user:{clerk_user_id}` only The Python SDK is still `mcp==2.1.1`; Quail no longer lets that SDK’s dual-era HTTP through. This is a protocol-era cut, not a product redesign. ## What changed - Product `MCPServer`s from `create_mcp_server` / `create_clerk_mcp_server` wrap Streamable HTTP as `stateless_http` with no event store, then gate the MCP path in ASGI (SSE bodies are not buffered). - `python -m quail.mcp_client` pins `Client(..., mode="2026-07-28")`. - Clerk sticky workspace is per Clerk user for the process, not per transport session. - Connector file GET routes stay on a raw `MCPServer` (not the product wrap). Clerk OAuth discovery (`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`) stays as resource-origin AS metadata, not a second MCP era. ## What did not change - Frozen host tool names and signatures (no `workspace_id` args). - Analysis language, exec, search, operator TOML, analysis `session_id`. - Clerk `AuthSettings`, token verifier, well-known proxy. - Connector public SDK types. ## Tests `uv run ruff check quail tests`, `uv run mypy quail`, and `uv run pytest -q` are green (327 passed). Handshake POSTs return `-32022`; GET `/mcp` is 405; headerless allowed POSTs are stamped `2026-07-28`; `Client(mode="legacy")` cannot connect; `mode="auto"` and `mode="2026-07-28"` still list tools. Empty Clerk POST stays 401.

author: hesnottheguy
body:
So work can continue in Grok Build — or any other agent — without the context living only in one Claude session.

`grok inspect` picks it up automatically:

```
Project Instructions (1)
└ ...\gronk\AGENTS.md (project, ~1059 tokens)
```

`AGENTS.md` is the filename the CLI actually looks for (50 references in the binary; `CLAUDE.md` is its fallback).

## What it carries

Only what is specific to this repo and costly to learn by discovery:

- **the shape of a change** — one idea per PR, tests that fail without the fix, mutation-check by breaking the fix on purpose, never push to `main`, never push a tag
- **verify against the live CLI** — including the two traps that have already cost real time here: `--reasoning-effort` works in exactly one argv position and is silently ignored in another, and the CLI does not validate that flag's value at all
- **`GRONK_LIVE_CLI=1 npm test` costs nothing** and is the canary after any CLI update — protocol calls are not prompts, and `session/prompt` is refused inside the helper
- **comments state constraints, never process** — the maintainer's own recent instruction
- **changes that look like cleanup and are not** — the always-emitted permission flag, restart-as-a-mechanism, reading settings for a live session, containment checks
- **the jsdom asymmetries** that make renderer tests fail in confusing ways, with a pointer to working helpers
- **how to talk to the maintainer** — outcome first; they do not read code

Security rules are pointed at, not duplicated: `CLAUDE.md` at the workspace root stays the single source for those.

author: sollama58
body:
## Summary
Integrates the TrenchScanner dashboard into the site as a new top-nav tab, **Trenches**, served at `/trenches/`. Source is `apps/web` from sollama58/TrenchScanner@`b03d6ae` (since deleted from that repo's main), moved in wholesale as a self-contained `trenches/` package and built into the published tree at `frontend/trenches/`.

## ⚠️ Requires a Render Dashboard change to deploy correctly
`frontend/trenches/` is generated at build time and git-ignored. **Until the static site's settings are updated, `/trenches/` will 404 while the new nav link is live on every page.** Change together with this merge:

| Setting | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| Root Directory | `frontend` | *(blank — repo root)* |
| Build Command | *(blank)* | `npm ci && npm run build` |
| Publish Directory | `.` | `frontend` |

Existing URLs are unaffected — Publish `frontend` from the repo root resolves to the identical file set the old config published. Verified all six pages plus `_headers`/`_redirects` land at the same paths.

## Changes

**Build** — Vite `base: '/trenches/'`, `outDir: ../frontend/trenches`. `envDir` repointed from the old monorepo root (`../..`), which would have resolved outside this repo. `node_modules` stays in `trenches/`, never under the published root. Root `package.json` + `package-lock.json` so `npm ci` works at the repo root.

**Wallet bridge** (`trenches/src/bridge/`) — The site uses per-request signatures; TrenchScanner uses SIWS for a session cookie. Rather than a second Connect Wallet button, `/trenches/` renders the real site header (same markup, same `js/wallet.js`) and the app adopts whatever wallet that button connected: read the stored connection → match against wallets registered in this browser → `select()` → `autoConnect` reconnects silently → SIWS runs automatically. One connect button, one extra signature.

**Styling** — App stylesheet scoped under `.trenches-app` at build time, since this page now loads the site stylesheet too and the app's bare `*` / `html, body` / `button, input, select` rules would restyle the shared header. Palette variables repointed at the site's design tokens (original values kept as fallbacks); gain/loss split out from the brand accent.

**Also** — CSP `connect-src` for the API and RPC host; SPA rewrite in `_redirects`; immutable caching for the content-hashed bundle; nav link on all six pages that have a nav.

## Bugs found and fixed along the way

- **The wallet connection is in `sessionStorage`, not `localStorage`.** `wallet.js` moved it for privacy and now actively deletes the legacy localStorage copies — reading localStorage would have missed ~100% of the time and the bridge would have silently never fired.
- **Service worker was caching per-user authenticated API responses.** The TrenchScanner API's endpoints (`/auth/me`, `/filters`, `/matches`) don't carry the `/api/` prefix the existing pattern matches and are cross-origin, so they fell through to the catch-all network-first branch and were written to `DYNAMIC_CACHE` — persisted to disk and served stale after sign-out. Added a `NEVER_CACHE_HOSTS` bypass.
- **`.gitignore` would have broken the build two ways:** `.env.production` was ignored (so `VITE_API_URL` would be `undefined` in Render's bundle — a silent runtime failure), and `frontend/trenches/` needed ignoring as generated output.
- **`npm ci` at the repo root had no lockfile** — the deploy would have failed on its first command.
- **The app's inner navbar collided with the site header** — both `position: sticky; top: 0`, and the header wins at `z-index: 1200`, so the app bar slid underneath and vanished. Un-stickied.
- **Bridge hung on "Checking your wallet…" forever** in a browser with no wallet extension, because Wallet Standard registration never fires. Bounded the wait.

## Testing
- Exact Render build command (`npm ci && npm run build`) run end-to-end from a clean tree.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean (part of the build).
- Browser-verified: exactly one Connect Wallet button and zero wallet-adapter modal buttons on `/trenches/`; header computed styles identical between `/` and `/trenches/` (confirming no style leakage); correct nav active-state; both bridge states (no site wallet / wallet unavailable) render their intended messaging.
- No test suite exists in this repository to run.

## Backend-side, cannot verify from this repo
Neither is a change here, but both break sign-in silently if wrong:
1. **CORS + cookie** — the client sends `credentials: 'include'` cross-origin, so the API must send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://holdex.live` exactly (not `*`, invalid with credentials), `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, and a `SameSite=None; Secure` session cookie.
2. **SIWS domain binding** — the wallet validates `signInInput.domain` against the page origin before signing. If the backend still issues its old domain, every Phantom/Solflare sign-in is rejected by the wallet. It must issue `holdex.live`.

Worth smoke-testing sign-in with a real wallet before announcing the tab.

author: dr14-make
body:
## Summary

The write-path reconcile diffs the webview's reported layout against a fresh base read from OMC (`diffLayouts(current, next)`), and reads anything `current` holds that `next` lacks as a user deletion (or, for the graphics layer, as a positional overwrite). But the webview refuses a `layout` push from the host while a gesture is in flight or a commit is still debounced — deliberately, since applying one there would move what's under the pointer or undo the gesture that just committed. That refusal leaves the webview's next report computed against a base that's behind canonical, and the reconcile reads whatever it doesn't know about yet as something the user deleted (or, for graphics, silently overwrites/duplicates it).

Two concrete ways this fires, per the issue:
1. Paste (or a library placement) settles into OMC, and the push carrying it is refused because a gesture is already in flight (e.g. a drag started within ~300ms). The gesture's own commit then reports a layout without the pasted component, and the reconcile deletes it.
2. An external text edit adds a component; the resulting `reverseSync` push is refused because the user is mid-drag; the drag's commit reports a layout without it.

## Fix

Implements the smaller of the two options the issue lays out: carry a stale-base signal.

- `CommitSlot` (`packages/extension/src/webview/commit-slot.ts`) tracks whether a `layout` push was refused since the last one it actually applied via a single `takePush(gestureActive)` method that both answers "may this push land?" and records the verdict, and rides that bit alongside the layout when it flushes a commit.
- The `change` gesture (`packages/extension/src/webview/gestures.ts`) gained a `staleBase: boolean` field, validated at the boundary like every other gesture field.
- `DiagramEditController.applyChange` (`packages/extension/src/diagram/diagram-editor-provider.ts`) takes the report's `staleBase` bit through `pendingChange`, passes it to `applyDiagramEdits`, and forces a settle (pushes the canonical layout) whenever the report was stale — regardless of the usual "nothing left to tell the webview" shortcut — so the webview is resynced onto whatever it never saw.
- `applyDiagramEdits` (`packages/extension/src/diagram/open-diagram.ts`) gained a `staleBase` option that filters the diff against an exhaustive `TRUSTED_ON_STALE_BASE` classification (`packages/extension/src/diagram/diff-layout.ts`, `satisfies Record<LayoutEdit["kind"], boolean>`) of every `LayoutEdit` kind `diffLayouts` can produce. Untrusted on a stale base: `componentDeleted`/`connectionDeleted` (inferred from absence), `connectionRenamed` (the same absence hazard via its 1:1 re-index grouping), and every `graphics*` kind (keyed by array index — a shape the report never learned about shifts every later index into an in-place overwrite, not a clean delete). Trusted: `componentPlacement`/`connectionAdded`/`connectionWaypoints`, which carry their own absolute value from a diff against the freshly-refetched true OMC state.

## Scope note

Per the issue, this covers paths 1 and 2 (a refused/discarded push racing a gesture's own commit or a reverse sync), not path 3 (the icon and diagram editors open on the same class, with no cross-notification between their separate queues) — the issue's acceptance criteria don't require path 3, and closing it needs the larger "make deletion an explicit intent" redesign the issue documents as a separate, bigger option.

`staleBase` is also one bit for the whole report, not per-entity: while it's set, a genuine edit to something the webview already knew about is dropped alongside the phantom one, and the forced settle reverts it. Telling the two apart needs the webview to report what its local base actually contained, not just that it missed a push — out of scope here; documented as an accepted trade-off in `applyChange`'s docstring. The failure mode is one edit silently not taking effect (self-heals on retry), not data loss.

## Review

Went through four rounds of `/code-review`, `/security-review`, and `/joris-review` (see PR comments for details) — round 3's `/joris-review` caught that the initial fix only filtered `componentDeleted`/`connectionDeleted`/`graphicsDeleted`, missing that `diffGraphics` is positional so a stale report could still silently overwrite or duplicate a shape via `graphicsModified`/`graphicsAdded` rather than a filterable delete. Fixed by moving the classification to the exhaustive `TRUSTED_ON_STALE_BASE` map, with regression tests for the shrink, growth, and `connectionRenamed` cases (each verified to fail against the pre-fix classification).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build`
- [x] `pnpm -r typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm format:check`
- [x] `pnpm -r test:unit` (1147 passed; integration suites skip — no live `omc` on PATH)
- [x] Every new regression test verified to fail against the specific pre-fix behavior it pins, then pass with the fix.

Closes #408

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved diagram synchronization after layout updates are refused or missed.
  * Prevented unintended component, connection, rename, and graphics changes when edits are based on outdated layout data.
  * Ensured genuine deletions and trusted placement or connection updates continue to apply correctly.
* **Protocol**
  * Change messages now include information indicating whether the reported layout is out of date.
* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for stale-layout reconciliation, refused pushes, invalid payloads, and subsequent updates.

body:
Took **E19**, scoped to the windows VST3 cell. **The cell is not measured and the row goes back to TODO** — what stopped it is three defects upstream of REAPER, all measured, all filed here. **No product code changes in any repo**, so nothing here can break a build.

### Why the cell is not measured

E19 recorded its VST3/GMPI cells as blocked on **E27** and **E29**. Both have closed, so the cell looked reachable. It is not: **I could not get a prepared rack to reload in the standalone**, never mind inside a host.

| what | evidence |
|---|---|
| **E48** — reload raises a modal `Connectors lost while loading` and drops document | 49,607 B in → **46,030 B out**, 3,577 bytes of connectors gone. Headless: alive, `Responding=True`, **CPU 0.09 s over 30 s**, no pipe name, no window; the only handle is the Win32 `MainWindowTitle` |
| **E49** — yesterday's 38,658 B saved rack now faults on load | **4/4**, and now diagnosed under `cdb`: `ExceptionAddress: ug_patch_param_setter::ConnectParameter+0x5e`, `Parameter[1]=0x64` — **a read at offset 0x64 from NULL**. Faulting insn `mov ecx,[rbp+64h]` then `call HostControlisPolyphonic` = `HostControlisPolyphonic(parameter->getHostControlId())` with `parameter` null, from an unchecked `GetParameter(moduleHandle, moduleParameterId)` at `SynthEditLib/ug_patch_param_setter.cpp:172`. **On the WASAPI render thread** |
| **E50** — a `VCV: Compare` runs at startup from a default rack containing none | `grep -c Compare` is **0** in `DefaultRack.synthedit` (repo and staged bundle, same 25,257 B), yet it is constructed and `processing (block 96)`. Control: same binary with a session file present builds a **13,464 B** rack and constructs no Compare |

**E50 is the probable common cause of the other two** — the S46 shape, a module resolving to the wrong class once the VCV pack registers — and the row says plainly that this is a hypothesis, untested. **The test is one `TIDE_VCV_FUNDAMENTAL=OFF` build and one number.**

### E49 versus E46 — same shape, different site, and it sharpens both

E46 asks not to be quoted as a measured crash. **This is that measured crash, in E46's shape but not at E46's line**: an assert-only guard on a lookup that can miss, dereferenced under `-DNDEBUG`. E46's own data condition **is** absent — parsing the crashing document for every handle-bearing attribute gives **25 defined, 13 referenced, zero dangling**. The refinement: `GetParameter` takes a `(moduleHandle, parameterId)` **pair** and that test only checked module handles, so **the miss comes from the parameter id on a module that does exist** — narrower and more findable than E46's case.

### The `PROPOSED:` entry

Jeff asked in session whether dialogs should be reported over the command channel, and for it to be filed as a decision rather than a bug. It is in `docs/decisions.md` with **E51** as the parked row. The load-bearing part: report / report-and-answer / never-raise all need the same prerequisite — **one app-owned function every prompt goes through** — and that prerequisite commits to none of them, so it can proceed while the question is open. E43 bounded the same modal mechanism one layer up, but its deadline needs a connection to answer on and **this dialog is raised before the channel opens**.

### Also in here

- **X2** IN-REVIEW → **TODO** (E32 precedent): [#484](https://github.com/JeffMcClintock/TideSynth/pull/484) merged, nothing open, and the row's own words are *"ACCEPT MET FOR TIDE'S OWN CODE; NOT MET TREE-WIDE"*. Remaining work split in the row; its Windows half is takeable and belongs to this box.
- The **`win` NEXT cell re-pointed** — it was dated 2026-08-25 and still described a build break that was fixed two days ago. It now says take E50.
- **Journal rotated** (78 KB → 56,874 B), five entries moved verbatim to `JOURNAL-2026-08.md`.

### One correction made before pushing, left visible

E48's first draft said the loss happened *"on TIDE's OWN modules, with no third-party module involved"*. **That was wrong** — the rogue Compare was in the rack the whole time. It was the most load-bearing sentence in the row and would have sent whoever took it into the wrong repo.

### ID collision, resolved here

I filed the dialog row as **E47** at 11:20; the mac box filed a different **E47** at 11:28 on `tide/mac/E47-properties-dangling-module`. Mine was first and **I renumbered it to E51 anyway** — theirs is already cited from an open SynthEditLib#59 and from its own branch name. A23's check cannot see this: both are legal until they meet on `main`.

### Not done, stated rather than implied

REAPER was never launched this session; **E50 is untested** (one `TIDE_VCV_FUNDAMENTAL=OFF` build settles it); nothing built for macOS or Linux, and none of the three defects checked there.

**One correction inside the run itself, recorded in the journal because it nearly shipped:** I first wrote *"there is no `cdb.exe` on this box"* into E49. `WindowsApps` denies directory **listing**, so my recursive search with `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` swallowed an access-denied and returned empty. cdb is exactly where this project's own notes said it was, and it is what produced the diagnosis above. Same failure the archive already records: *an empty result from a missing input is not evidence.*

Machine left clean: all six repos on their default branches, `%APPDATA%\TIDE Rack\` restored byte-for-byte (verified by md5 — it cannot be redirected by environment, Windows resolves it with `SHGetKnownFolderPath`), no TIDE process running, build tree outside every repo.

author: kalebefukuda
body:
## Summary
Implements the hosting decision and records it. ADR-0002 explains why the design moved off the RFC's EC2-with-SSH plan, and `infra/` is that design expressed as Terraform.

The RFC still describes what this replaces: EC2 `t2.micro` with RDS `db.t3.micro` provisioned by hand, deployed by a step that reads *"conecta via SSH na instância EC2"*. SSH deployment is a direct-failure item of the Web App track, so both the reasoning and the replacement need to exist — the ADR is the reasoning, `infra/` is the replacement.

Nothing is applied. `terraform apply` creates billable resources and stays manual.

## Structure
* `infra/network.tf` — VPC across two AZs, public subnets for the ALB and the tasks, private subnets for the database, and three security groups chained ALB → API → database
* `infra/iam.tf` — the GitHub OIDC provider and the role the pipeline assumes, plus the task execution and task roles
* `infra/storage.tf` — ECR with an expiry policy, and the private image bucket
* `infra/database.tf`, `infra/alb.tf`, `infra/ecs.tf` — the hourly-billed layer, created only when `enable_runtime` is true
* `infra/secrets.tf` — generated database password and JWT secret in Secrets Manager
* `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — a fourth job running `terraform fmt -check`, `init` and `validate`
* `docs/adr/0002-hospedagem.md` — the decision record
* `frontend/.dockerignore`, `backend/.dockerignore` — exclude `.env` and git metadata
* `.github/dependabot.yml` — removed

## Notes
* **`enable_runtime` is what makes the three-phase cost strategy work.** ALB, RDS and the Fargate service are the whole bill; VPC, ECR, S3 and IAM cost close to nothing. Setting the flag to false drops the expensive layer without destroying what is slow to rebuild — a fresh database endpoint, a re-validated certificate, a repository with no images. It defaults to false, so a first apply provisions only the free layer. The cost is `count` on five resources, which makes some references read as `aws_lb.this[0]`.
* **The region is a variable and the decision is still open.** `sa-east-1` was chosen for latency when the credit assumption was US$ 200; at US$ 120, `us-east-1` is roughly 35% cheaper and buys about a month more runway. Keeping it as a variable means that decision costs one line when the Pricing Calculator settles it, instead of a rewrite.
* **The tasks sit in public subnets on purpose.** A private subnet would need a NAT Gateway to reach ECR and Secrets Manager, and NAT alone costs more than ALB, Fargate and RDS combined. Inbound is restricted to the ALB's security group, so the exposure is a public IP with no reachable port. This wants its own ADR.
* **No state backend yet.** Nothing has been applied, so there is no state to protect. State files are gitignored and the backend has to be decided before the first apply — losing state means orphaned resources billing against the credit with nobody watching.
* **`terraform plan` is not in the pipeline**, because it needs AWS credentials. The job runs `fmt` and `validate`, which do not. Plan lands with the OIDC role, once the infrastructure exists.
* **Two SonarCloud findings on `frontend/Dockerfile` are deliberately left open** for triage with a written reason: `--ignore-scripts` (S6505) would break `npm ci`, since `unrs-resolver` ships a real `postinstall`; and the root-user rule (S6471) targets production images, while this one only ever runs under `docker compose` — the frontend deploys to Vercel.
* **Dependabot is removed at the author's request.** It opened thirteen pull requests on its first run. The consequence is that the SHA-pinned actions no longer update on their own, so that becomes manual work.

author: victorquilgars
body:
Closes #130.

## The composer (#130, all four sections)

- **The shape (§4)** — a drawer out of the left panel, on the \`PanelDrawer\` built for it in #145: full panel height, the graph readable beside it, holding at a VS Code panel's width. The old modal is gone; \`PRModal\` is renamed \`PRComposer\`. In the extension's webview shell a zero-width measuring post gives the drawer its emergence edge in every layout mode, stacked included.
- **Generated together (§1)** — \`ai:generate-pr-description\` reads the branch: every commit subject (capped at 50), the diffstat always, and as much of the three-dot diff as a 12k budget allows — **the prompt says when the diff was cut** rather than letting the model describe half a branch with full confidence. One call returns title and body so they cannot disagree; it fills the fields and never submits. The base resolves remote-first, the head local-first. Ported to the extension host, which assembles the same material from its own git service.
- **Both ends (§2)** — source repository and branch into target repository and branch, prefilled by \`prIntentFor\`, which stays the sole judge of whether a row offers a request; the composer overrides from there. The selectors offer what the repository is **connected to** — its git remotes (same host) plus the fork parent from a new \`github:repo-parent\` lookup — not everything the account can see. A cross-repository head spells itself \`owner:branch\`; re-choosing the head re-asks \`branchNeedsPush\` (extracted from the same module the intent uses).
- **Draft (§3)** — *Submit as draft* rides the same create call on both products.
- **Staffing** — reviewers, assignees and labels behind a *More options* fold (the count keeps the fold honest), each picker filtering as you type, and **a missing label can be created from the picker itself** — an explicit POST in the target repository with a colour derived deterministically from the name. Applied right after creation (\`requested_reviewers\` POST + issues PATCH); a refusal there is reported, never mistaken for a failure to create.
- **Entry points** — a \`+\` on the PULL REQUESTS header opens the composer for the checked-out branch (absent on the default branch, rule 2); GITHUB ISSUES' \`+\` opens the host's own new-issue form. The provider tabs are **not** built: #94 has not decided any provider beyond GitHub.

## Fixed on the way

- Every press on the header's ⟳/+ landed on the invisible count chip (opacity 0 still catches clicks, #144's cross-fade) and folded the section instead of acting — the chip is \`pointer-events: none\` now, verified in the running app.
- The header's \`+\` stands on a filled accent square: hue could not separate it — Dracula's accent seed is grey, faithfully — but a fill does, in any theme, and the accent/on-fill pair is one the theme validator holds at 4.5:1.
- The composer belongs to the repository it opened on: a drawer open when a tab closed no longer greets the next open of that repo.
- New host-side methods (\`aiPrDescription\`, \`githubRepoParent\`, \`githubRequestReviewers\`, \`githubCreateLabel\`) keep \`KNOWN_GAPS\` empty; host parity green.

Desktop: 968 tests. Extension: compile + 121 nodisplay tests. Typecheck at zero. Drawer, + buttons and click routing verified in the launched app via CDP.

author: selfcontained
body:
## Problem

On the Changes tab with **Hide test files** on, the file list hid test files but the header's `+/−` badge kept showing unfiltered totals — the badge came from the server's `/diff-stats` endpoint, which knows nothing about the tab's display settings. Some non-test JSON files were also being hidden by the filter.

## What changed

**One selector feeds both.** New `hooks/use-visible-diff.ts` is the single place that decides which files a diff shows and in what order. The Changes tab renders its output; the header badge sums that same array via `diffFileTotals`. While the tab is visible the badge *is* the totals of the list below it — unconditionally, with no per-setting special cases to drift.

That also closes a second divergence nobody had noticed: `/diff-stats` computes without `-w` while `/diff` honours it, so a whitespace-only file counted on the server but never appeared in the list. A branch that only reindents a file showed `+3 −3, 1 file` over an empty list.

With the tab closed there is no list to agree with, and a cached diff only goes stale while `/diff-stats` keeps polling — a frozen badge is worse than an unfiltered one — so the live server totals are used as-is. No extra requests: the badge reuses the query the visible tab already drives, and truncated diffs (server caps at 1000 files) fall back to server totals.

**Tighter test detection.** `isTestFile`'s filename conventions (`foo.test.x`, `test_foo.x`, `FooSpec.x`) now only apply to extensions a test can be written in. They previously matched *any* extension, so `config/test_defaults.json`, `openapi-spec.json`, `tsconfig.test.json` and this repo's own `docs/03-api-spec.md` were all classified as tests and hidden. Directory rules are unchanged, so fixtures that genuinely live under `test/` or `__tests__/` still get hidden. Hspec, Gherkin, Julia, Zig and Nim conventions added while in there.

## Verification

- `pnpm run check`, `pnpm run finalize:web`, 1249 apps/web unit tests, 181 Playwright E2E — all pass.
- Confirmed live in a browser against a scratch repo with a mixed diff: toggling the setting moves the badge `+113 −1 / 4 files` → `+73 −1 / 3 files`, the `.json` and `.md` files correctly stay visible, and switching to the Terminal tab hands the badge back to live server totals rather than freezing.
- Reviewed by the `backend-security-review` persona (review 855); all three findings fixed and verified.

author: zhangfand
body:
## What this PR does

`/api/persons` had two decode sites: the People page, and the chat composer's mention list behind `usePersons`. The second one is what kept the legacy route from retiring — the People page can move off it on its own, but only if nothing else is still reading it. Each site also carried its own local `Person` type over the same payload, so the two could drift while both still typechecked.

The composer now reads the curated people listing, `GET /api/people`, and types against the contract's `PersonResource` rather than a local view of it. The People page's own reads and writes still speak `/api/persons`; that is the only thing keeping the route alive now.

## Design & Invariants

The listing is the people contract's (`@rome/api-types/people`): `GET /api/people` answers `{ people, counts }`, the stranger sentinel never appears in it, and `bondLevel` is the stored value including levels off today's ladder. The composer holds no rule about any of that — it filters the guardian out, because speaking *as* the guardian is what it already does by default, and renders the rest.

- `usePeople` replaces `usePersons`: same one-cache-many-subscribers shape, unwrapping the listing envelope into its rows. A failed read still answers an empty listing rather than an error — the mention list is an optional affordance, and a person list nobody could fetch is a menu with nothing in it, not a chatbox that will not mount.
- `useInvalidatePeople` keeps the People page's create/link/mark-stranger writes refreshing the composer's cache, as `useInvalidatePersons` did.
- `chat-types`' `Person` and `chat-api`'s unused `listPersons` are gone. Both existed only to decode `/api/persons` a second way; `PersonResource` is the one type now, and `ImpersonationMenu` takes it.
- The mock backend serves `/api/people` from the same fixture store, projected by `buildPeople` off `buildIdentities` rather than derived from the store a second time — the two surfaces list the same people, so a second derivation is two answers to who is on the list.

`refactor` rather than `feat`: the endpoint the composer reads changes, the list it renders does not.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter rome-web test` — 147 files, 1099 tests pass.
- [x] `packages/web/src/components/chat/ChatComposer.test.tsx` — new `composer mention list` cases, written failing first: the list renders from `GET /api/people`, excludes the guardian, offers nobody when the listing holds only the guardian, and issues no `/api/persons` request.
- [x] `packages/web/src/hooks/use-people.test.tsx` — the hook requests `/api/people`, unwraps the envelope whole, and answers `[]` on a failed read.
- [x] `packages/web/src/components/chat/chat-people-endpoint.test.ts` — a source guard over the composer's modules, its hooks and `chat-api`, pinning the absence of `/api/persons` so the one call site cannot come back.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/web` (covers `mock/` too), and `biome check` over every touched area.
- [ ] Not exercised in a browser: the change is one endpoint swap behind an existing menu, and the mock backend serves the new route for `pnpm start:web:mock`.

## Not in this PR

- The People page's move off `/api/persons` — out of scope per the issue, and the route stays until it lands.
- Retiring `/api/persons` itself, which that move unblocks.

Closes rome-os/rome#68

author: plribeiro3000
body:
The daily re-check job filtered which pull requests it would evaluate, using its own copy of a condition the verification script already applies. The script's copy covers lockfile changes as well; the job's copy does not, so the two have disagreed since that coverage was added.

The disagreement matters because the two copies do different things when they skip. The script posts a green status and exits, so branch protection stays satisfied. The job skipped silently, posting nothing. A pull request that changes no dependency file therefore reached the job, was filtered out before the script could speak for it, and was left with no status on its head commit — while that status is required for merge here. Nothing else posts it once the pull-request event has passed, so the daily job that exists to heal a missing status was structurally unable to heal this one.

The filter is removed rather than taught to post a status of its own. Every open pull request now reaches the script, which decides for itself whether there is anything to age and posts the status either way. That leaves one copy of the condition and one place the status comes from, so the two cannot drift apart again.

The verification script itself is unchanged.

## What changed

- promotes `robot_spec_uri` to a first-class optional input of the canonical compositional 14-stage Sim2Real workflow
- resolves and content-addresses RobotSpec plus URDF dependencies in Stage 2, then publishes a complete immutable Isaac USD asset-tree manifest
- carries the same embodiment digest and 8-action/36-observation contract through rollout, PPO, validation-selected checkpoint loading, untouched gold evaluation, and final visualization
- preserves the stock Franka path when `robot_spec_uri` is unset and fails closed on missing assets, digest/dimension mismatches, or silent fallback
- packages the workflow runtime and its prerequisites into all five public workflow images, with guardrails and documentation
- makes scenario reset assignment exhaust the curated set before cycling, so partial vector resets cannot under-report real coverage

## Why

BYO robot specifications were previously not a clean end-to-end workflow input. In particular, a declared resolved USD could be lost during Isaac Kit shutdown, relative USD dependencies were not published as one immutable tree, and downstream stages needed stronger proof that they were using the same embodiment and checkpoint dimensions.

## User and developer impact

Operators can provide an immutable S3 RobotSpec URI to the ordinary `npa workbench workflow ... --runtime --resume` path. Existing users who omit it retain stock Franka behavior. The new records expose actionable source, asset-tree, embodiment, image, split, checkpoint, and visualization evidence for debugging and audit.

## Validation

- full repository suite: 11,934 passed, 36 skipped, 12 deselected, 1 xpassed
- focused Sim2Real/Isaac selection: 675 passed
- final focused change selection: 101 passed
- Ruff, docs-drift, diff checks, gitleaks across the branch commits, and infrastructure-confidentiality scan passed
- trusted publication produced five distinct immutable images for exact source SHA `2c5588e4a117b9ba6b49674dd36a94d7198710fc`; every publication job and anonymous-pull verification passed

## Sanitized live proof

A fresh standard-runtime run used only the canonical `npa/workflows/workbench/npa-workflows/sim2real.yaml` with durable resume and exact-SHA image digests. Private operator evidence is retained out of tree.

- 14/14 canonical ComponentRecord pointers verified, including each canonical content digest and immutable history record
- 2,038 non-empty durable objects; exact source/image attestations matched every non-seam stage
- Stage 2 source URDF digest verified; all seven resolved-USD tree members independently downloaded and digest/size checked
- rollout, all three PPO passes, and gold evaluation used the same embodiment digest with action dimension 8 and observation dimension 36
- sealed split was disjoint: 18 train / 3 validation / 3 untouched gold, with no configuration-digest leakage
- scenario application was 18/18 in each of three real PPO passes
- gold evaluation independently loaded the exact selected learned-actor checkpoint; no stock/scripted fallback
- final RRD independently verified and decoded; final MCAP independently decoded as 281 messages across 34 channels and 5 schemas

## Cleanup

All run-owned managed jobs were terminal before cleanup. Proof-only seed/warm Jobs, the seed ConfigMap, and proof-specific RBAC were removed and their absence verified. Shared clusters, reserved capacity, storage, cache PVCs, controllers, and unrelated resources were not modified.

## Genuine limitations

- This proves the RobotSpec path and full standard-runtime orchestration, not policy quality. After three real 500-iteration PPO passes, the measured untouched-gold strict stable-placement rate was 0.0 against the unchanged 0.50 gate. No threshold, 5 cm distance, stability requirement, or checkpoint semantics were weakened; the below-gate result is preserved honestly.
- Stage 12 remains the documented external physical-validation seam.

author: clubanderson
body:
Three guide-agent docs findings, verified against `v4` before filing this PR.

## #4841 — stale "v2" labels on current docs

`README.md` linked `src/docs/README.md` as the **"v2 docs index"** in two places. That file opens by stating the `v2` branch was retired in August 2026 — it *is* the current index. The label told readers the current documentation was deprecated.

**The same bug appears twice more in `src/README.md`, which the issue did not cite:**

| File | Line | Was |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | 491 | `[v2 docs index]` |
| `README.md` | 519 | `[v2 docs index]` |
| `src/README.md` | 291 | `[v2 docs index]` |
| `src/README.md` | 350 | Troubleshooting — "**v2 container logs**, config validation…" |

All four corrected. A repo-wide sweep confirms no stale label remains (migration guides, which legitimately reference v2, are untouched).

## #4843 — legacy troubleshooting still full-text searchable

`docs/troubleshooting.md` carried 171 lines of v1 supervisor/tmux/systemd content (`AGENT_READY_MARKER`, `/etc/hive/agent.env`, `systemctl restart hive`) behind a redirect header. The header does not help anyone arriving from GitHub search — they land mid-document on `systemctl` steps that no longer exist.

Reduced to a redirect stub. The content stays recoverable from git history, and the stub says how.

**The issue's alternative — deleting the file — would have broken a live link.** `src/docs/agent-configuration.md:516` pointed at the legacy path and described it as current ("stuck sessions, login expiry, restart loops"). That link now targets `src/docs/troubleshooting.md`. Verified no other inbound reference to the legacy path remains.

## #4844 — env-var reference upkeep (scope corrected)

The issue asks for guidance on which files to grep. **`env-vars.md` already ends with a `## Verification commands` section carrying exactly those searches** (`os.(Getenv|LookupEnv)` across `src`, plus manifest and script sweeps), so that part of the premise does not hold.

The real gap is contributor-facing: nothing told a PR author the file was their responsibility, or what belongs in each column. Added a `## Keeping this reference current` section covering:

- the same-PR expectation for any added/renamed/removed lookup
- what triggers an entry (new `os.Getenv`/`os.LookupEnv` in `src/`, a `src/deploy/` manifest reference, a `bin/` script reference, or a change to a default or required-ness)
- per-column guidance — notably that `Default` should describe the *order* when the fallback is a lookup chain, since precedence is what operators get wrong

It references the existing searches rather than duplicating them.

## Scope

Docs only. No Go, no manifests, no behavior change.

Fixes #4841
Fixes #4843
Fixes #4844

author: kilbot
body:
Ports wcpos/monorepo#1596 (the fix for wcpos/monorepo#1595) to the electron build, which carries its own `rxdb-premium@17.4.0` and therefore its own copy of every dist patch — the #336/#337/#338 dance, same as the resurrection-leak patcher.

## Why electron needs it

rxdb-premium's abstract-filesystem `TaskQueue` — which the electron main process's filesystem-node storage runs every read/write through — ends each run with `cleanupAfterRun(runState)`, but a **throwing write** unwinds past it (no `finally`) and leaves `this.queue` permanently rejected. One failed write means: leaked access handles, every later task on that collection hanging silently (the promise never settles), and the same error re-logged forever. wcpos/monorepo#1595 has the full mechanism; on the web it presented as the demo store's dead coupons screen.

## What this adds

- `scripts/patch-rxdb-premium-task-queue-containment.mjs` — **verbatim copy** of the monorepo patcher (keep them identical; diff against the monorepo copy when bumping either). Self-healing `queue` accessor (one failure reported once, naming database/collection; the chain stays usable) + `try/finally` around the write run so handles are always released. Validate-all-then-write, idempotent, and it fails the install if an anchor stops matching on an rxdb-premium bump.
- `scripts/rxdb-premium-task-queue-containment.test.mjs` — verbatim copy of the containment test; drives the **real installed** TaskQueue, not a stand-in.
- `package.json` — patcher chained into `postinstall`, `package`, `make`, `publish-app` (so releases cannot silently ship unpatched), and `test:containment-patch` added to the `test` chain.

## Validation

- Red/green proven against this exact package version (`rxdb-premium@17.4.0`, same pin as this repo) in the monorepo: the containment test reports `hung` for every post-failure task on an unpatched dist and passes after the patcher runs.
- Not run locally in this checkout (no license-materialized dist without an install); this repo's CI applies the patcher at postinstall and runs `test:containment-patch` in the `pnpm test` chain — that is the gate for this PR.

author: laermannjan
body:
A complete rewrite against the five specification documents. Plain ES modules, no build step, no runtime dependencies, no framework.

## What is here

- **`app/card.js`, `app/amount.js`** — `.lekka` text to a card and back. Round-trip tested against the sample cards.
- **`app/grid.js`** — a card to a table: rows, spans, right-aligned columns, free rectangles. The four invariants from `LAYOUT.md` are property-tested against 200 random trees.
- **`app/render.js`, `app/style.css`** — the grid as DOM, per `STYLE.md`, including print.
- **`app/source.js`** — the source panel's editing: tab indents, enter keeps indentation, and *wrap in step* takes the subtree under the cursor and hangs it under a new step.
- **`server/store.js`** — a directory is the database. Two shelves, cards and collections, one implementation.
- **`server/http.js`, `server/main.js`** — routes, rights, limits and headers, tested against a real socket.
- **`app/sw.js`** — network-first service worker, versioned by a hash of the app directory computed as it is served.
- **Dockerfile, compose, CI** — multi-arch image published to ghcr.io.

## Format changes

- A preparation may hang under the step it precedes, so the card keeps *when* to preheat the oven. Previously all preparations were a band at the top.
- Every line must carry text; empty steps and ingredients are a parse error.
- One-word step names where the craft has one: `Stockgare`, `Stückgare`, `reifen`, `auskühlen`.
- No fraction glyphs, hyphens only for ranges.

## Rights

Collections are new and are not in the original documents. A collection is a list of card links and nothing else; cards do not belong to it, so the only permission question anywhere is whether you hold the key for the thing you are touching. Documented in `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## Known gaps

- No browser tests. Rights are enforced and tested server-side, and the app builds no control it does not mean - no key, no *Edit source*; no key on a row, no *Delete* - so absence, not hiding, carries the decision. `ARCHITECTURE.md` says why, and what would make end-to-end tests worth their weight: a UI with more in it than one hidden line.
- In-place editing of cells in the grid is not built; the source panel is the only editor.
- Threat model is a trusted network. Not hardened for the open internet, and `ARCHITECTURE.md` says what would have to happen first.

author: asantarelli
body:
The ask was one line long: *sales as columns, the trend as a line over them*. The class already drew lines and already held eight series — what it could not do was let **one** series pick its own shape. Everything else in this branch is something that got in the way of using it on real data.

## The combo

`SeriesPlot[s]`, set through `SetSeriesPlot(series, Plot:Line)` or `AddSeries`' third parameter, or the **Draw as** prompt on the Series tab of both extensions.

![bars and a line on one chart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asantarelli/templatemaker/graficabarra-combo/docs/graficaBarra-combo.png)

It is **not a fourteenth chart type**. It is the chart type plus a per-series override, so every scale, grid, label and legend decision stays where it was. Four small questions carry it — `PlotOf`, `IsCombo`, `BarSeriesCount`, `BarSeriesIndex` — and everything the feature touches is gated on `IsCombo`, so a chart that never calls it takes the path it always took.

The line series **takes no room in the category slot**: `PaintBars` divides by the bar-series count rather than the series count, so one bar series beside one line draws full-width bars instead of squeezing them into half a slot for a series that is not drawn there. Bars paint before lines, because a trend line under its own columns is a line nobody can see. The legend keys a line series with a stroke and its marker instead of a block.

`Chart:Column`, `Chart:Line` and `Chart:Scatter` only — a stack has nothing to overlay, a horizontal bar chart has no vertical line painter, and a pie is not a cartesian chart at all.

## The four that got in the way

**The Look tab had thirty prompts in five groups** and had stopped fitting on screen. Split the way BrowseGrid's seven tabs were, by what things share: *Look* keeps what is shown and its legend, *Shapes* takes the bars, lines, markers and the pie family, *Text & colors* the rest. Eleven, ten and thirteen. No prompt moved between groups and no symbol was renamed, so stored prompt values are untouched.

**The axis wasted half the plot.** `NiceMax` rounded the *top* up to the next 1/2/5 magnitude, which is fine until the data sits just above one: real sales with a maximum of 113,376,143 were drawn against an axis of 200,000,000 — every bar at half height. The step comes first now. `NiceStep` sizes the gap *between* two gridlines and each end is the first whole multiple past the data: the same figures get 0…125,000,000. It folds the mixed-sign case in as well, since both ends being multiples of one step puts zero on a gridline by construction. `GridDivs` becomes a **ceiling** rather than an exact count, because every line has to land on a whole step.

**A line could not stop short of a bar.** A row of periods with an *average* bar on the end wants the bar drawn and the trend not run out to it, and the only way to say "nothing here" was a zero — which is a value, so the line dived to the floor and drew the dive. `SetNoValue(series, category)` is the missing idea: no bar, no marker, and the line **breaks** rather than diving. A gap in the middle splits the line into two runs, and the smooth path was restructured so each Catmull-Rom segment primes its own left end and skipping one is free.

**A chart could not set its own type.** `SETFONT` on the drawing target is the *window's* font — measured: setting `PROP:FontName` on the IMAGE is ignored, setting it on the window is what the class reads back — so every chart wore whatever the rest of its window wore. `FontName` / `FontSize` / `FontStyle` now belong to the chart; `Paint` puts them on, draws, and hands the target's own back, widening the save-and-restore it already did for the text colour. `FontSize` **also scales `TextW`/`TextH`** while they are 0, so one property does the whole job and the label thinning starts working on its own.

Two things had to be established before that was safe: twenty save-apply-restore cycles raise **no `EVENT:Sized`** and move no control by a pixel, so a chart cannot walk its window into a redraw loop; and `GETPOSITION` has to be read **after** the swap, because a dialog unit is a fraction of the window's character cell — a control measured at 9 point and drawn at 14 overflowed its own bounds.

## Verified

- The class compiles under Clarion 11 and the combo draws: bars plus line, two bar series plus line, negatives across the zero baseline, a `Chart:Line` with one series forced back to bars, an average bar with the trend stopping short of it, and a gap punched into the middle of a row.
- **All thirteen types re-shot** against the current class and compared panel by panel. Thirteen of the eighteen panels are unchanged; five got a tighter, rounder axis, and `docs/graficaBarra-types1..3.png` are re-taken to match.
- The scale checked on six cases by hand, including the 113 million above and a maximum of 0.47.
- The template **registers clean** with `ClarionCL /tr` as v2.1 after every change.
- The class guide's `clw:` line references were remapped against the new file at each step rather than left to rot — and a bug in my own first remap (multi-number references with a space after the comma) was caught and fixed.

`examples/graficaBarra/ComboChart.clw` is a new runnable demo: the combo three ways.

body:
## Summary
- User-directed feature: replaces the `revival_score`/`REVIVAL_THRESHOLD`/"at most one suggestion per run" engine entirely.
- Every committed, non-dormant idea now gets a real, tagged `[idea] {title}` Calendar event written at its own `next_fit_start`, and gets texted at the exact instant that slot arrives ("yo u have 4h free right now — wanna bang out X?").
- **Y** promotes the same Calendar event in place (tag/description stripped). **N** (first dismissal) reschedules immediately, moving the placeholder to the next fitting slot. **N** (second dismissal) and **Later** both clear the placeholder (30d/7d dormancy, unchanged).
- New ADR 0009 records the deliberate, narrow departure from ADR 0003 ("never write on inference alone") this requires — the single-Calendar-writer boundary (`committer-svc` only) is preserved; `dispatcher-svc` requests the write via a new synchronous call, the second such cross-service asymmetry in this codebase after `ingest-svc`'s.
- No explicit cross-item reflow/cascade algorithm needed — verified empirically, not just reasoned about: every placeholder is a real Calendar event, so recomputing one item's slot naturally treats every other item's placeholder as busy time. The one real gap was self-exclusion (an item's own placeholder must not block its own recompute).
- All architecture docs updated: `capacity-engine.md` §5 (full replacement model), `state-machine.md` §2/§2.1-2.3, `agent-contracts.md` §4.2/4.4, `overview.md` §2/§3, `data-model.md` DDL, `infrastructure.md` (new IAM + a new §5.1 documenting Cloud Tasks IAM comprehensively, closing a pre-existing gap), `prd.md`.

## Real bugs found and fixed via live verification (not the mocked unit suite)
1. A test with a globally-mocked `committer_client` wrote a fake placeholder id into a real user's live `latents` row, since `/dispatch` iterates every real linked user in the shared dev DB — fixed by making the mock refuse (raise) for any item that isn't the test's own.
2. `sa-dispatcher` enqueueing a Cloud Task targeting **itself** needed `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` granted to itself, not just `run.invoker` — never surfaced before since every other Cloud Tasks caller in this project names a different SA as the target. Found as a real `PermissionDenied` in production logs, fixed live.

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run pytest services/ shared/ -q` — 267 passed, 25 skipped
- [x] `uv run ruff check` — clean
- [x] Real Postgres integration suite (`test_dispatcher_integration.py`) — 8/8 passed
- [x] New migration (`0020_placeholder_and_scheduled_suggestions.sql`) applied to the live DB
- [x] committer-svc and dispatcher-svc redeployed to Cloud Run; new IAM grants applied
- [x] **Full real end-to-end verification against live production Calendar/SMS/DB**: committed an idea → real tagged placeholder appeared on the actual Google Calendar with correct time/duration → fire-time Cloud Task → real SMS with the new wording + a real open `suggestions` row → real "n" reply → dismissal recorded, placeholder **moved in place** on the real calendar (same event id, `sequence` incremented, not duplicated) → real fresh fire → real "y" reply → item flipped to a real `obligation`, the **same Calendar event was PATCHed** (tag/description stripped, real title set, `calendar_event_id` matches the former `placeholder_event_id` exactly) → `next_fit_start`/`placeholder_event_id` correctly cleared

author: lesterbryanilao
body:
Closes TEN-314.

## What was wrong

`ExpenseService.update` resolved both the category and the project tag against the **acting
principal**. When an ADMIN edited another user's expense, the result was a row whose `user`
disagreed with its `category.user` and `project.user`: the owner could never see or rename the tag
(`GET /expenses/projects` and `PUT /expenses/projects/{id}` are caller-scoped), and the admin's own
tag list silently gained a tag created on someone else's behalf.

Found by `pr-reviewer` on #72 (TEN-178) and ruled out of that issue's scope by
`pr-review-auditor`, since the shape predates TEN-178 on the category side.

## The change

- `ExpenseService.update` reads `expense.getUser()` into `owner` and passes it to both
  `categorise` and `resolveProject`. `user_id` is `nullable = false`, so there is no fallback to
  the caller.
- `resolveProject(request, owner)` and `categorise(request, owner)` take the owner explicitly. In
  `categorise`, `resolveByMerchant` and `learnMerchantRule` are owner-scoped too — a rule learned
  against the admin would point at a category that is not theirs.
- `CategoryService.getOrCreateByName(name, owner)` renames its parameter so the next caller does
  not hand in its own principal by reflex. Behaviour unchanged; every other caller already passed
  the owner.
- `ExpenseService.create` still files against the caller, which is correct — a create always
  belongs to whoever made it.

## Was this executed at runtime? What was run, and what was observed?

Yes. Stack up via `python3 scripts/verify_local.py --up` (Postgres :5433, backend :8080 built from
this branch at `a833337`). A USER was registered and given an expense, a separate test ADMIN was
provisioned, and the admin issued:

`PUT /expenses/1149` with a brand-new category name and a brand-new project name → **HTTP 200**,
body carrying `"projectId": 2`.

Ownership read straight from Postgres:

```
  id  | expense_owner | category_id | category_owner | project_id | project_owner
------+---------------+-------------+----------------+------------+---------------
 1149 |            21 |         300 |             21 |          2 |            21
```

Owner is user 21; the acting admin was user 22. Both new rows carry the **owner's** id. The
admin's own list was unchanged before and after: `GET /expenses/projects` as admin → `[]`, and
`select count(*) from categories where user_id=22 and name like 'TEN314%'` → `0`.

This mattered because the unit tests are `@Mock`-based and hand-build the `Expense` with the owner
already set — they cannot prove the owner is populated on an entity loaded through
`expenseRepository.findById`. The runtime check is what shows that.

## Tests

Two new tests on the admin-edits-another-user's-expense path: one asserting `expense.user` equals
both `expense.project.user` and `expense.category.user`, with `never()` verifications that nothing
was looked up or saved against the admin; one proving the owner's existing tag is reused rather
than duplicated. `update_updatesAndReturnsResponse` gained `.user(user)` on its fixture, matching
what the non-null column guarantees in production.

Full suite: **806 passed, 0 failures.** `contract/openapi.json` regenerated and verified
byte-identical — no controller or DTO shape changed, so no contract version is due. `pom.xml`
0.85.0 → 0.85.1 (PATCH, per the `fix:` type).

author: mblua
body:
Step two of #1563. Completes the OIDC migration.

## OIDC is proven, not assumed

`v0.30.3` published through OIDC Trusted Publishing. The publish log does **not**
say which path it took, so this was verified from the registry metadata, which is
the only place that records it:

| | `_npmUser` | `_npmVersion` |
|---|---|---|
| **0.30.2** | `{"name":"mblua","email":"mariano.blua@gmail.com"}` | `10.9.8` |
| **0.30.3** | `{"name":"GitHub Actions","email":"npm-oidc-no-reply@github.com","trustedPublisher":{"id":"github","oidcConfigId":"oidc:90ca69bd-..."}}` | `11.6.2` |

The `trustedPublisher` object appears only on the OIDC path. 0.30.2 published as
a personal account via token; 0.30.3 published as GitHub Actions via the trusted
publisher.

## The change

With the replacement proven on a real release, remove the fallback:

- Drop the `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` env block. Publishing is OIDC only.
- Drop `--provenance`. Trusted publishing generates the attestation on its own;
  the flag was only ever needed on the token path.

Kept deliberately:

- `id-token: write`, still scoped to this job alone. OIDC does not work without it.
- The `npm@11.6.2` pin. Node 22 ships npm 10.9.8, below the 11.5.1 floor. Without
  the pin npm falls back to token auth silently, which after this PR means no auth

## Summary - Default Rule (and container identities that inherit it) currently reuse one generated fingerprint across every site. That lets unrelated websites correlate visits through identical noise seeds, hardware extras, and version-list headers. - This change adds an experimental **Domain fencing** option: with the flag on, generated fingerprint fields get a deterministic per-eTLD+1 variation, while manually chosen regional presets (time, languages, geo), `Accept-Language`, and `authKey` stay static. - Settings copy keeps the **Domain fencing** title. The description states Default Rule and Firefox container scope without putting Domain Rules next to that title. - Hostname-aware background channels rebuild the full fenced snapshot on both Chromium and Firefox (noise, hardware selection, and version rotation). Shared `"*"` templates keep the **unfenced Default Rule fingerprint** as baseline spoofing so first-inline never falls through to native canvas/WebGL/UA. They are never mutated to a site's fenced identity. Injected page, early, and worker graphs still do not ship the eTLD+1 suffix tables. - Firefox hash transport embeds one already-fenced state. Firefox `window.name` catalogs add a more specific `*` row from the background cache and leave `"*"` as the correlatable baseline, so one host cannot poison the next. After a host resolve, session preload is updated **without** rebuilding prepared decisions (that rebuild would wipe the fence cache). - Chromium session DNR still fences `Sec-CH-UA-Full-Version-List` per site in the background. Injected size ceilings dropped after the suffix tables left those graphs.
