body:
## Summary

Two instructions in `.rhapsody/PROMPT.md` contradicted how this repo actually works, and every
Rhapsody run hit them. Both were surfaced by the STUDIO-572 design run (PR #38, closed unmerged):
it committed a design document into the repo, and its first PR title was rejected by CI.

1. **A produced design/spec/plan document now has an explicit, repo-free home.** The prompt already
   said "never commit specs, plans, or design docs", but it only ever treated them as read-only
   *inputs* — a ticket whose *deliverable* is a document had nowhere to go, so the STUDIO-572 run
   committed its design to `docs/decisions/` and rationalised it via that ticket's "a design document
   in the Rhapsody repo" wording.
2. **The mandated PR title is now the one this repo's own `pr-title` CI accepts.** Phase 4.3 mandated
   `STUDIO-XXX: <imperative summary>` — a leading ticket id, precisely the shape
   `harness/release/check-pr-title.sh` rejects because release-please cannot parse it (the documented
   cause of STUDIO-408, where a release was silently skipped). Every run failed `pr-title` on its
   first attempt and then self-corrected.

Prompt text plus one harness test. No `crates/`, `web/`, or `desktop/` behaviour change; no golden or
fixture touched; no dependency added.

## Changes

**`.rhapsody/PROMPT.md`**

- Ground rules: the "process documents stay out of the repo" bullet now says the rule holds *even when
  the ticket's deliverable is itself a document*, and points at Phase 2.
- New Phase 2 subsection **"When the deliverable IS a design/spec/plan document"**, with three routes
  and no repo option:
  1. Linear write available → publish with `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_document`, parented to the
     ticket's project and linked from the ticket.
  2. Headless fallback (the common case — the Linear MCP is usually absent from a dispatched run, and
     tool denials here are permanent) → do **not** commit it; put the FULL text in the PR body under a
     `## Design document` heading and state under **Notes for reviewers** that a human must file it in
     Linear. Then hand off.
  3. No repo change at all *and* no Linear write → there is no PR to carry it, so the full text goes in
     the handoff message. Explicitly: do **not** manufacture a commit just to create a PR.
  - Closing sentence makes the override explicit: a description or Done-when that says the document
    belongs "in the Rhapsody repo" / "in `docs/`" is a ticket-authoring mistake, not a licence to
    commit it — produce it, route it, and note the discrepancy.
- Phase 4 step 3 rewritten: the title must be a conventional-commit subject `type(scope): <description>`,
  never a leading ticket id. It names `harness/release/check-pr-title.sh` as the source of truth and
  tells the run to execute it on its title *before* creating the PR, lists the twelve accepted types and
  the pre-1.0 bump semantics (copied from the validator, not invented), and puts the ticket id in the
  description as a trailing `(STUDIO-XXX)` plus `Fixes STUDIO-XXX` in the body. Four worked examples
  live between `<!-- pr-title-examples:begin/end -->` markers.

**`harness/release/pr_title_test.sh`** (run by the `pr-title` workflow, which already ran this file
before trusting the validator's verdict)

- Feeds every line between the `pr-title-examples` markers in `.rhapsody/PROMPT.md` through
  `check-pr-title.sh` and fails if any is rejected, if the marked block is empty/missing, or if the
  prompt goes back to a backticked `{{ issue.identifier }}: <...>` title mandate. The prompt and the
  gate that judges the titles it produces can no longer drift apart.

## Verification

`harness/release/pr_title_test.sh` (the `pr-title` job's first step):

```
ok   - accepts 'fix(orchestrator): stop a null attachment field hiding a project (STUDIO-406)'
ok   - accepts 'feat(config): add a capabilities field mirroring labels (STUDIO-412)'
ok   - accepts 'docs: route a produced design document to Linear instead of the repo (STUDIO-593)'
ok   - accepts 'refactor(store)!: drop the legacy history schema (STUDIO-500)'
ok   - all 4 PR-title example(s) in .rhapsody/PROMPT.md are accepted
ok   - .rhapsody/PROMPT.md does not mandate a leading-ticket-id PR title
ok   - missing argument is a usage error (exit 2)
pr_title_test: all passed
```

Mutation-tested (each mutation applied to a copy, then restored) — the new guard is not vacuous:

```
--- mutation 1 (leading ticket id) ---
FAIL - .../.rhapsody/PROMPT.md still mandates a leading-ticket-id PR title, the shape this validator rejects
pr_title_test: FAILED
--- mutation 2 (bad example) ---
FAIL - accepts 'STUDIO-593: route a produced design document to Linear instead of the repo': exit 1, ...
pr_title_test: FAILED
--- mutation 3 (markers gone) ---
FAIL - prompt examples: no titles between the pr-title-examples markers in .../.rhapsody/PROMPT.md
pr_title_test: FAILED
```

This PR's own title, checked before the PR was opened (the chicken-and-egg the ticket calls out):

```
$ harness/release/check-pr-title.sh "docs(prompt): send produced design docs to Linear, not the repo, and fix the mandated PR-title format (STUDIO-593)"
TITLE OK
```

`make lint` (`cargo fmt --all --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`):

```
    Checking rhapsody-mcp v0.1.0 (.../crates/mcp)
    Checking rhapsodyd v0.1.0 (.../crates/rhapsodyd)
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 35.44s
```

`cargo test --workspace` — every suite green, zero failures:

```
test result: ok. 315 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 3.56s
test result: ok. 162 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; ...
test result: ok. 123 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; ...
test result: ok. 108 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; ...
test result: ok.  89 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; ...
test result: ok.  81 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; ...
(… 12 further suites, all `0 failed`)
```

`web/` is untouched, so `npm ci && npm test` was not required by `ci.yml`'s conditions for this diff.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Why the harness test.** The ticket scopes this to `.rhapsody/PROMPT.md` "plus a test if one guards
  the prompt". Nothing guarded the prompt's *content* — the existing `PROMPT.md` references in
  `crates/` are all about path resolution (`.rhapsody/` → `.symphony/` fallback), not text. The new
  cases live in `harness/release/pr_title_test.sh` next to the validator they pin, run inside the
  existing `pr-title` job (no new CI job, no renamed branch-protection context), and make the
  Done-when — "its PR-title instruction matches the `pr-title` CI" — mechanically enforced instead of
  a point-in-time claim. If you would rather this stayed prompt-only, the second commit
  (`test(release): …`) reverts cleanly on its own.
- **Type choice.** `docs(prompt):` / `test(release):` rather than `fix:`. The prompt is markdown read
  from a target repo's checkout at run time, not code compiled into `rhapsodyd`, so nothing shippable
  changed and no version bump is warranted. The validator's own guidance is to pick the honest type
  rather than mislabel for a bump.
- **Follow-up, deliberately not fixed here (adjacent, out of scope).** `.rhapsody/PROMPT.md` still
  contradicts itself about merging: the opening paragraph and Phase 6 both say "**You do NOT merge**",
  while ground-rule 5 says "You DO merge your own PR — but only in Phase 6" and Phase 4.2 says "PR +
  merge must be done manually". Same class of defect as the two this ticket names, and worth its own
  ticket; the ticket scopes this change to the two enumerated fixes, so I left it alone rather than
  widening the diff.
- **Not addressed (explicitly out of scope per the ticket).** Why headless runs cannot write Linear at
  all — the Linear MCP credential does not reach the dispatched subprocess — is a separate infra issue.
  This run itself had no Linear MCP tools available, which is why fallback route 2 above is written as

author: timrecursify
body:
## Problem

Free-lane build agents (`build-laguna-1`, `build-nemotron-1`, `build-minimax-1`) are online but their tasks fail instantly with `exceeded retry limit, 429 Too Many Requests` (provider rate limit on the free OpenRouter models). The dispatcher keeps assigning to them because admission only checks archived / runtime-online — it never looks at whether the lane is currently burning on provider 429s (PPP-21346).

## Fix

Add a **lane rate-limit health gate** to the shared dispatch admission checks. An agent whose recent tasks failed with `agent_error.provider_capacity_or_rate_limit` is paused for new work for a 10-minute cooldown after a burst of ≥2 such failures in a 15-minute window. The pause is self-clearing and conservative — a single transient 429 never pauses a lane, and a paused lane resumes on its own.

Covered paths (all now refuse to enqueue to a paused lane, with reason `lane_rate_limited` / stable phrasing `agent lane rate-limited (429): ... paused until <ts>`):

- `service.AgentReadiness` — autopilot run_only dispatch, squad-leader dispatch, handler squad-leader ready check
- `service.WillEnqueueRun` — issue create / assignee change / backlog→active enqueue (the path that created the failing tasks)
- `service.isAgentAssigneeReadyWithQueries` + `handler.isAgentAssigneeReady` mirrors

No schema change. New sqlc query `GetAgentRecentRateLimitFailures` (existing `(agent_id, status)` index prefix covers it).

## Tests

- `TestLaneRateLimitDecision` — pure decision logic (threshold, cooldown, self-clearing)
- `TestAgentReadinessReasonCode` — rate-limited lane maps to `lane_rate_limited`
- `TestFormatAdmissionReason` — pause window kept verbatim for agent and squad phrasing
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `go test ./internal/service/ ./internal/handler/` all green; `sqlc generate` clean

author: arsh871-bot
body:
Closes the export gap named in our own gaps table, and the one three of the four proposed capabilities depend on.

`analysis/report.py` is a pure function over a findings list -- no web import, no Batfish, no model. `GET /api/report?format=html|csv` serves it as a download.

## F-4, on a medium where it matters more than on screen

A report is read later, by someone who cannot ask a question, often by someone deciding whether the work is finished. So **"could not check" is the first section**, rendered even when empty, counted in the header, and it says in words that it is not a pass.

## An honest account of the escaping

Every value is escaped. I tried to prove that mattered by putting `<script>` in a real Cisco config and running the real pipeline. **It never reached a finding:**

```
remark text reaches a finding? False
ACL RULE text reaches one?     True
device name reaches one?       True
```

ACL rule text and device names do reach `evidence.detail` -- but Cisco syntax will not parse `<` in either. So **for the Cisco path this is defence in depth, not a hole being closed.** Saying so, because the opposite claim was easy to make and would have been wrong.

**The live path is the feature landing next.** A user-supplied policy is a JSON file somebody uploads, `violation_summary` is one of its free-text keys, and it becomes a finding's `summary` verbatim:

```
access_control.py:313      summary=statement["violation_summary"]
access_control.py:401      summary=guarantee["violation_summary"]
policy_compliance.py:424   summary=rule["violation_summary"]
```

Once #181 lands, an uploaded file's free text reaches this report directly. A test pins that exact case.

## Mutations, on the real files

```
stop escaping (the injection hole)        7 failed
drop the empty could-not-check section    1 failed
put could-not-check LAST                  1 failed
CSV omits the error rows                  2 failed
CSV loses the status column               6 failed
stop ordering problems worst-first        1 failed
serve inline instead of as a download     2 failed
accept any format instead of refusing     1 failed
let dashboard-only keys into the report   621 passed   <- SURVIVES
```

## The survivor, and why I am not pretending otherwise

Stripping `explanation` before rendering changes **no output at all**. Both renderers read NAMED fields, so an extra key cannot reach either format however it arrives. The code now says that rather than leaving a no-op looking like a control.

My first test for it asserted `set(row) == set(CSV_COLUMNS)` -- true whatever the endpoint does, because `csv.writer` emits the columns it is given. Rewritten to assert the observable property instead: the explanation TEXT never appears in either format.

## Why HTML and CSV, not PDF

HTML is self-contained, opens anywhere, prints to PDF from any browser, and needs no new dependency. Adding `reportlab` to a security tool to produce a file a browser already makes would be a poor trade. CSV is the other half -- a human report and a machine-readable one answer different questions.

```
Batfish UP    621 passed, 6 skipped
Batfish DOWN  617 passed, 10 skipped
ruff clean
```

body:
## Summary

Zero tests existed anywhere in this repo before this PR (`go test ./...` reported "no test files" in every package). Adds both harnesses discussed, wired into `task validate` (and thus CI's Validate job) rather than a new lane - matching the project's own "tests before code, shift left" convention (#28) and "borrow existing tooling" philosophy: no new dependencies, no custom framework, both are the vendor-provided way to test each language.

**Go** - `scripts/ignite/internal/config` gets full coverage via the standard library's own `testing` package (`go.mod` has zero dependencies; none was needed here either). Covers `ResolveSiteNetwork`'s actual security-relevant logic - vendor/vault-provider matching, octet range/uniqueness, the AWS-key-on-a-Cloudflare-site check - and `AssertRenderedConfigComplete`'s op:// resolution checks.

**OpenTofu** - `registry.tf`'s `locals`/`precondition` logic gets its own `.tftest.hcl` suite under `management/cluster/tests/`, run via `tofu test`, scoped to just `terraform_data.invariants` via `plan_options.target` (no real provider credentials or infrastructure needed - the targeted resource is the built-in `terraform.io/builtin/terraform` type).

One small, deliberate production change this required: `config_path` in `variables.tf` is now a `variable` instead of a hardcoded path, defaulting to the exact same path as before. A real ignition run, `task validate`'s placeholder render, and CI never set it, so none of them see any different behavior - only `tofu test` overrides it, to point at small fixture JSON files (`management/cluster/tests/fixtures/`) that have nothing to do with 1Password or `op://` syntax. The real config template and render pipeline are completely untouched.

body:
⚡ **Bolt**: Pre-allocate span slice capacity dynamically in `FindSpans` using `slices.Grow`.

### What changed
In `internal/redact/redact.go`, updated `FindSpans` to call `spans = slices.Grow(spans, len(matches))` whenever a pattern yields matches.

### Why it improves performance
Previously, slice capacity was only pre-allocated for the first matching pattern. As subsequent patterns found matches, `append` calls resulted in multiple dynamic slice growing re-allocations. Using standard library `slices.Grow` ensures slice capacity is expanded efficiently in a single operation per matching pattern without modifying slice length.

body:
Recovered work. PR #40 was merged at 23:04:38, squashed at `0cbfaeb`; everything pushed to that branch afterwards was on a merged branch and reached nothing. Cherry-picked onto a fresh branch off `main`, trees verified identical.

## What's in it

**`CLAUDE.md` gets an outline.** 1,606 lines and no header below `##`. The longest run of prose with nothing to skim by was **175 lines**; it is now 76. Thirty-eight headers, **no text moved and nothing deleted** — deliberately, so there is something to read the file against before deciding what to cull. `## Commands` was the worst of it: 364 lines covering the command table, the binary's leak, the CLI, the MCP server, shell traps, CI, the check sweep and biome, under one word.

**The login-role boundary is measured, not deferred.** Probed against `docker/postgres`, which preloads AGE. A plain LOGIN role that never issues `LOAD`:

| | result |
| --- | --- |
| `agtype` resolves | works |
| Cypher read | works |
| **Cypher write — `createNode`** | works, minted a natural id |
| **Cypher write — `createEdge`** | works, connected two nodes |
| `LOAD 'age'` | refused, 42501 — and never needed |
| `SET ROLE postgres` | **refused, 42501** |

The write half had never been run. That last row is the difference from the step-down we ship, whose session can `RESET ROLE` back to superuser — a safety boundary, not a security one. Recorded with its date in `src/db/scoped.ts`. What is unbuilt is the seam, and it is per-backend: PGlite has no preload and one superuser session.

**`docs/mcp-server/` deleted**, 184 lines. Its status table recorded the agent-facing write contract as not done against 18 shipped write tools, and the suite ceiling as unresolved after it was re-measured to zero. The two ideas worth keeping are now items in `docs/TASKS.md`.

**The queue is restructured.** `/wrap` moves under "Tooling, not product", and the merge-race item is rewritten to say what it is actually about — not the wrap hook, but continuing to push to a branch whose pull request is already merged.

body:
## Resumo

- Adiciona `refinado: true` + `porFoco` ao preset **Estacionar o Ônibus** (Park the Bus) — o último dos 10 estilos de jogo do jogo a receber o tratamento dinâmico, reaproveitando 100% do motor genérico já construído nos 9 rounds anteriores. Nenhuma mudança no motor foi necessária, só dados do preset.
- Diferente de todos os presets anteriores, o próprio pedido define UMA "regra de sobrevivência" de formação e UMA Matriz Dinâmica de Funções que valem igualmente para os 7 Focos — só a predefinição/armação/linha defensiva mudam por Foco:
  1. **Formação** (`estrategiaFormacao: 'defensiva'` para todos os 7 Focos, não só Defensivo/Ext.Defensivo como nos outros presets): prioriza linha de 5 defensores sempre que disponível entre as 4 preferidas do treinador.
  2. **Pacote tático**: "Retranca Total" (trava Linha 0-30) na maioria dos Focos, "Padrão" destravando a linha só no Extremamente Ofensivo (linha 45), tudo validado contra `PREDEFINICOES_TATICAS.regra`.
  3. **Matriz Dinâmica de Funções** ("Regra Absoluta para Qualquer Foco") — GL Tradicional, Zagueiros 100% Defesa, Laterais travados atrás, Volantes viram 3º/4º zagueiro, meio-campo vira marcação pura, Pivô isolado na frente segurando a bola.
  4. **Regra de Afinidade Tática** (-8 pontos): prioriza "Brucutus" (Zagueiro/Lateral Defensivos, Cão de Guarda) sobre perfis ofensivos (Ala Ofensivo, Armador) — empilhada na escolha de quem entra.

## Desvios do pedido (documentados no código, em `ajustes`)

- Armação: o pedido citava "Ligação Direta" em 6 dos 7 Focos, mas isso é uma PREDEFINIÇÃO tática diferente no jogo, não um dos 3 Estilos de Armação reais — substituído por "Contra-ataque" (o Foco Segura o Jogo já usava "Passe Curto", uma armação real, sem precisar de ajuste).

- PD/PE (Ponta): "Ponta Operário" não é uma função do motor tático — é o nome de uma ESPECIALIDADE de jogador (cadastro), não algo que a Matriz possa atribuir. "Meia Aberto" também não existe nesse grupo — usado "Ala"/Equilibrado.
- ATA: "Pivô" não tem foco Apoio nesse grupo — usado Equilibrado, que na descrição do próprio jogo já é "segura a jogada e passa a bola pra colegas", batendo com o pedido.

author: shakilnubee
body:
## Symptômes
- Une **tâche marquée « terminée » disparaît** de l'onglet Terminées.
- Un **rappel coché** (« fait ce mois-ci ») **se décoche plus tard** tout seul.

## Cause racine
La fusion « delta » des réglages (`FP.settings._pushSettings` → `app_settings`) **remplaçait des clés entières**. Quand un 2ᵉ appareil ou une 2ᵉ session (téléphone, PC d'un collègue) enregistrait un réglage en ayant un cache légèrement ancien de `taches` / `rappelsFaits`, il **réécrasait toute la collection** → les coches faites ailleurs étaient perdues.

## Correctif (`assets/js/app.js`)
Pour les **collections de travail** toggées souvent et depuis plusieurs appareils, on fusionne désormais **entrée par entrée** sur la version fraîche du serveur, au lieu de remplacer toute la clé :
- **tableaux** d'objets `{id,…}` (`taches`, `rappelsPerso`) → fusion **par id** (ajouts/modifs/suppressions de ce poste appliqués, le reste préservé) ;
- **maps** (`rappelsFaits`, `vehImmobilise`, `amendeMontantPaye`, `amendeMontants`, `kmMajDates`, `sinistreStage/Statut/Groupes`, `docStatus`, `permisMasque`, `condDocs`, `leasingContrats`, `kmSuiviExclus`) → fusion **par feuille**.

Les autres clés (apparence, config…) gardent le comportement inchangé. Mono-appareil : identique (la coche s'applique et persiste) ; multi-appareils : **plus d'écrasement**.

- Bump cache-buster `?v=20260826m`.

Two families of sklearn operators let the column already chosen as the label be chosen a second time as an input column, and neither said anything while the workflow was being written.

`Target Attribute` names the label and `Text Attribute` names the columns `Count Vectorizer` tokenizes, on the fifty-one operators of the Sklearn and Sklearn Training groups. The generated code drops the target before the text pipeline reads its columns, so naming it there asks the pipeline for a column that is no longer present and the run ends with `ValueError: A given column is not a column of the dataframe`, which names neither field. Failing is right, since vectorizing the label would train a model on the answer, so the pairing is refused at compile time instead, in the same `getOutputSchemas` that already refuses `Count Vectorizer` on the two Gaussian Naive Bayes operators. Only while the vectorizer is on: with it off nothing reads `text` and the panel hides it, so a value left behind by an earlier configuration must not report the operator invalid.

`Ground Truth Attribute Column` names the label and `Selected Features` names the columns handed to `fit`, on the four advanced trainers. Here nothing failed at all. The features go to `fit` as they are named, so the ground truth among them is the answer given to the estimator as an input, and the model scores far better than what it learned deserves. On two hundred rows whose label is random noise, a KNN classifier reaches 0.685 train accuracy on the two real features and 0.995 once the label is included, and nothing in the run says why. `selectedFeatures` defaults to null, so the check reads it through an `Option` rather than assuming a list is there.

Both messages name the column and both fields, and say what to change.

### Any related issues, documentation, discussions?

Closes #8010.

### How was this PR tested?

`SklearnModelOpDescSpec` gains three cases: the target named as a text column is refused, text columns that are not the target are let through, and a stale text column is left alone while `Count Vectorizer` is off. `SklearnMLOperatorDescriptorSpec` gains two: the ground truth named as a feature is refused, and features that do not include it are let through. Both files already owned the assertions on the `getOutputSchemas` these checks live in. `WorkflowOperator/test` passes: 2381 tests.

author: mkerian10
body:
Closes #292.

Investigating #292 turned up that `ensures` isn't a parser gap — it was deliberately eliminated from the language (docs/design/contracts.md, "Why No `ensures`?"): postconditions are redundant with class invariants, return types, and whole-program compilation, and the user-facing docs already say postconditions are handled by invariants. The confusing part was that the parser rejected it *incidentally* — "expected fn, found identifier" on trait signatures, "expected {, found identifier" on methods — which read as missing syntax support, and six Liskov tests were tagged "unsupported syntax" on that premise.

## Changes

- The parser recognizes the identifier `ensures` in contract position (after a signature, chained after `requires`, or where a return type would be) and rejects it with a targeted message:

  ```
  'ensures' clauses are not supported: Pluto has no postconditions by design;
  express guarantees with class invariants or return types (see docs/design/contracts.md)
  ```

  `ensures` is not a keyword and remains a valid ordinary identifier everywhere else (`let ensures = 5` still works).
- `tests/typeck/traits/liskov_violations.rs` is rewritten to match the design: the four ignored ensures tests and the chained requires+ensures test are un-ignored and pin the targeted rejection; relic tests that used ensures with an any-failure expectation now assert the specific message; the requires-side Liskov rules keep their existing coverage (implementations may not declare `requires` at all).

The one remaining ignored test in the file (trait methods with their own type parameters) is #291 territory.

## Mechanism

The ranked M5 candidate charges the 512-token target seed prefill inside the decode window. Dense target projections at that width route through `affine_qmm_t_nax`.

The shipped transposed NAX quantized matrix-matrix kernel executes each K tile serially:

1. load/dequantize one packed-weight tile into threadgroup memory;
2. barrier;
3. consume that tile through MMA;
4. barrier;
5. stage the next tile.

The floating-point NAX family already carries the standard double-buffer pattern. This change ports that scheduling pattern to the dense affine quantized transpose path:

- two threadgroup weight tiles;
- stage tile `i+1` while MMA consumes tile `i`;
- switch read/write slots after the barrier;
- preserve the existing dequantization, MMA accumulation, and store arithmetic.

A default-false `pipeline` template flag keeps existing callers unchanged. Only dense `affine_qmm_t_nax` instantiates `pipeline = true` and allocates `2 * BN * BK_padded`. The loader's `shift_dst` retargets the threadgroup destination without changing device source, scale, or bias traversal.

The earlier neighboring archive `43925f2` applied the same pipeline to the shared implementation used by both dense QMM_T and `affine_gather_qmm_t_nax`. It doubled threadgroup memory on both launch shapes and ranked about 0.31% below its then-current threshold.

Gather has different occupancy economics. Candidate decode and proposal operations use gathers at shapes unrelated to the 512-row dense seed prefill. Doubling threadgroup memory there can reduce occupancy while buying no scored dense-prefill overlap.

This archive therefore keeps gather on:

- `pipeline = false`;
- one `Ws[BN * BK_padded]` tile;
- the original single-buffer loop.

Only the candidate's dense target prefill changes. Decode-side custom QMV and gather behavior are byte-for-byte the live crown.

author: noureldinshobier
body:
Second batch: **27.2% → 28.7%** overall, and **ActionView 24% → 35%** — it was the thinnest area and the one carrying the most everyday code.

**Options** — `optionsForSelect`, `optionsFromCollectionForSelect`, `groupedOptionsForSelect`, `optionGroupsFromCollectionForSelect`, `Select`, `CollectionSelect`, `CollectionCheckboxes`, `CollectionRadioButtons`, `weekdayOptionsForSelect`, `timeZoneOptionsForSelect`.

**Fields** — the whole `*_tag` family: text, password, email, number, search, tel, url, date, time, datetime, month, week, color, range, file, hidden, textarea, label, submit, button, fieldset, datalist, checkbox, radio.

## Three details a hand-written version gets wrong

**Selected values compare as strings.** The value comes back from a form or a URL as a string; the options come from the database as numbers. A strict comparison selects nothing and looks like a rendering bug.

**An unchecked box sends nothing at all.** So a checkbox carries a hidden `0` and a collection carries a hidden empty. Without it, a form that unticks everything is indistinguishable from one that never had the field — which is how a setting turns itself back on.

**`false` drops an attribute** rather than writing `="false"`. A browser reads any non-empty value as true, so `disabled={false}` would disable the field.

Each has its own case.

## A measurement fix, not a gaming of it

The coverage tool now lowercases the first letter before matching, so a JSX component counts as the Rails helper it replaces. `TextFieldTag` is how `text_field_tag` is spelled here — the same feature, not a different one — and not matching it understated ActionView by eleven points.

Forty-five cases. 3,651 tests, 0 failures.

author: chiefgyk3d
body:
A bare figure doesn't say whether it's good. "A-index 4" means nothing until you know 7 is the quiet threshold; "C2.1" means nothing until you know where C sits between B and X.

Eight metrics now render as **a dial and a number** — needle and coloured band for severity at a glance, figure for precision, text label so colour never carries the meaning alone.

## Where the judgement lives

**In `severity.py`, not the renderer.** Whether K=5 is a storm is a fact about geomagnetism, not a drawing decision — so it's Python, where it's tested (68 new tests), and the canvas only draws what it's handed. Thresholds follow NOAA's published G / R / S scales where they exist and operating convention where they don't.

## Two decisions that were computed, not chosen

**Three severity levels, not four.** Four status colours can't be told apart reliably — amber vs orange measures below the normal-vision separation floor before colour blindness enters into it. Three separate cleanly: ΔE 27.6 normal, 11.3 protan.

This also replaces the *existing* status trio, which measured **ΔE 14.5 normal — below the floor for distinguishing two colours at all** — and was already shipping in Band Conditions and the needed badges.

**The green is the validated one, not the one I preferred.** I first substituted a green that suited the theme better; it dropped protan separation from 11.3 to 8.3. A sweep showed the cost is monotonic:

| green | protan ΔE |
|---|---|
| `#0ca30c` | **11.3** |
| `#16a81a` | 9.7 |
| `#1fae24` | 7.9 |
| `#26b132` | 7.0 |
| `#2eb83c` | 5.1 |

Took the measurement. There's a comment in the stylesheet saying not to lighten it to taste.

## Three bugs caught

- **X-ray class boundaries were off by one class.** `M1.0` is exactly 1e-5 and was classifying as C-class; `X1.0` as M. The boundary value belongs to the *upper* class on a decade scale but the *lower* zone on a published index (K≤3 and A≤7 are quiet), so the two conventions are now explicit per scale.
- **Adjacent same-level zones drew abutting segments** with a seam the reader would try to interpret. They merge.
- **The A-index dial looked alarming while its label said "Quiet"** — a 0–100 range squeezed the quiet band into an invisible sliver. Topped at 50, where the quiet zone is readable and anything above pins the needle. That's the worst failure mode a severity display has, so it has its own regression test.

## Accessibility

Every dial carries a text severity label and an `aria-label` reading value and severity, so it works in greyscale, in print, and for a colour-blind reader.

## Verification

505 tests, `ruff check` clean. Rendered and inspected — which is how the A-index problem was found; it passed every test before that.

body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

The batch prefill launchers pick `NUM_MMA_KV` by sizing a per-`NUM_MMA_KV` shared-memory cost (`kKVSmemPerMmaKV`) against the occupancy budget, so the kernel keeps two blocks per SM. For NVFP4 KV that cost left out the scale-factor staging entirely.

`SharedStorageQKVO` inherits `KVScaleFactorSmem`, which stakes out one UE4M3 byte per `NVFP4_SF_VEC_SIZE` elements, for K and for V:

```cpp
// include/flashinfer/attention/prefill.cuh
alignas(16) uint8_t k_sf_smem[CTA_TILE_KV * HEAD_DIM_QK / NVFP4_SF_VEC_SIZE];
alignas(16) uint8_t v_sf_smem[CTA_TILE_KV * HEAD_DIM_VO / NVFP4_SF_VEC_SIZE];
```

`CTA_TILE_KV` is `NUM_MMA_KV * NUM_WARPS_KV * 16`, so those two planes grow with `NUM_MMA_KV` exactly like the K/V tiles sitting next to them. The single-prefill launcher already carries the term; the ragged and paged launchers did not, so their chooser could settle on a `NUM_MMA_KV` whose real storage exceeds the budget it was selected against, and the later hard check against `max_smem_per_threadblock` is left to reject a configuration that a smaller tile would have satisfied.

This adds the missing term to the two launchers, matching the single-prefill one. Non-FP4 KV dtypes are unaffected: the term is `0` for them.

author: sgrebnov
body:
Fixes #13537.

## What was wrong

`Runtime::build()` ran with no subscriber. `main` ends its temporary one before `spiced::run`, and the global one cannot be installed first because its task-history layer is built from the `DataFusion` the build returns. Everything the build emitted was dropped, at every log level: the DuckDB accelerator memory budget and its recommended limits, the query memory-limit defaults, the invalid `runtime.query.timeout` warning, secret-store load failures.

Call sites worked around it one statement at a time with `in_tracing_context`, which installs a thread-local default — and that outranks the global subscriber, so those events bypass task history, the service log and the configured filter once it exists (`AppBuilder` does, on every pods-watcher reload). It is also why `Initialized sql results cache` reached the console and the memory-budget warning did not.

## Change

- Wrap `builder.build()` in the same window subscriber `main` puts around the spicepod load and the CPU budget, and `run` already puts around the cluster config.
- `in_tracing_context{,_async}` defer to a subscriber already listening instead of shadowing it.
- Drop the per-statement wraps now covered by the window, and turn the two paths that had fallen back to `eprintln!` (secret-store load, extension initialization) into `tracing::error!`.

The window subscriber is a stopgap: it writes to stdout at INFO, so these events still miss task history, `--service-log-dir` and Cloud Connect capture, and ignore `SPICED_LOG` — the same as the banner and the CPU-budget lines above them. Closing that means installing the global subscriber before the build, which needs the task-history exporter's query engine to be late-bound. Follow-up, not this PR.

## Testing

- `bin/spiced/tests/build_logging.rs` builds a runtime under a probe subscriber and asserts both a bare build-time warning and one emitted through `in_tracing_context` reach it. Reverting `tracing_util.rs` and `init/caching.rs` to their previous form fails it.
- `cargo test -p util --lib tracing_util`, `cargo test -p spiced --test build_logging`.
- `make lint-rust PACKAGES="util app runtime spiced"`.

Add optional Windows-native stdout/stderr redirection through one append-only file handle. Foreground completion no longer waits for inherited output pipes. Positioned writes append, and truncation through the inherited handle is denied.

author: centerzl93-lang
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #42. That PR fixed the founding barn ghost being invisible; this one fixes a bug reported right after: "I can see the barn every time but when I actually place it, it jumps back to a different location and not where I had it."

## What was wrong

`refreshConfirmBar` rebuilt the "Found here" confirm bar's closures fresh every frame:

```ts
const { tx, ty } = this.foundingReticle();
this.ui.showConfirm(text, 'Found here', () => this.confirmFounding(tx, ty), ...);
```

But `ui.showConfirm` only rebinds the button's actual `onclick` handler when the bar's **text** signature changes (`confirmSig` dedupe, to avoid clobbering an in-progress tap on every 100ms UI refresh). Founding's bar text is always one of two fixed strings ("Pan to where you want to found your village" / "Too close to the water..."), so that signature never changes as the player pans around — meaning the *first* closure built (capturing whatever `(tx, ty)` the reticle was on the moment founding began) is the only one that ever actually gets wired to the button. Every later pan updates the ghost and the reticle math, but clicking "Found here" still ran the stale, first-bound `(tx, ty)`.

## Fix

`confirmFounding()` now takes no parameters and reads `this.foundingReticle()` itself at click time — the same "defer to live state, don't snapshot it in a closure" pattern `confirmPaths()`/`confirmDemolish()` already use (both call parameterless methods that read `this.pendingPaths`/`this.pendingDemolish` live, which is why they weren't affected by this bug).

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` clean.
- Reproduced precisely with a headless repro: begin founding, let the confirm bar bind at the initial reticle tile, pan to a second valid dry tile far away, click confirm.
  - **Before the fix:** barn founded at the original (stale) tile, ignoring the pan entirely.
  - **After the fix:** barn founded at the tile actually panned to.
- Confirmed no other `showConfirm` call site shares this pattern — path/demolish confirms already read live state rather than capturing a snapshot.

author: rpsene
body:
Closes #212.

The report asked why profiles appear in two places, how they interact, and why selecting one does not set the other. They are not duplicates — they do different jobs — but nothing in the UI said so.

| | Main frame chips | Builder "Start from profile" |
|---|---|---|
| Writes | nothing | `setWorkspaceIds(new Set())` then `addWorkspaceIdsSmart(list)` |
| Effect | `isHighlightedByProfile` + `isDimmed` — a lens over the catalogue | replaces the workspace |
| Job | *show me what is in RVA23* | *build from RVA23* |

They stay independent deliberately: highlighting RVA23 to read it must not overwrite a configuration in progress, and seeding a configuration must not re-filter the catalogue being picked from. `risc_v_visualizer.jsx` already carries a comment explaining why the seed replaces rather than merges — mixing would "silently produce a configuration matching neither".

So this is a labelling defect, not an architectural one.

## Change

The filter row label goes from **Profile** to **Highlight**, and each chip gains a title: *"Highlight the extensions in RVA23 — does not change your ISA configuration"*.

One short word, not "Filter by profile": the comment above that row records it already overran at 320px with the old label plus four buttons, and a longer label would regress narrow viewports. Verified at a 500px viewport — no horizontal overflow.

## What I did not change

I first added a "Replaces the current selection" hint under the builder's menu header. On rendering it, the menu already ends with *"Replaces the current selection. Dependencies are resolved automatically, so the result may include more than the profile lists."* — the hint duplicated that sentence verbatim, so it was dropped. The builder side already explains itself; only the main frame was ambiguous.

## Verification

Checked in a browser rather than by assertion, per `AGENTS.md`:

- label renders, `textTransform: uppercase` applies, row is 355px with no body overflow
- both chip titles read correctly
- `npm test` 235 pass, `npm run lint` and `npm run build` clean

## Separate finding, not fixed here

At a 500px viewport the "Start from profile" dropdown is clipped off the left edge — its bounding box starts at `-108`. Pre-existing and horizontal, so unrelated to this change, but worth its own issue.

author: cassiebuhler
body:
One line in `k8s/configmap.yaml`.

The deployed default model was `"llm_model": "qwen"` — the **DSE-nimbus** entry in the picker. This switches it to `"glm-5"`, which is the **NRP GLM-5.2** entry:

```diff
-        "llm_model": "qwen",
+        "llm_model": "glm-5",
```

`glm-5` is already in `llm_models`, so this is a default change only — DSE-nimbus, NRP Gemma, Qwen3, GPT-OSS, Kimi, minimax-m2 and the OpenRouter entries all stay selectable.

The nginx sidecar's `proxy_read_timeout 600s` was raised specifically because GLM-5.2 decodes slowly and the 300s sidecar was the odd hop in the chain, so no timeout change is needed alongside this.

## Deploy note

⛔ **This touches `k8s/`, so `rollout restart` alone is not enough** — it would re-run the ConfigMap already in the cluster and serve the old default:

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s/configmap.yaml
kubectl rollout restart -f k8s/deployment.yaml   # picks up the new config.template.json at startup
kubectl rollout status  -f k8s/deployment.yaml
```

The startup command runs `envsubst` over `config.template.json`, so the new default lands in the served `config.json` only after the pods restart.

author: f5yct67kcv-source
body:
## Anlass

In ENT-184 stand als Risiko: *„Das Modul ist noch nie mit einer echten Datenbank gelaufen — alle Prüfungen bilden die Serverantworten nach."* Neun neue PHP-Endpunkte, kein einziger je ausgeführt. Ein Tippfehler in einem **Spaltennamen** kommt an jeder bestehenden Prüfung vorbei und fällt erst beim ersten echten Speichern auf.

## Was dazukommt

`pruefungen/pruef_sql.php` vergleicht jeden Spaltennamen im Backend-SQL mit dem Schema aus vier Quelldateien (`schema.sql`, `schema_planung.sql`, `schema_verfuegbarkeit.sql`, `planung_einrichten.php`):

- `INSERT INTO t (a, b, c)` — gibt es die Spalten? Und passt die Zahl der **Werte** zur Zahl der Spalten?
- `UPDATE t SET a = ?`
- `SELECT a, b FROM t` (eine Tabelle, kein JOIN)
- `… WHERE a = ? AND b IS NULL`

**878 Prüfungen über 312 Abfragen und 30 Tabellen, keine übersprungene Tabelle.** Eingebunden in `test_php.mjs` und dort wirklich ausgeführt, nicht nur statisch gelesen.

## Der Fund: ein echter Fehler, der schon länger drin war

`backend/api/einsatz_position.php` fragte `einsatz_zuteilung` zweimal über eine Spalte `id` ab:

```sql
SELECT id FROM einsatz_zuteilung WHERE einsatz_id = ? ORDER BY id
UPDATE einsatz_zuteilung SET position_id = ? WHERE id = ?
```

Diese Tabelle hat keine Spalte `id` — ihr Schlüssel ist zusammengesetzt aus `(einsatz_id, mitarbeiter_id)`. Mit `PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION` wirft das zur Laufzeit, und zwar im Zweig `aus_bedarf`, der genau dann läuft, wenn ein Einsatz noch keine Positionen hat — also beim **ersten Öffnen eines Einsatzplans**. Beide Abfragen laufen jetzt über den zusammengesetzten Schlüssel.

Der Fehler stammt **nicht** aus dem Offerten-Modul. Die Prüfung, die für die neuen Endpunkte gebaut wurde, hat einen Altbestand gefunden.

## Zwei Funde über die Prüfung selbst

**1. Der erklärende Kommentar hat den Fehler zugedeckt.** Die erste Fassung fand den Fehler — die Gegenprobe blieb trotzdem grün. Der Kommentar über der reparierten Abfrage enthielt selbst die Worte `SELECT id`; das Muster fand sie dort, las bis zum echten `FROM` weiter und verwarf den Treffer als „enthält eine Variable". Die Abfrage darunter wurde nie geprüft. Behoben, indem PHP-Kommentare vor der Suche per `token_get_all()` entfernt werden — ein eigenes Muster würde ein `//` in einer Zeichenkette nicht von einem Kommentar unterscheiden.

**2. Ein Fehlalarm auf korrektem Code.** Bei `UPDATE einsaetze SET bedarf = (SELECT … WHERE einsatz_id = ?) WHERE id = ?` wurde das `WHERE` der Unterabfrage der äusseren Tabelle zugeschrieben. Wo die Zuordnung nicht entscheidbar ist, wird jetzt nicht geraten — eine Prüfung mit Fehlalarmen wird ignoriert, und das ist der teurere Fehler.

## Gegenproben

Elf Stück, jede mit einer Zusicherung, dass die Änderung tatsächlich griff — alle rot, Grundzustand danach wieder grün:

- falscher Spaltenname in `INSERT` / `UPDATE SET` / `SELECT` / `WHERE`
- ein Wert zuwenig in `VALUES`
- beide Hälften des Originalfehlers einzeln
- Tippfehler in einer neu erfassten Tabelle (`sessions`)
- Kommentar-Entfernen abgeschaltet → zwei Selbstproben rot
- naives Muster statt `token_get_all` → Zeichenketten-Probe rot
- Schemaquelle entfernt → vier Tabellenproben plus Abdeckungsschwelle rot

Dass die Zusicherung nötig war, ist selbst ein Befund: Mehrere Gegenproben mit `perl -0pi` haben still **nichts** ersetzt. Das sah aus wie „Prüfung bleibt grün, obwohl der Fehler drin ist" — dabei war der Fehler nie drin.

## Was die Prüfung nicht kann

Sie ersetzt **keinen Lauf gegen eine echte Datenbank** (offen als OP-110). Ungeprüft bleiben: Abfragen mit JOIN, zur Laufzeit zusammengesetztes SQL, Datentypen, `NULL`-Zulässigkeit, Fremdschlüssel — und ob eine Abfrage fachlich das Richtige tut. Sie schliesst genau eine Lücke, diese dafür vollständig.

## Regression

**57 von 57 Suiten grün, 706s.** `test_php.mjs` von 64 auf 67 Prüfungen.

tdacomp
body:
## What this does

Replaces single-category navigation with flat, multi-valued tags. Tools and dashboards now live in one bucket (the Toolbox at /dashboard), browsed through a tag navigation in the global sidebar: **All Tools → ★ Favorites → My Most Used → [Tags divider] → 🔥 Company Hits + publisher tags**. Home and Links stay; Management is click-to-expand at the bottom. Home is the landing page after sign-in.

## Schema changes (additive only)

- **Tag** — id, unique lowercase slug, displayName, sortOrder; implicit many-to-many with PortalApp (`_AppTags`).
- **Favorite** — userId + appId, unique composite; cascade deletes.
- `PortalApp.category` is kept, deprecated, untouched. No existing data modified.

## Behavior

- **Filtering:** multi-select AND semantics; state lives in the URL (`/dashboard?tags=a,b&q=…`) so the sidebar works from any page and selections are shareable. Tile tag chips toggle the same state. Clear-all lands on All Tools.
- **Search:** tokenized, cross-field — every word must match somewhere in name/description/tags, each word may hit a different field ("sales map" → an app tagged sales + map).
- **Smart tags** (computed, no Tag rows): My Most Used = viewer's own opens, 90-day window, top 8, hidden with no history. Company Hits = org-wide top 10 by opens (5-min in-process cache), intersected with the viewer's accessible set afterward — never reveals an app the viewer can't access.
- **Sidebar:** publisher tags ranked by real usage (fallback: tag frequency); type tags (tool/dashboard) never take top-N slots; **coverage guarantee** greedily adds tags until every accessible app is reachable through publisher tags alone (marked with a life-ring + tooltip). While filtering, only co-occurring tags show — a click can never yield zero results.
- **Favorites:** star on tiles, optimistic toggle, server-validated against canAccessApp.
- **Admin:** /admin/tags (create/rename/merge/delete with usage counts, smart tags shown read-only) + tag picker in the Access Studio app editor. All tag mutations ADMIN-only.
- **Access control untouched:** tags are discovery only. Every count, list, coverage calc, and search result is computed from the viewer's canAccessApp set.

## Judgment calls

- **/dashboards page kept as-is** (URL-reachable) but its sidebar link is gone — dashboards surface in the Toolbox via the "dashboard" type tag. Smaller change than retrofitting the tag sidebar onto a second page; easy to delete the page later.
- **Department-derived tags are allowlist-only.** Prod uses departments as access-control groups too ("Test", "Limited", "Advanced Claude", "Sales Report") — those never become tags. Caught by dry-running the backfill on a prod snapshot.
- **Sign-in now lands on /home** (was /dashboard); non-admin /admin redirects go to /home.
- Vitest added as devDependency (`npm test`) — repo had no test runner. 25 unit tests cover AND filtering, coverage guarantee, co-occurrence, tokenized search, smart-tag computation and access scoping, and per-user count scoping.

## Rollout

1. Merge → Railway runs `prisma migrate deploy` (idempotent, additive).
2. Run the backfill once: `npx tsx prisma/backfill-tags.ts` — auto-tags every app (department, type, keyword heuristics; idempotent and additive; already dry-run against a prod snapshot: 20/20 apps tagged, 4 flagged for a manual department tag: Map Tool, Executive Dashboard, NAV Approval Reminder, Blueprint).
3. Fix flagged apps in Access Studio → edit app → Tags.

author: jeremyames-gmail
body:
ops #3282 closed with one open question: *"Check `deploy-staging.yml` against the real staging host before changing it — do not assume it is equally broken or equally fine."*

It has now been checked. **There is no staging host, and there is no staging anything.** Every claim below has a control that answered correctly:

| checked | result | control |
|---|---|---|
| `develop` branch (its only push trigger) | **absent** | `ls-remote`: 13 heads, `main` present |
| `STAGING_*` secrets | **none** | repo has 5 secrets, org has 0 |
| `staging` environment | **absent** | only `production` exists |
| `docker-compose.staging.yml` | **404** | `install.sh` → 200 |
| `runs-on` | `ubuntu-latest` — cannot reach `.mgmt.lakehouse.wtf` | `deploy.yml` uses `self-hosted` |
| install path (line 118) | `/opt/homelab-gitops-auditor` — the pre-#3282 wrong path | real dir is `/opt/gitops` |
| run history | **12 runs, ALL failure, last 2026-04-20, not one success ever** | `deploy.yml` has 204 runs |

Its deploy steps are gated on `HAS_STAGING_SSH`, which is false — so even if it reached them it would skip to green, the same silent failure mode #3282 found in `rollback.yml`. It never gets that far; it fails first.

## Also removed, because deleting the file alone leaves them dangling

**`release.yml`'s two staging steps** — the only live caller. This removes nothing that gated anything: `createWorkflowDispatch` returns immediately, and the step that followed was `sleep 180` whose result was never read. Production was dispatched regardless of whether staging succeeded, failed, or never started. **The production dispatch itself is left byte-for-byte unchanged.**

**`release.yml`'s release-notes template**, which told users to run:

```bash
gh workflow run deploy-staging.yml    # now deleted
gh workflow run deploy-production.yml # NEVER EXISTED — no such workflow in this repo
```

Both replaced with the real command, `gh workflow run deploy.yml`.

**`rollback.yml`'s comment** claiming `deploy-staging.yml` *"is NOT touched by this change — its host was never measured."* True when PR #271 was written, false now. Updated rather than left to rot — a stale comment in a file nobody runs is exactly how the original defect survived four months.

## Verification

```
no live workflow references the deleted file   only the 2 explanatory comments remain
all 15 remaining workflows parse                yaml.safe_load, each file
production dispatch unchanged                   diff confirms
```

## Not done / unverified

- **`release.yml`'s deploy chain is left in place and is broken in a second way** — its production dispatch targets `deploy-production.yml`, which does not exist, so it would 404. Whether that job should exist at all is **ops #3307**, not this change.
- **A `v*` tag still deploys production** — via `deploy.yml`'s own `tags: ['v*']` trigger, independent of `release.yml`. Untouched here; noted on #3307.
- **`deploy.yml`'s `workflow_dispatch` still offers a `staging` environment choice.** Another vestige, but it is an input option whose code path I did not trace, so I left it alone.
- **`.mcp/templates/**` and `CI_CD_PIPELINE_IMPLEMENTATION.md` still reference staging.** Templates and docs, not live workflows — deliberately untouched.
- **The rollback rehearsal #3282 asks for is still not done.** That needs production access and is unaffected by this change.

body:
Adds a `.gitleaks.toml` configuration file to narrow the secret-scan CI job's detection ruleset around confirmed false positives, and updates the CI workflow to use this config.

## Summary
The secret-scan job now uses a custom gitleaks configuration that extends the bundled default ruleset with a narrow allowlist for verified non-secrets. This prevents false positives from blocking CI while maintaining security by only allowlisting exact strings that have been manually verified.

## Changes
- **`.gitleaks.toml`** (new) — Configuration file that:
  - Extends the default gitleaks ruleset
  - Allowlists two confirmed false positives with `regexTarget = "line"` to match against the whole source line (not just the rule's captured span):
    - `DISMISS_KEY` localStorage key name used in `AllStarBanner.tsx` and its design doc
    - A progress-log line in `.superpowers/sdd/progress.md` narrating that a placeholder value (not a real key) was appended to `.env.local`
  - Includes detailed comments explaining the rationale for each allowlist entry and the policy for future additions

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — Updated the gitleaks Docker invocation to pass `--config=/repo/.gitleaks.toml`

- **`CLAUDE.md`** — Expanded the secret-scan job description to document the new configuration approach and policy: entries are only widened to the exact string that triggered them, and whole paths are never allowlisted just to quiet the tool

## Implementation notes
The allowlist uses `regexTarget = "line"` because generic-api-key's match window is narrower than the full phrases being allowlisted — matching only the rule's captured span would silently fail to allowlist anything. Each entry is verified by hand against the actual file contents and documented with its source location.

author: phix33
body:
- [x] Mark this if you consider it ready to merge
- [x] I've added tests (optional)
- [ ] I wrote some lines in the [book](https://github.com/radareorg/radare2book) (optional)

**Description**

`esil.gotolimit` is documented as "maximum number of gotos per ESIL expression", but `runword()` decremented the budget on **every word**, so it was really a 4096-word cap. That used to be invisible: no arch emits an expression anywhere near that length. With `r_esil_define` (#26560/#26556) it no longer is, because every token of an expanded definition counts too — `+=` now costs 6 words of budget instead of 1, and a long straight-line definition (a stack-only `CLZ` is ~100 tokens) traps as an "infinite loop" after a few dozen uses in one expression.

This makes the limit mean what its name says:

- the budget is consumed only when a `GOTO` is actually taken (`eval_word`), so straight-line expressions of any length run;
- definition nesting draws on the same budget (decrement on entry, restore on exit), which keeps the recursion bound that #26560 relied on the word counter for — a self-referencing definition still traps instead of overflowing the C stack;
- `esil.gotolimit=N` now allows exactly N jumps; before, the `< 1` check made it N-1.

Tests: `db/esil/esil` gets an 80-word straight-line expression and a counted `GOTO` loop under `esil.gotolimit=4` (both trapped before), plus a runaway `0,GOTO` that must trap; `test/unit/test_esil.c` gets a recursive-definition case. `db/esil` and `db/anal` are unchanged otherwise.
